title: P0-17: Flaky engine tests under load: loopback cap allowance and process-wide instance lock
description:
## Background
During P0-12 verification the full `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/all.sh` gate failed once on an existing engine test and passed unchanged on rerun (receipt: docs/validation/2026-10-18/P0-12.md, failure log retained by the agent). The read-only review (gpt-6-astra pane, 2026-10-18) traced it to the loopback partial-transfer assertions in `src/engine.rs` around line 2547: the test asserts partial progress and then `partial <= NO_UPLOAD_LIMIT * (elapsed + 1.5)`. With a 256 KiB fixture at 32 KiB/s, reporting the whole payload needs at least 6.5 s under that allowance, so a late observer alone cannot explain the recorded failure; the test is timing-sensitive and the cause is not established. No change in P0-12 touches the engine, the constant, the runtime or all.sh.

## Why
`all.sh` is the gate every P0 bead and the orchestrator's batch-verify rely on (PLAN §8.4, §9.1). A flaky assertion either hides real regressions behind reruns or blocks closes on noise. Honest credit requires the gate to be deterministic or the flake to be understood and owned.

## Do
1. Add failure diagnostics immediately before both assertions: the observed `partial`, payload length, elapsed time (monotonic), the effective upload limit, and the observer timestamps, printed through the test's JSONL logging (Appendix E `action`/`expect`/`observed`).
2. Reproduce the existing test unchanged in a loop (at least 30 runs, locally and once under load) and record the failure rate with the diagnostics attached.
3. Only then choose a fix: either a deterministic observation point (wait for the engine's own progress notification instead of a timer) or a corrected allowance derived from the actual cap and payload, with the derivation written in a comment. Do not loosen the assertion by a constant factor and do not delete it.
4. Keep both assertions and their intent; the fix must still fail if the upload cap is not applied.

## Acceptance criteria
- Diagnostics are printed on failure for both assertions and appear in the JSONL log.
- The failure rate before the fix is measured and recorded (runs, failures) in the receipt.
- After the fix, 50 consecutive runs of the test pass locally; the run log is retained.
- A deliberate removal of the upload cap in a scratch run still fails the assertion (planted negative, result recorded, cap restored).
- Receipt at docs/validation/2026-10-18/P0-17.md.

## Tests
- `cargo test --locked -p fbittorrent -- <the loopback partial-transfer test name>` in a 50-run loop with JSONL logging to target/test-logs/fbt-p0-17/.
- The planted-negative scratch run.

## Owned files
`src/engine.rs` (test module only, plus the minimal production change if step 3 needs an observation hook), docs/validation/2026-10-18/P0-17.md.

## Dependencies
None to start; coordinate with P0-10 (also edits src/engine.rs) by landing after it if both are in flight.

## Second flake (added 2026-10-18 by the orchestrator)
`engine::tests::queue_caps_downloads_preserves_fifo_pause_delete_completion_and_restart` panicked once during the P0-15 gate run under heavy load: `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: fbittorrent is already open; use the existing app` at `src/engine.rs:1514` (`InstanceLock::acquire_in(directory.join("runtime"))` inside `test_app`). The directory is unique per test (`review_directory` uses pid plus nanoseconds), so the lock that was busy is held in-process by another engine test running on a parallel test thread; the instance lock is effectively process-wide. The test passed 3 of 3 reruns in isolation. Fix direction: make the lock per directory (what the production code needs anyway for the daemon split) or serialize the engine tests with a test-only mutex; do not mark the test ignored. Acceptance: 50 consecutive full `cargo test --locked -p fbittorrent` runs with default parallelism pass; record the before-fix failure rate under load (run while a release build is compiling).
close_reason: Merged to main from ntm/fbittorrent/cod_4 @da37f93. Evidence: agent measured before-fix failure rates (1/30 local, 3/30 under build load) and 50/50 focused + 50/50 full passes after; planted uncapped negative fails at the cap assertion; fork-inherited lock descriptor regression fixed (explicit LOCK_UN on drop in src/ipc.rs, scope deviation accepted by the orchestrator); orchestrator re-ran the full suite 5x (130 passed each); gpt-6-astra review found the fixes sound; receipt docs/validation/2026-10-18/P0-17.md.

title: M0: Safe on main
description:
# M0: Safe on main

Milestone **M0** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3451, §9.7). Phase P0;
topological level 5 of 22.

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-06 (CI workflow and gates), P0-07 (The widget never starts the app), P0-08
(Graceful shutdown on terminal close), P0-09 (One bad record no longer blocks startup), P0-10 (Resume on a
finished torrent tells the truth), P0-11 (Truthful peer labels), P0-12 (Contract and README drift), P0-13
(Destructive confirms default to No), P0-14 (Private store permissions), P0-15 (Test logging contract and
shared harness module), P0-16 (Golden-render harness for the TUI).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-01 (A lifecycle object replaces the process-global statics).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## What this milestone is
M0 "Safe on main" closes phase P0: the product is in git with CI, the JSONL test logging and the golden-render
harness exist, and the live defects are fixed on today's architecture (no relaunch bug, no yes-by-default
delete, no startup blocker, no "0 seeds" or `eta: 8640000`). Release: **v0.1.1** (the landing, P0-04) then
**v0.1.2** (the fixes). Tag `v0.1.2`; install it. It is the first node of the critical path to every later
milestone (P0-01 → P0-02 → P0-04 → P0-05/P0-15 → P0-06 → M0 → P1-01 → …; weight 32 S-units to M1a and M1).

## What the owner can do at M0 (§9.7)
Use today's app, now in git, without the relaunch bug, the yes-by-default deletes or the startup blocker.
§0.5: "Today's app, now in git with CI, the JSONL test logging and the golden-render harness; the live defects
fixed on today's architecture: no relaunch bug, no yes-by-default delete, no startup blocker, no '0 seeds' or
`eta: 8640000`."

## Success Criteria
(the plan's definition of done (§9.5, phase P0))
A phase is done when every item's acceptance criteria pass **and** the phase's scripts are green on `main`.
Nothing else (no sign-off meeting, no report).
- Scripts that must be green: `all.sh` (90+ tests, `native.py` with JSONL logs, goldens, `fbtlog_test.py`);
  `cargo test -p librqbit-core -p librqbit`; CI on `main`.
- The one concrete human check: the owner installs `v0.1.2`, closes the Ghostty window during a download and
  sees no stale socket (P0-08).

## Items this milestone requires (the §9.4 edges into M0)
P0-06 (CI workflow and gates), P0-07 (the widget never starts the app), P0-08 (graceful shutdown on terminal
close), P0-09 (one bad record no longer blocks startup), P0-10 (resume on a finished torrent tells the truth),
P0-11 (truthful peer labels), P0-12 (contract and README drift), P0-13 (destructive confirms default to No),
P0-14 (private store permissions), P0-15 (test logging contract and shared harness module), P0-16
(golden-render harness). P0-01 to P0-05 are reached through those (P0-04 lands the product; P0-05 pins the
toolchain).

## Why this milestone exists
- R1 (low, critical): the uncommitted tree is the only copy of the product; one `git checkout` away from
  losing a month of work (§1.1). Until P0-04 is merged **no agent may run `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or
  `clean`**.
- The live defects D1, D2, D4, D5, D6 (labels), D7, D8, D10, D11, D14 are fixed on today's architecture
  because the owner runs the app daily and the daemon (P1) is weeks away (R18).
- Principle 10: every later item's tests are written on `fbtlog.py` (P0-15) and proven by goldens (P0-16); CI
  (P0-06) is in the Done definition of every later item.

## Demo (what to show at the M0 receipt)
1. `git log --oneline main | head` shows commits C1 to C6 and the merge "Land the native engine"; `git tag`
   lists `v0.1.1` and `v0.1.2`.
2. A fresh clone builds (`cargo build --release --locked`) and `all.sh` is green; the summary table lists the
   11 `native.py` cases.
3. Re-run the probe of `evidence/reconcile-autolaunch-probe.txt`: `status`, `reconcile` and `--no-start list`
   never invoke the launcher (P0-07).
4. Open the TUI during a download, close the Ghostty window: no `engine.sock` remains; `tui.stderr` has
   `engine drained in <ms> ms` (P0-08).
5. Start with one bad record: the app opens in under 10 s and lists it with its message (P0-09).
6. Press Enter on "DELETE … AND ITS FILES?": nothing is deleted (P0-13); a done torrent's footer shows `(U)
   Seed`, and `start` on it exits 1 with the hint `fbittorrent seed <hash>` (P0-10).
7. The captured screens show no "0 seeds" (P0-11); `stat -c %a shows.json` prints 600 (P0-14); `capabilities`
   says 32 KiB/s (P0-12).

## What is deliberately not in M0
- No daemon, no API, no new popup: today's architecture stays (the TUI hosts the engine) so the fixes ship
  fast.
- No `cargo fmt` (§8.4: a format-only diff would bury the history).
- No CPU optimisation (DL-18): only the resource gate scaffold.

## Owner decisions, risks and decisions
- Q3/Q30 (answered): the Asupersync fork with the full tree as fallback (P0-02's checkpoint is the one owner
  act before C3). Q4 (open, default `~/Archive/fbittorrent/`): archive backup location.
- R1, R11 (CI minutes), R19 (P0-02's checkpoint).
- DL-15 (Asupersync fork), DL-16 (receipts leave git), DL-46/DL-58 (C3 and option B), DL-59 (cuts), DL-66
  (P0-07's `online` test keeps the v0.1 popup hiding under the 1.2.0 stopped shape), DL-69 (`LICENSE` and
  `NOTICE` in P0-03).

## Containment in br (verified 2026-10-18 during polish round 1)
`br`'s `parent-child` relation makes the child depend on its parent epic: `br update <item> --parent <epic>`
removed the item from `br ready`, and `br dep add <epic> <item> -t parent-child` is refused with
`CYCLE_DETECTED: epic containment participates in blocking cycles`. That is incompatible with this plan's rule
that a milestone is blocked by its items (the §9.4 `blocks` edges), so no parent-child relation is recorded.
Membership is the `milestone:<ID>` label carried by every item whose first downstream milestone is this one;
list them with `br list -l milestone:M0 --json`. `br epic status` reports 0 children for this epic by design;
close it by hand (`br close`) once every item in that list is closed and the definition of done above is met.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Scripts that must be green: `all.sh` (90+ tests, `native.py` with JSONL logs, goldens, `fbtlog_test.py`); `cargo test -p librqbit-core -p librqbit`; CI on `main`.
- [ ] The one concrete human check: the owner installs `v0.1.2`, closes the Ghostty window during a download and sees no stale socket (P0-08).
- [ ] P0-06 (CI workflow and gates) is closed
- [ ] P0-07 (The widget never starts the app) is closed
- [ ] P0-08 (Graceful shutdown on terminal close) is closed
- [ ] P0-09 (One bad record no longer blocks startup) is closed
- [ ] P0-10 (Resume on a finished torrent tells the truth) is closed
- [ ] P0-11 (Truthful peer labels) is closed
- [ ] P0-12 (Contract and README drift) is closed

# M1: First demo (v0.2.0)

Milestone **M1** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4375, §9.7). Phase P2;
topological level 17 of 22.

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-14 (Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters), M1a (Daemon behind
today's UIs (v0.2.0-pre, installed, not tagged)), P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P2-05 (Theme-token lint and
light/dark check), P2-06 (Isolated Quickshell smoke test), P2-07 (Menu, keybinding, desktop entries, install
script).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P4-09 (Remove legacy qBittorrent mode and the compat paths).

and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

## What this milestone is

the same as M1a: after P1-08 the daemon branch (P1-12 → P1-17 → P1-11 → P1-15 → M1a) and the plugin branch
(P2-01 → P2-02 → P2-03 → P2-05) both weigh 9.

## What the owner can do at M1 (§9.7)

  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent

  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

# M1a: Daemon behind today's UIs (v0.2.0-pre, installed, not tagged)

Milestone **M1a** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4091, §9.7). Phase P1;
topological level 16 of 22.

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-04 (systemd user unit and start on demand), P1-11 (The CLI on the API client;
contract 1.2.0), P1-12 (Stop rule and idle exit), P1-13 (Daemon notifications and the icon), P1-15 (The TUI
attaches to the daemon; quit verbs), P1-16 (Lazy restore of completed torrents), P1-17 (Upgrade detection and
`restart`), P1-18 (Agent event stream and raw API verb).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M1 (First demo (v0.2.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## What this milestone is
M1a "Daemon behind today's UIs" closes phase P1: `fbittorrent serve`, systemd on demand, API v1 behind today's
UIs, agent `events`/`api`. Release: **v0.2.0-pre, installed on the owner's machine, not tagged** (DL-57). It
is the first moment the owner lives with the new lifetime (R5) and makes the one-time upgrade check of §3.6 by
hand; its receipt records that compat check. Round 3 added it because the first user-visible change would
otherwise be at the end of P2, after 32 S-units of serial work (R18). Weight to M1a: 32 S-units, the same as
M1.

## What the owner can do at M1a (§9.7)
Magnet clicks without terminals; downloads survive closing the TUI; idle exit with `fbittorrent status`
showing the countdown; completion and added notifications; `events`/`api` for agents; the old popup still
works through the new CLI (`status --json`, `--no-start` actions). §0.5: "`scripts/install.sh`, then a magnet
click with every window closed: no terminal, one 'Added' toast with Undo and Open window; the TUI's `q` leaves
the download running; `fbittorrent status --json` counts down the idle exit; `events --follow` streams
`torrent.completed` to an agent; the v0.1 popup still works and still hides when the daemon stops."

## Success Criteria
(the plan's definition of done (§9.5, phase P1))
- Scripts green on `main`: `all.sh` + `daemon.py` (every P1 case) + `agent_contract.py` + `native.py` (the TUI
  as a client); `resources.py --daemon` baseline written (P1-08).

  not a terminal.

verbs), P1-16 (lazy restore of completed torrents), P1-17 (upgrade detection and `restart`), P1-18 (agent
event stream and raw API verb). Through them: P1-01, P1-02, P1-19, P1-03, P1-05, P1-06, P1-07, P1-08, P1-09,
P1-10, P1-14.

still `Starting` waits for the session instead of failing (the §9.3 preamble's 60 s rule); exactly one toast

  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on

title: M2: Every step of W1, W2 and W8 works from the dashboard (v0.3.0)
description:
# M2: Every step of W1, W2 and W8 works from the dashboard (v0.3.0)

Milestone **M2** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4863, §9.7). Phase P3;
topological level 19 of 22.

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P3-16
(Dashboard smoke, captures, README).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** nothing (a terminal milestone).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## What this milestone is
M2 "Every step of W1, W2 and W8 works from the dashboard" closes phase P3: search, RSS, Shows and IMDb run in
the daemon (A4); the dashboard window with its six views (Torrents, Search, Shows, RSS, Settings, Log), the
poster grid and show quality. Release: **v0.3.0**. Weighted longest path 38 S-units (§9.4: M2 ← P3-16 ← P3-18
← P3-07 ← P1-15 ← …).

## What the owner can do at M2 (§9.7)
Run everything from the dashboard window, including the poster grid and show quality. §0.5: "Search, RSS,
Shows and IMDb run in the daemon; the dashboard window with its six views, the poster grid and show quality;
every step of W1, W2 and W8 from the window."

## Success Criteria
(the plan's definition of done (§9.5, phase P3))
- Scripts green on `main`: P2's set + `qs-dashboard.sh` (every case, `width_tiers` at the four tier boundaries
  1599/1399/1099 ± 1 px and ≥ 1600) + `daemon.py` P3 cases + captures at 900/1280/1500/1600.
- The one concrete human check: the owner runs the M2 demo script without a hitch.

## Items this milestone requires (the §9.4 edges into M2)
P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback) and P3-16 (dashboard smoke, captures,
README). Through them: P3-01 to P3-06, P3-08 to P3-15, P3-17, P3-18, P2-06.

## M2 demo script (§9.7)
Open the dashboard with the keybinding (P2-07's chord); search "Sintel"; see deduplicated results with posters
and IMDb ratings (P3-12, P3-01, P3-04); Enter stages the add; the add sheet shows files, the seed switch and
the destination (P3-11, P3-06); Enter downloads; the torrent appears in Torrents with a details pane (P3-09,
P3-10); uncheck a file in Files; press `2` with an empty query and see the poster grid (P3-17); open Shows,
set a show's quality to 2160p, mark a release read, undo it (P3-13, P3-18, P3-03); open Settings, change max
downloads, see it apply live (P3-15, P3-05); narrow the window below 1,400 px and see the details become a
sheet (§4.3.3); close the window while downloading; the download continues (A1).

## The workflows this milestone completes (§2.3)
- **W1 Find, inspect, deliberately download, watch.** Done when: a result can be downloaded with one key from
  either UI, the torrent shows progress within 2 s, "Ready to watch" appears before completion on a video
  (that last part is P5-05, M4), and `o` opens the file.
- **W2 Follow shows.** Done when: the inbox survives restarts, a check never downloads anything, and read
  state and transfer state are shown independently.
- **W8 Clean up.** Remove one at a time through an explicit choice between "Remove" and "Remove and delete
  files" (the 10 s undo and bulk remove are P6-08, M5).

## Dashboard geometry recap (§4.2.2, §4.3.3; DL-30)
Panes sidebar 200 / details 360 in `Style.space`; fixed table columns 748 px; NAME floor 210 px; tiers ≥ 1600
(all columns), 1400–1599 (↑, RATIO, ADDED hidden), 1100–1399 (details as a sheet), 900–1099 (sidebar as a chip
row); chrome 636 / 246 / 16 px; default window 1600×900, minimum 900×560; the owner's tiled ~960 px window
lands in the chip-row tier by design (Q17).

## Migration state at M2 (§3.6 row v0.3.0)
`api.sock`: daemon. `engine.sock`: daemon, compat adapter. CLI: API v1. Plugin: API v1 popup and dashboard.
TUI: moves to API v1 in P4-03 (M3).

Milestone **M3** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5088, §9.7). Phase P4;

  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.

  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait

  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the

  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,

  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;

  with new names.

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays

running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## What this milestone is
M4 "T1 complete" closes phase P5: peers and true seed counts, recheck, turtle and global limits, "Ready to
watch" that does not cry wolf (`stall_free`), the low-disk banner, in both UIs. Release: **v0.5.0**. Weighted
longest path 42 S-units (§9.4: M4 ← P5-02 ← P4-03 ← P3-07 ← …). T1 features land in the dashboard **and** the
TUI (§6.1 rule; A2).

Peers, true seed counts, recheck, turtle and global limits, ready to watch (with "may stall"), low-disk
warning, in both UIs.

  `have_pieces_snapshot_*`).
- The one concrete human check: the owner starts a film and gets "Ready to watch" before it finishes, and a
  "may stall" row when the turtle limit is below the bitrate.

## Items this milestone requires (the §9.4 edges into M4)
P5-02 (peers views), P5-03 (recheck), P5-04 (global and alternative speed limits), P5-05 (ready to watch),
P5-07 (low disk space warning and `disk_full`). Through them: P5-01 (seed count and peer list), P5-06 (the
fork's have-bitfield accessor).

## M4 demo script (§9.7)
Start a film from Search; within the first minute the row turns "Ready to watch" and a notification offers
"Open" (P5-05); press `o` and the player starts while the download continues; throttle the connection below
the bitrate (`z` with a 200 KB/s turtle limit, P5-04) and the row changes to "Playable · may stall (finishes
in 18 min)" within two seconds, then back when the limit is lifted; open Peers and see seeds and leechers with
moving rates (P5-01, P5-02); `R` rechecks after a deliberate corruption and the torrent heals (P5-03); fill
the destination with a filler file and the "Not enough space" banner appears in the popup, the dashboard and
the TUI before any torrent errors; delete the filler and the banner clears (P5-07).

## Why T1 (§6.1)
T1 fixes a lie the UI tells today (D6 "0 seeds"; `ENOSPC` as a raw error), or directly serves workflows W1 to
W5 (ready to watch is W1 step 4; turtle is the owner's named OmaTorrent capability; recheck after a crash),
and costs at most M once the daemon exists. "Better than qBittorrent" (§2.7) is earned here: ready-to-watch
with `stall_free` (Fragments and qBittorrent have nothing like it), proven by `daemon.py::playable_*` with a
local seed throttled to 1 MiB/s on a 64 MiB fixture.

title: M5: T2 complete (v0.6.0)
description:
# M5: T2 complete (v0.6.0)

Milestone **M5** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5593, §9.7). Phase P6;
topological level 20 of 22.

**Depends on (blocked by):** P6-01 (Tracker status and reannounce (fork change)), P6-02 (Pieces bar), P6-03
(Speed history and sparklines), P6-04 (Statistics, session and all-time), P6-05 (Force start and queue order),
P6-06 (App-owned fast resume (fork change)), P6-07 (Live per-torrent upload cap without rebuild (fork
change)), P6-08 (Origin field, filters, bulk remove, undo for keep-files removal), P6-09 (Peer port setting
and sleep inhibitor), P6-10 (New-release notifications for Shows), P6-11 (Destination picker with free space
in the add sheet), P6-12 (Private-torrent rules (BEP 27) check), P6-13 (Clipboard magnet watch (opt-in, A7)).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** nothing (a terminal milestone).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## What this milestone is
M5 "T2 complete" closes phase P6: trackers, pieces, graphs, statistics, queue control, fast resume, undo, the
opt-in clipboard watcher, and the smaller T2 items (live upload cap, port setting and sleep inhibitor, Shows
notifications, destination picker, the private-flag check). Release: **v0.6.0**. Weighted longest path 48
S-units (§9.4: M5 ← P6-01 ← P4-04 ← P4-03 ← …). T2 lands in the dashboard first and in the TUI when the work
is small (A2; §6.1).

## What the owner can do at M5 (§9.7)
Trackers, pieces, graphs, statistics, queue control, fast resume, undo, clipboard watch.

## Success Criteria
(the plan's definition of done (§9.5, phase P6))
- Scripts green on `main`: P5's set + `daemon.py` P6 cases + the `FBT_TEST_RESOURCES=1` gate (the resource
  regression gate of P0-06 against P1-08's baseline: margin 3 × the spread over three runs, never below 10 %).
- The one concrete human check: the owner turns on clipboard watching for a day and reports whether it is
  useful (Q11).

## Items this milestone requires (the §9.4 edges into M5)
P6-01 (tracker status and reannounce), P6-02 (pieces bar), P6-03 (speed history and sparklines), P6-04
(statistics), P6-05 (force start and queue order), P6-06 (app-owned fast resume), P6-07 (live per-torrent
upload cap), P6-08 (origin, filters, bulk remove, undo), P6-09 (peer port and sleep inhibitor), P6-10
(new-release notifications for Shows), P6-11 (destination picker with free space), P6-12 (private-torrent
rules check), P6-13 (clipboard magnet watch).

## What to show at the M5 receipt (there is no §9.7 script for M5; these are the items' acceptance criteria run in sequence)
1. Against the fixture tracker, the first announce shows `status: error` and `e` turns it `ok` with `peers: 1`
   in both UIs; no query string appears anywhere (P6-01).
2. The Pieces tab shows first and last pieces and the playable prefix for a 1,000-piece fixture in both UIs
   (P6-02).
3. `status --json`'s `history` has 60 entries; the dashboard status row and the TUI tab bar draw the sparkline
   (P6-03); `all_time` survives a restart (P6-04).
4. With `max_active_downloads = 1`, `P` force-starts a second torrent and both run; `K`/`J` reorder the queue
   without pausing the running one (P6-05).
5. Restart the daemon with untouched data: no `checking`; touch one file: only that torrent re-checks; `kill
   -9`: every torrent re-checks (P6-06). A cap change never re-checks (P6-07).
6. `X` on a filtered view removes the set keeping files with a count-and-size confirm; `U` within 10 s brings
   them back as `done` without re-downloading; the sidebar's "From:" filters group by origin (P6-08).
7. A port change restarts the engine with clients connected; `systemd-inhibit` is held only while a download
   runs (P6-09).
8. A Shows check with new releases posts one "3 new episodes" notification; none when nothing is new (P6-10).
9. The add sheet shows "N GiB free" and refuses an unwritable folder (P6-11); a private fixture torrent

T2 helps diagnose a slow or stuck download (trackers, pieces, graphs, peers' rates), or adds comfort (undo,
queue control, fast resume, clipboard watch), and may need a change in the rqbit fork (P6-01, P6-06, P6-07).

  delete-files), Q29 (open, default undo per batch), Q5 (open, default no automatic downloads for shows).
- R7 (fast resume trusts changed data: the clean marker, size and mtime, `recheck`), R8 (three fork changes),
  R16 (the clipboard watcher reads sensitive text: off by default; `clipboard_never_logged`), R9 (the resource
  gate is in this phase's Done).

`br`'s `parent-child` relation makes the child depend on its parent epic: `br update <item> --parent <epic>`

`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## What this milestone is
M6 "T3 complete" closes phase P7: Torznab indexers, move, rename, tracker editing, the quick-add palette, the
per-torrent download cap, deferred add while waiting for the VPN. Release: **as they land** (no single tag is
promised; §0.5 "P7 → M6: as they land"). Weighted longest path 50 S-units (§9.4: M6 ← P7-04 ← P6-01 ← P4-04 ←
…). The last of the 22 topological levels.

## What the owner can do at M6 (§9.7)
Torznab, move, rename, tracker editing, quick-add palette, deferred add.

## Success Criteria
(the plan's definition of done (§9.5, phase P7))
- Scripts green on `main`: P6's set + the P7 cases (`daemon.py::torznab_*`, `move_*`, `tracker_add_remove`,
  `download_cap_holds`, `deferred_add_saved_record`; `agent_contract.py::{move_verb, rename_verb,
  limit_verb}`; `qs-smoke.sh::palette`; `qs-dashboard.sh::palette_summon_routing`; the fork tests
  `tracker_set_mutation`; the unit tests `torznab::tests::parse_fixture`,
  `display_name_survives_restore_and_metadata`, `rename_validation`, `effective_rate_is_min`).
- Human check: n/a.

## Items this milestone requires (the §9.4 edges into M6)
P7-01 (Torznab indexers), P7-02 (move / set location), P7-03 (rename display name), P7-04 (tracker add and
remove), P7-05 (quick-add and search overlay palette), P7-06 (per-torrent download cap), P7-09 (deferred add
while waiting for the VPN).

## Superseded IDs that are not work (and must not become beads)
- **P7-07 "TUI retirement review"**: superseded in round 1, removed as ceremony. A review meeting produces no
  capability; the owner decided to keep the TUI (A2) and can read the per-kind counters of P1-14 at any time
  (the `clients` object of `fbittorrent api app.info --json`).
- **P7-08 "Marketplace readiness"**: superseded in round 3, removed as ceremony. The marketplace is not a goal
  (DL-17, §7.1); §7.4 keeps a two-line note of what a listing would take (a separate public plugin repository
  with a root `manifest.json`, README, licence and real screenshots; a build without the curated providers and
  browse lists; the plugin detecting a missing or old binary; a security note listing §7.2's bounds), and
  nothing is designed until the owner asks.

## What to show at the M6 receipt (the items' acceptance criteria)
1. A Torznab fixture returns results deduplicated with the other providers; a key over plain HTTP to a
   non-loopback host and a cross-origin redirect are refused; the key never appears in logs (P7-01).
2. `move` within and across filesystems; a completed torrent stays `done` without a re-check; a failed copy
   leaves the source intact (P7-02).
3. `rename` survives a restart and a metadata re-resolution; an empty name reverts (P7-03).
4. An added tracker receives announces; a removed one receives none after the next cycle (P7-04).
5. The palette: type a magnet, Enter adds; type a query, Enter stages; the bar plugin's toggle routing is
   unaffected (P7-05).
6. `limit <sel> --down 64K` holds within ±25 % and never re-checks (P7-06).
7. With a missing interface, `add` answers `deferred: true`; when the interface appears, the torrent starts
   (P7-09).

## Why T3 (§6.1)
Marginal for this owner, or large engine work; each lands when cheap and reaches the TUI only when the work is
small (A2; P7-02 and P7-06 have no TUI side).

## Owner decisions, risks and decisions
- Q6 (a second free chord for the palette), Q27 (open, default keep the rename override).
- R8 (two fork changes: tracker set mutation; none new for Torznab), R10 (the deferred add's namespace
  fixture), R2/R3 (the palette as a separate plugin id).
- DL-04 (no overlay in v1; the palette is the later option), DL-17 (no marketplace goal; P7-08 superseded),
  DL-03 (P7-07 superseded), DL-64 (`display_name` revert), DL-69 (Torznab key file, 4 MiB and 30 s caps).

## Containment in br (verified 2026-10-18 during polish round 1)
`br`'s `parent-child` relation makes the child depend on its parent epic: `br update <item> --parent <epic>`
removed the item from `br ready`, and `br dep add <epic> <item> -t parent-child` is refused with
`CYCLE_DETECTED: epic containment participates in blocking cycles`. That is incompatible with this plan's rule
that a milestone is blocked by its items (the §9.4 `blocks` edges), so no parent-child relation is recorded.
Membership is the `milestone:<ID>` label carried by every item whose first downstream milestone is this one;
list them with `br list -l milestone:M6 --json`. `br epic status` reports 0 children for this epic by design;
close it by hand (`br close`) once every item in that list is closed and the definition of done above is met.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
