description:
# P0-01: Archive validation receipts out of the working tree

Plan item **P0-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3066). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M0**; topological level 0 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** nothing: this is a level-0 item.

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P0-02 (Host the Asupersync patch as a pinned git fork), P0-04 (Land the native
product on `main`).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Nothing of the native engine is committed. Branch `codex/shows-native-engine` has zero commits beyond `main`
  (2026-09-03, the legacy qBittorrent-nox WebUI client): 19 modified files (+6363/-426) and about 3,575
  untracked files, including `vendor/` (60 MB) and `docs/validation/` (279 MB, 2,197 files, six dated
  directories: the receipts of the October 9 to 14 download-CPU qualification, 231 MB from one day). A `git
  checkout`, `git clean` or a disk failure would turn the product back into the September legacy app (R1).
  Until P0-04 lands, **no agent may run `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` in this repository.**
- Inside the receipts sit four copies of IMDb's `title.ratings.tsv` (28.7 MB each). They are regenerable
  caches of a dataset whose terms do not allow redistribution.
- Tracked Markdown files link into the receipts, for example `docs/tui-ux-review.md` links
  `validation/2026-10-10/native-integration.txt`. Moving files out must not break those links.
- There is no `scripts/` directory yet; this item creates it.

## Goal and user value
Receipts are evidence, not source: 279 MB must not enter git history (RC §12; DL-16 "Validation receipts leave
git except READMEs and small linked files"). This item makes the first commit (P0-04) small and reviewable,
and it takes the whole-tree backup that lets P0-02 later remove `vendor/asupersync/` safely (R19). It is the
first item on the critical path to every milestone (P0-01 → P0-02 → P0-04 → …, weight 32 S-units to M1a and
M1).

## Do (exact steps)
1. **Back up the whole working tree first** (§8.1 step 1), from the repository root: `tar --zstd -cf
   ~/Archive/fbittorrent/worktree-2026-10-18.tar.zst --exclude=./target .` (`mkdir -p ~/Archive/fbittorrent`
   first). Record its SHA256 in the receipt. Reading the tree is safe; nothing is modified by this step.
2. **Write `scripts/check-doc-links.sh`** (the `scripts/` directory is new here). It lists every Markdown link
   from tracked `*.md` files into `docs/validation/` (`rg -o '\]\((validation|docs/validation)/[^)]+\)'`),
   resolves each against the tree, and writes one line per link to `target/test-logs/docs/links.jsonl` in the
   E.1 shape: `{ts, suite: "docs", case: "links", step, action: "<file>:<line> -> <target>", expect: "exists",
   observed, ok}`; it exits 1 on any broken link.
3. **Compute the keep-set** of §8.3: every `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` (six dated directories today)
   plus every linked file under 256 KB.
4. **Write `docs/validation/MANIFEST.sha256`**: one line `<sha256>  <size>  <path>` for everything outside the
   keep-set.
5. **Delete** the four `title.ratings.tsv` copies (28.7 MB each) instead of archiving them (regenerable;
   redistribution not allowed).
6. **Pack the rest** into `~/Archive/fbittorrent/validation-2026-10-09_14.tar.zst`; verify the archive by
   listing it and comparing every hash with the manifest; then remove the archived files from the working
   tree.
7. **Write `docs/validation/ARCHIVE.md`**: archive path, SHA256, size, and the restore command `tar --zstd -xf
   … -C docs/validation`.
8. **Write the receipt** section `## P0-01` in `docs/validation/2026-10-18/README.md` (Appendix D "Receipt"):
   the two archive SHA256s (worktree backup and validation archive) and the link-check summary.
9. Where the archive is backed up beyond `~/Archive/fbittorrent/` is the owner's call (Q4, default:
   `~/Archive/fbittorrent/` only).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §8.3 Validation receipts: keep in git every `docs/validation/<date>/README.md`, every file under 256 KB that
  a tracked markdown file links to, and the new `MANIFEST.sha256`; move out everything else (about 279 MB) to
  the archive with its SHA256 in `ARCHIVE.md`; delete the `title.ratings.tsv` copies; from now on `.gitignore`
  ignores `docs/validation/**` except `README.md`, `MANIFEST.sha256`, `ARCHIVE.md` and files explicitly added
  with `git add -f` (P0-03 writes those rules); receipts over 1 MB never enter git.
- Appendix D "Receipt": the record of an item's verification, a section `## <ID>` in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with their exit codes, the `target/test-logs/`
  paths, and any manual observation or decision. Nothing else is a receipt, and no receipt carries files over
  256 KB.
- Appendix E.2: `scripts/check-doc-links.sh` covers "markdown links into `docs/validation`"; it does **not**
  run in CI (once here, then by hand whenever receipts move; DL-59 cut the CI job because nothing under
  `docs/validation/` changes between releases).
- P0-15's `fbtlog.py` does not exist yet, so the JSONL here is written by the shell script itself in the E.1
  shape.

## Acceptance criteria
- `du -sh docs/validation` is under 2 MB.
- `scripts/check-doc-links.sh` exits 0 (every link from tracked Markdown into `docs/validation/` resolves).
- The validation archive's SHA256 matches `docs/validation/ARCHIVE.md`; the archive lists every path in
  `MANIFEST.sha256` with matching hashes.
- The worktree backup `~/Archive/fbittorrent/worktree-2026-10-18.tar.zst` exists and its SHA256 is in the `##
  P0-01` receipt.
- No `title.ratings.tsv` remains under `docs/validation/`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `scripts/check-doc-links.sh` logs each link and its result to `target/test-logs/docs/links.jsonl` (`action`
  = `<file>:<line> -> <target>`, `expect` = `exists`, `observed` = found/missing, `ok`) and exits non-zero on
  a broken link. It runs once here and by hand whenever receipts move; it is not a CI job.
- Archive verification: list the archive and diff its hashes against `MANIFEST.sha256`; the output goes in the
  receipt.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on nothing: it is one of the two level-0 items (with P0-03) and starts the critical path.
- Consumed by P0-02 (its step 6 removes `vendor/asupersync/`, which must not happen before the whole-tree
  backup exists) and P0-04 (the landing commits must not include the 279 MB).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q4 (open): where the validation archive (about 279 MB, outside git) is backed up. Default:
  `~/Archive/fbittorrent/` only.

## Risks and decisions
- R1 (low likelihood, critical impact): the uncommitted tree is lost before P0-04 lands. Mitigation: this
  backup first; P0-04 is the first change; no destructive git commands.
- R19: P0-02 removes `vendor/asupersync/`; this item's backup is what makes that safe, hence the P0-02 → P0-01
  edge.
- DL-16: validation receipts leave git except READMEs and small linked files.
- DL-59 (cuts of machinery): no CI job for `check-doc-links.sh` (and none for `dagcheck.py` or
  `mockwidth.py`); they run by hand.
- Effort lesson (§1.7): October 11 to 14 went into download-CPU qualification (231 MB of receipts) while
  nothing was committed; the plan schedules no further CPU optimisation (DL-18), only a regression gate
  (P0-06).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

title: P0-02: Host the Asupersync patch as a pinned git fork
description:
# P0-02: Host the Asupersync patch as a pinned git fork

Plan item **P0-02** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3093). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M0**; topological level 1 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-01 (Archive validation receipts out of the working tree).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- `vendor/asupersync/` (57 MB) is crates.io Asupersync 0.5.0 (upstream rev `78b64636…`) plus a local patch.
  `Cargo.toml:49-52` uses `[patch.crates-io] asupersync = { path = "vendor/asupersync" }`; the `asupersync`
  entry at `Cargo.lock:218` has no `source` line today.
- The patch is **not** only the timer wheel, although `vendor/asupersync/FBITTORRENT_PATCH.md` says so today.
  `diff -r` against the registry copy (`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/asupersync-0.5.0`) shows 10 files, about 1,308
  lines added and 11 removed: `src/time/wheel.rs` (+192, the `next_deadline` cleanup) and the restored
  upstream `src/time/wheel_metamorphic_tests.rs` (626 lines the crates.io package left out); the
  `epoch-diagnostics` feature (`Cargo.toml` +2, `src/runtime/epoch_diagnostics.rs` 196 lines,
  `src/runtime/epoch_tracker.rs` +113/-10, `src/runtime/mod.rs` +3, `src/runtime/builder.rs` +26);
  `RegionOwnerKey` and `Cx::reusable_region_owner_key()` in `src/cx/cx.rs` (+63, with
  `src/cx/region_owner_tests.rs`), which the rqbit fork calls
  (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/spawn_utils.rs:63,86,96`) and without which the build fails; and an
  unconditional change in `src/runtime/state.rs`
  (`EpochConsistencyTracker::with_independent_module_sequences`, a `VecDeque` violations store).
- `vendor/asupersync/LICENSE` is "MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)", `license =
  "LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider"` in `vendor/asupersync/Cargo.toml:118`; every distribution must
  carry the rider unmodified, and a fork is a distribution. The owner answered Q3 and Q30 on 2026-10-18: "who
  cares, continue" (the public fork; the rider's risk accepted; the plan draws no legal conclusion; DL-70).
- `regression_tests/timer_wheel_tests.rs` and `run_timer_wheel_tests.py` hard-code the vendored path
  (`timer_wheel_tests.rs:3,65`, `run_timer_wheel_tests.py:55-57,112-113`), default `--support-lock` to a file
  that does not exist (`:83-84`), and can never pass from a clean clone because `select_core` accepts only a
  registry or vendored rlib.
- The `cargo` on `PATH` is a mise shim with no version until P0-05 pins the toolchain; use the rustup
  toolchain `~/.rustup/toolchains/1.98.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/cargo`, as `all.sh:6` does.

## Goal and user value
57 MB in every clone, forever, for a 690-line change is the wrong trade (§8.2; DL-15 "Asupersync through a
pinned git fork; rqbit and nova3 stay in-tree"). A `rev` pin is as reproducible as a path. Hosting the patch
as a fork also lets the wheel fix be offered upstream (R8). This item is on the critical path (P0-01 → P0-02 →
P0-04).

## Do (exact steps)
**Checkpoint before anything is pushed.** The **owner** creates the empty public repository
`github.com/odcpw/asupersync` (creating or pushing a public repository is publishing; an agent never does it
on its own) or says "fallback". The agent asks once, in one message that offers both, and proceeds on either
answer without asking again. On "fallback", skip steps (1) to (7) and run option B below.

With the rustup toolchain:
1. Import the crates.io package as the first commit: `~/.cargo/registry/src/*/asupersync-0.5.0`, from
   `~/.cargo/registry/cache/*/asupersync-0.5.0.crate`, sha256
   `f34b1a19ffd6b74570339a156912436335bb09c594c675c62ea164b19a1f2511`; exclude the registry marker
   `.cargo-ok`.
2. Add one commit "fbittorrent patch" that is `vendor/asupersync/` copied over it (`cp -a`, then `git add -A`;
   the tree has no symlinks or empty directories). Rewrite `vendor/asupersync/FBITTORRENT_PATCH.md` to list
   exactly the ten files above and carry it in the fork commit. Branch `fbittorrent-0.5.0` is the default
   branch; tag the commit `fbittorrent-0.5.0-1` so the rev survives a branch rewrite.
3. In the fork's working copy run `cargo test --all-features` (the 63 timer-wheel tests of
   `docs/validation/2026-10-11/cpu-optimization/timer-wheel-tests/receipt.json` plus `region_owner_tests`
   green) before pushing.
4. Switch `Cargo.toml:49-52` from `path = "vendor/asupersync"` to `[patch.crates-io] asupersync = { git =
   "https://github.com/odcpw/asupersync", rev = "<40-hex sha>" }` with the comment "Asupersync 0.5.0 plus the
   fbittorrent patch (FBITTORRENT_PATCH.md in the fork); drop when upstream has it"; run `cargo update -p
   asupersync` once (afterwards the lock reads `git+https://github.com/odcpw/asupersync?rev=<sha>#<sha>`),
   then `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --locked -p fbittorrent -p rqbit-runtime`.
5. Retire the timer-wheel runner instead of retargeting it: delete `regression_tests/timer_wheel_tests.rs` and
   `run_timer_wheel_tests.py` from the tree C5 commits. The patch's 63 timer-wheel tests and
   `region_owner_tests` live in the fork and run there in step 3; the receipt records that run; P0-01's
   archive keeps the receipt-era runner.
6. Archive the vendored tree: `mkdir -p ~/Archive/fbittorrent`; from the repository root `tar --zstd -cf
   ~/Archive/fbittorrent/asupersync-vendored-2026-10-18.tar.zst vendor/asupersync`; verify by listing and
   `sha256sum`; remove `vendor/asupersync`. (P0-01's whole-tree backup must already exist.)
7. Add the §8.2 sentence to the README: `cargo build --locked --offline` works after one online build (with
   the fork, CI and `install.sh` need network for the first fetch).
8. Write the receipt `## P0-02` (Appendix D) with the fork URL, tag and sha, the archive SHA256, the test
   counts, and the link to the upstream offer: an **issue** on `Dicklesworthstone/asupersync` describing the
   `wheel.rs` fix only (the region-owner key and the epoch changes are fbittorrent-specific; upstream `main`
   has moved past `78b64636…`), opened by the owner or with the owner's explicit permission.

**Option B, the runnable fallback (the owner said "fallback"):** commit `vendor/asupersync/` as it is, with
the `FBITTORRENT_PATCH.md` rewrite of step 2 and `LICENSE` byte-identical to the registry copy's, as commit C0
before C1 in the §8.1 table; leave `Cargo.toml:49-52` (`path = "vendor/asupersync"`) as it is; run the patch's
tests in place (`cargo test --all-features --manifest-path vendor/asupersync/Cargo.toml`, the 63 timer-wheel
tests and `region_owner_tests`) and record the counts; still delete the two runner files of step 5; skip the
archive of step 6 (the tree stays in git); write the receipt with "option B" and the tree's SHA256 in place of
the fork URL. Nothing is asked again. Accept under option B: `cargo build --release --locked --offline` passes
from a clean clone with no network. (A git submodule is rejected: it complicates clones and builds and offers
nothing over a git dependency. A `cargo package`-shaped copy is not smaller: `src/` alone is 56 MB in 959
`.rs` files; DL-46, DL-58.)

## Canonical rules copied in
- §8.1 commit table slot C0: `vendor: asupersync 0.5.0 with the fbittorrent patch` exists only under option B;
  otherwise the slot is empty. C3 carries `Cargo.toml` (dependencies, workspace members, and the
  `[patch.crates-io] asupersync = { git = "…", rev = "<sha>" }` entry from this item), `Cargo.lock` and `src/`
  together, because a `[patch]` for a crate the legacy manifest does not depend on is not a buildable
  intermediate state (`--locked` fails on a lock that names crates the manifest does not reference; DL-46).
- §8.2 decision row for `vendor/asupersync`: a pinned git fork; offer the wheel fix upstream; the patch note
  already asks to drop the patch once upstream has it.
- `all.sh` worker-panic scan (`all.sh:12-16`) applies to every build and test run here.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --locked -p fbittorrent -p rqbit-runtime` pass with the git
  dependency; `Cargo.lock` pins the revision.
- `diff -r --exclude=.git --exclude=.cargo-ok` between the fork checkout at the tag and the extracted archive
  is empty.
- `cargo test --all-features` in the fork checkout passes the 63 timer-wheel tests and `region_owner_tests`
  (recorded in the receipt).
- The two runner files (`timer_wheel_tests.rs`, `run_timer_wheel_tests.py`) are absent from the tree C5
  commits.
- Under option B: `cargo build --release --locked --offline` passes from a clean clone with no network.

## Tests (and what they log)
- The build and test runs, logged by hand (P0-15's `fbtlog.py` does not exist yet) in the §9.1 / E.1 shape to
  `target/test-logs/asupersync/{build,test,fork_test}.jsonl`: one step per command with its exit code and
  duration, plus `final` lines. The worker-panic scan of `all.sh:12-16` applies.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-01: the worktree backup must exist before step 6 removes `vendor/asupersync/`.
- The owner's one act before the landing commit C3 is the checkpoint above (create the repository or say
  "fallback"); Q3 and Q30 were answered on 2026-10-18.
- Consumed by P0-04 (the landing commits need the final `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` and, under option B, commit
  C0).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q3 (answered 2026-10-18): the public fork `odcpw/asupersync`; the full tree stays the runnable fallback if
  the repository is not created.
- Q30 (answered 2026-10-18): the rider's "available to" reading is accepted for the whole project; the plan
  proceeds as written and draws no legal conclusion.

## Risks and decisions
- R19 (low, medium; mostly closed round 6): P0-02 waits on the owner for one act. Mitigation: the checkpoint
  asks once; option B needs no repository; the runner that would have broken is retired; P0-02 depends on
  P0-01 so the backup exists.
- R8 (medium, medium): the forks drift from upstream; TLS security fixes tracked by hand. Mitigation: offer
  the wheel fix upstream here; weekly `cargo audit` (P0-06).
- DL-15 (git fork), DL-46 (C3 carries sources, manifest, lock and `[patch]` together), DL-58 (option B is the
  full tree; Q3 answered, fork with option B fallback), DL-68 (the timer-wheel runner retargeting is cut; the
  fork's `cargo test` is the test of record), DL-70 (the owner's answers).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

# P0-03: Repository hygiene

Plan item **P0-03** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3169). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M0**; topological level 0 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** nothing: this is a level-0 item.

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The working tree contains `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/__pycache__/` (untracked), the 279
  MB of receipts under `docs/validation/` (P0-01 moves them out), and `target/test-logs/` will appear with
  P0-15. The existing `.gitignore` covers `target/` and `agent_ergonomics_audit/.scratch/`.
- `vendor/nova3/` (64 KB) is qBittorrent's nova3 search runtime, embedded into the binary with `include_str!`
  (`src/search.rs:37-47`). fbittorrent is MIT (the licence `plugin/oliver.torrents/manifest.json` already
  declares), so the embedded files' licences must allow it. This is **unverified** until this item checks the
  header of every file (§8.2, §10.4).
- No root `LICENSE` file exists today. `vendor/rqbit/LICENSE` is Apache-2.0; `vendor/asupersync/LICENSE`
  carries the OpenAI/Anthropic rider (relevant only under P0-02's option B, when the tree stays in git).
- Nothing has ever been committed from this tree, so no secret scan has been run over it.

## Goal and user value
Nothing junk or secret may enter the first commit of the product (P0-04). The `.gitignore` rules of §8.3 keep
receipts out for good; the licence files make the repository publishable (DL-69 "`LICENSE` (MIT) and `NOTICE`
land in P0-03"). This is a level-0 item and can run in parallel with P0-01.

1. **`.gitignore`**: add `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, the `docs/validation/**` rule of §8.3 (ignore all, then
   `!docs/validation/*/README.md`, `!docs/validation/MANIFEST.sha256`, `!docs/validation/ARCHIVE.md`),
   `target/test-logs/`, plus the existing `target/` and `agent_ergonomics_audit/.scratch/`.
2. **nova3 licence check**: read the licence header of every file in `vendor/nova3/` and record file, licence
   and copyright line in `vendor/nova3/README.md`. If a file's licence does not allow embedding in an MIT
   binary (`include_str!`, `src/search.rs:37-47`), **stop and ask the owner**.
3. **Root licence files**: add `LICENSE` at the repository root (MIT) and a `NOTICE` line pointing at
   `vendor/rqbit/LICENSE` (Apache-2.0) and, under P0-02's option B, `vendor/asupersync/LICENSE` with its
   rider; with the fork, the rider travels with the fork and the README names it.

# P0-04: Land the native product on `main`

Plan item **P0-04** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3190). Phase P0; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this item feeds: **M0**;
topological level 2 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-01 (Archive validation receipts out of the working tree), P0-02 (Host the
Asupersync patch as a pinned git fork), P0-03 (Repository hygiene).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P0-05 (Pin the toolchain and fix the multi-crate engine test build), P0-07 (The
widget never starts the app), P0-08 (Graceful shutdown on terminal close), P0-09 (One bad record no longer
blocks startup), P0-10 (Resume on a finished torrent tells the truth), P0-11 (Truthful peer labels), P0-12
(Contract and README drift), P0-13 (Destructive confirms default to No), P0-14 (Private store permissions),
P0-15 (Test logging contract and shared harness module), P0-16 (Golden-render harness for the TUI).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- `main` and `origin/main` (2026-09-03) hold the legacy app: a qBittorrent-nox WebUI client with a 3-screen
  TUI. No `engine.rs`, `ipc.rs`, `shows.rs`, `rss.rs`, `search.rs` or `native_runtime*` in git. Branch
  `codex/shows-native-engine` has zero commits beyond `main`; the native engine (the product the owner runs
  daily from `~/.local/bin/fbittorrent`, 21,555,840 bytes, built 2026-10-14) exists only as the uncommitted
  working tree (RC §2).
- `main.rs` declares every module, so intermediate slices of `src/` would not compile; the source must land as
  one commit.
- Today's suites: `cargo test --release` 90 passed (TUI interaction 21, shows 11, search 11, legacy client 11,
  engine 10, rss 8, imdb 4, misc 14); `native.py` 11/11 steps (isolated XDG, real tmux TUI); engine libraries
  182 passed per crate (combined command fails to build, D11, fixed by P0-05 after this item).
- The reality check found `capabilities --json` from a clean build byte-identical to the installed binary's
  output for the working tree.

## Goal and user value
The total-loss risk (R1, RC §12): one `git checkout` away from losing a month of work. After this item `main`
holds the native product, a fresh clone builds and passes `all.sh`, and every later item has a base to branch
from. Tag `v0.1.1`. This item ends the P0 prefix of the critical path (P0-01 → P0-02 → P0-04 → P0-05/P0-15 →
P0-06 → M0).

## Do (exact steps)
§8.1 steps 3 to 5. Commit on `codex/shows-native-engine`, in this order and with these contents (the §8.1
table); every commit message lists the areas so the history stays readable:

| Commit | Content | Builds? |
|---|---|---|
| C0 `vendor: asupersync 0.5.0 with the fbittorrent patch` | only under P0-02 option B: `vendor/asupersync/` (57 MB) with its rewritten `FBITTORRENT_PATCH.md` and the licence file carried unmodified; otherwise this slot is empty | n/a (not yet referenced) |
| C1 `vendor: rqbit 9.0.1 fork ported to Asupersync` | `vendor/rqbit/` (3.3 MB) with its provenance README and LICENSE | n/a |
| C2 `vendor: nova3 search runtime` | `vendor/nova3/` (64 KB) with P0-03's licence note | n/a |
| C3 `app: native engine, IPC, VPN binding, queue, encryption, Shows, RSS, search, TUI` | all of `src/`, `Cargo.toml` (dependencies, workspace members, and the `[patch.crates-io] asupersync = { git = "…", rev = "<sha>" }` entry from P0-02), `Cargo.lock`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` starting at v0.1.1 (§8.5). One commit because the manifest, the lock and the sources that use them are one change. The message body carries the former "Asupersync 0.5.0 timer-wheel patch from a pinned fork" paragraph. | yes, first buildable commit |
| C4 `plugin: bar widget on the native app` | `plugin/oliver.torrents/` | yes |
| C5 `tests: native integration, engine benchmarks` | `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/` without `__pycache__`, and without `timer_wheel_tests.rs` and `run_timer_wheel_tests.py` (P0-02 step 5 retires them) | yes |
| C6 `docs: engine evaluation, queue and VPN plan, TUI review, validation receipts, 2026-10-18 plan` | `docs/` (after P0-01's archive: READMEs, `MANIFEST.sha256`, `ARCHIVE.md`, small linked files, the plan folder) | yes |

Then:
1. **Prove completeness from a clean clone:** `git clone <repo> "$TMP/fbt" && cd "$TMP/fbt" && cargo build
   --release --locked && agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/all.sh`. This catches any file still
   untracked but needed.
2. Push the branch, open a pull request "Land the native engine", merge with a merge commit (the slices stay
   visible), tag `v0.1.1`.
3. Write the receipt `## P0-04`: the clone log, the `capabilities --json` diff (clean-clone build vs the
   installed binary), and P0-03's reviewed secret scan.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §8.1 "Order matters, because the working tree is the only copy of the product": back up first (P0-01), move
  the blobs out (P0-01), settle Asupersync (P0-02), fix `.gitignore` and licences (P0-03), then these commits.
- §8.5: `CHANGELOG.md` starts at `v0.1.1`.
- §8.6 versions: the binary and the plugin share one SemVer number; the API protocol (`proto` 1) and the CLI
  contract (1.x) are versioned separately.
- §9.1 git safety: no `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until this item is merged; afterwards none
  on files an agent did not create.
- §8.4: `cargo fmt --check` is **not** added: the code base does not follow rustfmt today, and a format-only
  diff would bury the history of the uncommitted work. Do not reformat in C3.

## Acceptance criteria
- `main` holds the native engine (merge commit of the PR "Land the native engine").
- A fresh clone builds (`cargo build --release --locked`) and passes `all.sh` (the 90 unit tests and
  `native.py`).
- `capabilities --json` from the clean-clone build equals the installed binary's output (the reality check
  found them byte-identical for the working tree).
- The tag `v0.1.1` is pushed.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Clean-clone logs in `target/test-logs/land/clone.jsonl`, one E.1 line per step: clone, build, each suite,
  the capabilities diff (written by hand or by a small shell loop; `fbtlog.py` arrives with P0-15).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-01 (receipts out, backup taken), P0-02 (the Asupersync decision settled:
  `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` final, C0 present or absent), P0-03 (`.gitignore`, licences, secret scan).
- Consumed by every other P0 item (P0-05, P0-07 to P0-16): nothing else may change the tree before the product
  is in git.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q3/Q30 answered through P0-02 (fork vs option B decides whether C0 exists).
- Opening the PR and pushing are ordinary repository operations on the owner's private repository
  (`odcpw/fbittorrent` is private); the public-fork publishing act belongs to P0-02's checkpoint, not here.

## Risks and decisions
- R1 (low, critical): total loss before this lands; this item is the fix.
- R11 (medium, low): GitHub Actions unavailable or slow; irrelevant for landing (CI arrives in P0-06).
- DL-46: C3 carries sources, manifest, lock and the `[patch]` entry together (no unbuildable intermediate).
- DL-58: option B for Asupersync is the full vendored tree as commit C0.
- DL-68: the two timer-wheel runner files leave C5.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] A fresh clone builds (`cargo build --release --locked`) and passes `all.sh` (the 90 unit tests and `native.py`).
- [ ] `capabilities --json` from the clean-clone build equals the installed binary's output (the reality check found them byte-identical for the working tree).
- [ ] The tag `v0.1.1` is pushed.
close_reason: Landed. By the owner's instruction the commits went directly on main (no pull request, no merge commit; codex/shows-native-engine was identical to main and is deleted). C0 3f3eccc vendor asupersync, C1 47fa008 vendor rqbit, C2 2b6f15d vendor nova3, C3 ff7dbe2 app (src, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README, CHANGELOG.md from v0.1.1, .gitignore, LICENSE, NOTICE), C4 8181475 plugin, C5 7de96d2 tests and scripts, C6 c89a4ec docs and plan, 06f6fd7 receipts. Fresh clone of main at c89a4ec: cargo build --release --locked --offline exit 0; all.sh exit 0 (90 + 14 unit tests, worker-panic scan clean, native.py 11 checks); capabilities --json byte-identical to ~/.local/bin/fbittorrent (SHA256 603331c7...). Receipt ## P0-04 with the reviewed secret scan in 06f6fd7. Tag v0.1.1 on the final landing commit, pushed with main. --force because P0-02 stays open only for its patch-test item (see its comment); the Asupersync decision itself (option B, C0) is settled.

# P0-05: Pin the toolchain and fix the multi-crate engine test build

Plan item **P0-05** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3205). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M0**; topological level 3 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P0-06 (CI workflow and gates), P5-06 (Fork: have-bitfield snapshot accessor),
P6-12 (Private-torrent rules (BEP 27) check).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)

and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D11: the documented multi-crate engine test commands no longer build. `librqbit-core` enables the
  `sha1-crypto-hash` SHA-1 backend by default (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit-core/Cargo.toml:30`) while `librqbit`
  wants `sha1-ring` (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/Cargo.toml:33`); combined in one `cargo test` invocation the two
  backends meet and the build fails (`evidence/cargo-test-engine-libs-combined-FAILED-BUILD.txt`). Run per
  crate, the engine libraries pass 182 tests with 4 ignored.
- `all.sh:6` already uses Rust 1.98.0 through the rustup toolchain path
  (`~/.rustup/toolchains/1.98.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/cargo`); the `cargo` on `PATH` is a mise shim
  with no version, so a plain `cargo` in CI or on a fresh machine is undefined until the toolchain is pinned.
- `docs/engine-evaluation.md` documents the reproduction commands that fail today.

## Goal and user value
The documented reproduction commands must work, and CI (P0-06) needs one command for the fork's tests. The
fork tests added later (P5-01 seed flag, P5-06 bitfield accessor, P6-06 trusted resume, P6-12 private flag,
P6-01 tracker stats) all run through this command inside CI's `engine-libs` job, which is why P5-06 and P6-12
depend on this item directly.

## Do (exact steps)
1. Add `rust-toolchain.toml` at the repository root with `channel = "1.98.0"` (the version `all.sh:6` already
   uses).
2. Make `librqbit-core` resolve one SHA-1 backend when combined with `librqbit`: depend on it from
   `vendor/rqbit/librqbit/Cargo.toml` with `default-features = false, features = ["sha1-ring"]`, and check the
   other crates that enable `sha1-crypto-hash` by default (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit-core/Cargo.toml:30`).
3. Update the commands in `docs/engine-evaluation.md` to the one that works: `cargo test --locked -p
   librqbit-core -p librqbit --features librqbit/rust-tls --lib`.
4. Run that command and the documented per-crate commands; record pass counts.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §8.4 CI table: job `engine-libs` runs "the combined engine library command, which builds again after P0-05";
  `rust-toolchain.toml` pins 1.98.0 for every job.
- Appendix E.2: `cargo test --locked -p librqbit-core -p librqbit --features librqbit/rust-tls --lib` covers
  the fork tests (seed flag, bitfield accessor, private flag, resume); runs in CI; added by P0-05, P5-01,
  P5-06, P6-06, P6-12.
- §9.1 Done: acceptance criteria pass and `all.sh` is green; docs updated in the same change
  (`docs/engine-evaluation.md` here).

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test --locked -p librqbit-core -p librqbit --features librqbit/rust-tls --lib` builds and passes.
- The documented commands in `docs/engine-evaluation.md` pass as written.
- At least 182 engine library tests pass in total.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` exists with `channel = "1.98.0"`, so `cargo` resolves to 1.98.0 everywhere.

## Tests (and what they log)
- The commands above, logged to `target/test-logs/engine-libs/run.jsonl` (one E.1 step per crate with its pass
  count; `fbtlog.py` does not exist yet, so a shell loop writes the lines).

## Dependencies and why

  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item

  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on

  value.

description:
# P0-06: CI workflow and gates

Plan item **P0-06** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3219). Phase P0; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this item feeds: **M0**;
topological level 4 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-05 (Pin the toolchain and fix the multi-crate engine test build), P0-15 (Test
logging contract and shared harness module).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M0 (Safe on main).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The native engine has never had CI. `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/all.sh` is the local
  umbrella: it runs `cargo test` (90 tests), `native.py` (11 steps), and scans for background worker panics
  (`all.sh:12-16`). `run.sh`, `tui_smoke.sh`, `widget_keys.sh` need legacy qBittorrent or the live shell;
  `vpn.py` and `resources.py` need a namespace fixture or a `release-perf` build.
- `resources.py` measures the TUI's CPU and RSS today; there is no baseline and no gate. Download CPU is about
  3.2x qBittorrent's (R9) and the plan schedules no further optimisation (DL-18), only a gate so changes
  cannot make it worse unnoticed.
- Unverified: whether GitHub Actions minutes are available for this repository (§8.4, §10.4). If not, `all.sh`
  is the gate and this item documents running it before every merge.
- `scripts/dagcheck.py` and `scripts/mockwidth.py` exist as review-round tools (the round-2 reviewer's script,
  `reviews/round-2-architecture.md` §D); they are committed here but never run in CI (DL-59).

## Goal and user value
Every later phase relies on CI being green on `main` (the Done definition names it). The resource gate keeps
the effort lesson of §1.7 from repeating silently. Milestone M0 cannot close without it.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**, on push and pull request, with `rust-toolchain.toml` pinning 1.98.0
   (P0-05), these jobs, each uploading `target/test-logs/` as an artifact:

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| `test` | `cargo test --locked -p fbittorrent -p rqbit-runtime -- --nocapture`, then the worker-panic scan from `all.sh` |
| `engine-libs` | `cargo test --locked -p librqbit-core -p librqbit --features librqbit/rust-tls --lib` (P0-05) |
| `native` | `cargo build --release --locked`; install `tmux` and `util-linux`; `native.py`; later `daemon.py --no-systemd` (P1-07), `agent_contract.py` and `scripts/verify-determinism.sh` (P1-11) and the native tmux smoke (P4-10) |
| `lint` | `git diff --check`; later the QML token lint (P2-05), the plugin structure lint (P2-04), `scripts/lint-sizes.sh` (P1-02, P4-01) |
| `audit` (weekly schedule) | `cargo audit` over the lockfile (R8) |

2. **`all.sh` flags** with a `--help` header documenting each: `FBT_TEST_QS` (Quickshell fixture and smoke
   tests; need Quickshell, Qt 6.12 and the Omarchy shell modules), `FBT_TEST_VISUAL` (captures),
   `FBT_TEST_WIDGET` (`widget_keys.sh`), `FBT_TEST_VPN` (`vpn.py` namespace fixtures), `FBT_TEST_RESOURCES`
   (the resource gate), `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE` (mirror every JSONL line to stderr),
   `FBT_TEST_FORCE_FAIL=<suite>/<case>` (force one case's first step to fail).
3. **Resource gate scaffold:** `resources.py --baseline regression_tests/baselines/resources.json` compares
   idle and active CPU and RSS with the baseline and fails above the margin: three times the spread observed
   over three baseline runs, never below 10 %. Take a first baseline from today's `resources.py` (P1-08 later
   writes the daemon baseline in the shape `{"configs": {"<torrents>x<subscribers>": {"cpu_s": [3 runs],
   "rss_kb": [3 runs]}}, "reference": {...}}`).
4. `all.sh` ends by running `scripts/testlog-summary.py` (P0-15) and uploading `target/test-logs/` in CI.
5. Commit `scripts/dagcheck.py` and `scripts/mockwidth.py` (Appendix E; review-round tools, not CI jobs).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §8.4: local-only suites run through `all.sh` flags (Quickshell, visual, widget keys, VPN, resources). `cargo
  fmt --check` is not added (the code base does not follow rustfmt; a format-only diff would bury the
  history).
- §8.4 resource gate: `resources.py` runs before each release and compares idle and active CPU and RSS with
  the baseline JSON from P1-08; margin = 3 × the spread over three baseline runs, never below 10 %.
- §9.1 test logging contract: `all.sh` ends with the table of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest
  five; unit tests run with `--nocapture`.
- Appendix E.2: `scripts/dagcheck.py` (PLAN §9.3 vs §9.4: undefined IDs, cycles, orphans, consumed-by, level
  table, weighted critical paths) and `scripts/mockwidth.py` (mockup cell widths against 80/120/160; overflow
  and ragged boxes fail) run by hand in review rounds only.

## Acceptance criteria
- CI is green on `main`.
- A deliberately failing test on a throwaway branch turns CI red and the uploaded `target/test-logs/` artifact
  contains the failing case's JSONL.
- `all.sh --help` documents every flag above.
- `all.sh` ends with the summary table of §9.1.

## Tests (and what they log)
- The workflow itself (green on `main`, red on the throwaway branch).
- `scripts/testlog-summary.py` has a unit test over a fixture `test-logs/` tree at
  `regression_tests/fixtures/testlogs/` (two suites, one failure, the expected table text next to it).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-05 (the toolchain pin and the working `engine-libs` command) and P0-15
  (`scripts/testlog-summary.py` and the JSONL shape the artifact upload is for).
- Consumed by M0 only.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None. If GitHub Actions minutes are unavailable (R11), document `all.sh` as the gate in the README and the
  receipt.

## Risks and decisions
- R11 (medium, low): GitHub Actions unavailable or slow (a release build takes about 8 minutes). Mitigation:
  cache builds; tests in debug where possible; `all.sh` as the gate otherwise.
- R8: weekly `cargo audit` is the mitigation for fork and TLS-dependency drift.
- R9 (known, low to medium): download CPU about 3.2x qBittorrent's; the gate prevents regressions; no new
  optimisation work unless the owner notices heat or noise.
- DL-18 (no further CPU optimisation; a regression gate only), DL-59 (no CI jobs for `dagcheck.py`,

title: P0-07: The widget never starts the app
description:
# P0-07: The widget never starts the app

Plan item **P0-07** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3238). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `cli`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M0**; topological level 4 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`), P0-15 (Test logging contract and
shared harness module).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M0 (Safe on main).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D1: the widget's 60 s `reconcile` timer can reopen the app after the user quit it. Chain:
  `plugin/oliver.torrents/Service.qml:121-126` runs `fbittorrent reconcile` → `src/main.rs:627-632` →
  `connect()` → `backend::ensure_running` → `open_app()`, which launches the TUI in a terminal through
  `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` and polls up to 60 s for the socket (`src/main.rs:775-778`,
  `src/backend.rs:17-30,62-86`). Proven in `evidence/reconcile-autolaunch-probe.txt`.
- Today `status` never starts the app (`src/main.rs:407-432`) and the closed case prints `{"ok": false, …}`
  with exit 0 (`src/main.rs:407-415`). `Service.qml:15` computes `online` from `status.ok`.
- The v0.1 popup keeps polling `status --json` until P2-03 replaces it; at M1a the CLI adopts contract 1.2.0's
  stopped shape `{ok: true, running: false, …}` (DL-22), weeks before P2-03. Without a change here the widget
  would show "online" for a stopped daemon.
- The agent contract is 1.1.0 (`src/agent.rs:7`); `capabilities_json` at `src/agent.rs:134-210`; exit code
  dictionary `src/agent.rs:12-45` (`code_name: "backend"` is exit 4).

## Goal and user value
Principle 5 and §2.4: the bar widget never starts the daemon; reads never start anything (§3.2.3 "writes start
it, reads never do", DL-10). This fixes the most trust-damaging live defect (a widget that resurrects the app)
on today's architecture, and it closes the M1a chain (DL-66): the old popup keeps hiding under the new

## Do (exact steps)
1. Remove the `reconcile` timer and function from `plugin/oliver.torrents/Service.qml` (`:78`, `:121-126`).
2. In native mode `reconcile` answers `{"ok": true, "touched": 0, "note": "native scheduling is intrinsic"}`
   without connecting (`src/main.rs`, the `Cmd::Reconcile` arm). This stub stays forever (Appendix F:
   `reconcile` → none, exit 0; DL-14).
3. Add the global flag `--no-start` and the environment variable `FBITTORRENT_NO_START=1`:
   `backend::connect()` then fails with exit 4 (`code_name: "backend"`, the existing dictionary) instead of
   calling `ensure_running`.
4. The plugin passes `--no-start` on every action (`Service.qml`'s argv builder).
5. `Service.qml:15` becomes `readonly property bool online: status.ok === true && status.running !== false`,
   so the widget keeps hiding when `status` adopts the 1.2.0 stopped shape at M1a.
6. Contract 1.1.1 (`src/agent.rs:134-210`) lists the flag under `global_flags[]`, a new top-level key of
   `capabilities_json` (today it has none; additive within contract 1.x, with a `changes[]`-free 1.1.1 bump
   because `changes[]` itself arrives with 1.2.0 in P1-11).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.2.3 (the start rule, applied here on today's architecture): any command with `--no-start` or
  `FBITTORRENT_NO_START=1` never starts the daemon; a command that would have started it exits 4 with a hint;
  reads still fall back to the ledger with `running: false` and exit 0 (the fallback itself arrives with
  P1-11). `autostart = false` (the existing key, `src/config.rs:39`, README:164-169) is the persistent form of
  `--no-start` (DL-44).
- §3.2.13: `status` never starts the daemon; today's closed case prints `"ok": false` with exit 0, an envelope
  inconsistency (RC §3 #21); contract 1.2.0 changes it to `{"ok": true, "running": false, "app_open": false,
  "backend": "stopped", "total": N}` (P1-11). The only consumer of the old shape is the v0.1 widget; this item
  changes its `online` test so it keeps hiding under the new shape.
- §4.4 rule 10 (the future service): the service never starts the daemon on its own; only the explicit
  `startDaemon` action does, and only when a person pressed Start. This item is the v0.1 equivalent.
- §1.2 agent surface: `Code` 0..8 (`src/agent.rs:12-29`), error envelope `{ok:false, code, code_name, error,
  hint}` (`src/agent.rs:113-123`).

## Acceptance criteria
- Re-running the probe of `evidence/reconcile-autolaunch-probe.txt`: `status`, `reconcile` and `--no-start
  list` never invoke the launcher.
- A widget action while the app is closed reports "fbittorrent is closed".
- `Service.qml` tests `status.running !== false` in its `online` expression (a one-line `rg` in `all.sh` until
  P2-04's lint takes it over).

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit: `Cmd::Reconcile` in native mode returns the stub without `connect`.
- E2e: `native.py::launcher_never_called` with a `PATH` shim for `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that records

  invocation's argv and exit code as one E.1 step each (the case uses P0-15's `fbtlog.py` `Case`/`step`
  structure).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-04 (the product is in git) and P0-15 (the `native.py` case structure the test is written in).
- Consumed by M0.

- Q13 (open, default keep): `autostart = false` stays as the persistent form of `--no-start`.

## Risks and decisions
- R5 (the new lifetime surprises the owner): a widget that starts the app is the opposite surprise; removing
