  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the

  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`

title: P0-08: Graceful shutdown on terminal close
description:
# P0-08: Graceful shutdown on terminal close

Plan item **P0-08** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3261). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M0**; topological level 4 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`), P0-15 (Test logging contract and
shared harness module).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M0 (Safe on main).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)

running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D2: closing the terminal window kills the TUI-hosted process without running `Drop`, leaving a stale
  `engine.sock`. The app handles only SIGPIPE itself (`src/main.rs:288`). ftui's own signal thread records the
  signal, performs best-effort terminal cleanup and waits up to `SIGNAL_SHUTDOWN_GRACE = 2 s` for the runtime
  to clear `ftui_core::shutdown_signal::pending_termination_signal()`; if the runtime does not, it calls
  `exit(128 + sig)` (`ftui-core-0.6.0/src/terminal_session.rs:107,147-167,1270-1295`). The runtime's event
  loop polls the pending signal on every iteration (`ftui-runtime-0.6.0/src/program.rs:5254-5441`, through the
  wrappers at `:110-117`) and clears it only in `complete_lifecycle` **after** `shutdown_once` has restored
  the terminal (`:5462-5490`); the signal thread also accepts an explicit teardown as acknowledgement
  (`EXPLICIT_TEARDOWN_STARTED`, `terminal_session.rs:121,151,1078`). This matches the observed 2.2 s
  (`evidence/app-lifecycle-observations.txt`). `Drop` at `src/engine.rs:517-546` (session drain ≤ 4 s, then
  runtime shutdown) and `src/ipc.rs:278-286` (socket unlink) never runs.
- So the model needs no `Cmd::quit()` of its own; the 2.2 s are lost between the signal thread's record and
  that clear, most likely in `shutdown_once` writing to the dead pty, or a second SIGHUP arriving mid-drain.
  Which of the two fixes below is needed is unverified (§10.4) and decided by instrumentation in this item.
- The instance lock is `flock` on `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/engine.lock` (`src/ipc.rs:136-164`). The
  engine drop prints only on failure today (`src/engine.rs:536-537`).

## Goal and user value
P1 makes the TUI a client, but until then the owner closes the Ghostty window every day and gets a stale
socket (§9.5's P0 human check: "closes the Ghostty window during a download and sees no stale socket").
Durable intent is never lost (the ledger is fsync'd), but a clean drain is what makes the next open fast and
the lock acquirable.

## Do (exact steps)
1. With `FBT_DEBUG_SIGNALS=1`, append one line per event (`<ms since signal> <event>`) to
   `$XDG_STATE_HOME/fbittorrent/tui-signals.log` (stderr is the dead pty) for: signal recorded, loop observed
   it, `shutdown_once` begin/end, clear, `drop(app)` begin/end (`src/main.rs:819`).
2. If the clear happens after the grace: call `clear_pending_termination_signal()` from the model's
   `Msg::Hover` tick (`src/tui/mod.rs:1673`, the 300 ms tick) as soon as it observes the signal and before
   returning `Cmd::quit()`, so the signal thread is acknowledged within 300 ms and the engine drop (≤ 4 s,
   `src/engine.rs:517-546`) runs to the end.
3. If the loop never observes the signal because the input reader blocks on the dead pty: spawn a watchdog
   thread on first sight of the pending signal that drains the engine directly through a shared
   `Arc<AppEngine>` handle (sets `stopping`, runs the session drain with its 4 s bound, unlinks the socket)
   and then clears the signal itself.
4. Keep whichever of 2 and 3 the instrumentation shows is needed; the acceptance is the same either way.
5. In both, the engine drop logs `engine drained in <ms> ms` at info level (today `src/engine.rs:536-537`
   prints only on failure); this is the "drain message" the acceptance looks for.
6. Expected exit status after a graceful signal exit stays `128 + sig` (the runtime's `SignalTerminationError`
   contract).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.2.6 (the daemon's future rule, for contrast): in `serve` the main thread blocks SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP and

  the TUI client. This item is about the TUI-hosted app of P0 only.

description:
# P0-09: One bad record no longer blocks startup

Plan item **P0-09** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3302). Phase P0; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this item feeds: **M0**;
topological level 4 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`), P0-15 (Test logging contract and
shared harness module).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M0 (Safe on main).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D4: one bad record blocks startup. `engine::start` (`src/engine.rs:453-466`) restores every ledger record in
  series with `?`, and each magnet-only restore waits the 90 s metadata timeout (`src/engine.rs:213-219`). A
  record whose cached `.torrent` is missing and whose magnet cannot resolve makes the app unusable for minutes
  or forever.
- Cached `.torrent` files live under the engine's torrent store (`src/engine.rs:164-168`). The parked path
  already lists ledger records without a live handle (`src/engine.rs:1233-1355`). `torrents/info` uses
  qBittorrent-shaped state strings (`checkingDL` at `src/engine.rs:1431`; `metaDL`, which `src/qbt.rs:51`
  already treats as active).
- librqbit admits new torrents while others initialise: `concurrent_init_limit` only serialises the checks
  (`src/engine.rs:432`).

## Goal and user value
Principle 4 (truthful state) and the daemon's lifetime: under the owner's stop rule (A1) the daemon starts
after every idle period, and today's serial restore would put the whole library's check time between a magnet
click and "Added" (§3.2.4). This item makes each restore independent so the session exists in seconds; P1-03
builds the engine slot on it (DL-49: "The slot is `Running` as soon as the session exists; restores run in
background tasks and show as `checking`/`metadata`"). It also fixes the live defect for today's TUI-hosted
app.

## Do (exact steps)
1. In `engine::start` (`src/engine.rs:453-466`) return as soon as the librqbit session exists.
2. Restore every record in a spawned task: records with a cached `.torrent` under the engine's torrent store
   (`src/engine.rs:164-168`) first; then magnet-only records with the existing 90 s metadata timeout.
3. A failed restore marks the record `error` with reason `restore_failed` and the message, keeps it and
   continues with the next record. In today's qBittorrent-shaped `torrents/info` (until P1-19's normalized
   `state`/`reason` exist) the row's `state` string is qBittorrent's `error` and the message travels in a new
   additive optional key `error_message` (`qbt::Torrent` gains `error_message: Option<String>` with
   `#[serde(default)]` and `skip_serializing_if`; today the struct has no error field at all,
   `src/qbt.rs:11-36`), which the TUI details strip and `fbittorrent show --json` print; P1-19's
   `TorrentView::to_legacy_json()` keeps emitting it.
4. `torrents/info` lists unrestored records from the ledger as `checkingDL` (today's qBittorrent-shaped string
   for `checking`, `src/engine.rs:1431`) or `metaDL` (for `metadata`), as the parked path already does for its
   records (`src/engine.rs:1233-1355`).
5. `torrents/start` on such a record retries the restore.
6. Expose the per-record outcome so P1-03 can read it to drive the slot and `engine.changed`.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.2.4: `READY=1` is sent once the daemon's socket listens and the engine slot exists in `Starting`, not
  after hash checks finish; the slot becomes `Running` as soon as the librqbit session exists; saved records
  are restored by background tasks and show as `checking` or `metadata` meanwhile; operations that need the
  engine wait only for the session (seconds, not minutes); `torrents.add` keeps a 60 s bound and fails with
  retryable `engine_unavailable` past it.
- §3.5 normalized states (the future mapping, for the strings this item emits): `checking` = "Hashing existing
  data" (`Initializing { paused: false }`); `metadata` = "Magnet resolving" (handle without metadata); `error`
  with `reason: restore_failed` renders as "could not restore: <error>" (§4.3.4 reason phrases).
- §3.2.7 crash recovery: data is re-checked on the next start (until P6-06); nothing is ever half-removed.

## Acceptance criteria
<!-- accept:split -->
- With one valid record and one whose cached `.torrent` is missing and whose magnet cannot resolve, the app
  opens in under 10 s.
- Both records are listed; the bad one shows state `error` with its message (in today's qBittorrent-shaped
  list: `state: "error"` plus the additive `error_message` key; the normalized `reason: restore_failed`
  arrives with P1-19). A record whose restore is still in progress shows `checkingDL` (cached `.torrent`) or
  `metaDL` (magnet-only), never `error`.
- `torrents/start` on the bad record retries the restore.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit: `engine::tests::bad_record_does_not_block` with a corrupted cache file and an unresolvable local
  magnet: `engine::start` returns within 10 s while the magnet is still resolving in the background (its row
  is `metaDL`); the corrupted-cache record fails at once and lists as `error` with `error_message`; the valid
  record restores. The test prints each row's `state`/`error_message` and the start duration.
- E2e: `native.py::startup_survives_bad_record`, logging open time and the listed states as E.1 steps.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-04 (in git) and P0-15 (the `native.py` case structure).
- Consumed by M0. P1-03 (daemon core) and P1-09 (magnet records created at add time, resolved in the
  background using this task pattern) and P1-16 (lazy restore of completed records inside this restore task)
  build on it.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R5: a daemon that starts often must start fast; this item is the precondition.
- DL-49 (round 2): the slot is `Running` as soon as the session exists; restores run in background tasks and
  show as `checking`/`metadata`.

  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed

# P0-10: Resume on a finished torrent tells the truth

Plan item **P0-10** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3321). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M0**; topological level 4 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`), P0-16 (Golden-render harness for the
TUI).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M0 (Safe on main).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,

toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D5 / RC §9 defect 7: "Resume" on a finished, stop-on-complete torrent reports "started" and does nothing.
  The TUI offers `(P) Resume` on every non-running row (`src/tui/mod.rs:2040`, `1325-1328`); the engine stops
  at completion when seeding is off (`src/engine.rs:306-310`); a finished stop-on-complete record is
  `completion_on != 0` and `ratio_limit == 0.0` (`src/engine.rs:90-92`).
- The legacy route match is `src/engine.rs:586-651`; the CLI error envelope is `src/agent.rs:106-116` (`{"ok":
  false, "code", "code_name", "error", "hint"}`).
- Seeding model (unchanged by the plan): off by default, 32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when
  complete, per-torrent `seed` override (`src/qbt.rs:40-44`, `src/engine.rs:833-848`); the API exposes `seed:
  bool` as one switch (`src/qbt.rs:504-520`).

## Goal and user value
Principle 4: the UI must not report an action that did nothing. The honest answer to "resume" on a complete
torrent is "it is complete; seeding is off; use `seed`". The §5.4 action table later makes labels depend on
state (a finished torrent shows `(U) Seed`, never `(P) Resume`); this item does it by hand first.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `torrents/start` (the legacy route, `src/engine.rs:586-651` match) on a finished stop-on-complete record
   returns a typed refusal that the CLI prints as `{"ok": false, "code": 1, "code_name": "failure", "error":
   "already complete; seeding is off for this torrent", "hint": "fbittorrent seed <hash>"}` (the envelope of
   `src/agent.rs:106-116`). After P1-11 the same case is the API's `invalid_state`, which A.3 maps to exit 1.
2. `start all` skips such torrents and lists them in `skipped: [{hash, reason: "complete_no_seed"}]`.
3. The TUI footer shows `(U) Seed` instead of `(P) Resume` for them (`src/tui/mod.rs:2040`).
4. The widget hides its start button for them (`Panel.qml`, the row action visibility).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §9.3 preamble "Defaults for edge states": `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state`
  with the hint `fbittorrent seed <hash>` (P0-10, A.3) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`.
- A.5 `torrents.start` result (the shape this grows into): `{state: "done", started: [hash], skipped: [{hash,
  reason: open(complete_no_seed|already_running|staged)}]}`.
- A.3 `invalid_state`: "the operation does not apply now (resume on `done`, …)"; `details {state?, reason?}`;
  CLI exit 1.
- §4.3.4 reason phrase for `complete_no_seed`: "complete; seeding is off".
- Appendix F `start <sel>… [--force]`: JSON unchanged plus `skipped`; exit codes 0, 1 (`invalid_state`), 4, 6,
  7. Exit code 1 reachability: "`start` on `done`".

## Acceptance criteria
- RC §5 defect 3 no longer reproduces (resume on a finished torrent is refused with the hint).
- The 80×24 footer golden shows `(U) Seed` for a done row.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit: engine test for the typed refusal and the `skipped` list.
- TUI interaction test for the footer label.
- Golden render (P0-16 harness; the fixture state has a `done` torrent).
- E2e: `native.py::resume_done_refused` asserting exit 1 with the hint in the JSON envelope.
- Logging (polish round 1): `native.py::resume_done_refused` records the full JSON envelope as `observed`

  asserted on under `--nocapture`.

- Consumed by M0.

  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in

- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`

description:
# P0-11: Truthful peer labels

Plan item **P0-11** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3338). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M0**; topological level 4 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`), P0-15 (Test logging contract and
shared harness module), P0-16 (Golden-render harness for the TUI).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M0 (Safe on main).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and

`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over

`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D6: seeds are always 0; every peer is reported as a leecher. The engine hard-codes `num_seeds: 0`
  (`src/engine.rs:1480`); the TUI details line says "0 seeds, N leechers" (`src/tui/mod.rs:2199`); the widget
  builds an "Ns" suffix (`plugin/oliver.torrents/Model.js:79`); browse rows show a seed count for YTS even
  when the source gives none (`src/browse.rs`, the YTS mapping); `capabilities` documents `num_seeds` without
  saying it is unknown.
- The captured screens that show the lie: `screens/01-torrents-160x45.txt`, `08`, `10`, `14` (RC §9 defect 9:
  misleading counts "0 seeds", "0s", YTS "0" seeds, RSS "0 B").
- The real count arrives only with P5-01 (fork change: `seed: bool` on `PeerStats`). Until then the truthful
  statement is "N peers connected".

## Goal and user value
Principle 4 (truthful state): an unknown value is absent, never a fake zero. A streaming user who sees "0
seeds" on a torrent that is downloading at full speed learns to distrust every number. The fix on today's
architecture costs a few lines and removes the lie from every surface until P5-01 supplies the truth. `seeds`
means connected seeds and is labelled so (DL-19; no tracker scrape, §2.6).

## Do (exact steps)
1. TUI details say "N peers connected" instead of "0 seeds, N leechers" (`src/tui/mod.rs:2199`).
2. The widget drops the seeds part (`plugin/oliver.torrents/Model.js:79`).
3. Browse rows show no seed count when the source gives none (`src/browse.rs`, the YTS mapping).
4. `capabilities` documents `num_seeds` as "always 0 in native mode: unknown" (`src/agent.rs`, the field notes
   of contract 1.1.1).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.4.9 "Unknown values are absent": `seeds` is absent until P5-01 can count them; always present afterwards
  for live torrents. Rust uses `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; a
  contract test later fails on `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in a field documented as "absent when unknown".
- P1-11's contract-1.x rule (for the CLI shape later): the old numeric field `num_seeds` keeps qBittorrent's
  sentinel `0` until P5-01 fills it, `num_leechs` is the peer count, and `capabilities.changes[]` says so
  under `field: "list[].num_seeds"`; the truth lives in the new `seeds` field (DL-69).
- §4.3.1 popup meta line (the future row): built from present fields only, in this order: state word · percent
  · ↓ rate · ETA · peers (and "seeds" after P5-01); absent fields are omitted, never zero.
- §2.6 non-goal "Tracker scrape for swarm-wide seed counts": `seeds` means connected seeds; a scrape adds
  tracker traffic for a number that does not change what the user does.

## Acceptance criteria
<!-- accept:split -->
- Re-taken captures of screens 01, 08, 10 and 14 (`screens/`) contain no "0 seeds" or "0s".
- `capabilities` documents `num_seeds` as "always 0 in native mode: unknown".
- Browse rows from a source that gives no seed count (YTS) show no seed number.

## Tests (and what they log)
- TUI render tests and goldens (P0-16).
- `plugin/tests/lint.sh` greps `Model.js` for `"s"`-suffix construction (the rule lands with the lint in
  P2-04; until then the grep is a line in `all.sh`).
- E2e: `native.py::no_fake_seed_counts` greps the captured panes and logs each capture it asserts on as an E.1
  step.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-04 (in git), P0-16 (goldens prove the render change), P0-15 (the `native.py` case structure).
- Consumed by M0. P5-01 later replaces "unknown" with the connected-seed count in every surface.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- DL-19: `seeds` means connected seeds and is labelled so; no tracker scrape.
- DL-69: contract-1.x numeric fields keep qBittorrent's sentinels with the truth in new fields, declared in
  `capabilities.changes[]`.
- §5.7 row 9 (misleading counts) is fixed by this item, P3-01 (search) and P4-07 (RSS "0 B", everything else).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)

  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into

  s; bye{reason:idle}

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any

  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,

  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,

  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,

  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item

  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before

  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on

  value.

for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,

§8.5: the README is rewritten in stages so it is never wrong for long; the stale claims are corrected here to
describe today's behaviour and restored in P4-07 when the code matches them. Deriving the text from the
constant means it cannot drift again.

1. `src/agent.rs:186,221`: describe the native cap as "32 KiB/s while downloading (non-zero caps must be at
   least 16 KiB/s); stops when complete unless seeding is enabled". Derive the number from `NO_UPLOAD_LIMIT`
   (`src/qbt.rs:44`) rather than typing it.
2. README: YTS loads in the app; 1337x stays browser-only (`README.md:219-224`); the UPLOADED column and

  value.

is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

  ledger save in `src/engine.rs`), `legacy-migration.json`, `config.toml` (`src/config.rs`).

## Goal and user value
§3.9 security model, "Files": every store is 0600 and written through temp file, fsync, rename and directory
fsync. A torrent client's ledger and watchlist describe what a person downloads and watches; on a shared or
backed-up machine they must not be readable by other users. This is also the review bar the marketplace
reviewer held ucmz851 to (§7.2 "0600 files, written atomically, failing closed"), adopted whether or not a
listing ever happens.

1. Create every store's temporary file with mode 0600 before renaming (`shows.json` today ends up 0644;
   `src/shows.rs:259-262`).

   (the writers in `src/rss.rs:93-100`, `src/search.rs`, `src/engine.rs` ledger save, `src/config.rs`).
3. Keep the existing pattern: temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync (the pattern in `src/config.rs` and

  listener, no WebUI (the socket side arrives with P1-03 and P1-06).
- §3.2.7: the ledger is fsync'd on every change so a crash loses no intent ([EE "Ownership and durable
  state"]).
- §3.7 Concurrency: the stores already lock and merge on save, so a daemon and an in-process CLI can run at

# P0-15: Test logging contract and shared harness module

Plan item **P0-15** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3389). Phase P0; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `hygiene`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M0**; topological level 3 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-04 (Land the native product on `main`).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P0-06 (CI workflow and gates), P0-07 (The widget never starts the app), P0-08
(Graceful shutdown on terminal close), P0-09 (One bad record no longer blocks startup), P0-11 (Truthful peer
labels), P0-14 (Private store permissions), M0 (Safe on main), P1-07 (Integration harness `daemon.py`).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- `regression_tests/native.py` is the best end-to-end test (isolated XDG, real tmux TUI): 11 steps that print
  `ok: <label>` lines (`native.py:172-376`); it has one `tui.stderr` for the whole run (`native.py:157`) and
  no per-step log file. Its XDG isolation (`native.py:44-50`) is the model every later suite copies.
- `qs` (Quickshell) logs on stderr with a `DEBUG qml:` prefix; QML tests will print `FBTQS-*` marker lines
  that need converting.
- `all.sh` already fails the run on background worker panics (`all.sh:12-16`) and runs `cargo test` and
  `native.py`.

## Goal and user value
Principle 10 ("tests that explain themselves") and the owner's explicit ask: logging that lets a reviewer see
what every test did. Every later e2e suite (`daemon.py`, `agent_contract.py`, `tui_smoke.py`, the `qs-*.sh`
scripts) is written on this module, which is why P1-07 (the daemon harness skeleton) depends on it and P0-06
uploads its output. Appendix E.1 is the contract.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`regression_tests/fbtlog.py`**: `Case(suite, name)` context manager that writes the JSONL lines of §9.1
   and E.1 to `<repo>/target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl` (`<repo>` is the parent of
   `agent_ergonomics_audit/`, never the current directory; the suite directory is emptied when the suite
   starts). `step(action, expect)` returns a step handle whose `ok(observed)` or `fail(observed)` closes it;
   `ms` is the wall time between `step()` and the close; `step` numbers from 1 per case; `ts` is UTC ISO-8601
   with milliseconds and a `Z`. A failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
   continues to its end (so one failure shows every later symptom); the suite exits non-zero if any case
   failed.
2. **Case slugs** are snake_case of today's `ok:` labels: `dec_mouse_mode`, `closed_status_stays_closed`,
   `one_enter_adds_once`, `refresh_preserves_read_history`, `rss_mouse_and_scoped_shortcuts`,
   `mouse_selection_at_scroll_offset`, `native_cli_fields_and_deletion_safety`, `shows_inbox_and_targets`,
   `file_modal_shows_help_80x24`, `settings_queue_vpn_restart`, `quit_restart_down`.
3. **Child stderr capture**: `Case` captures a child process's stderr into one suite-wide file and records the
   byte offset at each case boundary, so `<case>.daemon.log` is the slice for that case (the slice is what
   gets printed on failure).
4. **Verbosity**: only the capture a step asserts on is logged; polling captures inside `wait_for` are logged
   only under `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1`, which also mirrors every line to stderr.
   `FBT_TEST_FORCE_FAIL=<suite>/<case>` makes that case's first step fail (for the acceptance check and for
   `fbtlog_test.py`).
5. **`plugin/tests/qs-log.py`** (outside the symlinked plugin folder): runs `qs -p <dir>` with the given
   arguments and `NO_COLOR=1`, reads stdout and stderr merged, turns each `FBTQS-STEP {json}` marker found
   anywhere in a line (same field names as §9.1) into a JSONL line, turns `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL
   <case> <diff>` into the case's `final` line, and exits 1 on any FAIL. Built here, first used by P2-02.
6. **Convert `native.py`** to `fbtlog.py`: its 11 `ok:` prints become the cases above; `native.py --case
   <slug>` and `--list` select and list them (the same switches `daemon.py` gets in P1-07).
7. **`scripts/testlog-summary.py`** reads `target/test-logs/`, prints the table of §9.1 (suite, cases, passes,
   failures, slowest five) and exits 1 when any case has `ok: false`; `all.sh` calls it last, in this item
   (P0-06 adds the CI upload).
8. **Shapes an implementer would otherwise have to guess (bead review, 2026-10-18):** the case's `final` line
   is `{"ts", "suite", "case", "final": true, "ok": <every step ok>, "steps": <count>, "failed": [<step
   numbers>], "ms": <case wall time>}`; `target/test-logs/<suite>/summary.json` is `{"suite", "cases",
   "passed", "failed", "slowest": [{"case", "ms"}]}` (at most five) and `scripts/testlog-summary.py` reads
   only the `.jsonl` files and these summaries; a step closes with `ok(observed, artifacts=[...])` or
   `fail(observed, artifacts=[...])` (the `artifacts` list of E.1, default empty); `Case.popen(argv, **kw)`
   wraps `subprocess.Popen` with `stderr` routed into the suite-wide capture file so the per-case slice of
   step 3 works (only the child's stderr is captured; stdout stays the caller's); `plugin/tests/qs-log.py
   --suite <name> -- qs -p <dir> …` names the suite, the case comes from the `FBTQS-PASS/FAIL <case>` marker,

## Canonical rules copied in
- Appendix E.1 example line:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  Rules: `ts` is wall clock; `step` increments per case; `expect` and `observed` are human sentences;
  `artifacts` lists files the step produced (pane captures, PNGs, daemon logs); a case's last line has
  `"final": true` and the verdict; the suite summary `target/test-logs/<suite>/summary.json` counts cases and
  lists the slowest five.
- Appendix D "Case slug": the snake_case name of one end-to-end case, the `case` field of its JSONL lines and
  the argument of `--case`.
- Appendix E.2 rows added by this item: `scripts/testlog-summary.py` (yes in CI),
  `regression_tests/fbtlog_test.py` (yes), `plugin/tests/qs-log.py` (opt-in), `native.py` (exists; converted
  here).

## Acceptance criteria
- `native.py` produces `target/test-logs/native/<case>.jsonl` for each of the 11 cases with at least one line
  per CLI call or asserted pane capture.
- `FBT_TEST_FORCE_FAIL=native/quit_restart_down` prints both file paths and their last 20 lines and makes

- The summary table lists 11 cases.

`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- `src/tui/mod.rs` is 3,504 lines with one `TuiApp` of about 70 fields, four screens (Torrents, Search, Shows,
  RSS) and modals (files, providers, settings, prompt, help). There are 21 interaction tests but no render
  goldens, so a reviewer cannot see what a change did to the screen.
- The §5.6 mockups name the fixture torrents: "The Diplomat S04E01 1080p WEB-DL H264-GROUP" (downloading),
  "Some.Movie.2026.1080p" (ready / downloading), "Other.Movie.2026.1080p" (metadata), "The Diplomat S04 (2026)
  1080p WEBRip x265" / "Sintel.2010.1080p" (done). The Search mockup (Appendix C) carries a mojibake name
  `[philosophy-raws][辛特尔][sintel][BDRIP…` from `screens/07-search-sintel-16s.txt`.
- FrankenTUI 0.6 (pinned, `ftui-core-0.6.0`, `ftui-widgets-0.6.0`, `ftui-extras-0.6.0`) renders into a
  headless frame whose cells can be joined into text.

## Goal and user value
P0-10, P0-11, P0-13 and the whole of P4 change renders; without goldens a reviewer cannot see what changed
(principle 10). The goldens are created from the **unsplit** code so every later change, including P4-01's
isomorphic module split (which must leave them byte-identical), shows up as a diff. This item is also where
the three canonical terminal sizes (80×24 narrow, 120×30 medium, 160×45 wide; §5.6 breakpoints narrow < 100,
medium 100–139, wide ≥ 140) enter the test suite.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `src/tui/tests/fixture.rs`: a fixture `TuiApp` state with three torrents in the states `downloading`,
   `done` and `metadata` with the names of the §5.6 mockups, two followed shows with two unread releases, one
   feed with three items, ten search results including one mojibake name.
2. `src/tui/tests/golden.rs`: render the fixture into a headless ftui frame at 80×24, 120×30 and 160×45 for
   each screen (Torrents, Search, Shows, RSS) and modal (files, providers, settings, prompt, help); compare
   with `src/tui/tests/golden/<screen>-<w>x<h>.txt`; `FBT_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites them; a failure prints a
   unified diff.
3. Create the goldens from the unsplit code (before any P4 change).
4. The golden text is the frame's cells joined by lines, no colour (colour is tested by `palette::tests`,
   P4-05).
5. A meta-test asserts the fixture renders without panics at 60×20.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §5.9 TUI tests: golden renders for each screen and modal at 80×24, 120×30 and 160×45, stored as text in
  `src/tui/tests/golden/`, created in P0-16 from the unsplit code and updated only deliberately with
  `FBT_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`; a golden test prints a unified diff on failure.
- §5.3 method: an isomorphic split first (P4-01); code moves without behaviour changes; `cargo test`, the
  golden renders at the three sizes and the tmux smoke must be identical before and after.
- §5.6 breakpoints: narrow below 100 columns, medium 100 to 139, wide 140 and above; today the Torrents
  details pane needs 140 columns and the Search pane 100 (`src/tui/mod.rs:2770-2785`); the owner's tiled
  window is about 90 columns (`screens/tui-real.png`).
- §5.6 mockups later become goldens: Torrents at 80×24 and 120×30 and the details modal at 80×24 (P4-04);
  Search and Shows at 80 in Appendix C are their targets.
- Appendix E.2: `cargo test --locked -p fbittorrent -p rqbit-runtime` covers "unit; goldens; …"; added by
  P0-16 among others.

## Acceptance criteria
- 3 sizes × (4 screens + files, providers, settings, prompt, help) = 27 goldens exist and pass.
- Changing one character of a label fails the test with a readable unified diff.

## Tests (and what they log)
- The golden test itself (prints the unified diff on failure under `--nocapture`).
- The meta-test at 60×20 (no panic).
- Logging (polish round 1): the golden test prints the unified diff under `--nocapture` and names the golden
  file; the receipt lists the 27 golden paths with their line counts; the meta-test logs the 60×20 render
  size.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P0-04 (in git).
- Consumed by P0-10, P0-11, P0-13 (their render changes are proven by goldens), M0, and P4-01 (the isomorphic
  split must leave the goldens identical).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R4 (the two UIs drift): goldens are the TUI half of the discipline; `contracts/ui/states.json` (P2-08) and
  `format.json` (P4-07) are the shared half.
- DL-29: ftui stays at 0.6 for M3; its widget set suffices (`table`, `tabs`, `sparkline`, `virtualized`,
  `log_viewer`, `toast`, `notification_queue`, `badge`, `scrollbar` in `ftui-widgets-0.6.0/src/`; `charts`,
  `image`, `canvas` in `ftui-extras-0.6.0/src/`).
- A8: the monochrome theme is the design constraint; goldens are colour-free by design so state words and
  glyphs, not hue, are what they prove.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

# P1-01: A lifecycle object replaces the process-global statics

Plan item **P1-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3456). Phase P1; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1a**;
topological level 6 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** M0 (Safe on main).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-02 (Engine split (isomorphic)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Lifecycle is process-global statics: `QUIT_REQUESTED` (`src/engine.rs:32`), `RESTART`, `CLOSE` and
  `EXPECTED` (`src/network_app.rs:9-11`), polled by the TUI tick every 2 s (`src/tui/mod.rs:1699-1702`). The
  engine, `network_app` and the TUI all read and write them.
- Statics prevent a daemon that restarts engines in place (§3.2.8: the engine slot cycles Running → Starting →
  Running while connections stay) and prevent tests with two engines in one process (RC §10).
- Exit codes the daemon will use (§3.2.6, §3.2.12): 0 for a normal stop, 70 after a panic
  (`Restart=on-failure` then restarts it), 75 for "binary replaced while idle; start the new one"
  (`RestartForceExitStatus=75`, `SuccessExitStatus=75`).

## Goal and user value
The first daemon item: a `Lifecycle` object that P1-03's `run_serve()`, the supervisor, the signal thread, the
panic hook, P1-10's legacy adapter (`app/shutdown` → `request_stop(StopReason::Quit)`), P1-12's idle net
(`StopReason::Idle`) and P1-17's upgrade check (`StopReason::Upgrade`) all drive, with no behaviour change
yet. It is on the critical path (M0 → P1-01 → P1-02 → P1-19 → P1-05 → P1-06 → P1-08 → …).

## Do (exact steps)
1. Create `src/daemon/mod.rs` (declaring only `pub mod lifecycle;` until P1-03 fills the rest) and
   `src/daemon/lifecycle.rs`.
2. `Lifecycle` is an `Arc<(Mutex<State>, Condvar)>` with: `request_stop(StopReason)`,
   `request_restart(RestartReason)`, `wait(Duration) -> Option<Request>` (returns the oldest pending request
   or `None` on timeout), `expected_network() -> Option<NetworkState>` and `set_expected_network(..)`.
3. `StopReason::{Signal(i32), Idle, Explicit, Panic, Upgrade, Quit}` carries its exit code: `Signal`, `Idle`,
   `Explicit`, `Quit` → 0; `Panic` → 70; `Upgrade` → 75 (§3.2.6, §3.2.12). `RestartReason::{Settings, Network,
   Explicit}`.
4. Replace `QUIT_REQUESTED`, `RESTART`, `CLOSE` and `EXPECTED` with a `Lifecycle` passed to the engine,
   `network_app` and the TUI. Behaviour does not change.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.3 module layout: `src/daemon/lifecycle.rs` "Lifecycle; replaces QUIT_REQUESTED, RESTART, CLOSE,
  EXPECTED"; `src/daemon/mod.rs` "run_serve(): lock, signals, sd_notify, supervisor, shutdown" (P1-03).
- §3.2.7 transitions this object will carry: "any → Draining" on idle countdown reaching 0, `app.shutdown`,
  SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, panic (exit 70), binary replaced while idle (exit 75); "Running → Starting → Running"
  on a restart-class setting (`peer_encryption`, `network_interface`, `peer_port`) or `app.restart {scope:
  "engine"}`.
- §3.2.8 supervisor loop: every 1 s, or immediately when the lifecycle is signalled: stop requested → leave
  the loop; restart-class setting changed → `restart_engine(reason = settings)`; network changed while binding
  configured → `restart_engine(reason = network)`.
- §3.2.6: one `sigwait` thread calls `lifecycle.request_stop(StopReason::Signal(n))`; the panic hook requests
  a stop with exit code 70.

## Acceptance criteria
- No lifecycle `static` remains: `rg -n "static .*(QUIT_REQUESTED|RESTART|CLOSE|EXPECTED)" src` is empty.
- All tests and `native.py` are green (no behaviour change).
- A new test runs two engines with separate temporary directories in one process.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `engine::tests::two_engines_one_process`.
- `lifecycle::tests::{stop_reason_wins, restart_then_stop}` (a stop request outranks a pending restart; a
  restart followed by a stop yields both in order).
- The existing suites (`cargo test`, `native.py`).
- Logging (polish round 1): `two_engines_one_process` prints both temp directories and each engine's socket
  path; `lifecycle::tests` print the request sequence they observed (for example `[Restart(Settings),
  Stop(Idle)]`).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on M0 (the P0 fixes and harness must be on `main` before daemon work starts: git safety, goldens,
  JSONL logging).
- Consumed by P1-02 (the engine split moves code that now takes a `Lifecycle`).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R18 (medium, high): the first user-visible change is at the end of P2 after 32 S-units of serial work; M1a
  and parallel lanes mitigate. This item is the first of that serial chain; keep it to moves and the object,
  no scope creep.
- RC §10 code-health fact: lifecycle is process-global statics; this item removes that obstacle.

  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.

  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.

description:
# P1-02: Engine split (isomorphic)

Plan item **P1-02** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3475). Phase P1; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1a**;
topological level 7 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-01 (A lifecycle object replaces the process-global statics).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-03 (Daemon core: `fbittorrent serve`), P1-19 (Typed operations and the
normalized model).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- `src/engine.rs` (2,694 lines) mixes ledger persistence, queue policy, string-route dispatch and the parked
  server. Route names are matched in four places (`src/engine.rs:549-571`, `586-651`, `1233-1246`,
  `src/network_app.rs:78-90`). The qBittorrent state vocabulary exists three times (`src/engine.rs:1396-1440`,
  `src/tui/mod.rs:2933-2949`, `Model.js:32-57`) (RC §10, §1.7).
- Known seams: `AppEngine` start and drop (`src/engine.rs:395-499`, `517-546`); `Record` (`:37-53`) and the
  ledger save; `reconcile_queue` (`:280-343`); the `torrents/info` JSON builder (`:1396-1486`);
  `dispatch_parked_in` (`:1233-1355`); `migrate_legacy`.
- `AppEngine` runs the Asupersync runtime plus the librqbit `Session` plus a 1 s queue loop; engine operations
  enter the runtime with `block_on` from dispatch threads (`src/engine.rs:577-583`).

The typed operations and the normalized model (P1-19) need seams that a 2,694-line file does not have. Keeping
the move separate from behaviour change is what makes its isomorphism test meaningful (DL-47: "P1-02 is the
isomorphic file split only; P1-19 adds the typed operations and the normalized model"). The same discipline is
applied to the TUI in P4-01. On the critical path.

## Do (exact steps)
1. Split `src/engine.rs` isomorphically into `src/engine/{mod,ledger,queue,ops,view,parked,legacy_import}.rs`
   as §3.3 names them:
   - `mod.rs`: `AppEngine` start and drop (from `src/engine.rs`);
   - `ledger.rs`: `Record`, read, save, fsync;
   - `queue.rs`: `reconcile_queue` and limits;
   - `ops.rs`: today's string dispatch (P1-19 replaces it with `EngineOp`);
   - `view.rs`: today's `torrents/info` JSON builder (P1-19 generalises it into `TorrentView`);
   - `parked.rs`: `ParkedLedger` from `dispatch_parked_in`;
   - `legacy_import.rs`: `migrate_legacy` (deleted in P4-09).
2. Moves only; no behaviour change.
3. Before the move, capture the `torrents/info` JSON of a fixture ledger into
   `src/engine/tests/info-before-split.json`.
4. Create `scripts/lint-sizes.sh`: fails when any file under the directories it is given exceeds 900 lines
   (`src/engine/` here; P4-01 adds `src/tui/`).
5. `rss.rs`, `shows.rs`, `search.rs`, `imdb.rs` and `browse.rs` stay where they are unless moving them under
   `src/features/` costs little; the decision is by diff size, because these files carry the owner's
   uncommitted work and churn makes review harder (§3.3).

- §3.3 module layout (the engine part): `src/engine/mod.rs` AppEngine start and drop; `ledger.rs` Record,
  read, save, fsync; `queue.rs` reconcile_queue and limits; `ops.rs` EngineOp enum and execute() (replaces
  string routes, P1-19); `view.rs` TorrentView (normalized) and the one legacy qBittorrent mapping (P1-19);
  `parked.rs` ParkedLedger (from dispatch_parked_in); `legacy_import.rs` migrate_legacy (deleted in P4-09).

  `src/engine/` or `src/tui/` over 900 lines", runs in CI.
