title: P1-10: Legacy socket adapter
description:
# P1-10: Legacy socket adapter

Plan item **P1-10** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3805). Phase P1; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M1a**; topological level 9 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-03 (Daemon core: `fbittorrent serve`), P1-19 (Typed operations and the
normalized model).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-15 (The TUI attaches to the daemon; quit verbs).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The TUI talks to its engine through `qbt::Client` → `ipc::request` with today's 4-byte length-prefixed JSON
  framing (`src/ipc.rs:62-85`; `ipc::request` at `:87-122`): request `{method, path, args: [[k,v]], file}`,
  response `{value, error}`. The routes it uses: `torrents/info`, `torrents/files`, `torrents/add`,
  `torrents/start`, `torrents/stop`, `torrents/delete`, `torrents/filePrio`, `torrents/setUploadLimit`,
  `torrents/setShareLimits`, `app/version`, `app/shutdown`, `app/restart`, `app/setQueue` and the `controls`
  routes.
- After P1-03 the daemon serves `engine.sock` with today's string dispatch moved under it; after P1-19
  `EngineOp::parse(route, body)` exists and `TorrentView::to_legacy_json()` produces the qBittorrent-shaped
  JSON.
- The v0.1 TUI owns its engine and never attaches (`src/main.rs:787,804-806`), so after installing v0.2 the
  only TUI is the new one; one binary serves daemon, CLI and widget, so no v0.1 CLI or widget survives
  `install.sh`.

## Goal and user value
§3.6 migration: v0.2.0 (M1) keeps the TUI on `qbt::Client` and the 4-byte framing until P4-03 moves it to API
v1 (§5.2 step 1), so the daemon must answer that framing. The TUI of P1-15 is the adapter's only consumer
(DL-59 cut legacy-binary compatibility tests). The adapter is removed in P4-09 (v0.4.0).

## Do (exact steps)
1. `src/api/legacy.rs`: the daemon serves `engine.sock` with the 4-byte length-prefixed JSON framing of
   today's `src/ipc.rs` (`ipc::request`'s format).
2. Each request's `route` and body parse into `EngineOp` through `EngineOp::parse` (P1-19).
3. Responses use the qBittorrent-shaped JSON of `TorrentView::to_legacy_json()` (`src/engine/view.rs`).
4. `app/shutdown` calls `lifecycle.request_stop(StopReason::Quit)`; `app/restart` restarts the engine in place
   (§3.2.8: connections survive).
5. The adapter is removed in P4-09 (§3.6, v0.4.0).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.6 migration table: v0.1.x `engine.sock` inside the TUI, CLI 4-byte, plugin spawns `status --json`, TUI
  owns the engine; v0.2.0 (M1) daemon serves `api.sock` and `engine.sock` (compat adapter), CLI API v1, plugin
  API v1 popup, TUI client over `engine.sock` (P1-15); v0.3.0 (M2) same plus the dashboard, TUI moves to API
  v1 in P4-03; v0.4.0 (M3) `engine.sock` removed (P4-09). A new CLI that finds only an old TUI-hosted
  `engine.sock` (no `api.sock`) still reads through it but refuses writes with "an older fbittorrent app is
  running; quit it with Q and retry" (P1-11; checked by hand in the M1a receipt).
- §3.2.5: `api.sock` (new) and `engine.sock` (legacy, until v0.4.0) are unlinked and bound only while the lock
  is held.
- §1.2 today's transport: 32 MiB cap; JSON double-encoded inside `value` (`src/ipc.rs:29-56`).
- Appendix D "Compat socket": `engine.sock` with the old 4-byte framing, served by the daemon until v0.4.0.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every `qbt::Client` call the TUI makes (`torrents/info`, `files`, `add`, `start`, `stop`, `delete`,
  `filePrio`, `setUploadLimit`, `setShareLimits`, `app/*`) answers from the daemon's `engine.sock` with the
  qBittorrent-shaped JSON of `src/engine/view.rs`.
- `app/shutdown` stops the daemon and `app/restart` restarts the engine.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit `legacy::tests::route_parse_roundtrip`: every route above parses and re-serialises through `EngineOp`.
- `native.py`'s 11 cases run against the TUI-as-client in P1-15 and cover every route above.
- Logging (polish round 1): `route_parse_roundtrip` prints each route and the `EngineOp` variant it parsed to;
  the `native.py` cases log every CLI call's argv, exit code and the pane capture they assert on.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-03 (the daemon owns `engine.sock`) and P1-19 (the route parser targets `EngineOp`).
- Consumed by P1-15 (the TUI attaches to the daemon through this adapter).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R6 (version skew during development): the compat socket period (§3.6) is the mitigation for the first
  upgrade.
- DL-06 (NDJSON on a new `api.sock`; the 4-byte `engine.sock` stays until v0.4.0), DL-14 (legacy mode removed
  in v0.4.0), DL-59 (legacy-binary compatibility tests cut: the TUI of P1-15 is the adapter's only consumer).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] Every `qbt::Client` call the TUI makes (`torrents/info`, `files`, `add`, `start`, `stop`, `delete`, `filePrio`, `setUploadLimit`, `setShareLimits`, `app/*`) answers from the daemon's `engine.sock` with the qBittorrent-shaped JSON of `src/engine/view.rs`.
- [ ] `app/shutdown` stops the daemon and `app/restart` restarts the engine.

title: P1-11: The CLI on the API client; contract 1.2.0
description:
# P1-11: The CLI on the API client; contract 1.2.0

Plan item **P1-11** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3825). Phase P1; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `cli`; first milestone this item feeds:
**M1a**; topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-04 (systemd user unit and start on demand), P1-09 (Mutations: refs, pending,
confirmed), P1-12 (Stop rule and idle exit), P1-14 (Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters), P1-17
(Upgrade detection and `restart`).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-15 (The TUI attaches to the daemon; quit verbs), P1-18 (Agent event stream and
raw API verb), M1a (Daemon behind today's UIs (v0.2.0-pre, installed, not tagged)), P2-07 (Menu, keybinding,
desktop entries, install script), P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P7-06
(Per-torrent download cap).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over

and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in

`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The CLI is `qbt::Client` over the 4-byte socket; today's `Cmd` enum is `src/main.rs:48-234`; the agent
  surface is `Code` 0..8 (`src/agent.rs:12-29`), `capabilities_json` (`src/agent.rs:134-210`), `triage`
  (`src/agent.rs:296-384`), the error envelope `{ok:false, code, code_name, error, hint}`
  (`src/agent.rs:113-123`, hint printed after "try:" at `:121`), contract version `1.1.0` (`src/agent.rs:7`).
  `list`, `show`, `status`, `wait` print the qBittorrent-shaped `qbt::Torrent` (`src/qbt.rs:11-36`).
- `status` closed case prints `{"ok": false}` with exit 0 (`src/main.rs:407-415`), an envelope inconsistency
  (RC §3 #21); the running shape has `engine`, `dl`, `up`, `active`, `queued`, `seeding`, `stopped`, `total`,
  `torrents` with the active ones first then up to 12 others (`src/main.rs:416-430`), which the v0.1 popup
  reads until P2-03 (`Model.js:102-115`).
- `add` diffs lists to find the hash (`src/main.rs:525-532`, `550-560`); `wait` ends with "every waited
  torrent is stopped" and exit 8 (`src/main.rs:761-763`); the parked path removes a record's `<hash>.torrent`
  on offline delete (`src/engine.rs:1338-1340`); `run.sh` holds cases R-001 to R-012 and needs legacy
  qBittorrent.
- `std` has no Unix-socket connect timeout (use a non-blocking `connect` plus `poll`).

## Goal and user value
W4 and W5: the agent surface stays stable and additive (principle 9) while every verb moves to the daemon:
`--json`, the envelope, exit codes, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` keep their meaning; reads never start the
daemon and answer `running: false` when it is down; `stop` and keep-files `delete` work offline on the ledger
(DL-10). Contract 1.2.0 documents every change, with the one declared break (`status` stopped shape,
DL-22/DL-43). On the critical path (P1-12 → P1-17 → P1-11 → P1-15 → M1a).

## Do (exact steps)
**Client** (`src/api/client.rs`, created by P1-04):
1. The blocking NDJSON client: connect with a 200 ms timeout; `hello` with `client.name = "cli-<pid>"`, `kind:
   "cli"` (`"agent"` under `--json`, so `app.info.clients` tells agent use from human use); a reader thread
   that matches responses to requests by `id` (at most 8 in flight, a channel per request) and queues
   unsolicited events separately; a `subscribe` iterator that yields frames and tracks `rev` (tested against
   the `subscribe*.ndjson` fixtures and the live bus); the reconnect backoff of §3.2.11 (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 s,
   then every 10 s); the mid-request rule of §3.2.4 step 6 with the idempotent set hard-coded from A.1 until
   P1-18's `api::ops::TABLE` replaces it.
2. `ensure_daemon()`'s liveness probe becomes `hello` on `api.sock` first, then `engine.sock` (§3.6: a
   TUI-hosted v0.1 engine answers reads through `torrents/info` and refuses writes with "an older fbittorrent
   app is running; quit it with Q and retry"; checked by hand in the M1a receipt). `ensure_daemon()` reads
   `FBITTORRENT_UNIT` (set by `setup`, default `fbittorrent.service`; harnesses set a throwaway name).
**Scope**: every Appendix F row whose verb exists now (today's `Cmd` enum plus P1-04's `up`, `down`,
`restart`, `dashboard` and P1-03's `serve`) moves to the client with the "Starts" rule of §3.2.3; rows for
later verbs (`undo`, `recheck`, `reannounce`, `queue`, `limits`, `limit`, `move`, `rename`, `shows quality`,
`api`, `events`, `log`, `wait --until`, `list --state/--origin`) land with their items.
3. Reads fall back to the ledger with a top-level `running: false` (`list`, `show`, `triage`), exit 0, with or
   without `--no-start`.
4. `stop` and keep-files `delete` write the ledger offline in the lock order of §3.2.3: `hello` fails with
   `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` → acquire `engine.lock` (`LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`, retried for 2 s; if it stays held the
   daemon is starting or draining, so retry `hello` instead) → read the ledger → write it (temp, fsync,
   rename, dir fsync) → release; at most two lock/hello rounds, then exit 4 with the daemon's hint; a `hello`
   that answers `stopping` waits for `deactivating` to end (§3.2.4 step 3); an offline delete also removes the
   record's `<hash>.torrent` (`src/engine.rs:1338-1340`); the JSON carries `running: false`.
5. `settings` keeps today's `app/setQueue` and `app/restart` through the compat adapter until P3-05; `rss
   grab` and `shows grab` call `torrents.add` until P3-07; `search`, `imdb`, `rss *`, `shows *` stay
   in-process until P3-07. In legacy mode (`engine = "qbittorrent"`, until P4-09) the WebUI path stays and
   every command prints one stderr line "engine = \"qbittorrent\" is deprecated and is removed in v0.4.0; see
   the README" plus a `warnings[]` entry.
**Shapes stay contract 1.x**:
6. `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent (`qbt::Torrent`), rebuilt from the
   A.9 `Torrent` by `cli::shapes::torrent()` (`src/cli/shapes.rs`, the twin of
   `TorrentView::to_legacy_json()`); additions are new fields with new names: `native_state` (the §3.5 enum),
   `reason`, `checked`, `origin`, `eta_s` (absent when unknown), `seeds` (P5-01), later `playable`; `state`
   keeps its qBittorrent string; the old numeric fields keep qBittorrent's sentinels so a 1.x parser never
   meets a missing key: `eta` is `8640000` when `eta_s` is absent, `num_seeds` stays `0` until P5-01 and
   `num_leechs` is the peer count, `progress_known: false` with `progress: 0` when `progress` is absent;
   `capabilities.changes[]` (1.2.0) says so under `field: "list[].eta"` and `field: "list[].num_seeds"`, and
   `robot-docs` tells agents to read `eta_s`/`seeds`/`native_state`.
7. `warnings: [{code, message}]` at the top level of every JSON envelope when non-empty (version skew §3.2.12;
   the deprecation).
8. The add path uses the hash returned by `torrents.add` and no longer diffs lists; `add --origin
   manual|handler|agent` (default `manual`; the desktop entry runs `fbittorrent add --origin handler %u`;
   `robot-docs` tells agents to pass `--origin agent`) feeds `torrents.add {origin}`; `add --json` is today's
   `{ok, action: "add", hash, name, source, sequential, first_last}` plus `duplicate` and later `deferred`.
9. `all` expands client-side in chunks of 256 for every bulk verb; `stop all` with nothing to stop prints
   `count: 0` without calling.
10. `wait`: one `ensure_daemon()` reconnect after `bye {reason: restart|upgrade}` or EOF; `bye {idle}` ends
    with today's "every waited torrent is stopped" envelope and exit 8; `bye
    {slow_client|hello_required|invalid_message}` exit 1.
11. **`status`** (§3.2.13): running → `{ok: true, running: true, connection: "api", backend: "native",
    app_open: <interactive count > 0>, daemon: {state, idle_exit_in_s?, busy_reasons, upgrade_pending}}` plus
    every 1.x running field unchanged (from `hello`, `transfer.info` and one `subscribe summary`'s first
    `state` frame); stopped → `{ok: true, running: false, app_open: false, backend: "stopped", engine:
    <config>, total: N}` from the ledger; `status --quiet` prints nothing and exits 0 when running, 4 when
    stopped (the menu gate of §8.6).
**Contract 1.2.0** (`src/agent.rs`):
12. `contract_version: "1.2.0"`; `commands[]` generated at runtime from clap's command tree (nested verbs as
    `rss list`, `shows follow`, …) with `CommandDoc` keeping `needs_backend` and gaining `starts: bool` (the
    §3.2.3 column) and `since: str`; `changes: [{since, breaking, command?, field?, note}]` with the
    `status.ok` break and every addition; new text for `engines`, `conventions.native_connect` (the daemon,
    `ensure_daemon`, the start rule), `defaults` and `files.socket` (`api.sock`); the §8.5 list as far as it
    exists at P1 (the 32 KiB/s cap, the daemon, `serve`, `restart`, `dashboard`, `--no-start`, the "reads
    never start, writes do" rule, the new `status` shape, a pointer to `docs/IPC.md`); `robot-docs` rewritten
    for the daemon. Later items bump the patch version (1.2.1 at P1-18 for `events`/`api`, …).
**Tests and scripts**:
13. `regression_tests/agent_contract.py` on `fbtlog.py` (the successor of `run.sh`: R-001 to R-012 ported
    against a disposable daemon started as a foreground child in the temp XDG directory, `--systemd` locally
    with the throwaway unit).
14. `scripts/verify-determinism.sh`: starts a disposable daemon, runs `status`, `list`, `show <h>`, `triage`,
    `config`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs --json` twice with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set and diffs; when
    `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set the CLI uses it for every wall-clock-derived field it prints (`elapsed_secs` in
    `wait`, `generated_at` in `capabilities`); ledger `*_at`/`*_on` values are untouched; runs in the `native`
    CI job.
15. README: a new "Lifecycle" section before `## CLI` (from §3.2: the daemon, `up`/`down`/`restart`, the start
    rule, idle exit) and the CLI section updated.

## Canonical rules copied in
- Appendix F determinism rule for every `--json` output: keys in a fixed order (serde struct order), arrays in
  a documented order (torrents by `added_at` descending, files by index, releases newest first then `key`,
  search results by seeders descending then name then first provider, feeds by `id`, feed items by
  `published_at` descending then `id`, shows by title, trackers by `url`), no wall-clock fields except
  documented `*_at` values; `NO_COLOR`, `CI` and a non-TTY stdout never change the bytes.
- Appendix F reachability of every exit code: 1 (`start` on `done`; `internal`), 2 (`seq`; `api nope`; bad
  flag), 3 (`delete --files` without `--yes`), 4 (`--no-start` with a stopped daemon; `events` when down;
  `status --quiet` when stopped; `busy`), 5 (`search` provider failure), 6 (`show zzzz`), 7 (ambiguous
  selector), 8 (`wait --timeout`).
- Appendix F rows for the P1 verbs: `triage` (`hello`, `torrents.list`, `transfer.info`, `app.network`;
  extended: `backend.running`, `backend.daemon`, `counts.ready`, `next_commands` gains `events --follow`);
  `capabilities`, `robot-docs [guide|keys]` (extended); `status [--quiet]` (**changed**, DL-22); `list`
  (extended); `show` (extended: `seeds`, `peers`, `playable`, `undo_until`); `add` (unchanged plus
  `duplicate`, `deferred`; exit 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 8); `wait` (extended; reconnects once across an exit-75
  restart; exit 8 when the daemon idles out with the condition unmet); `start` (plus `skipped`); `stop`
  (offline write when down); `delete` (`--files`: starts; else offline write); `seed`/`noseed`;
  `seq`/`first-last` (stubs, exit 2); `reconcile` (stub); `open`; `add-clipboard`; `up`, `down`, `restart`,
  `dashboard`, `tui`, `settings`, `config`, `setup`, `register-magnet`, `serve`.
- §3.2.12 version skew: same version and build silent; different → `warnings[]` in JSON and one stderr line in
  human mode ("daemon 0.2.0+564fa18 is running; this binary is 0.2.1+9c1d2e0; run `fbittorrent restart` to
  switch"); an unsupported protocol major is a hard error `proto_unsupported` with the same hint.
- §8.5: why a minor bump: every change is additive for an agent following `robot-docs` except the `status`
  stopped shape, declared with `breaking: true` (Q12); `commands[]` is generated from clap, so it never lists
  a verb before it exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- `agent_contract.py` passes against the daemon; `capabilities --json` lists the 1.2.0 changes and
  `contract_version == "1.2.0"`.
- Read commands never start the daemon and answer `running: false` with exit 0 when it is down, with or
  without `--no-start`.
- Every `--json` output is byte-identical across two runs with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set and the daemon idle;
  nothing but JSON appears on stdout in `--json` mode.
- `list --json` entries equal `cli::shapes::torrent()` of the A.9 objects `api torrents.list` returns (checked
  when P1-18 lands).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `agent_contract.py::{R-001…R-012 (ported), exit_code_dictionary_total (1: `start` on the completed local
  fixture; 2: a bad flag; 3: `delete --files` without `--yes`; 4: `--no-start add` with the daemon down, and
  `busy` through 33 held connections; 5: `imdb --refresh` with `FBT_IMDB_BASE_URL` at a closed port; 6: `show
  zzzz`; 7: an ambiguous selector; 8: `wait --timeout 1`), reads_never_start, reads_fall_back_offline,
  json_determinism, stdout_stderr_split, status_stopped_shape, status_running_shape, version_skew_warning (two
  builds through `FBT_BUILD_ID_OVERRIDE`, P1-17), capabilities_upload_text, commands_match_help (every
  subcommand `fbittorrent --help` lists is in `commands[]` and vice versa; today `commands[]` omits
  `add-clipboard` and `register-magnet`, `src/agent.rs:134-210`), deprecation_warning_legacy_mode,
  add_origin_flag, stop_all_empty_count_0, wait_survives_upgrade_restart,
  wait_exits_8_when_daemon_idles_out}`.
- Unit `api::errors::tests::retryable_never_maps_to_1` (over the A.3 table) and
  `agent::tests::commands_match_clap`.
- `daemon.py::{offline_stop_ledger, offline_delete_keep_files_ledger,
  offline_write_waits_for_draining_daemon}` (the last starts `down` and an offline `stop` together and asserts
  afterwards that `torrents.json` holds the torrent paused and no record was lost to the daemon's final save).
- Logging (polish round 1): `agent_contract.py` logs, per case, the exact argv, exit code, stdout (JSON) and
  stderr as `observed`, and the expected exit code and shape as `expect`; `json_determinism` logs both runs'
  SHA256; `scripts/verify-determinism.sh` writes one E.1 line per verb with the diff size.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-04 (`ensure_daemon()`, the new verbs, `FBITTORRENT_UNIT`), P1-09 (the add hash, refs and the
  resend rule), P1-12 (`summary.daemon` fields in `status`), P1-14 (`app.info.clients` and the log the hints
  point at), P1-17 (`hello.server.build` for the skew warning).
- Consumed by P1-15 (the TUI's presence connection reuses `api::Client`), P1-18 (`events`/`api` build on the
  client and bump to 1.2.1), M1a, P2-07 (`setup` flags and `status --quiet`), P3-07 (the CLI's feature verbs),
  P7-06 (`limit`).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q12 (open, default: the declared break): `status --json` while stopped answers `ok: true, running: false` at
  1.2.0.
- Q13 (open, default keep): `autostart = false`.

## Risks and decisions
- R6 (skew), R5 (the new lifetime; the README Lifecycle section is the owner-facing explanation).
- DL-10, DL-22 (status stopped shape), DL-43 (`busy` → exit 4; `status --quiet` exits 4 when stopped; the
  break declared in `capabilities.changes[]`), DL-48 (resend rule), DL-66 (the running `status --json` shape
  keeps every 1.x field), DL-69 (contract-1.x sentinels with the truth in new fields).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] Read commands never start the daemon and answer `running: false` with exit 0 when it is down, with or without `--no-start`.
- [ ] Every `--json` output is byte-identical across two runs with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set and the daemon idle; nothing but JSON appears on stdout in `--json` mode.
- [ ] `list --json` entries equal `cli::shapes::torrent()` of the A.9 objects `api torrents.list` returns (checked when P1-18 lands).

description:
# P1-12: Stop rule and idle exit

Plan item **P1-12** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3935). Phase P1; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1a**;
topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-11 (The CLI on the API client; contract 1.2.0), P1-15 (The TUI attaches to the
daemon; quit verbs), P1-17 (Upgrade detection and `restart`), M1a (Daemon behind today's UIs (v0.2.0-pre,
installed, not tagged)), P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P3-02 (RSS in the daemon), P3-03 (Shows in the daemon), P3-06
(Staged add).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Quitting the TUI stops every transfer (D9); there is no daemon, so there is no notion of "busy" or "idle".
  The owner's words (2026-10-18): "I don't want running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops,
  and is done." Encoded as A1 and DL-70: the daemon runs while the bar icon is lit and stops when the owner
  stops it; an idle net catches what the owner forgets. Earlier rounds had a `stop_policy` enum (`idle`,
  `last-ui`, `explicit`); the owner's answers to Q1 and Q31 deleted it (DL-02 superseded by DL-70).
- After P1-03 the supervisor ticks; after P1-06 `hello {interactive}` and `app.client {interactive, glance}`
  are recorded per connection; after P1-08 `summary` can carry `daemon.idle_exit_in_s` and `busy_reasons`.

## Goal and user value
Principle 5 ("on demand and visible"): nothing runs when nothing happens (§2.7 row "Nothing runs when nothing
happens": idle exit with a visible countdown; `status` never starts anything). The popup can say "stops in 4
min"; a forgotten daemon does not run for days; a daemon mid-download never exits by itself. On the critical
path (P1-08 → P1-12 → P1-17 → P1-11).

## Do (exact steps)
`src/daemon/policy.rs` (§3.2.10):
1. The one config key `idle_exit_secs` (default 300, minimum 30 unless 0; `0` disables the idle net; `serve
   --idle-exit-secs` overrides), evaluated by the supervisor every 5 s.
2. The busy table:

| Busy reason (`summary.daemon.busy_reasons` value) | Busy? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `downloading`: a torrent with intent "run" that is incomplete (downloading, stalled, metadata, checking, queued) | busy | Staged torrents in the add sheet do not count (P3-06). |
| `seeding`: a torrent with `seed = true` that is running | busy | An explicit user choice. |
| `parked_waiting`: parked (waiting for the VPN) with at least one download waiting | busy | Exiting would silently drop the intent. |
| `interactive`: a TUI, or a visible dashboard window | busy | The bar icon never counts (§4.4 rule 8). |
| `glance`: the bar popup is open (`app.client {glance: true}`) | not busy; the countdown **pauses** while a glance is open and resumes where it was when it closes | A popup that announces "stops in 4 min" must not stop while it is being read; a glance never starts the daemon and never counts as interactive; the shell closes the popup on focus loss. |
| `search`: a search session | busy | Sessions end 30 s after their client leaves (P3-01). |
| `mutation`: a pending long mutation (metadata resolution, payload deletion, recheck, move) | busy | |
| `clipboard_watch`: the opt-in watcher is on (P6-13) | **not busy** | The watcher restarts with the daemon; it never keeps it alive. |

3. Interactive counting through `hello {interactive}` and `app.client {interactive}` (the bar connection is
   never interactive); the glance pause (`app.client {glance}` freezes the countdown and releases it on
   `false` or disconnect; the daemon treats a connection drop as `glance: false`).
4. `summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s` (the frozen value while a glance is open) and `summary.daemon.busy_reasons`
   (A.9).
5. The idle net: when nothing is busy, a countdown of `idle_exit_secs` starts; anything busy cancels it; at
   zero the daemon sends `bye {reason: "idle"}` and exits 0. With `idle_exit_secs = 0` the daemon stops only
   when the owner stops it.
6. The owner's stop (`app.shutdown {reason: "user"}` from the popup's power button, `fbittorrent down` or the
   TUI's `Q`, P1-03's drain) is never gated by the busy table; downloads pause and resume when the daemon next
   starts, because their intent stays "run" in the ledger. The confirm when transfers are active belongs to
   the client (§4.5, §5.2), never to the daemon.
7. There is no `stop_policy` key, no `last-ui` branch and no `explicit` value (DL-70).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.2.10 why 300 s: it covers "close the popup, click another magnet a minute later" without a cold start and
  its hash checks, and nothing lingers for long after the work is done. It is a setting.
- A1 encoded: the torrent icon in the bar is visible exactly while the daemon runs (hidden when stopped, Q2);
  the icon's power button, `fbittorrent down` and `Q` in the TUI stop the daemon with everything in it (the
  popup and the TUI confirm when transfers are active); closing the TUI or the dashboard window never stops a
  transfer, dismissing the popup never stops anything, and the bar widget never keeps the daemon alive (an
  open popup only pauses the countdown while it is open).
- A.2 `hello.policy: {idle_exit_secs: u64}` (0 means the idle net is off). A.9 `Summary.daemon: {state,
  idle_exit_in_s?, busy_reasons: [open(downloading|seeding|parked_waiting|interactive|search|mutation)],
  upgrade_pending}`; `Settings.idle_exit_secs`.
- §4.11: the idle countdown is a dim line under the popup hero ("Idle · stops in 4 min"), never a banner; the
  bar tooltip says "Idle · stops in 4 min".
- Appendix D "Glance", "Interactive client", "Stop rule".

## Acceptance criteria (each a `daemon.py` case with `idle_exit_secs = 2`)
- Exits with no torrents.
- Stays while a local download runs.
- Stays while an interactive client is connected.
- Exits with only a bar client.
- Stays while parked with a waiting download.
- With `idle_exit_secs = 0` never exits on its own and still drains on `app.shutdown`.
- `busy_reasons` names the reason in every "stays" case.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::idle_exit_{no_torrents, download_keeps_alive, interactive_keeps_alive, bar_does_not,
  parked_keeps_alive, disabled_never_exits, disabled_shutdown_drains, glance_pauses, glance_drop_resumes}`.
  `glance_pauses` runs with `idle_exit_secs = 30`: open a glance at 20 s remaining, wait 5 s, close, assert
  `idle_exit_in_s` resumes at 20 and the exit happens 20 s after the close, not 15. `glance_drop_resumes`:
  kill the glancing client; the countdown resumes. Each step logs `summary.daemon` as observed.
- Unit `policy::tests::{countdown_cancel, countdown_pause_resume, zero_disables}`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-08 (the `summary` topic carries `idle_exit_in_s` and `busy_reasons`; `bye {idle}` is a bus
  frame).
- Consumed by P1-11 (`status` shows `daemon.*`), P1-15 (the TUI's presence connection counts as interactive;
  `Q`), P1-17 (an upgrade restarts only when not busy), M1a, P2-03 (the popup's glance and countdown line),
  P3-02 and P3-03 (refresh "when a client becomes interactive"), P3-06 (staged torrents must not count as
  busy).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q1 (answered): one stop rule; Q2 (answered): hidden when stopped; Q31 (answered): no `stop_policy` at all.

## Risks and decisions
- R5 (medium, medium): the new lifetime surprises the owner. Mitigation: A1 is the owner's own rule; the
  one-time notice (P1-15); the visible countdown; `Q`, `down` and the power button always work.
- DL-02 (superseded), DL-27 (clipboard watching never keeps the daemon alive), DL-36 (a glance pauses the
  countdown; the 10 s stopped-recently state), DL-70 (the owner's answer).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.

  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

# P1-13: Daemon notifications and the icon

Plan item **P1-13** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3962). Phase P1; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M1a**; topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M1a (Daemon behind today's UIs (v0.2.0-pre, installed, not tagged)), P5-05 (Ready
to watch), P6-10 (New-release notifications for Shows), P6-13 (Clipboard magnet watch (opt-in, A7)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Notifications exist only for "added" and "add failed", posted by the CLI with a plain `notify-send -i
  qbittorrent` (`src/main.rs:527-623`, `1296-1300`); no completion notification (RC §8; §6.2 row 18). The
  desktop entries use the borrowed `Icon=qbittorrent` (`src/setup.rs:112-114`).
- `notify-send --help` on this machine lists `-A/--action` ("Implies --wait … The name of the action is output
  to stdout", verified 2026-10-18). `--wait` blocks until the notification closes, which can be minutes for
  `critical`. The user manager exports `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, so `notify-send` and
  `xdg-open` work from the unit (R14 verified).
- The shell's notification service owns Do Not Disturb (`plugins/bar/indicators/Dnd.qml`), and `notify-send`
  goes through it (§6.2 row 39: nothing to build for quiet hours).
- Transmission's wording "Open File" / "Open Folder" (`gtk/Notify.cc:234-253`) is the borrowed model (§4.18).

## Goal and user value
T1 notifications (§6.2 row 18) and A5 (a `magnet:` click adds immediately and notifies with "Undo" and "Open
window"; it never opens a window). "Tell me when it is ready to watch" starts here with "Download complete"
and its "Open" that starts the player (W1 step 4, W4). The brand becomes one glyph across bar and
notifications. In M1a's demo: a browser click produces exactly one toast (DL-66).

## Do (exact steps)
`src/daemon/notify.rs` (§3.8):
1. A queue drained by at most 4 threads (further notifications wait); the same `(kind, hash)` pending twice is
   collapsed; each runs `notify-send -a fbittorrent -i fbittorrent -A <action>=<label>… "<title>" "<body>"`
   and reads the chosen action name from stdout.
2. Rows and actions:

| Event | Title | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| added (`origin: "handler"` only) | "Added" | `undo` → `torrents.remove {delete_files: false}`; `window` → `fbittorrent dashboard` |
| add failed | "Could not add" | `log` → `fbittorrent log` |
| completed | "Download complete" | `default` and `open` → `xdg-open <open_target>` (the body click invokes `default`); `folder` → `xdg-open <dir>` |
| VPN waiting / back | "Waiting for <interface>" / "VPN back; N downloads resumed" | none; once per transition |

   Later rows through the same notifier: "Ready to watch" (P5-05), "Disk almost full" (P5-07), "3 new
episodes" (P6-10), "Magnet on clipboard: <name>" (P6-13).
3. Bodies are escaped for markup (`&`, `<`). `notify = false` (config, `README.md:162`) and `serve
   --no-notify` disable everything. No secret ever appears in argv.
4. **Who posts "Added"**: the daemon, with its two actions, only when `torrents.add` carries `origin:
   "handler"` (the desktop entry; the `undo` action must outlive the short-lived `add` process); the CLI keeps
   today's plain `notify-send` (no actions, no `--wait`) only on a TTY or with `--notify`, and never for
   `--origin handler`, so a click produces exactly one toast; agents, `--json` and `--quiet` get none, so ten
   `add` calls do not make ten toasts (Q33, DL-52).
5. Emit `torrent.completed` where the queue loop first sets `completion_on` (`src/engine.rs:301-304`) and
   `torrent.added {hash, name, origin}` after `torrents.add` (A.8).
6. **The icon**: an SVG glyph `assets/fbittorrent.svg`, monochrome, the `󰇚` shape (the same as the bar's
   download glyph, so the notification and the bar read as one app), installed by `setup` to
   `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/fbittorrent.svg`; replace `-i qbittorrent`
   (`src/main.rs:1296-1300`) and `Icon=qbittorrent` in the desktop entries (`src/setup.rs:112-114`) with
   `fbittorrent`.
7. A notification whose action handler process is killed (shell restart) never acts; nothing is left half-done
   because every action is a normal API operation with a `ref`.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.8 full event table (the later rows): ready to watch → "Ready to watch", `default` and `open` (play)
  (P5-05); disk almost full → "Disk almost full", `window` (P5-07); new releases → "3 new episodes", `window`
  (Shows view) (P6-10); clipboard magnet (opt-in) → "Magnet on clipboard: <name>", `add`, `dismiss` (P6-13).
- §3.2.9: the one-notification-per-transition rule stops a flapping tunnel from spamming; the bar icon carries
  the state continuously; messages name the configured interface, not "ProtonVPN".
- §2.4 Notifications surface: Added (with Undo), completed, ready to watch, failed, VPN waiting, new episodes,
  clipboard magnet (opt-in).
- §3.9: notifications escape markup; no secret ever appears in argv; arguments are always argv arrays.
- A.8 `torrent.added {hash, name, origin}`, `torrent.completed {hash, name, open_target}`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A fake `notify-send` records the calls with the right actions.
- The "open" action triggers a fake `xdg-open` with the right path.
- "undo" removes the just-added torrent keeping files.
- `notify = false` suppresses everything.
- A VPN flap of three transitions in 2 s produces at most two notifications.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::{notify_completed (the local magnet fixture completes; a fake notify-send on PATH records argv;
  assert one call with both actions), notify_action_open (feed "open" on the fake's stdout; a fake xdg-open
  received the file path), notify_added_undo ("undo" removes the torrent, keeps files), notify_off,
  notify_vpn_once_per_transition, notify_queue_bounded (40 completions at once: at most 4 notify-send
  processes alive, all 40 recorded)}`.
- Unit `notify::tests::escape_markup`.
- Logging (polish round 1): the fake `notify-send` shim appends its argv to `<tmp>/shims/notify-send.log`;
  each case logs the argv lines it asserted on (`-A undo=Undo`, `-A window=Open window`, the title and the
  body) as `observed`, and the fake `xdg-open`'s argv for the action cases; `notify_queue_bounded` logs the
  peak concurrent process count it measured.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-08 (the events `torrent.added`/`torrent.completed` are bus events; the notifier reacts to
  them).
- Consumed by M1a (the demo's toasts), P5-05 (ready-to-watch notification), P6-10 (Shows notifications), P6-13
  (clipboard notification).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- A5 / Q9 (open, default add immediately with the notification).
- Q33 (open, default plain toast on a TTY): a terminal `add` keeps a plain toast; the daemon posts the
  actioned one only for browser clicks.

## Risks and decisions
- R14 (low, medium): notification actions need the GUI environment inside the user manager; verified present;
  without it notifications still show, without working actions.
- DL-52 (the CLI notifies "Added" only on a TTY or with `--notify`; completion and ready notifications open on
  a body click), DL-66 (exactly one toast for a browser click, posted by the daemon), DL-37 (one bar mark; the
  notification icon shape is the same glyph).

title: P1-14: Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters

# P1-14: Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters

Plan item **P1-14** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3988). Phase P1; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M1a**; topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-11 (The CLI on the API client; contract 1.2.0), M1 (First demo (v0.2.0)), P3-10
(Details pane: Overview, Files, Log), P3-15 (Settings sheet, Log view, Help overlay), P4-08 (Log modal, toasts
and message history).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Feedback disappears after 8 or 15 s and is not logged (RC §9 defect 13, D13 "feedback is unlogged"); the
  only persistent error record is `engine/last-error.txt` (`src/engine.rs:484-487`). There is no execution log
  (§6.2 row 11: "In, T1: replaces ephemeral feedback and the hidden error file").
- After P1-03 the daemon logs `level source message key=value…` lines on stderr (journald captures them under
  systemd); after P1-08 the bus can serve an append-only keyed topic.
- Round 0 scheduled a "TUI retirement review" that would have read per-client usage counters; it was removed
  as ceremony (P7-07), but the counters stay because they cost one line in `hello` handling and the owner can
  look at them whenever they like (§0.1).

## Goal and user value
T1 log: "why is this torrent not moving" answered next to the torrent instead of in a message that vanished
(§4.7 Log tab, §5.7 row 13, P3-15's Log view, P4-08's Log modal). The `log` cap, `app.log` and the `log` topic
are the one source all three UIs and `fbittorrent log --follow` read. The usage counters (`app.info.clients`)
tell agent use from human use.

`src/daemon/log.rs` (add it to the §3.3 layout):
1. The ring of 2,000 `LogEntry` (A.9: `{seq, ts, level, source, hash?, message}`; sources per §3.2.15: an open
   enum `daemon`, `engine`, `queue`, `api`, `search`, `rss`, `shows`, `imdb`, `notify`, `network`, `watch`,
   `clipboard`) fed by the stderr logger, with the journald copy unchanged.
2. `app.log {since_seq?, limit? ≤ 1000 (default 200), level: enum(error|warn|info|debug)?, source?, hash?}` →
   `{entries: [LogEntry], next_seq}` (A.4).
3. The `log` topic (A.7: keyed by `seq`, append-only, on change).
4. `fbittorrent log [--follow] [--json] [--level error|warn|info|debug] [--source <s>]` (Appendix F: exit 4
   when the daemon is down, with the hint `fbittorrent up`; the hint also prints `journalctl --user -u
   fbittorrent` because journald keeps the long history; `--follow` prints NDJSON).
5. `app.info.clients` counters per `client.kind` in memory (connections since start; reset at start; nothing
   leaves the machine).
6. Retire `engine/last-error.txt` (`src/engine.rs:484-487`).
7. `caps` gains `log`.

- §3.2.15 Logging: each log line on stderr is `level source message key=value…`; journald adds timestamps; the
  same entries enter an in-memory ring of 2,000 entries that the `log` topic serves; sources are an open enum.
- §3.8 Log: a ring of 2,000 entries `{seq, ts, level, source, hash?, message}`; `app.log` and the `log` topic
  serve it; journald keeps the long history.
- §3.2.3: `log` and `events` never start the daemon; when it is down they exit 4 with the hint `fbittorrent
  up` (the log ring and the event ring exist only inside the daemon).
- §3.4.10: log ring 2,000 entries. §3.4.4: log `source` is an open enum, so new sources are additive.
- Appendix F `log [--follow] [--level] [--source] [--json]`: `app.log`, topic `log`; starts: no; JSON new
  (`entries: [LogEntry]`; `--follow` prints NDJSON); exit 0, 4.
- §4.7 Log tab (P3-10): log entries for this torrent, the `log` topic filtered by hash. §4.6: the dashboard's
  last-message row opens the Log view (P3-15). §5.7 row 13: message history plus a Log modal `L` fed by the
  daemon log (P4-08).
- Contract bookkeeping: `log` is listed in `capabilities.commands[]` (1.2.x patch bump with its `changes[]`
  entry).

- An injected engine error (`FBT_TEST_INJECT_ERROR=<hash>`) appears once in `fbittorrent log --json` with
  `source: "engine"` and its hash.
- Counters increase per `hello` kind.
- `log --follow` prints a new entry within 1 s.

- Unit `log::tests::{ring_bound, seq_monotonic, filter_level_source}`.
- `daemon.py::{log_injected_error, log_follow, hello_counters}`.

- Depends on P1-08 (the `log` topic is a bus topic; `app.info.subscriptions` and the per-kind counters live
