zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D9: quitting the TUI stops every transfer without warning (`src/tui/mod.rs:1178`, `1207-1212`); `q` and `Q`
  both quit. The TUI hosts the engine (`run_native_app`, `src/main.rs:786-827`) and polls it every 2 s
  (`src/tui/mod.rs:1670-1674`) through `qbt::Client`'s native path; the in-process lifecycle checks are
  `src/tui/mod.rs:1699-1702`; a second launch only focuses the first window (`src/main.rs:787`); the desktop
  entry and the menu use `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` (`/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui`),
  which focuses an existing window by app id.
- After P1-04 `ensure_daemon()` exists; after P1-10 the daemon answers the 4-byte framing on `engine.sock`;
  after P1-11 `api::Client` exists; after P1-12 the idle net counts interactive clients.

## Goal and user value
§5.2 step 1: the TUI becomes a client of the daemon while keeping `qbt::Client`, the 2 s poll and every key
(the owner's muscle memory and the 21 interaction tests). D9 and A1: `q` closes the TUI and leaves downloads
running; `Q` stops the daemon after a confirm when transfers are active; the first `q` ever explains the new
lifetime once (R5). W6: `ssh host fbittorrent tui` attaches to the running daemon. The last item on the
critical path before M1a.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `fbittorrent tui` calls `ensure_daemon()` and runs the TUI against the daemon through `engine.sock` with
   `qbt::Client`'s native path and the 2 s poll unchanged (`src/tui/mod.rs:1670-1674`).
2. The in-process lifecycle checks (`src/tui/mod.rs:1699-1702`) become "daemon gone" detection: two failed
   polls show the banner "fbittorrent stopped" with Enter → `ensure_daemon()`.
3. `q` and Ctrl+C close the TUI only. `Q` sends `app.shutdown {reason: "user"}` after "Stop fbittorrent? N
   downloads pause until it starts again. y/N" when transfers are active (only `y` confirms, P0-13); `q` never
   asks, because closing the TUI never stops a transfer (A1).
4. The first `q` ever shows the one-time notice "Downloads continue in the background; fbittorrent stops
   itself when idle. Q here, or the bar icon's power button, stops it now.", stored as `{"first_quit_seen":
   true}` in `~/.local/state/fbittorrent/notices.json`.
5. The TUI also opens an `api.sock` presence connection (`hello` with `client.name = "tui-<pid>"`, `kind:
   "tui"`, `interactive: true`, heartbeats; `app.shutdown` for `Q`) while its data still flows over
   `engine.sock`, so the idle net counts it as interactive.
6. `fbittorrent tui` always runs a client in the current terminal, so a second one over SSH attaches (today a
   second launch only focuses the first window). The desktop entry and menu keep
   `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui`, which focuses an existing window by app id.
7. "On open" RSS and Shows checks stay in the TUI until P3-07 moves them into the daemon.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §5.1 what stays: four screens with `1`-`4` and Tab; hover preview, click to select, double-click to
  activate, wheel; the two-row footer; `?` help; IMDb cards with kitty posters; F6 settings; the add prompt
  with F4; the files modal keys (Space, `1`, `a`, `n`); the Shows and RSS read models (`m`, `Shift+M`, `u`);
  every key letter the README documents.
- Appendix B rows: "Close this UI": TUI `q`, Ctrl+C (no longer stops downloads); "Stop fbittorrent (the daemon
  and everything in it, A1)": TUI `Q` (confirms when active); `q` closes the surface it is pressed in and `Q`
  quits, everywhere (DL-54).
- §3.2.10: the owner's stop is `app.shutdown {reason: "user"}` from the power button, `down` or `Q`; the
  confirm when transfers are active belongs to the client, never to the daemon.
- A.2 `hello`: `client.kind: tui`, `interactive: true`; `client.name` must be unique per process (`tui-<pid>`,
  §3.4.8).
- §4.11 banner wording the TUI shares later: "Reconnecting… (retry in N s)", "fbittorrent stopped" with Enter
  → start (P4-03 brings the full set; this item brings the stopped banner).
- Appendix D "Presence connection": the TUI's API connection used only to be counted as interactive while its
  data still uses the compat socket (P1-15 to P4-03).
- W6: `ssh host fbittorrent tui` attaches to the running daemon (or starts it) and offers the same features as
  locally; quitting the TUI leaves downloads running under A1.

## Acceptance criteria
- Starting the TUI with no daemon starts it.
- `q` leaves a local download running.
- `Q` with an active download asks and stops on `y`.
- The first `q` shows the notice once.
- Killing the daemon shows "fbittorrent stopped" in the TUI within 5 s.
- A second TUI in another tmux pane attaches and both show the same torrent.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `native.py::{tui_starts_daemon, q_detaches, Q_confirms, first_q_notice_once, daemon_gone_banner,
  second_tui_attaches}`; from this item `native.py` starts a disposable daemon in its temp XDG directory and
  the TUI attaches to it (Appendix E.2: "from P1-15 the TUI runs as a client of a disposable daemon").
- TUI interaction tests for the prompts.
- `native.py`'s 11 existing cases now exercise P1-10's adapter end to end.
- Logging (polish round 1): `native.py` cases log every keystroke sent (`tmux send-keys -l`), the pane capture
  asserted on (the notice text, the `Stop fbittorrent?` prompt, the `fbittorrent stopped` banner) and
  `fbittorrent status --json` after each step as `observed`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-04 (`ensure_daemon()`), P1-10 (the compat adapter the TUI's data flows through), P1-11 (the
  `api::Client` the presence connection uses), P1-12 (interactive counting and `app.shutdown` semantics).
- Consumed by M1a (the demo's step 4), P3-07 (moves the on-open refreshes out of the TUI), P4-01 (the TUI
  split starts from the client TUI).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q1/Q31 (answered): `q` closes, `Q` quits; no `stop_policy`. Q21 (open, default `q` closes, `Q` quits):
  confirmed by the same rule. Q22 (open, default yes): install M1a and live with the new lifetime before the
  popup rewrite.

## Risks and decisions
- R5 (medium, medium): the new lifetime surprises the owner; the one-time notice and `Q` always working are
  this item's mitigations.
- DL-33/DL-54 (`q` closes, `Q` quits everywhere), DL-57 (M1a is a milestone: installed, not tagged), DL-59
  (the TUI of P1-15 is the compat adapter's only consumer), DL-70.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

title: P1-16: Lazy restore of completed torrents
description:
# P1-16: Lazy restore of completed torrents

Plan item **P1-16** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4028). Phase P1; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1a**;
topological level 9 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-07 (Integration harness `daemon.py`), P1-19 (Typed operations and the
normalized model).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M1a (Daemon behind today's UIs (v0.2.0-pre, installed, not tagged)), P5-03
(Recheck), P6-06 (App-owned fast resume (fork change)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D3: every open re-hashes all data (7 s for the owner's 3.4 GiB). `fastresume: false` (`src/engine.rs:437`);
  the fork refuses fastresume (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/session.rs:567-568`,
  `torrent_state/initializing.rs:113-114`). Under A1 the daemon starts after every idle period, so the cost
  repeats many times a day.
- A completed stop-on-complete record is `completion_on != 0` and `ratio_limit == 0.0`
  (`src/engine.rs:90-92`); after P0-09 records are restored by a background task; after P1-19 `TorrentView`
  has `checked: bool` and `reason: missing_files`.
- The daemon serves the ledger for records without a live handle already (the parked path,
  `src/engine.rs:1233-1355`).

## Goal and user value
The common case of D3 without trusting anything (R7): completed torrents, which are most of a library, are
served from the ledger as `done` with `checked: false` and never opened until the user acts on them. P6-06
later adds trusted fast resume for live torrents behind a clean-shutdown marker. §6.2 additional item "Lazy
restore of completed torrents (T1): under A1 the daemon starts often; checking finished data every time wastes
minutes on a large library".

## Do (exact steps)
1. In `src/engine/mod.rs`'s restore task (P0-09), records with `completion_on != 0` that stop on complete
   (`ratio_limit == 0.0`) are restored **dormant**: served from the ledger and the saved `.torrent` as `state:
   done, checked: false` (A.9) without opening files or adding them to the librqbit session.
2. `torrents.start`, `torrents.set_seed {on: true}`, `torrents.recheck` and `torrents.set_files` with a
   non-empty `include` on a dormant record trigger the real restore with a check first. **Bead review change
   (2026-10-18):** `torrents.open_target` on a dormant record does **not** trigger a hash check: it answers
   from the ledger (`save_path` plus the saved `.torrent`'s file list, as `qbt::open_target` does today,
   `src/qbt.rs:706`) after a `stat` of the target path; a missing path makes the record `error` with `reason:
   missing_files` exactly as a failed restore would, and the record stays dormant (`checked: false`)
   otherwise, so a later `seed` or `recheck` still checks. Why: a full check costs seconds per GiB (D3: 7 s
   for 3.4 GiB) and `o` must start the player at once (W1 step 4; §2.7 "Ready to watch": `o` opens it); the
   plan's reading of "acted on" is kept for every mutation and relaxed only for this read.
3. A dormant record whose files are missing then becomes `error` with `reason: missing_files` (the §4.3.4
   phrase "files are missing") when acted on, not before.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §9.3 preamble edge-state defaults: a mutation that needs a live engine handle on a dormant torrent answers
  `invalid_state` unless the item says what it does instead; `recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty
  `include`, restore a dormant torrent first (this item); `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is
  `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed <hash>` (P0-10), so the "start" trigger above applies to the
  seeding path (`set_seed {on: true}`) and to `start --force`/`force_start` once P6-05 exists.
- §3.5: `checked: false` marks a completed torrent restored without hashing (P1-16). A.9 `Torrent.checked:
  bool`.
- §3.4.9: a dormant torrent is "engine not live for that torrent", so `peers`, `dl_bps`, `ul_bps` are absent;
  `progress` is 1.0 from the ledger.
- §3.2.7 crash recovery: data is re-checked on the next start (until P6-06); this item narrows that to
  incomplete and seeding torrents.
- Appendix D "Dormant / lazy restore": a completed torrent served from the ledger without a hash check until
  the user acts on it.
- P5-03 interaction: if a recheck finds missing data, `completion_on` is reset to 0 and `completed_at`
  cleared, so this item can never restore a corrupt torrent as dormant `done`; a dormant torrent is restored
  with its check, which is the recheck (no second check).

## Acceptance criteria
- Starting with five completed fixture torrents performs no piece checks for them (no initial-validation log
  lines) and lists them as `done` within 1 s.
- `seed` on one checks it and seeds.
- A dormant torrent whose files were deleted reports `error` with reason `missing_files` when acted on, not
  before.
- `torrents.open_target` (`o`) on a dormant torrent answers within 100 ms with no validation log line and
  leaves it dormant (`checked: false`); on a missing file it answers `invalid_state` with `reason:
  missing_files` and the record turns `error`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::{lazy_restore_no_checks, dormant_seed_checks, dormant_missing_files, dormant_open_no_check}`.
  "No piece checks" is observable two ways and the cases assert both: `lazy_restore_no_checks` subscribes to
  `torrents` before `READY=1` and asserts none of the five records ever carries `state: checking`, and greps
  the daemon log for `source=engine` lines matching `initializ|validat|check` that name their hashes (there
  must be none); "within 1 s" is measured from the `READY=1` datagram. Each case logs the state sequence per
  hash, the matching log lines (expected none) and, for `dormant_open_no_check`, the `open_target` round-trip
  time and the `checked` flag afterwards.
- Engine unit test `restore_dormant_record`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-19 (`checked`, `reason`, the typed view) and P1-07 (the harness).
- Consumed by M1a (the daemon starts fast on the owner's library), P5-03 (recheck of a dormant torrent is one
  check), P6-06 (fast resume for the rest).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R7 (low, high): fast resume trusts data that changed; this item trusts nothing (it does not open files at
  all until acted on) and leaves `recheck` available.
- DL-66: `set_files` with a non-empty `include` restores a dormant torrent.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /

  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table

  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least

  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,

  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item

- [ ] A dormant torrent whose files were deleted reports `error` with reason `missing_files` when acted on, not before.

# P1-17: Upgrade detection and `restart`

Plan item **P1-17** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4045). Phase P1; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M1a**; topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-04 (systemd user unit and start on demand), P1-12 (Stop rule and idle exit).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-11 (The CLI on the API client; contract 1.2.0), M1a (Daemon behind today's UIs
(v0.2.0-pre, installed, not tagged)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- During development `~/.local/bin/fbittorrent` is replaced by `install.sh`'s `mv` (a `cp` onto a running
  binary fails with `ETXTBSY`) while a long-lived daemon keeps running old code, and the plugin is a symlink
  into the repository that hot-reloads on every save (`~/.config/omarchy/plugins/oliver.torrents ->
  …/fbittorrent/plugin/oliver.torrents`), so both directions of skew are real (FO §7.2; R6 is rated "high"
  likelihood).
- The unit (P1-04) has `RestartForceExitStatus=75` and `SuccessExitStatus=75`; `StopReason::Upgrade` (P1-01)
  exits 75; P1-03's supervisor has a 30 s slot for this check; P1-12's busy table says when a restart is safe.
- There is no build id in the binary today; `hello.server.version` is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`.

## Goal and user value
Version skew between a long-lived daemon and a replaced binary or a hot-reloaded plugin (R6). The owner
installs a rebuilt binary and the daemon switches by itself when idle, or says "Update installed; restarts
when idle" while a download runs (M1 demo step 10). Clients can tell skew (`warnings[]`, the dim banner) and
`fbittorrent restart` switches now. Feature skew is handled by `caps` (§3.4.3), not here. On the critical path
(P1-12 → P1-17 → P1-11).

## Do (exact steps)
§3.2.12 in `src/daemon/upgrade.rs` and `build.rs`:
1. `build.rs` exports `FBT_BUILD_ID`: the short git hash plus `-dirty`, or `unknown`; `FBT_BUILD_ID_OVERRIDE`
   wins (for tests). `hello` returns `server.version` (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`) and `server.build`.
2. The daemon records `(dev, inode, mtime)` of `current_exe()` at start and compares every 30 s from the
   supervisor.
3. Changed and not busy → `lifecycle.request_stop(StopReason::Upgrade)` (exit 75); the unit restarts it at
   once with the new binary. Changed and busy → `summary.daemon.upgrade_pending = true` ("update installed;
   restarts when idle") until idle.
4. `app.restart {scope: daemon}` → drain and exit 75 now; `fbittorrent restart` sends it and waits for the new
   `hello` (Appendix F: exit 8 after 30 s).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.2.12 client behaviour: same version and build: silent. A different version or build: the CLI adds an
  entry to `warnings[]` in JSON and prints one stderr line in human mode ("daemon 0.2.0+564fa18 is running;
  this binary is 0.2.1+9c1d2e0; run `fbittorrent restart` to switch"); the TUI and the plugin show a
  dismissible banner (§4.11 "Version skew, same protocol": dim banner "fbittorrent 0.2.0 runs; 0.2.1 is
  installed. Restart to update."). An unsupported protocol major is a hard error `proto_unsupported` with the
  same hint (§4.11 "Protocol major mismatch": urgent banner "This plugin speaks API 1; the running fbittorrent
  speaks API 2. Update the plugin or run `fbittorrent restart`.").
- §3.2.12 feature skew: `caps` lets a client hide what the daemon cannot serve; the daemon rejects unknown ops
  with `unknown_op` so a newer client fails loudly on exactly the missing feature.
- §4.11 "Upgrade pending": bar icon normal; popup dim line "Update installed; restarts when idle"; dashboard
  status line.
- A.2 `server: {version, build, pid, launcher, log}`; A.4 `app.restart {scope: enum(engine|daemon)}` →
  `{state: "pending"}`; A.9 `Summary.daemon.upgrade_pending: bool`; A.8 `bye {reason: upgrade}`;
  `engine.changed.reason` includes `upgrade`.
- §3.2.8 supervisor: every 30 s check whether the binary was replaced; exit with the reason's code (0, 70 or
  75).
- §8.6 install: copy to a temporary name and rename, so a running daemon keeps its inode and detects the
  replacement.
- Appendix F `restart` (new): `app.restart {scope: daemon}`; starts: no; exit 0, 4, 8.

- Replacing the binary (copy and rename) while idle makes the daemon exit 75 and systemd start the new build

  before and after and the unit's exit status.

- Consumed by P1-11 (`hello.server.build` feeds the skew warning; `version_skew_warning` test) and M1a.

- None.

- R6 (high, medium): version skew during development; this item plus `caps`, `warnings`, protocol checks and

surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake

lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Agents poll `triage --json` for state (§6.2 row 33); there is no event stream and no way to call a daemon
  operation that has no CLI verb yet. `robot-docs` (`src/main.rs:56-60,322-328`) has a positional `section`;
  `capabilities` lists `commands[]`.
- After P1-08 the `events` topic exists with a `seq` ring of 1,000 entries or 10 minutes and `since_seq`
  replay; after P1-11 `api::Client` has a `subscribe` iterator and the contract is 1.2.0.
- The idempotent set is hard-coded in the client from A.1 until this item's table replaces it.

## Goal and user value
W5 and §2.7 "Agent ergonomics": `events --follow` ends polling; `api` exposes every operation to scripts the
day it lands (§6.3: items without a CLI verb are reachable through `fbittorrent api <op>` until they get one).
This is the Σ "mega-command" principle applied to the daemon split. The compiled-in `api::ops::TABLE` is also
what the CLI uses to decide whether an op may start the daemon when `hello` is unreachable.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`fbittorrent events [--follow] [--since-seq N] [--kinds a,b] --json`**: connects, subscribes to the
   `events` topic with `since_seq` (A.7), filters by kind client-side, prints one JSON object per event on
   stdout; without `--follow` it prints the replay and exits 0; with `--follow` it continues until EOF or
   SIGINT (exit 0). Exit 4 when the daemon is down, 2 on a bad kind. Each printed event carries `seq` and
   `instance` so an agent can resume with `--since-seq` (`seq` restarts at 1 with every `instance`, so the
   agent stores `(instance, seq)`).
2. **`fbittorrent api <op> [--arg k=v]… [--json-args '{…}'] [--ref r]`** sends one operation and prints the
   result envelope unchanged (errors map to exit codes through A.3).
3. **`api --list [--json]`** prints every operation with its args, result, `mutating`, `idempotent` and
   `since` from `api::ops::TABLE` (`src/api/ops/mod.rs`), the compiled-in table the CLI also uses to decide
   whether an op may start the daemon when it is down (`hello` is not reachable then). `robot-docs api` prints
   the table (the same content `docs/IPC.md` documents).
4. A unit test asserts the table matches `docs/IPC.md`'s op list; `api nope` suggests the nearest names from
   it (`unknown_op.details.nearest`, Levenshtein ≤ 2).
5. Both verbs are listed in `capabilities` as `json: true, mutating: <per op>` and in `robot-docs`;
   `contract_version` becomes `1.2.1` with `changes[]` entries for `events` and `api`.
6. `api::Client` (P1-11) switches its idempotent set from the hard-coded A.1 list to the table.

## Canonical rules copied in
- A.7 `events`: keyed, append-only by `seq`; the unsolicited events of A.8 (`torrent.*`, `engine.changed`,
  `mutation.result`, `search.done`, `shows.checked`, `clipboard.magnet`) wrapped as `{seq, ts, ev, …}`;
  subscribing with `since_seq` replays the retained ring (1,000 entries or 10 minutes, whichever is smaller)
  then streams live; a `since_seq` older than the ring answers `snapshot.begin {reason: "resync",
  oldest_seq}`.
- A.8: every unsolicited event except `heartbeat` and `bye` carries `seq` (daemon-global, monotonic per
  instance) and `ts`.
- Appendix F `events` (new): `subscribe events {since_seq}` (replay, then live); starts: no; JSON new (NDJSON,
  one event per line, each with `seq` and `instance`); exit 0, 2 (bad kind), 4. `api <op> [--arg k=v…]
  [--json-args] [--ref]` (new): the named operation; starts: per op (`mutating` column of A.4..A.6); JSON new
  (the response envelope verbatim under `result`); exit: every code of A.3. Reads against a stopped daemon
  exit 4 with the hint `fbittorrent up` (§3.2.3).
- A.1: `api::ops::TABLE` carries the `idempotent` flag and `api --list` prints it; A.1's list is the source.
- §9.3 preamble contract bookkeeping: an item that adds an API op also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE`
  (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1, `since`); this item creates the table.
- A.12 example: `fbittorrent add "magnet:…" --json` →
  `{"ok":true,"action":"add","hash":"3f2a…",…,"duplicate":false}`; `fbittorrent wait 3f2a --until playable
  --timeout 600 --json` → `{"ok":true,"complete":false,"playable":true,"torrents":[…]}`; `fbittorrent events
  --follow --kinds torrent.completed --json` →
  `{"ev":"torrent.completed","hash":"3f2a…","name":"Sintel.2010.1080p","open_target":"/home/oliver/Downloads/Sintel.2010.1080p.mkv"}`.
- §8.5: `robot-docs` grows by patch versions as later items land (`events` and `api` at P1-18 → 1.2.1), each
  with a `changes[]` entry.

## Acceptance criteria
- `events --follow` prints `torrent.completed` within 2 s of a fixture completing.
- `api torrents.list` returns the A.9 objects and `list --json`'s `torrents` array equals
  `cli::shapes::torrent()` applied to them (the contract-1.x shape, P1-11).
- `contract_version` becomes `1.2.1` with `changes[]` entries for `events` and `api`.
- `api nope` exits 2 with `unknown_op` and a hint listing the nearest operation names (Levenshtein ≤ 2).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `agent_contract.py::{events_follow_completion, events_since_seq_replay (kill the agent, add two fixtures,
  resume with --since-seq and see exactly those two), events_resync_when_older (a since_seq below the ring
  gets reason resync and oldest_seq), events_down_exit_4, api_list_matches, api_list_matches_ipc_md,
  api_unknown_op_hint, api_mutating_starts_daemon_read_does_not}`.
- Unit `api::ops::tests::table_matches_ipc_md`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `events_*` cases log every NDJSON line received with its `seq` and `instance` as
  `observed`; `api_*` cases log the envelope verbatim; `api_mutating_starts_daemon_read_does_not` logs the
  unit's `is-active` state (or the foreground child's liveness under `--no-systemd`) before and after each
  call.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-08 (the `events` topic) and P1-11 (`api::Client`, contract 1.2.0 to bump from).
- Consumed by M1a (demo step 5: `events --follow --json` prints `torrent.completed`) and P5-05 (`wait --until
  playable` and the `torrent.playable` event ride `events`).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- DL-41 (`events` is a topic with a `seq` ring; `--since-seq` replays and reports `resync`), DL-62 (`events`
  exits 4 when the daemon is down), DL-55 (`api::ops::TABLE` carries the idempotent flag).
- §2.7 proof: `agent_contract.py` (the successor of `run.sh`).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `events --follow` prints `torrent.completed` within 2 s of a fixture completing.
- [ ] `api torrents.list` returns the A.9 objects and `list --json`'s `torrents` array equals `cli::shapes::torrent()` applied to them (the contract-1.x shape, P1-11).
- [ ] `contract_version` becomes `1.2.1` with `changes[]` entries for `events` and `api`.
- [ ] `api nope` exits 2 with `unknown_op` and a hint listing the nearest operation names (Levenshtein ≤ 2).

# P1-19: Typed operations and the normalized model

Plan item **P1-19** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 3493). Phase P1; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1a**;
topological level 8 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-02 (Engine split (isomorphic)).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P1-05 (API v1 contract: types, IPC.md, fixtures, contract tests), P1-06 (API v1
server), P1-10 (Legacy socket adapter), P1-16 (Lazy restore of completed torrents), P5-06 (Fork: have-bitfield
snapshot accessor), P6-07 (Live per-torrent upload cap without rebuild (fork change)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Today's engine dispatch is a string-route match (`src/engine.rs:586-651`): `torrents/info`,
  `torrents/files`, `torrents/add`, `torrents/start`, `torrents/stop`, `torrents/delete`, `torrents/filePrio`,
  `torrents/setUploadLimit`, `torrents/setShareLimits`, `app/version`, `app/shutdown`, `app/restart`, plus the
  `controls` routes of `src/network_app.rs:78-90`. The route lists are duplicated at `src/engine.rs:549-571`,
  `586-651`, `1233-1246` and `src/network_app.rs:78-90` (RC §10).
- The qBittorrent state strings are built in `src/engine.rs:1396-1440` (`:1418-1448` for the strings) from
  `TorrentStats.state`, `finished`, `is_paused`, `record.paused` and stop-on-complete (`ratio_limit == 0.0`,
  `:90-92`); the ETA sentinel 8640000 at `:1477`; `num_seeds: 0` at `:1480`.
- The ledger is an async `Mutex<Ledger>` (`src/engine.rs:154`); P1-08's event bus thread (a std thread) must
  not lock it.
- After P1-02 the seams exist: `src/engine/ops.rs` (string dispatch) and `src/engine/view.rs` (the
  `torrents/info` builder).

## Goal and user value
API v1 needs typed operations; one table ends the four-place route sync (RC §10). The normalized model of §3.5
replaces the three copies of qBittorrent state strings with one closed `state` enum plus a `reason`, which is
what lets the popup, the dashboard, the TUI and `fbittorrent list` share one state vocabulary
(`contracts/ui/states.json`, DL-32). Every API operation of P1-06 executes through `EngineOp`; the legacy
adapter (P1-10) parses old routes into it; the ledger generation counter is what P1-08's bus waits on (DL-67).
On the critical path.

## Do (exact steps)
1. In `src/engine/ops.rs` add `enum EngineOp` with one variant per route of today's match
   (`src/engine.rs:586-651`: `torrents/info`, `torrents/files`, `torrents/add`, `torrents/start`,
   `torrents/stop`, `torrents/delete`, `torrents/filePrio`, `torrents/setUploadLimit`,
   `torrents/setShareLimits`, `app/version`, `app/shutdown`, `app/restart`, the `controls` routes of
   `src/network_app.rs:78-90`) and `EngineDispatcher::execute(op) -> EngineResult`.
2. The string routes become one parser `EngineOp::parse(route, body)` used by the legacy socket (P1-10).
3. In `src/engine/view.rs` add `TorrentView` with the fields of A.9 `Torrent` that exist today (the "Source
   today" column of A.10) and the normalized `state`/`reason` derivation of §3.5, plus the single qBittorrent
   mapping `TorrentView::to_legacy_json()` for old clients (the strings of `src/engine.rs:1418-1448`).
4. Remove the duplicated route lists (`src/engine.rs:549-571`, `586-651`, `1233-1246`;
   `src/network_app.rs:78-90`).
5. Add `Ledger.generation: AtomicU64`, bumped on every ledger save, paired with a `std::sync::Condvar`, so the
   event bus thread of P1-08 can wait for ledger changes without locking the async `Mutex<Ledger>` from a std
   thread (§3.4.7).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.5 the normalized torrent model (one closed `state` enum, derived from `src/engine.rs:1396-1440` today):

| `state` | Meaning | Derived from |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata` | Magnet resolving | handle without metadata |
| `checking` | Hashing existing data | `Initializing { paused: false }`, or any `Initializing` while the daemon holds the hash in its `rechecking` set (P5-03) |
| `downloading` | Live, incomplete, receiving | `Live`, not finished, rate > 0 |
| `stalled` | Live, incomplete, nothing received | `Live`, not finished, rate = 0 |
| `queued` | Wants to run; held by the queue limit | handle paused, record not paused, not finished, no error |
| `paused` | Paused by the user (durable) | `record.paused` |
| `done` | Complete; stopped because seeding is off | finished and stop-on-complete (`ratio_limit == 0.0`) |
| `seeding` | Complete; seeding allowed; live | finished, not stop-on-complete, `Live` |
| `waiting_vpn` | Engine parked | parked slot |
| `error` | Engine error; `error` has the message | `Error` |

- Companions: `reason` (open enum: `user`, `queue_full`, `complete_no_seed`, `vpn_down`, `restore_failed`,
  `metadata_timeout`, `missing_files`, `disk_full`) explains why a torrent is not running (Fragments shows a
  stop reason, `connection_manager.rs:50-55`); `checked: false` marks a completed torrent restored without
  hashing (P1-16). Every combination of rqbit state and record flags maps to exactly one `state`.
- A.10 field provenance for `Torrent`: `hash`, `name`, `save_path`, `added_at`, `completed_at`, `intent`,
  `upload_limit_bps` from `Record` (`hash, name, source, output_folder, only_files, upload_limit, ratio_limit,
  category, tags, added_on, completion_on, paused`); `state`, `reason` per §3.5; `progress`, `size`,
  `completed_bytes` from `stats.progress_bytes / total_bytes` (`:1397-1404`); `dl_bps`, `ul_bps`, `peers` from
  `stats.live` (`:1405-1415`); `eta_s` = `(total − progress) / dl_bps` when `dl_bps > 0` (`:1474-1478`, minus
  the sentinel); `ratio` = `uploaded / progress_bytes` when `progress_bytes > 0` (`:1482-1486`); `seed`,
  `upload_policy`: `upload_limit == 0 && ratio_limit == -2` → `unlimited`; `== 32768 && 0.0` → `default_cap`;
  else `custom` (`src/qbt.rs:504-520`); `content_path` from `qbt::open_target` (`src/qbt.rs:706`); `seeds`
  P5-01; `checked` P1-16; `playable` P5-05; `queue_pos` P6-05; `origin`, `force` new.
- A.9 `Torrent` fields: `hash`, `name` (≤ 1,024 in lists), `state`, `reason?`, `error?`, `intent:
  enum(run|pause)`, `staged: bool`, `checked: bool`, `progress?`, `size?`, `completed_bytes?`,
  `uploaded_bytes?`, `dl_bps?`, `ul_bps?`, `eta_s?`, `peers?`, `seeds?`, `seed: bool`, `upload_policy:
  enum(default_cap|unlimited|custom)`, `upload_limit_bps?`, `ratio?`, `save_path`, `content_path?`,
  `added_at`, `completed_at?`, `origin?`, `imdb_id?`, `queue_pos?`, `force: bool`, `playable?`.
- §3.4.7 (why the generation counter): "Immediately" is event-driven; the bus waits on each live torrent's
  `state_changed()` and on the ledger's change counter, never by locking the async `Mutex<Ledger>` from a std
  thread (DL-67).

## Acceptance criteria
- Each route name appears once in the code.
- Old clients behave identically (`native.py`, all TUI tests).
- Every combination of rqbit state and record flags maps to exactly one `state`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `view::tests::state_mapping_table`: table-driven over every `TorrentStatsState` × `paused` × `finished` ×
  `stop_on_complete` × `record.paused` combination, logging the row that fails.
- `ops::tests::every_route_named_once`: greps the route parser table against the legacy socket's list.
- `ledger::tests::generation_bumps_on_save`: one save, one bump, one `Condvar` wake.
- `native.py`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-02 (the seams `ops.rs` and `view.rs`).
- Consumed by P1-05 (the serde types mirror `TorrentView`), P1-06 (every operation executes through
  `EngineOp`), P1-10 (the legacy parser targets `EngineOp`), P1-16 (dormant records are a `TorrentView`
  state), P5-06 and P6-07 (fork accessors are wired through the typed engine layer).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R4 (UI drift): one state vocabulary is the structural fix.
- DL-32 (one state table feeds popup, dashboard, TUI and CLI), DL-47 (P1-19 adds typed ops and the model after
  the split), DL-56 (P1-03 depends on P1-02 and not on P1-19), DL-67 (the bus waits on `Ledger.generation`
  plus a `Condvar`, never on the async mutex).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
