- [ ] Each route name appears once in the code.
- [ ] Old clients behave identically (`native.py`, all TUI tests).
- [ ] Every combination of rqbit state and record flags maps to exactly one `state`.

title: P2-01: Plugin restructure and the shared API client
description:
# P2-01: Plugin restructure and the shared API client

Plan item **P2-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4097). Phase P2; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1**;
topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas), P1-09 (Mutations: refs,
pending, confirmed).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P2-02 (Store reducer and fixture tests), P2-08 (Design tokens, visual capture
harness and contrast test), P3-08 (Dashboard window shell), P4-09 (Remove legacy qBittorrent mode and the
compat paths).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D13: the widget polls once per monitor. Each bar widget instance creates its own `Service` and its own
  processes (`Panel.qml:119-122`), so polling multiplies by the number of monitors (FO §1.4).
  `Service.qml:80-118` spawns `status --json` every 2 to 10 s (`manifest.json:18-19`: `refreshIntervalSec`,
  `idleRefreshIntervalSec`).
- The plugin's `IpcHandler` target `oliver.torrents` (`Panel.qml:124-139`) has
  `open/close/toggle/refresh/addClipboard/tui` and the `cursor()` test hook (`:134-138`).
- Quickshell facts (each learned by Sprout or omaqbt): `Socket.write()` adds no newline and buffers
  (`quickshell-src/src/io/socket.hpp:37-43`); an initial `connected: true` does not fire
  `connectionStateChanged`; there is no automatic reconnect; `SplitParser` buffers until the delimiter with no
  cap of its own (`datastream.cpp:37-41,91-98`); `Quickshell.clipboardText` is empty unless a Quickshell
  window has focus; `ScriptModel` keyed by `objectProp` does not emit row updates in 0.3.2; a `Process`
  destructor SIGKILLs its child on reload. The `service`/`serviceFor` facade is
  `services/PluginShellApi.qml:30-32`; entry points load from `entryPoints.service` (`shell.qml:931`) and
  `entryPoints.barWidget` (`:1453`).
- Omarchy's plugin watcher is `inotifywait -m -r` (`services/PluginRegistry.qml:716-727`); whether it follows
  a symlinked plugin folder is unverified (§10.4).

## Goal and user value
One connection per shell (W3: "the shell spawns no processes for status"); the `service` singleton holds the
one `ApiClient`, the `Store` and every action, so the bar widgets (per monitor) and the dashboard (P3-08) read
one state. The §4.4 socket rules are the hard-won list that keeps a pre-1.0 Quickshell plugin from stalling
the desktop shell (R2, R3). Start of the plugin lane (P2-01 → P2-02 → P2-03 → P2-05), which can begin against
P1-06's server before P1-08's bus exists (a first cut may poll `torrents.list` over `api.sock` for a day).

## Do (exact steps)
1. **The tree and manifest** of §4.1 minus the `panel` kind (`kinds: ["service", "bar-widget"]`, `entryPoints:
   {service: "Service.qml", barWidget: "BarWidget.qml"}`; the `panel` kind arrives with P3-08, so no
   half-built window is exposed): `Service.qml`, `ApiClient.js`, `Store.js` (P2-02 fills it), `Model.js`,
   `Glyphs.js`, `BarWidget.qml`; `components/`, `views/` later. Manifest: `schemaVersion 1`, `id
   "oliver.torrents"`, `name "Torrents"`, `version "0.2.0"`, `license "MIT"`, `barWidget: {displayName
   "Torrents", category "Network", allowMultiple false, defaultSection "right", defaults: {binary:
   "fbittorrent", showWhenStopped: false, showRates: false, middleClick: "dashboard", tuiCommand:
   "omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui --app-id=org.omarchy.fbittorrent fbittorrent tui"}, schema: [one entry per
   default]}`. Remove `refreshIntervalSec`/`idleRefreshIntervalSec`: nothing polls any more.
2. **`ApiClient.js`** (`.pragma library`) implements §4.4 rules 1 to 11 exactly: (1) `Socket { path:
   Quickshell.env("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR") + "/fbittorrent/api.sock" }`, overridable by the `useRuntimeDir` hook;
   (2) `write(JSON.stringify(frame) + "\n")` then `flush()`; (3) the bootstrap hello when `connected` is
   already true as well as from the signal handler; (4) the reconnect `Timer` with backoff 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 s
   then every 10 s, independent of socket signals; (5) `SplitParser` on `\n` with a 1 MiB line guard (a longer
   line is a protocol violation and resets the session) and `JSON.parse` in `try`; (6) increasing `id`s and a
   pending map with 20 s (100 s for `torrents.add`) timeouts, always longer than the server's 15 s/95 s so an
   answer can never arrive after the client gave up; a timeout marks that action "no answer"; after a
   reconnect, pending idempotent mutations (A.1) are resent with the same `ref`, nothing else; (7) 45 s
   without any frame (heartbeats every 15 s) resets the session; (8) `hello {proto: 1, client: {name:
   "oliver.torrents", version: <manifest version>, kind: "bar"}, interactive: false}`; `app.client
   {interactive: true|false}` on dashboard visibility and `app.client {glance: true|false}` on popup
   open/close; (9) subscriptions follow visibility: `summary` at 5,000 ms when nothing is open; `summary` and
   `torrents` at 1,000 ms while the popup is open or the dashboard is visible; detail topics only for the
   torrent on screen; resubscribe after every reconnect; (10) when the socket cannot connect, `online = false`
   and the backoff caps at 10 s; `reconnecting` is true from an EOF without `bye` until the backoff first
   reaches that cap (about 15 s), false on the next `hello` or on a `bye`; the service never starts the daemon
   on its own; (11) revision checks: a gap resubscribes that topic; a new `instance` resubscribes all.
3. **`Service.qml`** is the `service` singleton holding the one `ApiClient`, the `Store` and the action
   functions of §4.4: `pause`, `resume`, `toggleSeed`, `remove(hash, deleteFiles)`, `addFromClipboard`,
   `add(source, stage)`, `commitStaged`, `discardStaged`, `openTarget`, `setTurtle`, `recheck`, `quit`,
   `startDaemon`, `dismissClipboard`; every mutation gets `ref = "qs-" + startMillis + "-" + n`; `startDaemon`
   runs `["fbittorrent", "up"]` once through `Util.execArgv`
   (`/usr/share/omarchy/shell/Commons/Util.qml:77-79`) and is the only way the plugin ever starts the daemon
   (the dashboard's [Start], the popup's Enter on "not running", a click on the dimmed icon under
   `showWhenStopped`), never without a person's action, a one-shot, not a poller. Clipboard: read with a
   short-lived `wl-paste --no-newline` process; accept a magnet, an http(s) URL or a `.torrent` path; check
   the btih against the store first ("Already in your list: <name>"). Opening files: `torrents.open_target`
   returns a path; run `xdg-open <path>` with `Util.execArgv`. The service exposes `popupOpen: bool` (drives
   the `torrents` subscription and `app.client {glance}`) and `dashboardVisible: bool` (rule 8).
4. **`BarWidget.qml`** reads the service (today's `Panel.qml` icon and popup logic moved over unchanged until
   P2-03 and P2-04 rewrite them).
5. **Test hooks** (§4.17) on the one `IpcHandler` with target `oliver.torrents` in `BarWidget.qml` (Quickshell
   allows one handler per target), calling into the service: `state()` returns `{online, instance, subs:
   {<topic>: <last rev>}, pending: [<ref>], view: null}` as JSON (unguarded, like `cursor()`);
   `useRuntimeDir(path)` repoints the socket to `<path>/fbittorrent/api.sock` until `useRuntimeDir("")`,
   refused unless `FBT_TEST_HOOKS=1` is in the shell's environment.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.4 "The Store" (P2-02 implements): `Store.js` reduces frames into plain objects keyed by hash;
  `Service.qml` mirrors them into `ListModel`s with `setProperty` for changed fields and insert/remove only on
  membership changes; sorting runs on membership change, on a sort-key change, and at most once per second for
  rate sorts (DL-21).
- §4.15: all state lives in the daemon; the service reconnects within a second after a hot reload and
  resubscribes; only short-lived processes (`wl-paste`, `xdg-open`, `hyprctl`, `fbittorrent up`); no
  long-lived child.
- §3.4.8: the plugin keeps the fixed `client.name = "oliver.torrents"` because one shell process reconnects
  under the same name and must be able to resend a pending ref.
- §3.2.11: the reconnect ladder 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 s then every 10 s is the same in QML and Rust clients; the 10
  s cap is the old widget's idle poll, so the bar is never staler than today.
- §4.14: the palette singleton is imported as `qs.Commons as Commons` and referenced as `Commons.Color` (Qt
  6.12's `QtQuick.Color` shadows the bare name).

## Acceptance criteria
- The daemon counts exactly one `bar` connection with two monitors (a second, headless monitor can be added
  with `hyprctl output create headless` if only one exists; unverified on this Hyprland version, the test
  skips with a logged reason if the command fails).
- After a plugin reload the service reconnects and resubscribes within 1 s of the shell being back.
- `state()` reports the subscription and last `rev`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::bar_single_connection` reads `app.info`'s `clients.bar` count (A.4, P1-06) while the live shell
  is connected to a fixture daemon through `useRuntimeDir` (opt-in, `FBT_TEST_QS=1`).
- `qs-dashboard.sh::reload_reconnects` (live shell, opt-in; the harness arrives with P3-08, so this case is
  added then): touches `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/oliver.torrents/Service.qml` through the symlink, first
  asserts that the shell reloaded and logs "symlink reload: yes/no" (if no, `setup --plugin=copy` becomes the
  documented development default and §4.15 is corrected), then asserts `state().subs` lists `summary` again
  within 1 s of the reload with `instance` unchanged, logging the reconnect time.
- Added in polish round 1: `plugin/tests/qs-client.sh` runs `ApiClient.js` against a scripted fake socket
  object in a headless `qs` (no daemon): the backoff ladder is exactly 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 10 s; the pending
  map times out at 20 s (100 s for `torrents.add`) and marks the action "no answer"; after a reconnect only
  idempotent pending mutations (A.1) are resent with the same `ref`; 45 s of silence resets the session; a 1
  MiB + 1 byte line resets the session; `write()` is always followed by `flush()`; each assertion is an
  `FBTQS-STEP` line through `qs-log.py`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-08 (the subscriptions the client makes) and P1-09 (`ref` generation and the resend rule).
- Consumed by P2-02 (the Store), P2-08 (`useRuntimeDir` wiring and `Model.js`), P3-08 (the dashboard reads the
  same service), P4-09 (removal of legacy paths touches the plugin).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R2 (Quickshell/Omarchy/Qt changes break the plugin), R3 (a plugin bug stalls the shell): the §4.4 rules and
  the no-long-lived-children rule are the mitigations.
- DL-13 (hidden while stopped; `showWhenStopped` off), DL-21 (client-side sorting with a measured threshold),
  DL-36, DL-67 (`reconnecting` keeps the bar icon through a crash-restart).
- §10.4 unverified: symlinked-folder hot reload (verified by `reload_reconnects`); `hyprctl output create
  headless` (skips with a logged reason).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is

  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in

  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.

  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:

  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by

  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;

  with new names.

  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent

  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed

  value.

# P2-02: Store reducer and fixture tests

Plan item **P2-02** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4146). Phase P2; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1**;
topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-05 (API v1 contract: types, IPC.md, fixtures, contract tests), P2-01 (Plugin
restructure and the shared API client).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P2-04 (Bar icon states), P2-06 (Isolated Quickshell smoke
test), P3-09 (Torrents view).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Today's `Model.js` formats a polled `status --json` snapshot (`Model.js:102-115`); there is no reducer, no
  revision tracking and no fixture test for QML code. `qs -p <dir>` loads `<dir>/shell.qml` (Quickshell 0.3.2)
  and can run headless scripts that print to stderr with a `DEBUG qml:` prefix.
- After P1-05 the `contracts/ipc/v1/*.ndjson` fixtures exist with `c2s`, `s2c`, `expect` and `volatile` lines;
  after P0-15 `plugin/tests/qs-log.py` converts `FBTQS-*` markers to JSONL.
- The §4.6 sort keys: Added (newest first, today's order; the default), Name, Progress, ↓, Size, State, ETA;
  `S` reverses.

## Goal and user value
Correctness of the most delicate QML code, tested without a shell: the reducer that turns snapshots and deltas
into the rows every monitor's popup and the dashboard show. The same fixtures test the Rust server
(P1-05/P1-06) and later the TUI's `store.rs` (P4-03), which is how the two UIs cannot drift (R4, principle 6).
The 2 ms sort budget is the measured threshold of DL-21.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`Store.js`** (`.pragma library`): `apply(frame)` reduces `snapshot.begin`, `snapshot.chunk`,
   `snapshot.end`, `delta` (`changed` with `null` meaning delete the field, `added`, `removed`) and `state`
   frames (A.8) into plain objects keyed by hash (`torrents`), per-topic state objects (`summary`, `network`,
   `settings`) and per-topic `rev`; `counts` recomputed on membership or state change; `filter(state | "all")`
   and `sort(key, reverse)` over the keys of §4.6 (Added, Name, Progress, ↓, Size, State, ETA) on typed
   values; a gap (`rev != last + 1`) raises `resubscribe(topic)`.
2. **`Service.qml`** mirrors the store into `ListModel`s with `setProperty` for changed fields and
   insert/remove only on membership change (§4.4 "The Store"); sorting runs on membership change, on a
   sort-key change, and at most once per second for rate sorts. `ScriptModel` keyed by `objectProp` is not
   used (it does not emit row updates in 0.3.2).
3. **The fixture runner** `plugin/tests/store/shell.qml` (run as `qs -p plugin/tests/store`) loads `Store.js`
   and every `contracts/ipc/v1/*.ndjson`, applies each `s2c` frame, compares with each `expect` model (deep
   equality after sorting keys), prints one `FBTQS-STEP {json}` line per frame and `FBTQS-PASS <file>` /
   `FBTQS-FAIL <file> <diff>`.
4. **`plugin/tests/qs-store.sh`** wraps it in `plugin/tests/qs-log.py` (P0-15) and adds a timing line for
   sorting 500 synthetic rows.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.4.7 atomicity: all chunks of one snapshot come from one consistent state; no `delta` or `state` frame
  arrives between `snapshot.begin` and `snapshot.end`; changes meanwhile arrive as the first `delta` after
  `end`; `Store.js` may therefore apply chunks as they arrive and treat `snapshot.end` as "consistent now".
  Keyed snapshots arrive in natural order (torrents: `added_at` descending).
- §3.4.7 revisions: `rev` increases by exactly one per frame per subscription; a gap means a frame was lost;
  the client unsubscribes then subscribes for that topic and rebuilds from the new snapshot;
  `subscribe-gap.ndjson` exercises it.
- A.1: full objects never contain `null`; in a `delta`, a field set to `null` means "now absent" and the
  client deletes it.
- A.8 frames: `snapshot.begin {sub, topic, rev, count, reason}`, `snapshot.chunk {sub, topic, rev, items}`,
  `snapshot.end {sub, topic, rev}`, `delta {sub, topic, rev, changed, added, removed}` (each may be absent
  when empty), `state {sub, topic, rev, data}`.
- §4.16 Store fixtures: `qs -p plugin/tests/store` loads `Store.js` and the `contracts/ipc/v1` files, applies
  every `s2c` frame, compares with each `expect` model, prints one `FBTQS-STEP {json}` line per frame and
  `FBTQS-PASS <name>` or `FBTQS-FAIL <name> <diff>` and exits.
- §4.15 UI-thread rule: no JavaScript loop over all torrents per delta (loops live in `Store.js` only, P3-09's
  lint); `ListView` with `reuseItems`.
- §4.3.2: the list is a `ListView` over a `ListModel` patched in place (set/insert/remove/move), `reuseItems:
  true`, `currentIndex: -1`, the cursor painted by the delegate from a hash, so a status tick never resets
  scroll (omaqbt `TorrentTable.qml:9-15,166-179`).
- Appendix E.2: `plugin/tests/qs-store.sh` covers Store fixtures; needs `qs`; opt-in `FBT_TEST_QS=1`; added by
  P2-02.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every `expect` in the fixtures passes (including `subscribe-gap.ndjson`).
- Sorting 500 rows takes under 2 ms (otherwise move sorting server-side into the subscription arguments and
  log the decision in the receipt, DL-21).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-store.sh` (`FBT_TEST_QS=1`): one `FBTQS-PASS/FAIL` per fixture group plus a timing line for the sort;
  the JSONL conversion of §9.1 through `qs-log.py`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-05 (the fixtures) and P2-01 (`Service.qml` and the plugin tree the store lives in).
- Consumed by P2-03 (popup rows come from the store), P2-04 (icon state from `summary`), P2-06 (the smoke
  drives the store), P3-09 (the table's `ListModel` mirror).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R3 (shell stalls): the store is where per-delta work happens; keeping it O(changed fields) and sorting at
  most once per second is the budget.
- R4 (UI drift): same fixtures for QML and Rust.
- DL-21 (sorting in QML for now, measured threshold 2 ms at 500 rows), DL-60 (plugin tests live in
  `plugin/tests/`).

title: P2-03: Popup rewrite
description:
# P2-03: Popup rewrite

Plan item **P2-03** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4169). Phase P2; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds:
**M1**; topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-12 (Stop rule and idle exit), P2-02 (Store reducer and fixture tests), P2-08
(Design tokens, visual capture harness and contrast test).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P2-05 (Theme-token lint and light/dark check), M1 (First demo (v0.2.0)), P5-04
(Global and alternative speed limits (turtle)), P5-05 (Ready to watch), P5-07 (Low disk space warning and
`disk_full`), P6-13 (Clipboard magnet watch (opt-in, A7)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Today's popup (`plugin/oliver.torrents/Panel.qml`) is built from the right components (`Panel`,
  `KeyboardPanel`, `PanelHero`, `PanelActionButton`, `CursorSurface`, `PanelToolTip`:
  `Panel.qml:10,155,202,302,332`) with a two-line row and a thin progress rule (`Panel.qml:332-460`), but it
  is fed by polling up to 10 s stale, shows "0s" seed counts, removes on one click, dims with `Qt.darker(fg,
  1.55)` (`Panel.qml:18`) where the shell uses 1.4 (`Ui/PanelHero.qml:23`), animates a literal 400 ms
  (`Panel.qml:410`) ignoring `Style.reduceMotion` (`Commons/Style.qml:363-367`), is 400 px wide
  (`Panel.qml:162`; every first-party popup is `Style.space(380)`), treats `q` and `Q` alike and stops the
  daemon (`Panel.qml:179`), and its Space-to-pause mapping (`Panel.qml:180`) silently fails because
  `PanelKeyCatcher` consumes Space first. Enter opens the file (`Panel.qml:72-76`).
- The `IpcHandler` (`Panel.qml:124-139`) has `open/close/toggle/refresh/addClipboard/tui` and `cursor()`.
- Shell components and tokens the rewrite uses are listed under "Canonical rules" below; all exist in
  `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/` (`omarchy-dev 4.0.0.r7025`).

## Goal and user value
W3 and the owner's look-and-feel ask (§0.2 "Look": popup built only from shell tokens and components, captured
side by side with the Wi-Fi panel and judged by the owner). This is the first demo (M1): rows pushed over one
socket, no process spawned per tick, the add preview, the confirm strip and the power button that stops
everything (A1). End of the plugin lane's critical branch (P2-01 → P2-02 → P2-03 → P2-05).

## Do (exact steps)
`BarWidget.qml`'s `KeyboardPanel` popup per §4.5:
1. **Geometry**: `Style.space(380)` wide, height fitted up to `Style.space(560)`, `Style.spacing.popupPadding`
   (14) on all sides, sections separated by `PanelSeparator` and `Style.spacing.xxl` (12) of vertical rhythm;
   content passed as `content: PanelKeyCatcher { … }` so it is built on first open (`shell-dev.md` "Plugin
   contract").
2. **Hero** (`PanelHero`): title "Torrents" (`Style.font.title`, bold), the rates meta in uppercase caption
   ("↓ 4.2 MB/S  ↑ 32 KB/S", `Style.font.caption`, bold, letterSpacing 1.2, dim), the "2 DOWNLOADING" detail
   pill, trailing controls add `󰐕` · window `▢` · turtle `󰢃` (P5-04) · quit `󰐥`.
3. **Banner** component for §4.11 banners (urgent text on `Util.alpha(urgent, 0.10)` fill with a 0.35 border;
   VPN and disk), only when relevant.
4. **Sections**: `PanelSectionHeader` per group ("DOWNLOADING", caption bold dim); `components/PopupRow.qml`
   per §4.3.1 (below); collapsed groups "QUEUED 1 · PAUSED 1 · DONE 8 ›" expanding in place to at most 10 rows
   each; `w` opens the dashboard on that filter.
5. **KeyHint** caption row ("a add · / search · w window · t terminal · z turtle"; keys in foreground, labels
   dim; rendered like `PanelSectionHeader` without uppercase), **hidden until the first key press of this
   opening**, so the popup at rest has the Wi-Fi panel's structure (hero, separator, section headers, rows)
   (Q32, DL-69).
6. **The inline confirm strip** of §4.9 in the row: "Remove '<name>'? Files are kept." [Cancel] [Remove],
   Cancel focused, `y` or a click on Remove confirms; the popup never offers "delete files" (DL-11).
7. **The quick-add offer strip** of §4.8 on `a` or right click: "Add '<name>'? [Add] [Cancel]" with Add
   focused and the magnet's `dn=` name (or the `.torrent` file name, or the URL's last path segment); Enter
   adds, Esc cancels; a duplicate shows "Already in your list: <name>"; an empty or unrecognised clipboard
   shows "Clipboard has no torrent" for 3 s. One component shared with P6-13.
8. **Pending rendering** per §4.10: the verb in progress ("pausing…", "removing…") in dimmed italics with a
   spinner glyph at 8 fps, static "…" under `Style.reduceMotion`; the row keeps its last confirmed values;
   nothing is drawn optimistically; a timeout says "Result unknown; the list will tell" and offers "Refresh"
   (resubscribe, the `󰑐` glyph's only remaining use).
9. **The §4.11 popup states**: not running → "fbittorrent is not running" with "Enter Start · w Open window";
   Starting… ("Starting… checking 2 torrents"); Connecting… (first 2 s); Reconnecting… (retry in N s) with
   last-known rows dimmed; protocol mismatch (urgent banner "This plugin speaks API 1; the running fbittorrent
   speaks API 2. Update the plugin or run `fbittorrent restart`."); version skew (dim banner "fbittorrent
   0.2.0 runs; 0.2.1 is installed. Restart to update."); parked (urgent banner "Waiting for ProtonVPN
   (proton0). Downloads resume when it connects."; rows dimmed, progress absent); engine failed (banner with
   the message and "Show log"); no torrents ("Nothing here yet. Copy a magnet link and press a, or press / to
   search."); result unknown; upgrade pending (dim "Update installed; restarts when idle"); idle countdown as
   a dim line under the hero ("Idle · stops in 4 min"); stopped recently ("fbittorrent stopped. Enter Start ·
   w Open window"). Empty and degraded messages are never children of a `ListView` whose height collapses to
   0; they sit in a fixed overlay area with a minimum height only when the count is zero (Sprout's
   longest-lived bug).
10. **Motion** through `Style.duration` only (§4.13): progress rule width `NumberAnimation` `Easing.OutCubic`
    `Style.duration(400)`; banner opacity `Style.duration(140)`; cursor and hover fills instant; no row
    insert/remove transitions.
11. **Keys** per Appendix B's Popup column: `j`/`k`/↑/↓ move; Enter opens the file (exception 1); `o` open;
    `p` and Space pause/resume (told apart from Enter with `returnRequested`, §4.12); `u` seed; `d`/`x`/Delete
    → confirm strip; `a`/right click → offer strip; `/` → dashboard on Search; `w` → dashboard (exception 2);
    `t` → TUI; `z` turtle; `q` closes the popup; Esc closes. `Q` and the hero's power icon `󰐥` are the owner's
    off switch (A1): with nothing active `app.shutdown {reason: "user"}` at once; with transfers active the
    inline strip under the hero "Stop fbittorrent? N downloads pause until it starts again." [Cancel] [Stop],
    Cancel focused, `y` or Enter on Stop confirms, Esc cancels. The daemon drains, the icon turns dim for the
    10 s "stopped recently" state and leaves the bar.
12. The service sends `app.client {glance: true}` on open and `false` on close (pauses the idle countdown,
    §3.2.10). The `IpcHandler` keeps `open/close/toggle/refresh/addClipboard/tui` and `cursor()`. **No `Timer`
    or `Process` outside `Service.qml`.**

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.3.1 popup row: glyph column `Style.space(26)`; name in `Style.font.body`, `ElideMiddle`, full text in a
  `PanelToolTip` on hover (today's `FullTextTip`, `Panel.qml:311-330`), never scrolls; progress rule 3 px,
  radius ½, shown while `progress < 1 || state is live`, fill `foreground` for live states and dim otherwise,
  track `Util.alpha(foreground, 0.12)` (one of the two permitted local constants); meta line
  (`Style.font.caption`, dim) built from present fields only in this order: state word · percent · ↓ rate ·
  ETA · peers (and "seeds" after P5-01) · "Ready to watch · 4 min buffered" accent badge with [Open] (P5-05;
  "may stall · finishes in 18 min" when `stall_free` is false); absent fields omitted ("Fetching metadata ·
  0:12" shows elapsed time); row actions (pause `p`, open `o`, remove `d`) appear on hover or cursor only, the
  row keeps its height (DL-24; Sprout `Panel.qml:1072-1104`); row states: cursor (hover-cursor fill), pending
  (name at 0.55 opacity, meta shows the verb), error (`!` glyph in urgent, meta shows the message, no colour
  on the name), done (dim name, no rule), ready to watch (meta badge in accent); height = content +
  `Style.spacing.rowPaddingX` (12); gaps `Style.spacing.lg` (8).
- §4.2.1 tokens: `Style.space(px)`; `Style.spacing.{xxs 2, xs 3, sm 4, md 6, lg 8, xl 10, xxl 12, xxxl 14,
  huge 18}`; `controlGap 8, controlPaddingX 10, controlPaddingY 6, controlHeight 28, popupRowHeight 28`;
  `rowGap 8, rowPaddingX 12, labelGap 4`; `panelGap 14, panelPadding 18, popupPadding 14`;
  `Style.font.{caption 10, bodySmall 11, body 12, subtitle 13, title 14, heading 16, display 24, displayLarge
  28}`, `iconSmall 11, icon 14, iconLarge 18`; `Style.font.family` (monospace → JetBrainsMono Nerd Font);
  `Color.{foreground, background, accent, urgent, muted}`; `Color.popups.{background,text,border}`,
  `Color.tooltip.*`; `bar.foreground`, `bar.urgent`, `bar.foregroundAnimationEnabled`; fills
  `Style.{normalFill .04, hoverFill .08, selectedFill .18, pressedFill .22, selectionFill .35,
  selectedAccentFill .18}`; `Border.controlSpec(state, fg, accent)`,
  `Border.surfaceSpec("popups","border",…)`; `Style.cornerRadius`; `Style.reduceMotion`, `Style.duration(ms)`.
  **No literal colour, size or duration anywhere** (P2-05 lints). Dim text = `Model.dim(fg, bg)` (P2-08's
  ladder). Accent text only when `accent` ≥ 4.5:1 against `background`, else bold foreground.
- §4.2.3 number formats (from `Model.js`, P2-08): sizes "1.4 GiB" in sentences and "1.4G" in cells, never
  "GB"; rates "4.2 MB/s"; ETA "12 min", "1 h 05", "2 d", never seconds above a minute, never "∞" (absent →
  "—"); percent integers below 99.5 and "99.9" above.
- §4.3.4 state words and glyphs (`Model.js` from `contracts/ui/states.json`): metadata `◌`/dots-horizontal
  "Metadata"; checking sync "Checking"; downloading `󰇚` "Downloading"; stalled timer-sand "Stalled"; queued
  clock-outline "Queued"; paused `󰏤` "Paused"; done `󰄬` "Done"; seeding `󰕒` "Seeding"; waiting_vpn `󰦝`
  "Waiting for VPN"; error `󰀦` "Error"; every glyph is followed by its word.
- §4.12 keyboard model: `PanelKeyCatcher` (`Ui/PanelKeyCatcher.qml:36-99`) turns keys into signals
  (`j`/`k`/`h`/`l`, arrows, Enter/Space activate, `x`/`X`/Delete → one `deleteRequested()`, Esc closes, Tab →
  `tabRequested(±1)`, other characters → `textKey(text, modifiers)`); it emits `returnRequested` then
  `activateRequested` for Enter and only `activateRequested` for Space (`:86-92`), so the popup sets a flag in
  `onReturnRequested` and treats an `activateRequested` without it as Space.
- §4.5 popup mockup (keyboard mode): hero row `󰇚 Torrents … 󰐕 ▢ 󰢃 󰐥`; meta `↓ 4.2 MB/s ↑ 32 KB/s … 2
  DOWNLOADING`; separator; optional banner; `DOWNLOADING` header; rows; `QUEUED 1 · PAUSED 1 · DONE 8 ›`;
  separator; KeyHint row.
- Appendix B two exceptions (popup only): Enter opens the file; `w` opens the dashboard. `q` is not an
  exception: it closes the surface it is pressed in, everywhere (DL-54).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every popup state of §4.11 and every row state of §4.3.1 is reached against the fixture daemon (`daemon.py
  --serve-fixture <state>`) and captured in dark and light (P2-08).
- The updated `widget_keys.sh` passes; the lint of P2-05 passes; no `Timer` or `Process` exists outside
  `Service.qml`.
- `q` closes the popup and leaves the daemon running.
- The power icon (and `Q`) with an active download shows the strip with Cancel focused, Enter cancels, and
  Stop drains the daemon: `fbittorrent status --json` reports `running: false` and the icon leaves the bar
  within 10 s (the stopped-recently dim).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `regression_tests/widget_keys.sh::W-001…W-016` (cursor moves, actions, confirm strip Cancel-first, `z`, `w`,
  Esc layers; W-013 presses `a` with a magnet on the fake clipboard and asserts nothing is added until Enter
  and that the strip names the `dn=`; W-014 presses Space on a row and asserts a `pause` mutation, not an
  open; W-015 presses `q` and asserts the popup closed and `fbittorrent status --quiet` still exits 0; W-016
  clicks the power icon with a download active, asserts the strip with Cancel focused, presses Enter and
  asserts nothing stopped, then presses `y` and asserts `status --json` → `running: false` and the icon gone
  within 10 s), each logging `cursor()` and `state()`.
- `qs-visual.sh popup <state>` captures for every §4.11 popup row; the lints.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P2-02 (rows come from the store), P1-12 (the glance pause, the countdown line, `app.shutdown
  {reason: "user"}`), P2-08 (`Model.js` formatting, `Model.dim`, `Glyphs.js`, the visual harness).
- Consumed by P2-05 (lint and light/dark check), M1 (the first demo), P5-04 (turtle button), P5-05 (ready
  badge), P5-07 (disk banner), P6-13 (clipboard strip).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q32 (open, default hidden at rest): the key-hint row. Q19 (open, default strip then Enter): quick add. Q21
  (open, default `q` closes, `Q` quits). Q18 (open, default pauses): Space. Q23 (open, default the judged
  pair): the look-and-feel gate.

## Risks and decisions
- R2, R3 (Quickshell fragility; shell stalls): components and tokens only; no timers or processes outside the
  service.
- DL-11, DL-12 (middle click → dashboard), DL-24 (hover-only row actions), DL-33/DL-54 (`q`/`Q`; Space
  pauses), DL-35 (the offer strip before adding), DL-36 (glance pause; 10 s stopped-recently), DL-38 (380 px;
  one caption line of hints), DL-69 (hints hidden at rest), DL-70 (the power button).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least

description:
# P2-04: Bar icon states

Plan item **P2-04** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4217). Phase P2; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M1**; topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P2-02 (Store reducer and fixture tests), P2-08 (Design tokens, visual capture
harness and contrast test).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P2-05 (Theme-token lint and light/dark check), P5-05 (Ready to watch), P5-07 (Low
disk space warning and `disk_full`).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Today's icon: `󰇚` while downloading and `󰕒` when idle (`Panel.qml:145,214`, `Model.js:62,65`); left click
  toggles the popup, right click adds at once (`Panel.qml:149`), middle opens the TUI (`Panel.qml:150`). The
  widget is visible only while the app runs (the owner's rule). Glyphs are scattered across `Panel.qml` and
  `Model.js` (`paused 󰏤 Model.js:61, Panel.qml:433`; `done 󰄬 Model.js:61`; `error 󰀦 Model.js:64`; `add 󰐕
  Panel.qml:223`; `terminal 󰆍 :224`; `refresh 󰑐 :225`; `power 󰐥 :226`; `play 󰐊 :433`; `folder 󰝰 :442`; `trash
  󰆴 :451`, hover colour urgent `:454`).
- `󰕒` is `nf-md-upload` and reads as "uploading", the one thing seeding-off-by-default guarantees is not
  happening; the owner's menu uses `󰦝` for Proton (`omarchy-menu.jsonc:38`).
- Sprout gates its colour animation on `bar.foregroundAnimationEnabled` (`Sprout BarWidget.qml:306-320`).

## Goal and user value
W3: ambient state without opening anything; §2.7 "Truthful bar": icon state at a glance, pushed. A8: the
monochrome theme is the design constraint, so state is carried by glyph and weight, never by hue alone; the
tooltip always carries the words. A1/DL-13: the icon is visible exactly while the daemon runs, so a lit icon
means a running process, with the 10 s "stopped recently" dim so the exit is visible rather than a vanish
under the cursor (DL-36).

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`BarWidget.qml`'s `BarIconButton`** per the §4.5 icon table:

| State | Glyph | Colour | Tooltip | Rate text (`showRates`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daemon not running | hidden by default; with `showWhenStopped`, `󰇚` | dim (`Qt.darker(barForeground, 1.4)`) | "fbittorrent is not running · click to start" | none |
| Running, nothing active | `󰇚` (the brand mark; state by weight, not shape) | dim | "Idle · 8 done", or "Idle · stops in 4 min" | none |
| Seeding only | `󰕒` | `barForeground` | "↑ 120 KB/s · 1 seeding" | "120K" |
| Stopped recently (10 s after `bye`) | `󰇚` | dim | "fbittorrent stopped (idle)" or "fbittorrent stopped" after the power button (from `bye.reason`) | none |
| Downloading | `󰇚` | `barForeground` | "↓ 4.2 MB/s ↑ 32 KB/s · 2 downloading · 1 queued" | "4.2M" |
| Ready to watch (unacknowledged `Torrent.playable.acked == false`; P5-05 supplies the field, until then inert) | play-circle-outline | `barForeground` | "Ready to watch: <name>" | as downloading |
| Waiting for the VPN | `󰦝` | `bar.urgent` | "Waiting for ProtonVPN · 2 downloads waiting" | none |
| Engine error, or a torrent in error | `󰀦` | `bar.urgent` | the message | none |
| Turtle on (P5-04; driven by `summary.alt == true`) | the state's glyph plus a small tortoise glyph (`U+F0883`) after it | as the state | "… · turtle limits on" | |

2. **`Glyphs.js`** pins every codepoint by role in one place: download `U+F01DA`, upload `U+F0552`, paused
   `U+F03E4`, done `U+F012C`, VPN `U+F099D`, error `U+F0026`, add `U+F0415`, power `U+F0425`, refresh
   `U+F0450`, terminal `U+F018D`, play `U+F040A`, folder `U+F0770`, trash `U+F01B4`, turtle `U+F0883`; the
   metadata, checking, stalled, queued and ready glyphs (`dots-horizontal`, `sync`, `timer-sand`,

   `middleClick` (`dashboard` default, DL-12; `tui` restores today's behaviour; `t` in the popup always opens
   the TUI).
4. **Visibility**: `visible: svc.online || showWhenStopped || root.opened || svc.stoppedRecently ||
   svc.reconnecting`, where `stoppedRecently` is true for 10 s after a `bye` and `reconnecting` from an EOF
   without `bye` until the backoff reaches its 10 s cap (§4.4 rule 10; a crash-restart under
   `Restart=on-failure` shows the §4.11 "Reconnecting" icon instead of a vanish-and-return); `root.opened`
   keeps the anchor of an open popup on the bar. With `showWhenStopped` a left click on the dimmed icon calls
   `startDaemon` and opens the popup in its Starting… state.
5. Colour changes animate for `Style.duration(160)` only when `bar.foregroundAnimationEnabled` (§4.13).

- §4.2.4 iconography: glyphs come from the Nerd Font the bar already uses and live in `Glyphs.js` so a glyph
  is chosen once per role; existing glyphs keep their meaning; new ones are named by their Material Design
  Icon name and pinned to codepoints here, each rendered in a test that fails if `paintedWidth == 0` (a
  missing glyph renders as a box). Every state glyph is always followed by its word; the bar icon is the only
  place a glyph stands alone, and there its tooltip carries the word.
- §4.5 visibility rationale: under A1 the icon disappears a few minutes after the last download, visibly
  rather than mid-glance; the menu, a keybinding or `fbittorrent dashboard` bring the app back;
  `showWhenStopped` stays, off, for anyone else (Q2 answered: hidden when stopped).
- §4.14: the brand is the monochrome Nerd Font glyph already used (`󰇚`/`󰕒`); no brand colour (Sprout's "95 %

- §4.3.4 `contracts/ui/states.json`: glyphs written as `U+XXXX` codepoints so the file is font-independent;

- §8.4 `lint` job: the plugin structure lint (no `Timer`/`Process` outside `Service.qml`, P2-04).

`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Today's popup has literals: `Qt.darker(foreground, 1.55)` (`Panel.qml:18`), a literal 400 ms animation
  (`Panel.qml:410`), a 400 px width (`Panel.qml:162`), a literal `Qt.rgba` track. ucmz851's hard-coded palette
  is the counter-example the marketplace reviewer rejected (OR §5; principle 8).
- After P2-03 and P2-04 the popup and icon are rewritten on tokens; after P2-08 `plugin/tests/lint.sh` exists
  in skeleton form (P2-04 added the structure rule) and `qs-visual.sh` can capture with `--light <theme>`.
- The two results that grow with the library, `torrents.list` and `torrents.files`, are not bounded by the 1
  MiB line cap (§3.4.1); the plugin must subscribe instead of calling them.

## Goal and user value
Principle 8 (Omarchy-native look, tokens only) made mechanical: a lint that fails CI on any literal colour,
size or duration, and a capture list that proves every state is legible in the owner's monochrome theme and in
one light theme (§4.14; §9.5's P2 human check: "the owner opens the popup in their theme and in
`catppuccin-latte` and finds every state readable"). Also the guard that keeps the shell's memory bounded (no
uncapped results in `plugin/`, DL-67).

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`plugin/tests/lint.sh`** (ripgrep over `plugin/oliver.torrents/**/*.{qml,js}`): fail on a literal colour
   (`#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}`, `Qt.rgba(` with numeric channels, named colours), a literal pixel size in `width:`,
   `height:`, `font.pixelSize:`, `implicitWidth:`, `spacing:` or `margins:` that is not `Style.space(`,
   `Style.spacing.` or `Style.font.`, a literal `duration:` that is not `Style.duration(` (§4.2.1), and the
   operation names `torrents.list` and `torrents.files` anywhere under `plugin/` (the plugin subscribes; those
   two results are the ones the 1 MiB line cap does not bound), with an allow-list file
   `plugin/tests/lint-allow.txt` for the few justified literals, each with a reason (the two permitted local
   constants: the progress-track alpha `Util.alpha(foreground, 0.12)` and the cursor bar width
   `Style.space(3)`).
2. **`plugin/tests/VISUAL.md`**: the list of states to capture, one line each `<surface> <state> <fixture
   recipe>`: every row of §4.11 for popup and dashboard, every row state of §4.3.1, every icon row of §4.5.
   Each state name is also a fixture recipe `regression_tests/fixtures/states/<state>.json` for `daemon.py
   --serve-fixture` (P1-07).
3. **Captures** in the owner's theme and in `catppuccin-latte` (`qs-visual.sh --light catppuccin-latte`),
   stored under `target/test-logs/visual/<date>/` and archived with the receipts (§8.3), never under `docs/`.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.2.1 rules that follow from the tokens: no literal colour, size or duration anywhere in `plugin/`; dim
  starts at 1.4 and is computed (`Model.dim`), not fixed; hover and keyboard cursor are one state
  ("hover-cursor", `Style.qml:40-44`); selection uses `selectedFill`/`selectionFill`; focus rings only on
  controls that take Qt focus through `Border.controlSpec("focus")`.
- §4.14 theming: colours only from `qs.Commons` (`Color.*`, `Color.popups.*`, `Style.*`, `Border.*`) and the
  bar's `foreground`/`urgent`; tints derive from tokens (`Util.alpha`); every release checks captures in the
  owner's monochrome theme and in one light theme (`catppuccin-latte` or `flexoki-light`, both under
  `/usr/share/omarchy/themes/`); state must stay legible without hue; the contrast test (P2-08) runs over
  every installed theme in CI-less mode (TOML only).
- §4.11 the state table (popup and dashboard columns) is the capture list: daemon not running; starting;
  connecting; reconnecting; protocol major mismatch; version skew; parked for the VPN; engine failed to start;
  no torrents; filter matches nothing (dashboard); mutation result unknown; upgrade pending; idle countdown;
  clipboard magnet (P6-13); quick add offer; stopped recently; playable may stall (P5-05); disk low; disk full
  (P5-07).
- §4.3.1 row states: cursor, pending, error, done, ready to watch. §4.5 icon rows: not running (with
  `showWhenStopped`), idle, seeding only, stopped recently, downloading, ready to watch, waiting for the VPN,
  error, turtle on.
- §7.2 adopted review bar: screenshots match the real UI, captured from the running shell, dark and light,
  never mockups (OR §6 gotcha 8); the README's two hero screenshots are the only committed images.
- §8.4 `lint` CI job: the QML token lint (P2-05).

## Acceptance criteria
- The lint passes in CI and fails on a planted `#ff0000`.
- Captures stored under `target/test-logs/visual/<date>/` and archived with the receipts, never under `docs/`;
  the README's two hero screenshots are the only committed images.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `plugin/tests/lint.sh` with a negative fixture file `plugin/tests/lint-negative.qml`, which must fail on
  each rule once (the test asserts one failure per rule and logs them).
- `qs-visual.sh --light catppuccin-latte` (opt-in `FBT_TEST_VISUAL=1`; captures listed in the receipt).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P2-03 (the popup to lint and capture) and P2-04 (the icon states and the lint skeleton).
- Consumed by M1.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q23 (open, default the judged pair): the look-and-feel gate is the owner's verdict on the `--compare` image,
  not a pixel scan.

## Risks and decisions
- R17 (the visual harness depends on the live shell): captures are opt-in; the lint and `contrast.py` run in
  CI without a shell.
- DL-59 (no 1 px automated comparison against the Wi-Fi panel), DL-60 (captures go to
  `target/test-logs/visual/`), DL-67 (`torrents.list` and `torrents.files` banned in `plugin/` by lint).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The lint passes in CI and fails on a planted `#ff0000`.
- [ ] Captures stored under `target/test-logs/visual/<date>/` and archived with the receipts, never under `docs/`; the README's two hero screenshots are the only committed images.

title: P2-06: Isolated Quickshell smoke test
description:
# P2-06: Isolated Quickshell smoke test

Plan item **P2-06** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4268). Phase P2; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1**;
topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-07 (Integration harness `daemon.py`), P2-02 (Store reducer and fixture tests).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M1 (First demo (v0.2.0)), P3-16 (Dashboard smoke, captures, README).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- There is no automated test of the plugin against a daemon; `widget_keys.sh` needs the live shell. Sprout's
  `tools/test_quickshell.sh` runs a separate `qs` instance against a disposable backend (OR §8 item 9);
  Omarchy's guidance not to start extra Quickshell instances (FO §2.10) is about production.
- Quickshell resolves `qs.*` imports from the config root, so an isolated `qs -p <dir>` sees `qs.Commons` and
  `qs.Ui` only through symlinks `<dir>/Commons` and `<dir>/Ui` into `/usr/share/omarchy/shell` (a
  `QML_IMPORT_PATH` cannot work: it would look for `qs/Commons/qmldir`). **Unverified** until this item's
  `probe-ui.qml` runs (§4.16, §10.4); the fallback for the visual components is the captures in the real
  shell.
- A Unix socket path is limited to 108 bytes, so the temp dir must be short (`/tmp/fbt-XXXXXX`). The host
  normally injects `manifest` into the service (`shell.qml:944-950`).

## Goal and user value
Tests the plugin-to-daemon path (`Service.qml` → `ApiClient.js` → `api.sock` → daemon → `Store.js` →
`ListModel`) without touching the running shell or the owner's daemon (R3: Store logic tested outside the
shell). It becomes the M1 gate's `qs-smoke.sh` and is extended by P3-16 to every dashboard data path and by
later items (`turtle_toggle`, `history_points`, `palette`).

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`plugin/tests/qs-smoke.sh`**: `mktemp -d /tmp/fbt-XXXXXX` with the five XDG directories of P1-07 under it
   (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` 0700); a `config.toml` there with `network_interface = "lo"` (every engine socket, DHT
   included, binds to loopback, so the random hash never reaches the public DHT and the §9.1 "local only" rule
   holds), `peer_port` = a free port from `/proc/net/tcp`, `save_path` under the temp dir, `notify = false`;
   the binary `${FBT_BIN:-target/release/fbittorrent}`; `fbittorrent serve --idle-exit-secs 600 --no-notify`
   with that environment, readiness awaited with `fbittorrent status --quiet` (exit 0) for up to 10 s.
2. Then `env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<tmp runtime> WAYLAND_DISPLAY=<absolute path of the real Wayland socket>
   FBT_TEST_HOOKS=1 FBT_SMOKE_HASH=<40 random hex> QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP=1 NO_COLOR=1 timeout 60 qs -p
   plugin/tests/smoke 2>&1`, piped through `plugin/tests/qs-log.py` (suite `qs-smoke`; the shim matches
   `FBTQS-` markers anywhere in a line and reads both streams), so `Service.qml` connects to the disposable
   daemon from its first `hello` and never to the owner's (`Quickshell.env("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")`, §4.4 rule 1;
   `useRuntimeDir` is for the live-shell harnesses).
3. **`plugin/tests/smoke/shell.qml`** loads `../../oliver.torrents/Service.qml` with `manifest: ({version:
   "smoke"})`, sets `svc.popupOpen = true` so the `torrents` topic is subscribed (§4.4 rule 9), and runs the
   steps with a hard-timeout `Timer`: `add` (`svc.add({magnet: "magnet:?xt=urn:btih:" + hash +
   "&dn=fbt-smoke"}, false)`; the row appears with `state: metadata` at once because P1-09 creates the ledger
   record from the magnet's hash and name before metadata arrives), `pause` (`svc.pause(hash)` → `paused`),
   `resume` (`svc.resume(hash)` → `metadata` again), `remove_keep_files` (`svc.remove(hash, false)` → the row
   is gone), `reconnect` (a handshake, because the headless shell has no `IpcHandler` and therefore no
   `state()`: `shell.qml` records `svc.instance`, prints the marker `FBTQS-WAIT reconnect` and waits;
   `qs-smoke.sh` watches the merged output for that marker, kills the disposable daemon, starts it again and
   waits for `status --quiet` to exit 0; `shell.qml` then asserts that `svc.instance` changed within 1 s of
   that readiness and that `svc.subs` lists `summary` and `torrents` again. `instance` and `subs` are the
   service's own properties, the same values P2-01's `state()` hook serialises); each a `FBTQS-STEP` line and
   one `FBTQS-PASS`/`FAIL`; a `trap` kills the daemon and removes the temp dir.
4. **`qs.Commons` is required, not optional** (`Service.qml` uses `Util.execArgv`): the test root carries
   symlinks `plugin/tests/smoke/Commons -> /usr/share/omarchy/shell/Commons` and `Ui ->
   /usr/share/omarchy/shell/Ui`; a separate probe `plugin/tests/smoke/probe-ui.qml` imports `qs.Ui` and
   instantiates `PanelHero` first, so a failure there is recorded without killing the smoke.
5. Record the probe's outcome (`qs` version, date, PASS or the error) in `plugin/tests/README.md` (a table:
   file, what it tests, how to run it, last result); if the probe fails, the §4.16 fallback applies to the
   visual components only.
6. `all.sh` gains the `FBT_TEST_QS=1` block entry for `qs-smoke.sh`.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.16 "Smoke against a disposable daemon": creates temporary XDG directories, starts `fbittorrent serve
  --idle-exit-secs 600 --no-notify` there, runs `timeout 60 qs -p plugin/tests/smoke`; the smoke shell
  instantiates `Service.qml` with the temporary runtime directory, adds `magnet:?xt=urn:btih:<40 random
  hex>&dn=fbt-smoke` (a hash that can never resolve), waits for it in the model, pauses and resumes it,
  removes it with `delete_files: false`, and checks each step by marker lines. It never touches the user's
  daemon because the runtime directory differs.
- §9.1 fixtures local only: disposable info hashes; temporary XDG directories.
- Appendix E.2: `plugin/tests/qs-smoke.sh` covers plugin to daemon over a disposable runtime dir; needs `qs`
  and a build; opt-in `FBT_TEST_QS=1`; added by P2-06. `plugin/tests/qs-log.py` (P0-15) converts the markers.
- §4.4 rule 9 names `popupOpen` (P2-01) as the property that subscribes `torrents`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `FBT_TEST_QS=1 all.sh` runs it green.
- When the owner's daemon is running, `fbittorrent api app.info --json`'s `clients.bar` is the same before and
  after the run (the script performs the check itself and skips it with a logged reason when no owner daemon
  runs or its `instance` changed between the readings).
- The probe's result is in `plugin/tests/README.md`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-smoke.sh::{add, pause, resume, remove_keep_files, reconnect}` with `FBTQS-STEP` lines (observed text:
  the row's state after each step), plus `probe_ui`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P2-02 (the store and service actions it drives) and P1-07 (the XDG layout and fixture
  conventions; `fixtures.py`'s free-port and shim helpers).
- Consumed by M1 and P3-16 (extends the smoke to every dashboard data path).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R2/R3: an isolated instance is how the plugin is tested without risking the desktop shell.

  `probe-ui.qml`; the outcome goes to `plugin/tests/README.md`.

  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.

  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait

  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
