  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any

  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,

  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

# P2-07: Menu, keybinding, desktop entries, install script

Plan item **P2-07** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4313). Phase P2; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `cli`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M1**; topological level 15 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-04 (systemd user unit and start on demand), P1-11 (The CLI on the API client;
contract 1.2.0).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M1 (First demo (v0.2.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D18: the owner's menu extension `~/.config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc:33-36` gates its "Stop"
  entry on a qBittorrent unit (`systemctl --user is-active qbittorrent-nox`, `:36`) and its "Open" entries
  launch the TUI in a terminal. The desktop entries use `Icon=qbittorrent` (P1-13 changes the icon name).
- `scripts/install.sh` exists since P1-04 (build, `mv` the binary, `fbittorrent setup --magnet`); `setup`
  writes the unit and the magnet handler. The plugin is a symlink into the repository
  (`~/.config/omarchy/plugins/oliver.torrents -> …/plugin/oliver.torrents`).
- SUPER+CTRL+T is taken (Activity, FO §2.8); free chords are found by grepping
  `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/bindings/*.lua` and `~/.config/hypr/`.
- Until P3-08 adds the `panel` kind, `fbittorrent dashboard` falls back to the TUI when the plugin manifest
  has no `panel` kind (Appendix F), so the v0.2.0 menu never points at a window that does not exist.

## Goal and user value
A working install story for v0.2.0 (§8.6): one script builds, installs, registers the handler, links the
plugin and fixes the menu; `setup` is idempotent and has `--dry-run`, `--uninstall` and `--purge`. The README
install section is rewritten here (§8.5 staging). The chord choice is the owner's open question Q6, decided
here from the free chords and recorded in the receipt.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `scripts/install.sh` (created by P1-04) gains `--plugin=link` on its `setup` call: `fbittorrent setup
   --magnet --plugin=link`.
2. `setup` flags `--magnet`, `--save`, `--plugin=link|copy`, `--dry-run`, `--uninstall`, `--purge` (Appendix
   F: exit 0, 1, 3 for `--purge` without `--yes`; JSON extended with `actions[]`) and idempotence (a second
   run changes nothing): config and download folder, the magnet handler and desktop entries with the new icon
   (`Icon=fbittorrent`), the systemd unit plus `daemon-reload`, the plugin (`--plugin=link` symlinks the
   repository folder for development, `--plugin=copy` copies it for a stable install), `omarchy plugin enable
   oliver.torrents`, the bar placement only if it is missing, and the menu entries.
3. **Menu entries** in `~/.config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc` (D18): `torrents.open` → `fbittorrent
   dashboard`, `torrents.search` → `fbittorrent dashboard --view search`, `torrents.add` stays `fbittorrent
   add-clipboard`, `torrents.tui` keeps the terminal entry, `torrents.stop` gated on `fbittorrent status
   --quiet` (exit 0 running, 4 stopped; the gate only tests non-zero) instead of the stale `systemctl --user
   is-active qbittorrent-nox`.
4. A keybinding suggestion with a chord checked free once by grepping
   `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/bindings/*.lua` and `~/.config/hypr/` (SUPER+CTRL+T is taken); the chosen
   chord and the grep output go in the P2-07 receipt (Q6).
5. `setup --uninstall` removes the unit, desktop entries, icon, plugin link and menu entries and keeps the
   data; `--purge` also deletes data after a confirm.
6. The README install section.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §8.6 release and install: `scripts/install.sh` builds with `--release --locked`, installs the binary into
  `~/.local/bin` by copying to a temporary name and renaming so a running daemon keeps its inode and detects
  the replacement (§3.2.12), then `fbittorrent setup --magnet --plugin=link`. Release checklist (each line a
  script): `all.sh` green; `FBT_TEST_QS=1`, `FBT_TEST_VISUAL=1` and `FBT_TEST_RESOURCES=1` runs green; the
  capture set reviewed; `CHANGELOG.md` entry; tag. Versions: the binary and the plugin share one SemVer
  number.
- §2.4 Omarchy menu surface (`torrents.*`): open dashboard, search, add from clipboard, quit; opening starts
  the daemon.
- §4.1: a bar-layout entry counts as enabled (`PluginRegistry.qml:148-163`; the owner's
  `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json:38` lists the plugin only in the bar layout), so `setup` need not add a
  `plugins[]` entry; P3-08 asserts it with a summon loop.
- §0.4 "Does not change": nothing runs at login; Ghostty for the TUI (`omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui`); the bar
  widget uses the shell's `Panel` chrome, never a tray icon.
- Appendix F `setup [--magnet] [--save] [--plugin=link|copy] [--dry-run] [--uninstall] [--purge]`: none
  (files, systemd, shell IPC); starts: no; JSON extended (`actions[]`); exit 0, 1, 3 (`--purge` without
  `--yes`). `register-magnet`: the same step as `setup --magnet`.
- §10.4: whether the symlinked plugin folder hot-reloads is verified by P2-01's `reload_reconnects`; if not,
  `--plugin=copy` becomes the documented development default.

## Acceptance criteria
- `setup --dry-run` with a temporary `HOME` lists the exact actions.
- A second `setup` on the owner's machine changes nothing.
- The menu's "Stop" entry is gated on `status --quiet`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::{setup_dry_run_lists_actions, setup_idempotent}` with a temp `HOME` and a `systemctl` shim (each
  logs the `actions[]` JSON and the second run's empty diff).
- Added in polish round 1: `daemon.py::setup_uninstall_keeps_data` (temp `HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`: after
  `setup --uninstall` the unit, desktop entries, icon, plugin link and menu entries are gone and
  `engine/torrents.json`, `rss.json`, `shows.json` are byte-identical; `--purge` without `--yes` exits 3 and
  deletes nothing; each path is one E.1 step) and unit `setup::tests::unit_text_matches_plan` (the generated
  `fbittorrent.service` equals the §3.2.2 text with the `ExecStart` path substituted) and
  `setup::tests::menu_jsonc_edit_idempotent` (applying the menu edit twice yields one set of `torrents.*`
  entries).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-04 (`install.sh` and `setup`'s unit writing) and P1-11 (`status --quiet`, the `dashboard`
  verb's contract entry, the README's Lifecycle section this install section follows).
- Consumed by M1.

- Q6 (open): which free key chord toggles the dashboard; chosen here from the free chords and recorded in the
  receipt.

  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `setup --dry-run` with a temporary `HOME` lists the exact actions.
- [ ] A second `setup` on the owner's machine changes nothing.
- [ ] The menu's "Stop" entry is gated on `status --quiet`.

title: P2-08: Design tokens, visual capture harness and contrast test
description:
# P2-08: Design tokens, visual capture harness and contrast test

Plan item **P2-08** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4335). Phase P2; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M1**;
topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-07 (Integration harness `daemon.py`), P2-01 (Plugin restructure and the shared
API client).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P2-04 (Bar icon states), P3-09 (Torrents view), P4-05
(Contrast and low-chroma themes).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The popup dims with `Qt.darker(foreground, 1.55)` (`Panel.qml:18`); first-party panels use 1.4
  (`Ui/PanelHero.qml:23`, `Ui/PanelSectionHeader.qml:19`). On the owner's theme 1.4 gives `#b6b6b6` on black
  (about 10.4:1) and on `catppuccin-latte` 10.2:1, but on `everforest` it is 3.8:1 and on `gruvbox` and
  `tokyo-night` 4.3:1 (computed from their `colors.toml`), so a fixed factor cannot pass a 4.5:1 gate. `muted`
  reaches 4.5:1 on only 3 of 23 installed themes; `dark_foreground` is 2.6:1 on the owner's theme (D16).
  `accent` fails 4.5:1 on `catppuccin-latte` (4.3), `miasma` (3.9), `rose-pine` (3.1).
- Number formats are inconsistent across surfaces today (RC §9 defect 9, "0 B", "0s", `eta: 8640000`).
- `grim` is installed; `omarchy-theme-set <theme>` switches the live theme; `omarchy-shell shell summon` opens
  panels; the plugin's `cursor()` IPC hook exists. Omarchy themes live under
  `/usr/share/omarchy/themes/*/colors.toml`; the owner's is
  `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml`.

## Goal and user value
The owner's complaint is look and feel; without captures and a contrast check nobody can tell whether a change
made it better or worse (§0.2 "Look" row). This item defines the shared design values once: the dim ladder
(DL-31/DL-53: one ladder for QML and TUI, defined once, from one theme fixture), the number formats (§4.2.3)
and the state vocabulary file (`contracts/ui/states.json`, DL-32), plus the visual harness whose `--compare
omarchy.network` pair image is the owner's look-and-feel gate (Q23, DL-59). The TUI's `palette.rs` (P4-05) is
tested against the same `expected.json`.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`Model.js` number formatting** per §4.2.3 with unit tests: sizes "1.1G"/"963M"/"12K" with one decimal
   below 10 in table cells and "1.4 GiB" (binary units) in sentences, never "GB"; rates "3.1M"/"32K" in cells
   and "4.2 MB/s" in sentences (decimal, like the bar's other widgets); ETA "12m"/"1h05"/"2d" in cells and "12
   min", "1 h 05", "2 d" in sentences, never seconds above a minute, never "∞"; percent "43%", with "99.5%"
   shown as "99%" (integers below 99.5 and "99.9" above, so a nearly complete torrent is never "100%" before
   `done`) and "0.04%" as "<1%"; absent values "—"; counts with thin spaces above 9,999; `Model.when(ts)`
   ("12:41 today", "Oct 12", "2025-10-12") and `Model.ago(ts)` ("12 s ago").
2. **`Model.dim(fg, bg)`** as the one ladder of §4.2.1: rung 1 `Qt.darker(fg, 1.4)` (Qt's HSV darken: value ×
   100 ÷ 140, hue and saturation unchanged); rung 2 `mix(fg, bg, 0.75)` per 8-bit sRGB channel, `round(0.75·fg
   + 0.25·bg)`; rung 3 the same mix at 0.85; rung 4 `fg`; the first rung whose WCAG contrast against `bg`
   reaches 4.5:1 wins. `muted` and `dark_foreground` are never rungs.
3. **`Model.accentText(accent, bg)`**: accent only when ≥ 4.5:1 against `bg`, else bold foreground (§4.2.1
   "Accent text": for the ready badge, key letters, the sorted header and the active filter).
4. **`Glyphs.js`** skeleton (P2-04 pins the codepoints); the `useRuntimeDir` hook wiring.
5. **`plugin/tests/qs-visual.sh`** per §4.16 (opt-in `FBT_TEST_VISUAL=1`): starts a fixture daemon through
   `daemon.py --serve-fixture <state>` in a temporary runtime directory, points the plugin at it with the
   `useRuntimeDir` IPC hook, summons the popup or the dashboard with `omarchy-shell shell summon`, captures
   with `grim` to `target/test-logs/visual/<date>/<surface>-<state>-<theme>.png`, reports a pixel-diff
   percentage against the previous capture of the same state, `--light <theme>` switches with
   `omarchy-theme-set` for the capture and switches back, `--compare <plugin>` (for example `omarchy.network`)
   captures the named first-party panel in the same theme right after ours and writes the two PNGs side by
   side into one image with our hero title baseline, meta baseline, first `PanelSeparator` y and row pitch
   (read through `state()`) printed under it, `--dry-run` checks every tool it needs (`grim`, `omarchy-shell`,
   `hyprctl`) and logs their versions; restores the hook and the theme on exit (trap).
6. **`plugin/tests/contrast.py`**: for every `/usr/share/omarchy/themes/*/colors.toml` and the owner's current
   theme, compute the §4.2.1 ladder (which rung wins and its hex) and the WCAG ratios of `foreground`, the
   computed dim and `accent` against `background`; fail only when the computed dim or `foreground` is below
   4.5:1 (a theme whose own foreground fails is reported, not fixed; `rose-pine` is 6.7:1 today, every other
   installed theme above 7:1); `muted` reported for information; write `contracts/ui/themes/<theme>.toml` (a
   copy of each theme's `colors.toml` plus the owner's) and `contracts/ui/themes/expected.json` (one object
   per theme file: `{"owner": {"foreground": "#ffffff", "background": "#000000", "accent": "#8d8d8d", "dim":
   "#b6b6b6", "dim_rung": 1, "dim_ratio": 10.4, "fg_ratio": 21.0, "accent_ratio": 6.3, "accent_text": false,
   "low_chroma": true}}`), so the tests do not depend on which themes a CI box has installed.
7. **`contracts/ui/states.json`** in the shape of §4.3.4: a JSON array in the table's row order, each element
   `{"state": "downloading", "qml_glyph": "U+F041A", "text_glyph": "↓", "word": "Downloading", "short":
   "Down", "secondary": "rate · eta · peers"}`; the `ready`, `disk_full`, `added_before`, `in_list`, `unread`
   and `pending` rows use the same shape with those names in `state`, the pending verbs as a `verbs` array on
   the `pending` row ("pausing…", "resuming…", "removing…", "adding…", "checking…"), and a `reason` row
   carrying the phrases: `user` "paused by you"; `queue_full` "waiting for a download slot";
   `complete_no_seed` "complete; seeding is off"; `vpn_down` "waiting for <interface>"; `restore_failed`
   "could not restore: <error>"; `metadata_timeout` "no peers answered"; `missing_files` "files are missing";
   `disk_full` "disk full".

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.3.4 state table (`state` | text glyph | word | `short` ≤ 5 cells | secondary): metadata `◌` Metadata Meta
  "0:12" elapsed; checking `⟳` Checking Check percent checked; downloading `↓` Downloading Down "↓ rate · ETA
  · peers"; stalled `~` Stalled Stall "no peers" or "no data for 2 min"; queued `…` Queued Queue "3 of 3 slots
  busy"; paused `‖` Paused Pause percent; done `✓` Done Done size; seeding `↑` Seeding Seed "↑ rate · ratio";
  waiting_vpn `⏚` Waiting for VPN VPN interface name; error `!` Error Error the message; error+disk_full `!`
  Disk full Disk "1.2 GiB free, 3.1 GiB needed" (P5-07); ready `▶` Ready to watch Ready "4 min buffered" or
  "may stall" (P5-05); added earlier `+` Added before; in your list `+` In your list; unread `●` (U+25CF)
  Unread; pending verb: the state's glyph at 0.55 opacity. `◌` (U+25CC) replaces `…` for metadata because `…`
  already means queued/waiting on Shows; `⋯` is dropped as indistinguishable from `…`.
- §4.2.1 accent rule: `Color.accent` for the ready badge, key letters, the sorted header and the active filter
  only when `accent` reaches 4.5:1 against `background`; otherwise bold `foreground`.
- §5.5.1 (the TUI twin, P4-05): dim must reach 4.5:1; the TUI's text gate is 4.5:1, not 7:1; QML and TUI must
  match `expected.json` within ±1 per channel.
- §4.16 visual captures: "Looks first-party" is the owner's verdict on the pair image, recorded in the
  receipt; there is no pixel gate on someone else's panel (anti-aliasing and theme alpha make a 1 px scan
  flaky).
- Appendix E.2: `plugin/tests/qs-format.sh` (number formatting, opt-in, P2-08); `plugin/tests/qs-visual.sh`
  (captures and pixel diffs, light theme; needs grim, omarchy-shell; opt-in `FBT_TEST_VISUAL=1`);
  `plugin/tests/contrast.py` (WCAG ratios per installed theme; yes in CI, TOML only). E.3: theme TOML files
  copied into `contracts/ui/themes/*.toml` with `expected.json` by `contrast.py`, used by `contrast.py`,
  `qs-format.sh::dim_ladder`, `palette::tests`; `contracts/ui/states.json`, `contracts/ui/format.json` (P4-07)
  used by `qs-format.sh`, `format::tests`, `qs-glyphs.sh`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `qs-visual.sh popup downloading` produces a PNG of the live popup over the fixture daemon and restores the
  hook.
- `qs-visual.sh popup downloading --compare omarchy.network` writes the pair image with our geometry printed
  under it.
- `contrast.py` passes for every installed theme under the computed dim (or lists the failing ones with
  ratios, and the lint fails).
- `qs-format.sh::dim_ladder` asserts `Model.dim` returns the hex in `expected.json` (±1 per channel) for every
  fixture theme.
- `Model.js` formatting tests pass under `qs`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `plugin/tests/qs-format.sh`: formatting fixtures (sizes, rates, ETA, percent edge cases 99.5 and 0.04 %);
  `dim_ladder` and `accent_fallback` over `contracts/ui/themes/*.toml` (the same files `palette::tests` reads
  in P4-05); `states` over `contracts/ui/states.json`.
- `contrast.py --self-test` with a known-bad theme `contracts/ui/themes/_bad.toml` (foreground `#777777` on
  `#888888`).
- `qs-visual.sh --compare` self-test (the pair image exists and names both panels); `qs-visual.sh --dry-run`
  logs tool versions.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P2-01 (the plugin tree, `Model.js`, the `useRuntimeDir` hook) and P1-07 (`daemon.py
  --serve-fixture` and the fixture states).
- Consumed by P2-03 and P2-04 (formatting, dim, glyphs, captures), P3-09 (table formats and captures), P4-05
  (`palette.rs` cross-checks `expected.json`; this item creates `contracts/ui/themes/`, and the TUI's
  `dim_matches_fixture` test lives in P4-05 because `palette.rs` does not exist yet).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q23 (open, default the judged pair). Q24 (open, default identical `#b6b6b6`): one ladder for both surfaces.
  Q25 (open, default grey accent as the rule says): the owner's `#8d8d8d` accent is 6.3:1 on black and is
  used.

## Risks and decisions
- R17 (medium, low): the visual harness depends on the live shell and the owner's session; opt-in; restores
  theme and hook on exit; `--dry-run` checks tools.
- DL-23 (superseded), DL-31/DL-53 (one dim ladder, defined once, ±1 per channel against `expected.json`;
  `muted` and `dark_foreground` never text colours), DL-32 (one state table), DL-38 (the first-party width),
  DL-59 (no 1 px gate; the owner judges the pair), DL-63 (the three UI contract files have shapes), DL-69
  (sizes binary everywhere, "GiB" in sentences and "1.4G" in cells, never "GB").

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `qs-visual.sh popup downloading` produces a PNG of the live popup over the fixture daemon and restores the hook.
- [ ] `qs-visual.sh popup downloading --compare omarchy.network` writes the pair image with our geometry printed under it.
- [ ] `contrast.py` passes for every installed theme under the computed dim (or lists the failing ones with ratios, and the lint fails).
- [ ] `qs-format.sh::dim_ladder` asserts `Model.dim` returns the hex in `expected.json` (±1 per channel) for every fixture theme.
- [ ] `Model.js` formatting tests pass under `qs`.

title: P3-01: Search in the daemon
description:
# P3-01: Search in the daemon

Plan item **P3-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4380). Phase P3; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P3-12 (Search
view), P4-07 (Remaining UX defects), P7-01 (Torznab indexers (§7.3)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Search jobs run in the calling process (`src/qbt.rs:609-627`; the provider registry
  `src/search.rs:723-738`), so `fbittorrent search` works with the app closed and search jobs die with the TUI
  (RC §7). Providers are qBittorrent nova plugins (Python scripts the user installs with `search --install` or
  `--install-url`; the curated list at `src/qbt.rs:223-237` includes the nyaa.si engine bundled by commit
  `c7d311f`) run through the embedded nova3 runtime (`vendor/nova3/nova2.py:71-75,262-264`: one nova2 process
  plus a `spawn` pool of `min(cpu_count, 4)` workers), with bounded capture (2 MiB, `src/search.rs:27`),
  results capped at 5,000 (`src/search.rs:26`), process-group kill and `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`
  (`src/search.rs:583-688`), and `shutdown_all` (`src/search.rs:945-961`). Provider preferences are a file
  plus lock (`src/search.rs:254-256,399`). Browse lists live in the TUI (`src/browse.rs:31-44`; JSON capped at
  16 MiB, `src/browse.rs:60`).
- D15 / RC §9 defect 14: search shows duplicates and raw mojibake. Dedup falls back to the full URL
  (`src/tui/mod.rs:2979-2997`); `screens/07-search-sintel-16s.txt` shows `[philosophy-raws][辛特尔][sintel]…`
  rendered as mojibake.
- After P1-08 the bus can stream a keyed topic; after P1-12 a search session is a busy reason.

## Goal and user value
A4 (search moves into the daemon so QML never shells out and results survive closing a window) and D15. W1
step 2: results stream in from the enabled providers, deduplicated by info hash, with size, seeds, uploaded
date, provider and IMDb rating. The CLI keeps an in-process fallback (P3-07). Also the first of the P3 feature
namespaces, which the `caps` list negotiates.

## Do (exact steps)
`src/api/ops/search.rs` over `src/search.rs` (§3.7):
1. **Sessions** owned by the connection that started them: `search.start {query (1..256), providers?, limit? ≤
   5000}` → `{search_id}`; at most 4 concurrent sessions, the fifth is `busy` (`details.limit: sessions`); a
   session ends 30 s after its connection drops and its results are retained for that grace so a reloaded
   dashboard (Quickshell hot reload) can resubscribe and keep them.
2. Results stream on the `search:<id>` topic (A.7: keyed by `key`, 500 ms default interval) as `SearchResult`
   objects (A.9: `key`, `name`, `size?`, `seeds?`, `leechers?`, `uploaded_at?`, `providers: [str]`, `magnet?`,
   `url?`, `page_url?`, `imdb_id?`, `rating?`, `provider_url?`, `added: hash?` filled from the ledger as
   results stream, so no client needs the ledger; DL-51).
3. `search.done {search_id, total, warnings: [{provider, message}]}` (A.8); `search.stop {search_id}`;
   `search.providers` → `{providers: [Provider]}` (`name`, `full_name?`, `kind: enum(nova|torznab)`,
   `enabled`, `url?`, `version?`); `search.set_provider {name, enabled}` (idempotent); `search.install
   {curated? | sources? (https URLs)}` (pending, then `mutation.result {installed, failed: [{source,
   message}]}`); `search.browse_sources` → `{sources: [{id, label, provider, in_app, url?}]}`; `search.browse
   {source}` → `{items: [SearchResult]}` (bounded: the existing 16 MiB cap); `search.grab {search_id, key |
   result, …add args}` as `torrents.add` with `origin: "search"`; refused with `engine_unavailable` and the
   VPN hint while parked (§3.2.9).
4. Providers run as today (bounded capture, process-group kill, `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`) as children of the daemon;
   `shutdown_all` runs on drain. Provider download helpers stay refused while VPN binding is on
   (`src/qbt.rs:413-423`).
5. **Dedupe** (§3.7): key = the btih from the magnet or the `.torrent`; when a provider gives only a page URL,
   the normalized `(title, size)` pair. Keep the best-seeded entry and list every provider that returned it.
6. **Mojibake repair** (§3.7): if a name round-trips as UTF-8 that was decoded as Latin-1 ("è¾›ç‰¹å°”"),
   re-decode it; otherwise leave it unchanged. Re-encoding the string as Latin-1 and decoding the bytes as
   UTF-8 succeeds only when every byte sequence is valid multibyte UTF-8, which a real Latin-1 title
   ("Amélie", "Straße") almost never is, so the repair cannot damage a name that was right; the raw bytes are
   kept for the session so a false positive is recoverable.
7. **Fake providers** for tests: `regression_tests/fixtures/providers/{alpha,beta}.py` (nova-style scripts
   printing fixed results with a duplicate pair across them and one mojibake name, the
   `screens/07-search-sintel-16s.txt` sample).
8. `caps` gains `search`; contract bookkeeping (`api::ops::TABLE` rows, `docs/IPC.md`,
   `contracts/ipc/v1/search.ndjson`).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.4.10: concurrent search sessions 4 (each is one nova2 process plus up to 4 workers: about 5 processes and
  150 MB per session).
- §3.2.10 busy table: `search` (a search session) is busy; sessions end 30 s after their client leaves.
- §3.7 scheduling: search sessions belong to the connection that started them and stop 30 s after it
  disconnects.
- §4.15: at most 500 rendered search rows in QML (the daemon caps results at 5,000); §7.2 bounded reads:
  provider capture 2 MiB, results 5,000, browse JSON 16 MiB.
- §7.3 search sources: nova plugins stay Python scripts the user installs; the README says they run with the
  user's rights (`README.md:213-216`); the daemon runs them exactly as the CLI does today. Torznab arrives in
  P7-01.
- Appendix F determinism: search results by seeders descending, then name, then first provider. `search <q>
  [--wait] [--limit] [--plugins] [--install] [--install-url]`: `search.*` or in-process; starts: no; JSON
  unchanged (plus `providers[]` per result); exit 0, 2, 5.
- §5.7 row 14 (duplicates, mojibake) is fixed here; row 9 (YTS "0" seeds) partly here (`seeds?` absent when
  the source gives none).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fake local providers produce one deduplicated result listing both providers, with the name repaired.
- A disconnected client's session stops after 30 s and its process group is gone.
- A fifth concurrent session gets `busy`.
- A client that reconnects within 30 s resubscribes and gets the retained results.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `contracts/ipc/v1/search.ndjson`.
- `daemon.py::{search_dedupe_and_repair, search_session_grace, search_fifth_busy, search_process_group_gone}`
  (the last reads `/proc` for the provider pgid and logs it).
- Unit `search::tests::{dedupe_key_btih, dedupe_key_title_size, mojibake_roundtrip}`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-08 (the `search:<id>` topic and `search.done` event ride the bus).
- Consumed by P3-07 (CLI through the daemon with fallback), P3-12 (Search view), P4-07 (dedupe fixes RC §9 row
  14 in the TUI), P7-01 (Torznab as a provider kind).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q20 (open, default wanted): "In your list" on search results (`added`).

## Risks and decisions
- R3: bounded capture and session caps keep provider processes from exhausting the machine.
- DL-05 (search, RSS, Shows, IMDb move into the daemon in P3; the CLI keeps an in-process fallback), DL-17
  (the marketplace is not a goal; the curated list stays), DL-51 (`added` on search results; `+ In your
  list`).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] A client that reconnects within 30 s resubscribes and gets the retained results.

# P3-02: RSS in the daemon

Plan item **P3-02** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4411). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas), P1-12 (Stop rule and idle
exit).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P3-14 (RSS
view).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- RSS runs in the calling process (`src/qbt.rs:547-585`); `rss.json` is written with a lock and atomic rename
  (`src/rss.rs:69-71,93-100`); `rss::stable_id(url)` (`src/rss.rs:175`) is today's `uid`; the refresh timeout
  is at `src/rss.rs:222`. The TUI refreshes on every open (README:50-51; `rss_initial_refresh_pending`,
  `src/tui/mod.rs:193,282`, consumed at `:1921-1924`). RSS shows "0 B" for unknown sizes (RC §9 #4).
- Owner constraint: RSS is feeds and items, no rule engine; checking never downloads (§2.5, §6.2 row 12 Out).
  8 RSS unit tests exist.
- Unverified (§7.2, §10.4): explicit caps on RSS reads; this item adds 4 MiB per feed.

## Goal and user value
A4: the RSS view in the dashboard (P3-14) must not shell out; the daemon owns the feeds and pushes items.
Principle 2 (deliberate downloads): refreshes happen when a client becomes interactive and never add torrents.
The CLI's in-process path stays (P3-07) and edits made there appear in the UIs because the daemon re-reads the
store on mtime change.

## Do (exact steps)
`src/api/ops/rss.rs` over `src/rss.rs`:
1. Operations (A.6): `rss.feeds` → `{feeds: [Feed]}`; `rss.add {url, name?}` → `{feed}` (not idempotent);
   `rss.remove {feed}` → `{}`; `rss.refresh {feed?}` → `{state: "pending"}`; `rss.items {feed, unread_only?}`
   → `{items: [FeedItem]}`; `rss.set_read {feed, item, read}` → `{}` (idempotent); `rss.mark_feed_read {feed}`
   → `{count}` (idempotent); `rss.grab {feed, item, …add args}` as `torrents.add` with `origin: "rss"`,
   marking read only after a successful add.
2. Objects (A.9): `Feed {id (rss::stable_id(url)), name, url, title?, unread, last_refresh_at?, loading,
   error?}`; `FeedItem {id, title, description?, published_at?, size?, link?, magnet?, torrent_url?, read,
   grabbed}`.
3. Topics `rss.feeds` (keyed by `id`) and `rss.items:<feed>` (keyed by `id`), on change (A.7).
4. **Scheduling** (§3.7): refresh each feed once when a client becomes interactive (a TUI says hello, or the
   dashboard window opens) and its `last_refresh_at` is older than 30 minutes; never in the background while
   nobody looks.
5. Reload `rss.json` when its mtime changed before serving (CLI edits appear in the UIs).
6. Feed reads capped at 4 MiB; an oversized feed is refused with `upstream` and the cached items stay.
7. `caps` gains `rss`; contract bookkeeping (`contracts/ipc/v1/rss.ndjson`, `docs/IPC.md`, `api::ops::TABLE`).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.7 concurrency: the stores already lock and merge on save, so a daemon and an in-process CLI can run at
  once; the daemon re-reads a store when its mtime changed before serving it.
- §3.7 scheduling: "On app open" becomes "when a client becomes interactive": refresh each feed once if the
  last refresh is older than 30 minutes (today's rule for Shows, `README.md:36`); no periodic background
  polling while nobody looks, which keeps an idle daemon off the network.
- §3.4.9: RSS item `size` is absent when the source did not provide it (today RSS shows "0 B").
- §4.3.4: the Shows and RSS transfer symbols are the same rows as torrents (`…` queued/waiting, `‖` paused,
  `✓` complete, `+` added earlier); `●` (U+25CF) marks unread.
- Appendix F: `rss list|add|remove|refresh|items` → `rss.*` or in-process; starts: no; JSON unchanged; exit 0,
  2, 5, 6. `rss grab` → `rss.grab`; starts: yes; exit 0, 4, 5, 6. Determinism: feeds by `id`; items by
  `published_at` descending then `id`.
- §2.6 non-goal "RSS rule engine": owner decision; Shows covers episodic follow; revisit only if the owner
  asks (Q5, default no).

## Acceptance criteria
- A local feed fixture refreshes once per interactive connect when stale.
- A CLI edit (`fbittorrent rss add` in-process while the daemon runs) appears in the topic within 2 s.
- An oversized feed is refused with a message and the cached articles stay.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `contracts/ipc/v1/rss.ndjson`.
- `daemon.py::{rss_refresh_on_interactive, rss_cli_edit_visible, rss_oversized_refused,
  rss_grab_marks_read_only_on_success}` (the fixture server counts hits per feed).
- The existing 8 RSS unit tests stay green.

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;

  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on

  value.

- [ ] A CLI edit (`fbittorrent rss add` in-process while the daemon runs) appears in the topic within 2 s.
- [ ] An oversized feed is refused with a message and the cached articles stay.

description:
# P3-03: Shows in the daemon

Plan item **P3-03** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4431). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas), P1-12 (Stop rule and idle
exit).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P3-13 (Shows
view), P6-10 (New-release notifications for Shows).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Shows run in the CLI (`src/main.rs:1022+`) and the TUI; `shows.json` is written with a lock and a three-way
  merge on save (`src/shows.rs:246-262`); `Show::is_stale` (`src/shows.rs:115`) encodes the 30-minute rule
  (`README.md:36`); `Show.quality` exists (`src/shows.rs:62-64`) but only the CLI sets it; the EZTV endpoint
  is hard-coded at `src/shows.rs:547` and the same inline EZTV URL in `src/browse.rs:120` (the EZTV browse
  list served by `search.browse`; one variable redirects every EZTV call)
  (`https://eztv.re/api/get-torrents`); `shows check` keeps a `fresh`/`checked`/`failed` report and exits 5
  when every show fails (`main.rs:1067-1093`). 11 Shows unit tests exist; the TUI read model is `m` (toggle
  read), `M` (mark the show read), `u` (undo the last read).
- W2 "Done when": the inbox survives restarts, a check never downloads anything, and read state and transfer
  state are shown independently.

## Goal and user value
A4 and W2 (follow shows): the dashboard's Shows view (P3-13) reads pushed topics; the inbox semantics the TUI
already has become daemon semantics so both UIs agree; new-release notifications (P6-10) and per-show quality
(P3-18) build on this namespace. Beyond qBittorrent (§2.7 "Show inbox with quality").

## Do (exact steps)
`src/api/ops/shows.rs` over `src/shows.rs`:
1. Operations (A.6): `shows.list` → `{shows: [Show]}`; `shows.follow {query | imdb, quality?}` → `{show}`;
   `shows.unfollow {imdb}` → `{}`; `shows.check {imdb?}` → `{state: "pending"}` then `shows.checked {imdb?,
   new, warnings: [{imdb, message}]}` (A.8) and `mutation.result {new}`; `shows.releases {imdb | inbox: true,
   unread_only?, quality?}` → `{releases: [Release]}`; `shows.set_read {imdb, key, read}` → `{}` (idempotent);
   `shows.mark_show_read {imdb}` → `{count}` (idempotent); `shows.undo_read` → `{restored: {imdb, key}?}` (one
   level, the last read mark; not idempotent); `shows.grab {imdb, key, …add args}` as `torrents.add` with
   `origin: "shows"`.
2. Objects (A.9): `Show {imdb, title, year?, quality?, unread, added_at, counts: {episodes, seen, grabbed},
   last_check_at?, checking, catalogue_complete, warning?}`; `Release {key (S02E03 or S02), show_imdb, title,
   season?, episode?, season_pack, quality?, seeds?, size?, magnet?, candidates?, published_at?, read,
   transfer: enum(none|downloading|queued|paused|done|added_before)}` with `transfer` from the ledger by btih.
3. Topics `shows` (keyed by `imdb`) and `shows.releases:<imdb>` / `shows.releases:inbox` (keyed by `key`,
   `<imdb>/<key>` in the inbox), on change.
4. **The check scheduler**: on interactive connect, check each show whose `last_check_at` is older than 30
   minutes (`Show::is_stale`); never otherwise; a check never downloads.
5. Reload on `(mtime, size, inode)` change of `shows.json` so an in-process CLI edit while the daemon runs
   with `--no-start` appears in the topic (§3.7).
6. `FBT_EZTV_BASE_URL` overrides the hard-coded endpoint (`src/shows.rs:547`) so tests can point it at the
   EZTV fixture server (`regression_tests/fixtures/eztv/*.json`, `fixtures.eztv_server()`).
7. `caps` gains `shows`; contract bookkeeping (`contracts/ipc/v1/shows.ndjson`).

## Canonical rules copied in
- W2: on a search result, RSS item or torrent, `f` follows the show; on Shows, `n` follows by name or IMDb id;
  `=` sets the preferred quality per show (P3-18); when a UI opens and the last check is older than 30
  minutes, the daemon checks EZTV; new releases appear in "All unread", newest first; Enter downloads a
  release; `m` marks it read; `u` undoes the last inbox read.
- §3.7 scheduling: check each show whose last check is older than 30 minutes when a client becomes
  interactive; no periodic background polling.
- Appendix F: `shows list|follow|unfollow|check|episodes|seen` → `shows.*` or in-process; starts: no; JSON
  unchanged; exit 0, 2, 5, 6, 7. `shows grab` → `shows.grab`; starts: yes; exit 0, 4, 5, 6. Determinism: shows
  by title; releases newest first then `key`.
- §4.3.4 Shows transfer symbols: `↓` downloading, `…` queued/waiting, `‖` paused, `✓` complete, `+` added
  earlier; `●` unread.
- §0.4 "Does not change": RSS is feeds and items; checking never downloads; IMDb cards without an API key.

## Acceptance criteria
- Inbox semantics match the 11 Shows tests and the TUI read model (`m`, `M`, `u`).
- A check never downloads.
- A check with the daemon idle and no UI does not run (only on interactive connect or explicit `shows.check`).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `contracts/ipc/v1/shows.ndjson`.
- `daemon.py::{shows_inbox_semantics (the step sequence P3-13 replays: four unread newest first, set_read one,
  mark_show_read the inbox, undo_read, grab marks read), shows_check_never_downloads,
  shows_check_only_when_asked, shows_cli_edit_visible}`.
- The existing unit tests.
- Logging (polish round 1): `shows_inbox_semantics` logs one step per operation with the `unread` counts and
  `read` flags observed after each; `shows_check_never_downloads` logs the ledger size before and after the
  check; `shows_check_only_when_asked` logs the EZTV fixture's hit count over 60 s of idle daemon.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-08 (topics) and P1-12 (interactive connect drives the scheduler).
- Consumed by P3-07 (CLI), P3-13 (Shows view), P6-10 (new-release notifications).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q5 (open, default no): no automatic download for followed shows. Q26 (open, default stage): the dashboard's
  Shows view stages on Enter (P3-13); the TUI downloads directly.

- DL-05, DL-64 (the dashboard's Shows view stages on Enter like Search and RSS).

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
