title: P3-04: IMDb service in the daemon
description:
# P3-04: IMDb service in the daemon

Plan item **P3-04** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4456). Phase P3; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M2**; topological level 11 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-06 (API v1 server).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P3-10
(Details pane: Overview, Files, Log), P3-12 (Search view), P3-17 (Poster-rich browse grid).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- IMDb runs in the calling process; each process loads the 28.7 MB ratings file `title.ratings.tsv`
  (`src/imdb.rs:117-183`). Sources (no API key, `src/imdb.rs:1-4,13`): the IMDb ratings dataset, the
  suggestion endpoint, Wikipedia summaries (`src/imdb.rs:239,244`). Posters are cached under
  `~/.cache/fbittorrent/posters` (`src/imdb.rs:101-115`) with `std::fs::write` to the final path
  (`src/imdb.rs:111`), which a concurrent in-process CLI lookup can expose half-written to QML.
- Unverified (§7.2, §10.4): explicit caps on IMDb and poster HTTP reads; this item adds 2 MiB per JSON and 8
  MiB per poster.
- QML loads images from local files only (`poster_path` as `file://`; §4.15 "no network from QML").

## Goal and user value
A4 and §2.7 "Poster-rich browsing": one copy of the 28.7 MB index per daemon life instead of one per process;
posters as local files the dashboard (P3-10 Overview, P3-12 Search, P3-17 grid) loads asynchronously. The IMDb
card stays without an API key (owner constraint).

## Do (exact steps)
`src/api/ops/imdb.rs` over `src/imdb.rs`:
1. `imdb.lookup {name | id, refresh?}` → `{card: ImdbCard?}` (A.9: `id, title, year?, kind, rating?, votes?,
   stars?, blurb?, wiki_url?, url, poster_url?, poster_path?`); `refresh: true` re-downloads the ratings index
   and reloads it before answering (for `imdb --refresh`, P3-07), so a running daemon never keeps a stale
   index. Not mutating (`refresh` writes the cache).
2. The ratings index loaded lazily once per daemon life (log line `imdb index loaded`).
3. Posters cached under `~/.cache/fbittorrent/posters/<id>.jpg`, written to a temporary name and renamed
   (atomic; a reader never sees a partial file).
4. Read caps: 2 MiB for the suggestion JSON and the Wikipedia summary, 8 MiB per poster; over → `upstream` and
   the card renders without a poster.
5. `FBT_IMDB_BASE_URL` overrides the suggestion endpoint, the poster CDN and the Wikipedia summary host in one
   go, so tests point them at the fixture `fixtures.imdb_server()` serving
   `regression_tests/fixtures/imdb/{suggest.json, poster.jpg, poster-oversized.jpg, wiki.json}`.
6. `caps` gains `imdb`; contract bookkeeping.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.7 IMDb row: daemon: index loaded lazily once, posters cached as files; `imdb.lookup` returns
  `poster_path` for `file://` loading; CLI while the daemon is down: in-process.
- §3.4.9: IMDb `rating` absent when the source did not provide it.
- §4.15: asynchronous image loading from local poster files only (no network from QML); `Image { asynchronous:
  true; sourceSize }`.
- §5.5.5 TUI poster card rules (unchanged files `src/tui/poster.rs`): lookups debounced 300 ms after the
  cursor rests and cached per release name.
- Appendix F `imdb <name> [--refresh]`: `imdb.lookup` or in-process; starts: no; JSON unchanged; exit 0, 5, 6.
  Exit 5 reachability example: `imdb --refresh` with `FBT_IMDB_BASE_URL` at a closed port (P1-11's
  `exit_code_dictionary_total`).
- §3.9: every store and cache file written through temp, fsync, rename.

## Acceptance criteria
- Two lookups load the index once (log line `imdb index loaded`).
- `poster_path` exists and is under 8 MiB.
- An oversized poster fixture is refused and the card renders without a poster.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit with a fixture TSV: `imdb::tests::ratings_lookup`.
- `daemon.py::{imdb_index_loaded_once, imdb_poster_cap, imdb_poster_atomic (a reader never sees a partial
  file)}` with the local HTTP fixture standing in for the suggestion endpoint and the CDN.
- Logging (polish round 1): `imdb_index_loaded_once` greps the daemon log for `imdb index loaded` and logs the
  count; `imdb_poster_cap` logs the fixture poster's byte size and the error envelope; `imdb_poster_atomic`
  logs every size a concurrent reader observed (must be 0 or the final size).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-06 (a plain request/response op on the server; no topic needed).
- Consumed by P3-07 (CLI), P3-10 (Overview poster), P3-12 (Search poster card), P3-17 (poster grid).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None (IMDb without an API key is the 2026-09-03 constraint).

## Risks and decisions
- §7.2 bounded reads verified here for IMDb and posters (§10.4).
- DL-05.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] `poster_path` exists and is under 8 MiB.
- [ ] An oversized poster fixture is refused and the card renders without a poster.

description:
# P3-05: Settings operations

Plan item **P3-05** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4478). Phase P3; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M2**; topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-06 (API v1 server), P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-11 (Add sheet, drag and drop, handler mode), P3-15 (Settings sheet, Log view,
Help overlay), P5-04 (Global and alternative speed limits (turtle)), P6-09 (Peer port setting and sleep
inhibitor), P6-13 (Clipboard magnet watch (opt-in, A7)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Settings are F6-only in the TUI with three fields (RC §9); the CLI `settings` command writes the config and
  uses `app/setQueue` and `app/restart` over the compat socket (P1-11 keeps that until this item).
  `Config::validate` is `src/config.rs:95`; `max_active_downloads` default 3 (`src/config.rs:15`); `autostart`
  at `src/config.rs:39`.
- After P1-03 restart-class changes (`peer_encryption`, `network_interface`, `peer_port`) restart the engine
  in place with connections surviving (§3.2.8); after P1-08 the `settings` topic exists.

## Goal and user value
The dashboard's Settings sheet (P3-15), the TUI's F6 (P4-07) and the CLI (`settings`, `limits` later) need one
path with one vocabulary: every `Settings` key is the `config.toml` key (DL-61). Live settings apply at once;
restart-class ones restart the engine without dropping clients, which is the daemon's advantage over today's
TUI-hosted engine.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `app.settings.get` → `Settings` and `app.settings.set {any subset}` → `{applied: [str], restart: bool}`
   (A.4) in `src/api/ops/app.rs`, validated by `Config::validate` and refused with `invalid_args` naming the
   key.
2. Live settings apply at once: `max_active_downloads`, `save_path`, `seed_by_default`, `idle_exit_secs`,
   `notify`, `handler`, `clipboard_watch`, `open_command`, the limit keys (P5-04).
3. Restart-class settings (`peer_encryption`, `network_interface`, `peer_port`, listed in
   `Settings.restart_class`) write the config and restart the engine in place (`engine.changed` twice,
   connections stay, §3.2.8).
4. The `settings` topic (A.7, `state` frames on change).
5. `caps` gains `settings`; contract bookkeeping (`contracts/ipc/v1/settings.ndjson`).

## Canonical rules copied in
- A.9 `Settings`: `max_active_downloads: u64`, `peer_encryption: enum(off|prefer|require)`,
  `network_interface: str?`, `save_path: str`, `seed_by_default: bool`, `autostart: bool`, `idle_exit_secs:
  u64` (0 disables the idle net), `notify: bool`, `timeout_secs: u64`, `handler: enum(add|confirm)`,
  `open_command: str` (default `xdg-open`; mpv users set `mpv --keep-open=yes` so a growing file does not end
  playback early, §6.2 row 40, Q15), `clipboard_watch: bool` (P6-13), `peer_port: u64` (P6-09), `show_quality:
  str`, `download_limit_bps?`, `upload_limit_bps?`, `alt_download_limit_bps?`, `alt_upload_limit_bps?`,
  `alt_limits_on: bool` (P5-04), `restart_class: [str]`. Every key is also the `config.toml` key: one
  vocabulary for the file, the API and `fbittorrent settings`.
- §3.2.7 "Running → Starting → Running": restart-class setting or `app.restart {scope: "engine"}` →
  `engine.changed` twice; connections survive. §3.2.8: the API server and the bus belong to the daemon, not
  the engine.
- §3.4.8: live settings are synchronous (`{state: "done"}` after the save and apply); restart-class settings
  are long operations (`pending`, then `mutation.result`).
- A.1: `app.settings.set` is idempotent.
- Appendix F `settings [--max-downloads] [--encryption] [--vpn] [--interfaces] [--idle-secs] [--handler]
  [--clipboard-watch] [--port]`: `app.settings.set` when running; file write when down; starts: only to apply
  live; JSON extended; exit 0, 2. `config`: none; unchanged plus the new keys.
- §3.2.3: `settings` starts the daemon only if a running daemon must apply it; otherwise saved to config and
  applied at next start.

## Acceptance criteria
- An invalid value is refused naming the key.
- The queue limit applies live.
- An encryption change restarts the engine while clients stay connected (they receive `engine.changed`).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `contracts/ipc/v1/settings.ndjson`.
- `daemon.py::{settings_invalid_named, settings_live_queue, settings_restart_class_keeps_clients}`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `settings_*` cases log the `app.settings.set` request and reply, the `settings`
  topic frame and, for the restart-class case, the two `engine.changed` frames and the connection's unchanged
  `instance` as `observed`.
- Added in polish round 1: unit tests `settings::tests::{restart_class_list (equals peer_encryption,
  network_interface, peer_port), invalid_value_names_key (one row per key with a bad value; details.key
  matches the key), live_keys_apply_without_restart}`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-06 (the ops) and P1-08 (the `settings` topic and `engine.changed`).
- Consumed by P3-11 (the `handler` setting), P3-15 (Settings sheet), P5-04 (limit keys), P6-09 (`peer_port`),
  P6-13 (`clipboard_watch`).

## Owner decisions this item rests on

title: P3-06: Staged add
description:
# P3-06: Staged add

Plan item **P3-06** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4495). Phase P3; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M2**; topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-09 (Mutations: refs, pending, confirmed), P1-12 (Stop rule and idle exit).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-11 (Add sheet, drag and drop, handler mode), P3-12 (Search view), P3-13 (Shows
view), P3-14 (RSS view).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Adding is immediate everywhere; the only review is the TUI's add prompt with the F4 seed toggle
  (`README.md:67-69`). omaqbt's magnet confirm popup exists because qBittorrent cannot stage; our daemon can
  (A5, DL-20).
- After P1-09 `torrents.add` creates a ledger record at once and `stage`/`restore` arguments are reserved
  (`invalid_args` until their items land); after P1-12 the busy table exists and must ignore staged torrents.

## Goal and user value
"Deliberately download" (principle 2; §4.8; §2.7 "Deliberate add": dashboard add sheet with files, seed
switch, destination; `Esc` discards without touching files). A staged torrent is paused, outside the queue and
the counts, and never keeps the daemon alive. The dashboard's add sheet (P3-11) and every "Enter stages the
add" in Search, Shows and RSS (P3-12, P3-13, P3-14) rest on these three operations.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `torrents.add {…, stage: true}` creates a staged record (`Torrent.staged: true`, paused, outside the queue,
   excluded from `Summary.counts` except `counts.staged` and from every busy reason of §3.2.10). The flag is
   `Record.staged: bool` (serde default `false`), so a staged record lives in the ledger like any other and
   `torrents.get`, the TUI and the CLI see it with `staged: true`.
2. `torrents.commit {hash, files?, seed?, save_path?}` → `{state: "done"}` applies the choices and joins the
   queue (idempotent).
3. `torrents.discard {hash}` → `{state: "done"}` removes the staged record and **never deletes files** (a
   re-added torrent may point at data that already exists in `~/Downloads`) (idempotent).
4. A staged magnet whose metadata does not arrive within 90 s stays staged with `reason: metadata_timeout` for
   the sheet's "No peers answered yet." [Keep paused] [Discard] state.
5. **Bead review addition (2026-10-18), the lifetime of a staged record:** a staged torrent never keeps the
   daemon alive and the sheet that staged it can vanish without Enter or Esc (a Quickshell reload, a closed
   window, an idle exit), so at daemon start every record with `staged: true` is discarded with the
   `torrents.discard` semantics (record and cached `.torrent` removed, payload files never touched) and one
   log line `info engine staged record discarded at start hash=<h>`; `torrents.commit` and `torrents.discard`
   on a hash that is not staged answer `invalid_state` (A.3's own example, "commit on a non-staged torrent").
6. `caps` gains `staging`; contract bookkeeping: `contracts/ipc/v1/staging.ndjson` with `c2s`/`s2c` pairs for
   `torrents.add {stage: true}`, `torrents.commit` and `torrents.discard`, plus an `expect` model showing the
   staged row absent from every `Summary.counts` bucket but `staged`; `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry;
   `api::ops::TABLE` rows.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.8 the add sheet: (1) `torrents.add {source, stage: true}` creates a staged, paused record that the queue
  and the counts ignore; a magnet gives the hash at once; URLs and files give it with the metadata. (2) The
  sheet shows the name, the size once known (otherwise "resolving metadata… 0:12"), the file list with
  checkboxes in natural order, the seed switch (default `seed_by_default`), and the destination (default
  `~/Downloads`; P6-11 adds a picker with free space); a duplicate answers "Already in your list". (3) Enter
  sends `torrents.commit {hash, files, seed}`; Esc sends `torrents.discard {hash}`. (4) If metadata does not
  arrive within 90 s: "No peers answered yet." [Keep paused] [Discard].
- §3.2.10: staged torrents in the add sheet do not count as `downloading`.
- §9.3 preamble: `commit` on a non-staged torrent is `invalid_state` (A.3 example); a staged torrent answers
  `invalid_state` to `recheck`, `force_start`, etc.
- A.5: `torrents.add` arg `stage: bool?`; `torrents.commit {hash, files?, seed?, save_path?}`;
  `torrents.discard {hash}` (never deletes files). A.9 `Torrent.staged: bool`; `Summary.counts.staged`. A.1:
  `torrents.commit` and `torrents.discard` are idempotent.
- §4.8 why: it matches "deliberately download" and omaqbt's add-stopped-then-confirm flow; quick add stays for
  the popup, the CLI and the magnet handler, where the click itself is the deliberate act (DL-20).

## Acceptance criteria
- Discarding with pre-existing files in the target folder leaves them byte-identical.
- A staged torrent does not keep the daemon alive.
- A staged record does not survive a daemon restart (discarded at start with the log line, payload files
  untouched); `commit` or `discard` on a non-staged hash is `invalid_state`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::{staged_discard_keeps_files, staged_not_busy, staged_commit_joins_queue,
  staged_discarded_at_restart (stage a magnet, restart the daemon, assert the record is gone, the payload
  folder byte-identical and the log line present), commit_non_staged_invalid_state}`
  (`staged_discard_keeps_files` is the §2.7 proof for "Deliberate add"; the two new cases log the ledger
  before and after the restart and the error envelope).
- Logging (polish round 1): `staged_discard_keeps_files` logs the SHA256 of every pre-existing file before and
  after `torrents.discard`; `staged_not_busy` logs `summary.daemon.busy_reasons` and `idle_exit_in_s` with a
  staged torrent present; `staged_commit_joins_queue` logs the `Torrent.state` sequence.
- Added in polish round 1: unit test `ledger::tests::staged_excluded_from_counts_and_busy` (a staged record is
  absent from every `Summary.counts` bucket but `staged`, and from `policy::busy_reasons`).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-09 (the at-add record and the reserved `stage` argument) and P1-12 (staged torrents must not
  count as busy).
- Consumed by P3-11 (add sheet), P3-12, P3-13, P3-14 (Enter stages).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q9 (open, default add immediately): the handler adds; `handler = "confirm"` stages (P3-11). Q26 (open,
  default stage): Shows stages too.

## Risks and decisions
- DL-20 (staged add in the dashboard; quick add in the popup, CLI and handler; `handler = "confirm"` stages
  from the handler too), DL-64 (Shows stages on Enter).

  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] A staged torrent does not keep the daemon alive.

description:
# P3-07: CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback

Plan item **P3-07** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4508). Phase P3; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `cli`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 16 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-11 (The CLI on the API client; contract 1.2.0), P1-15 (The TUI attaches to the
daemon; quit verbs), P3-01 (Search in the daemon), P3-02 (RSS in the daemon), P3-03 (Shows in the daemon),
P3-04 (IMDb service in the daemon).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-18 (Show quality per show and inbox filters), M2 (Every step of W1, W2 and W8
works from the dashboard (v0.3.0)), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The CLI's `search`, `imdb`, `rss *` and `shows *` run in-process and print contract-1.x JSON shapes that
  agents parse today: the qBittorrent-shaped search result (`fileName`, `fileUrl`, `siteUrl`, `descrLink`,
  `engineName`, `nbSeeders`, `pubDate`, `imdb`); `rss list` as `qbt::RssFeed` with its articles
  (`src/qbt.rs:212-221`); `rss items` as `RssArticle` (`qbt.rs:162-176`); `shows list` as `Show::to_json`
  (`src/shows.rs:175-183`); `shows episodes` as `episode_json` (`shows.rs:184-197`); `imdb` as `imdb::Title`
  (`src/imdb.rs:17-28`). Selectors resolve by name substring (`main.rs:1152-1160`); `search --limit` truncates
  after dedupe and sort (`main.rs:686-701`); `shows check` reports `fresh`/`checked`/`failed` and exits 5 when
  every show fails (`main.rs:1067-1093`); legacy mode routes to the WebUI (`src/main.rs:644,649`).
- The TUI refreshes RSS on every open (`rss_initial_refresh_pending`, `src/tui/mod.rs:193,282`, consumed at
  `:1921-1924` → `refresh_rss`) and runs `refresh_shows(false)` in its init batch (`:1666`; the other init
  commands at `:1664-1665` stay); it reads `rss.json` and `shows.json` itself (`qbt.rs:576-578`;
  `tui/mod.rs:219`) until P4-03; the interaction test `rss_initial_check_and_download_dispatch_only_once` is
  at `:3437-3450`.
- After P3-01 to P3-04 the daemon serves these features and their `src/*.rs` functions return A.9 objects.

## Goal and user value
§3.7 and W5: one shape, two sources. Agents keep the shapes they parse today whether or not the daemon runs
(`fbittorrent search` still works for agents without starting a torrent engine, A4); the daemon path and the
in-process path produce byte-identical output. No double refresh: the TUI's on-open refreshes move to the
daemon's "when a client becomes interactive" rule. Ends the M2 chain (P3-07 → P3-18 → P3-16 → M2) and feeds
P4-03.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **One shape, two sources.** New module `src/cli/shapes.rs` (add `src/cli/{mod,shapes,fallback}.rs` to §3.3;
   `main.rs` stays dispatch only) builds today's shapes from the A.9 objects (`SearchResult`, `Provider`,
   `Feed`, `FeedItem`, `Show`, `Release`, `ImdbCard`); both paths produce A.9 objects: the API path receives
   them from the daemon, the in-process path (`src/cli/fallback.rs`) calls the same functions in
   `src/search.rs`, `src/rss.rs`, `src/shows.rs`, `src/imdb.rs` that the daemon's `src/api/ops/*` call. Human
   output comes from the same shaper, so it is identical too.
2. **Additive A.9 fields the old shapes need**: `FeedItem.description?`, `FeedItem.torrent_url?`;
   `Show.added_at`, `Show.counts {episodes, seen, grabbed}`; `Release.season?`, `Release.episode?`,
   `Release.season_pack`, `Release.magnet?`, `Release.candidates?`; `SearchResult.provider_url?`;
   `Provider.full_name?`; `ImdbCard.poster_url?`; `Feed.id` is `rss::stable_id(url)` (`src/rss.rs:175`), so
   nothing is lossy.
3. **Routing** (§3.2.3, §3.7): `hello` with the 200 ms timeout; if it answers `state: running` and the cap the
   verb needs (`search`, `rss`, `shows`, `imdb`), the API path; otherwise (no daemon, `stopping`, `parked`, a
   daemon that lacks the cap) the in-process path; in legacy mode (`engine = "qbittorrent"`, until P4-09) the
   WebUI path stays.
4. `rss grab` and `shows grab` move from `torrents.add` to `rss.grab`/`shows.grab` (results mapped to today's
   `{action, hash, name, feed}`).
5. **Pending operations wait** as today's synchronous CLI does: `rss refresh` subscribes to `rss.feeds` and
   returns when `loading` is false for the feeds it refreshed (the `src/rss.rs:222` timeout); `shows check`
   waits for `shows.checked` and keeps today's `fresh`/`checked`/`failed` report and exit 5 when every show
   fails; `search --install` waits for `mutation.result {installed, failed}`.
6. **Selectors** resolve client-side over `rss.feeds` and `shows.list` (name substring as today; `ambiguous` →
   exit 7). `shows seen` reads the current flag and sends `shows.set_read {read}` with one `ref`; `all` maps
   to `shows.mark_show_read` and `{count}` to today's `marked`.
7. `search --limit` truncates after the shared dedupe and sort as today (`search.start` keeps its default
   limit); `--wait` is complete when `search.done` has arrived; a `search.done` with zero results and
   `warnings` from every provider exits 5 as today. `imdb --refresh` sends `imdb.lookup {…, refresh: true}` so
   a running daemon never keeps a stale index.
8. **Orders** (Appendix F determinism): search results by seeders descending, then name, then first provider;
   feeds by `id`; items by `published_at` descending then `id`; shows by title; releases newest first then
   `key`.
9. **TUI**: remove the "on open" refreshes (`rss_initial_refresh_pending` and `refresh_shows(false)` in the
   init batch), because the daemon refreshes when the TUI's presence connection says hello (§3.7; the
   30-minute rule replaces today's refresh-on-every-open, README:50-51, which the README now says). Until
   P4-03 the TUI reads `rss.json` and `shows.json` itself, so its presence connection subscribes to
   `rss.feeds` and `shows` and reloads both files when a frame arrives. The interaction test
   `rss_initial_check_and_download_dispatch_only_once` becomes `rss_no_initial_refresh`.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.7 table "CLI while the daemon is down": search jobs, provider preferences, RSS, Shows, IMDb, browse lists
  all run in-process, as today.
- §3.2.3: `search`, `imdb`, `rss list/items/refresh/add/remove`, `shows
  list/episodes/check/follow/unfollow/seen` never start the daemon; `rss grab` and `shows grab` do.
- §3.3 module layout: `src/cli/shapes.rs` "today's CLI JSON shapes built from A.9 objects";
  `src/cli/fallback.rs` "the in-process path for search, rss, shows, imdb when the daemon is down".
- Appendix F rows: `search` (unchanged plus `providers[]` per result; exit 0, 2, 5), `imdb` (unchanged; 0, 5,
  6), `rss list|add|remove|refresh|items` (unchanged; 0, 2, 5, 6), `rss grab` (0, 4, 5, 6), `shows
  list|follow|unfollow|check|episodes|seen` (unchanged; 0, 2, 5, 6, 7), `shows grab` (0, 4, 5, 6), `shows
  quality` (new, P3-18), `triage` (in-process shows/rss/search reads when down).
- Appendix F determinism: `NO_COLOR`, `CI` and a non-TTY stdout never change the bytes; `warnings[]` is the
  one field only the API path can carry (removed before the diff).

## Acceptance criteria
- For every verb above, the JSON and human output are byte-identical with and without a daemon against the
  same fixtures (after `warnings[]` is removed).
- Opening the TUI triggers exactly one RSS refresh per stale feed and none for a fresh one.
- A running daemon's `imdb --refresh` reloads the index once (log line).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::{cli_search_both_paths_identical, cli_rss_both_paths_identical, cli_shows_both_paths_identical,
  cli_imdb_both_paths_identical}` (each runs the verb against the fixture servers twice, daemon up and down,
  and diffs stdout; fixtures: P3-01's fake providers, P3-02's local feed, P3-03's EZTV server, P3-04's IMDb
  server).
- `daemon.py::tui_open_one_refresh` (feeds made stale by editing `last_refresh_at` in `rss.json`; the fixture
  server counts hits per feed: exactly one for the stale feed, none for the fresh one).
- `agent_contract.py::{search_json_shape, rss_json_shape, shows_json_shape, imdb_json_shape}` (stored goldens
  of today's shapes under `regression_tests/golden/cli/`, created from the v0.1.2 binary).
- The interaction test `rss_no_initial_refresh`.
- Logging (polish round 1): the `*_both_paths_identical` cases log both stdouts' SHA256 and the first
  differing byte offset on failure; `tui_open_one_refresh` logs the fixture server's per-feed hit counter
  after the TUI opens; the shape goldens log the golden path and a unified diff on mismatch.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-01, P3-02, P3-03, P3-04 (the daemon ops and their A.9 returns), P1-11 (the API client and
  contract framework), P1-15 (the TUI presence connection the refresh rule relies on).
- Consumed by P3-18 (the `shows quality` verb goes through the daemon with fallback), M2, P4-03 (the TUI on
  API v1 takes its search/RSS/Shows/IMDb calls through the daemon).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R4 (drift): one shaper for both paths.
- DL-05 (features in the daemon with a CLI fallback), DL-62.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] For every verb above, the JSON and human output are byte-identical with and without a daemon against the same fixtures (after `warnings[]` is removed).
- [ ] Opening the TUI triggers exactly one RSS refresh per stale feed and none for a fresh one.
- [ ] A running daemon's `imdb --refresh` reloads the index once (log line).

  entry (`services/PluginRegistry.qml:148-163`; the owner's `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json:38` lists the plugin
  only in the bar layout); other kinds load from the key named like the kind (`shell.qml:1333`). Adding an
  `overlay` kind to a bar-widget plugin would break `omarchy-shell shell toggle` routing (OR §6 gotcha 4;
  P7-05 uses a separate plugin id).
- `FloatingWindow` has `minimumSize` and `implicitWidth/Height`
  (`/usr/lib/qt6/qml/Quickshell/_Window/quickshell-window.qmltypes:47-104`). Every Quickshell window has class
  `org.quickshell`, so Hyprland rules match the title (`^fbittorrent$`). A programmatic open does not reliably
  focus the window; omaqbt's `WmFocus.qml:8-17,85-130` is the only known working recipe. Calling
  `shell.hide()` from inside `close()` recurses (OR §6 gotcha 4); the dev gallery does the same split
  (`plugins/dev-gallery/GalleryPanel.qml:286-289`) and is the only first-party `FloatingWindow`
  (`GalleryPanel.qml:71,281`).
- The dashboard window counts as interactive for the idle net (§3.2.10); the bar connection serves it (§4.4
  rule 8).

## Goal and user value
A3: a long-lived surface you keep open on a workspace while watching (an overlay is modal and full-screen and
suits short tasks). This item is the window shell and the dashboard test harness `qs-dashboard.sh`; the views
follow (P3-09 to P3-15). The full app in Omarchy's own look (§0.4 "A dashboard window (Torrents, Search,
Shows, RSS, Settings, Log)").

## Do (exact steps)
1. Add the `panel` kind to the manifest (`kinds: ["service", "bar-widget", "panel"]`, `entryPoints.panel:
   "Dashboard.qml"`, §4.1).
2. `Dashboard.qml` per §4.6: `open(payloadJson)` creating or showing the `FloatingWindow` titled `fbittorrent`
   (`minimumSize` 900×560, `implicitWidth/Height` 1600×900, omaqbt's size, so a floating first open lands in
   the full tier; the owner's tiled half-screen window of about 960 px lands in the chip-row tier, which is
   designed for it); the payload routing `{"view": "torrents"|"search"|"shows"|"rss"|"settings"|"log",
   "query": "…", "hash": "…", "filter": "downloading"}`; `close()` hides it; user-initiated closes go through
   a separate `dismiss()` that calls `shell.hide("oliver.torrents")` through the injected `shell` facade (the
   entry-point `Item`s receive `shell`, `manifest` and the registries as injected properties, `shell-dev.md`
   "Plugin contract").
3. Surfaces of §4.6: the window paints `Commons.Color.background` with text in `Commons.Color.foreground`;
   pane frames use `Border.controlSpec("normal")`; sheets and the help overlay are cards on a
   `Util.alpha(Commons.Color.background, 0.7)` scrim with `Border.surfaceSpec("popups", "border", …)` (the
   `Ui/ConfirmDialog.qml:13-15,52-58` recipe); tooltips use `PanelToolTip`; `Color.popups.background` is never
   used for the window itself (translucent popup alpha would render a see-through application window).
4. The focus ladder: `forceActiveFocus`, `requestActivate` on the backing window, the foreign-toplevel
   `activate`, then a Hyprland focus dispatch by address, giving up after 1.5 s with a log line (omaqbt
   `WmFocus.qml`).
5. `app.client {interactive: true|false}` on visibility (the service's `dashboardVisible`, P2-01).
6. The "not running" empty state: "fbittorrent is not running" with [Start] focused (Enter) → `startDaemon`,
   then the service reconnects.
7. View tabs `1`-`4` and Tab/Shift+Tab (§4.12) with empty placeholder views until P3-09 to P3-15 fill them;
   the Hyprland title-rule note in the README (by default no rule is installed and the window tiles like any
   application; an optional float rule is documented); the keybinding from P2-07.
8. Test hooks (§4.17): `summonView(json)` (the dashboard's `open(payload)` from the CLI without going through
   the shell's summon; guarded by `FBT_TEST_HOOKS=1`) and `state().view = {window: {visible, width, height,
   view}, cursor, selection: [hash], filter}`.
9. **`plugin/tests/qs-dashboard.sh`**: the harness for every dashboard case (summons through `omarchy-shell
   shell summon oliver.torrents '<json>'` or `summonView`, drives keys with `wtype`, reads `state()`, resizes
   with `hyprctl dispatch resizewindowpixel` after `hyprctl dispatch setfloating`, logs through `qs-log.py`;
   opt-in `FBT_TEST_QS=1`, live shell). Assert summoning works with the plugin referenced only from the bar
   layout. Add P2-01's `reload_reconnects` case here.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.12 keyboard model: Esc steps back one layer at a time: dialog, then filter text, then details, then the
  selection; at the top level it does nothing, and `q` closes the window (DL-34: a long-lived window must not
  vanish on a reflex key); Tab and Shift+Tab cycle the four views; `h`/`l` move focus between sidebar, list
  and details; PgUp/PgDn/Home/End are handled by a `FocusScope` with `Keys.priority: Keys.AfterItem` so they
  bubble past the catcher (`GalleryPanel.qml:303-320`).
- §4.2.2 layout grid: three panes on a horizontal axis: sidebar `Style.space(200)`, list (fill), details
  `Style.space(360)`; panes separated by `Style.spacing.panelGap` (14) and framed by `PaneFrame` (a
  `BorderSurface` with `Border.controlSpec("normal")`, padding `Style.spacing.lg`); each pane has a title row
  of `Style.space(30)`; chrome with both side panes docked = 200 + 360 + 2 × 14 + 3 × 16 = **636 px**; with
  the details as a sheet 200 + 14 + 2 × 16 = **246 px**; with the sidebar collapsed to chips and the details
  as a sheet = **16 px**.
- §4.15 hot reload: an open dashboard window closes on a plugin reload; that is accepted. After a hot rescan
  the first summon can run a stale component; `omarchy-restart-shell` before debugging QML.
- §4.11 dashboard column: daemon not running → empty state with [Start]; connecting → "Connecting…";
  reconnecting → rows dimmed and labelled "last known"; stopped recently → empty state with [Start], rows
  dimmed "last known" for the 10 s.
- §2.4: opening the dashboard window starts the daemon (it is an interactive UI). Appendix F `dashboard
  [--view v] [--query q]`.
- Appendix E.2: `plugin/tests/qs-dashboard.sh` covers dashboard behaviour on the live shell; needs the live
  shell, `wtype`; opt-in; added by P3-08..P3-18, P5-02, P6-*.

## Acceptance criteria
- `omarchy-shell shell summon oliver.torrents '{"view":"search","query":"sintel"}'` opens the window on Search
  with that query and keyboard focus inside (typing through `wtype` reaches the field).
- 50 open and close cycles leave the daemon's open file count flat (Sprout's test).
- `app.client {interactive}` follows visibility (daemon `busy_reasons`).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-dashboard.sh::{summon_focus, open_close_50_fd_flat, interactive_follows_visibility}` (opt-in, live
  shell), logging fd counts from `/proc/<pid>/fd` and the focus ladder's step count.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P2-01 (the service singleton, `dashboardVisible`, the IPC hooks).
- Consumed by P3-09, P3-12, P3-13, P3-14, P3-15 (the views live in this window).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- A3 (assumed): `FloatingWindow` in a `panel` kind; no overlay in v1 (P7-05 later). Q17 (open, default both
  designed; tiled is the daily case).

## Risks and decisions
- R12 (medium, low): drag and drop or focus on a Quickshell `FloatingWindow` misbehaves on Hyprland; the focus
  ladder is the mitigation. R2, R3: the dashboard can be disabled by removing the `panel` kind.
- DL-04 (dashboard is a `FloatingWindow` in a `panel` kind of the same plugin), DL-30 (geometry computed:
  panes 200/360, default window 1600×900), DL-34 (`q` closes; Esc never closes the dashboard).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] `app.client {interactive}` follows visibility (daemon `busy_reasons`).

description:
# P3-09: Torrents view

Plan item **P3-09** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4597). Phase P3; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds:
**M2**; topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P2-02 (Store reducer and fixture tests), P2-08 (Design tokens, visual capture
harness and contrast test), P3-08 (Dashboard window shell).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-10 (Details pane: Overview, Files, Log), P3-11 (Add sheet, drag and drop,
handler mode), P5-04 (Global and alternative speed limits (turtle)), P5-07 (Low disk space warning and
`disk_full`), P6-03 (Speed history and sparklines), P6-05 (Force start and queue order), P6-08 (Origin field,
filters, bulk remove, undo for keep-files removal).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- There is no torrent table outside the TUI. omaqbt's `TorrentTable.qml` is the only Omarchy torrent table
  built on the shell's tokens and reviewed by users (§4.18): column widths in `Style.space`
  (`TorrentTable.qml:48-56`), uppercase letter-spaced headers (`:120-135`, using `muted`, which we do not
  adopt), cursor bar + fill (`:205-217`), hash-keyed cursor and in-place `ListModel` patching
  (`:9-15,166-179`), `hideColumns` computed once per width change (`:36-38`), a row named in a failed action
  shows `!` (`:225-226`), sort arrow (`:69-72`). Transmission's filter bar (`gtk/FilterBar.cc:474-482`) is the
  sidebar model. The shell's `ConfirmDialog` defaults focus to the destructive button (`selectedIndex: 1`,
  `Ui/ConfirmDialog.qml:12`) and handles only Esc, arrows, Tab and Enter (`:24-40`); hovering a button selects
  it (`:122`).
- After P3-08 the window exists; after P2-02 the store and `ListModel` mirror exist; after P2-08 `Model.js`,
  `contracts/ui/states.json` and the visual harness exist. `QSG_RENDER_TIMING=1` makes Qt Quick print
  per-frame `time in renderer: … ms` lines to stderr.

## Goal and user value
W1 and W8 in the dashboard: the Torrents view is where the owner lives while watching. Geometry is computed,
not borrowed (DL-30): every width tier keeps NAME ≥ 210 px and column visibility monotonic, so the owner's
tiled ~960 px window is a designed tier, not a degraded one (Q17). Every destructive step confirms with Cancel
focused (DL-25). The frame budget (no frame over 32 ms with 200 rows at 1 Hz) is the shell-safety rule (R3).

## Do (exact steps)
`views/TorrentsView.qml` and
`components/{TorrentTable,PaneFrame,StateText,ProgressRule,KeyHint,EmptyState}.qml` per §4.6:
1. **Top bar**: view tabs with accent-dot badges (`Color.accent` dot plus count), `FilterInput`
   (`Ui/FilterInput.qml`; keeps IME composition working), rates, the turtle indicator after P5-04, the VPN
   pill when binding is configured.
2. **Sidebar** (`Style.space(200)`): the fixed filter order All; Downloading (= `downloading + stalled +
   metadata + checking`); Ready (present from the start, 0 until P5-05); Queued; Paused; Done; Seeding;
   Errors; Waiting for VPN (present only while binding is configured), with live counts from `Summary.counts`,
   zero counts dim and still selectable, `selectedFill` for the active filter, hover-cursor fill for the
   cursor; later "From:" buckets (P6-08); then links to Shows and RSS with unread counts.
3. **Table** of §4.3.2: columns glyph 26, STATE 110, NAME ≥ 210, SIZE 76, PROGRESS 120, ↓ 80, ↑ 80, ETA 64,
   PEERS 56, RATIO 56, ADDED 80 (in `Style.space`; fixed columns without NAME sum to **748 px**); row
   `Style.spacing.popupRowHeight` (28), header `Style.space(30)`, cell padding `Style.space(10)`; numerics
   right-aligned; NAME left-aligned with `ElideRight`, full name in the details pane and a tooltip; glyph +
   word from `contracts/ui/states.json`; `Style.selectedAccentFill` cursor with the `Style.space(3)` accent
   bar at the left; `selectionFill` for multi-select ranges; a row named in a failed action shows `!` in
   urgent until the next key; the progress cell is eight block characters (`█▉▊▋▌▍▎▏` fractions,
   `Style.space(120)` minus the percentage) plus the percentage, "done" at 100 %, an empty bar and "—" when
   unknown; double-click is Enter; no context menus (right-click does nothing in the table); the list is a
   `ListView` over the `ListModel` patched in place, `reuseItems: true`, `currentIndex: -1`, the cursor
   painted by the delegate from a hash so a status tick never resets scroll.
4. **Width tiers** of §4.3.3 (in `Style.space` units from `width / Style.effectiveSpacingScale`,
   `Commons/Style.qml:213`):

| Window width | Sidebar | Details | Table columns beyond glyph, STATE, NAME, PROGRESS, ↓ (never hidden) | Chrome | Fixed | List → NAME |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≥ 1600 | docked (200) | docked (360) | SIZE, ↑, ETA, PEERS, RATIO, ADDED | 636 | 748 | ≥ 964 → ≥ 216 |
| 1400 to 1599 | docked | docked | SIZE, ETA, PEERS (↑, RATIO, ADDED hidden) | 636 | 532 | 764–963 → 232–431 |
| 1100 to 1399 | docked | a sheet over the list (Enter opens, Esc closes) | SIZE, ETA, PEERS | 246 | 532 | 854–1153 → 322–621 |
| 900 to 1099 | collapsed to a chip row above the table ("All 12 · Downloading 2 · …") | sheet | SIZE, ETA, PEERS | 16 | 532 | 884–1083 → 352–551 |

   Drop order as width shrinks: ADDED → RATIO → ↑ → PEERS → ETA → SIZE; the details pane undocks at 1399
before PEERS would be dropped (the pane costs 360 + 14 + 16 = 390 px, PEERS 56). Why ↑ goes at 1400–1599: with
↑ kept the fixed columns are 612 px and NAME 152–351 px, below the floor. Hidden columns' values remain in the
details pane and the row tooltip. `hideColumns` computed once per width change.
5. **Sort** with `s` (cycle: Added newest first, then Name, Progress, ↓, Size, State, ETA; Queue after P6-05),
   `S` reverses, header click sorts by that column (↑, PEERS, RATIO included) on typed values; the sorted
   header in foreground with an arrow glyph; the sort key and direction persist in
   `~/.local/state/fbittorrent/dashboard.json` (plugin-owned, written by `Service.qml` through
   `Quickshell.Io.FileView` with a 500 ms debounce; panels receive no `settings`).
6. The `/` filter; the status rows (`KeyHint` row for the focused pane and the last message with its time,
   which opens the Log view from P3-15; the speed sparkline arrives with P6-03).
7. **Remove dialogs** through `ConfirmDialog` with `selectedIndex: 0` and `y` mapped to `confirmed()` before
   `handleKey` (§4.9): "Remove '<name>'? <size> in <path>" [Cancel] [Remove, keep files]; "Delete '<name>' and
   its files? <size> will be deleted from <dir>. This cannot be undone." [Cancel] [Delete files] in urgent.
8. **Pending rendering** (§4.10) with the braille spinner `⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧` at 8 fps (static "…" under
   `Style.reduceMotion`).
