## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

description:
# P3-10: Details pane: Overview, Files, Log

Plan item **P3-10** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4655). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 15 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-14 (Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters), P3-04 (IMDb service
in the daemon), P3-09 (Torrents view).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-16 (Dashboard smoke, captures, README), P5-02 (Peers views), P5-03 (Recheck),
P5-05 (Ready to watch), P6-01 (Tracker status and reannounce (fork change)), P6-02 (Pieces bar), P7-02 (Move /
set location), P7-03 (Rename display name), P7-06 (Per-torrent download cap).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The TUI shows an IMDb card and details in a side pane at 140+ columns (`src/tui/mod.rs:2223`); the files
  modal has include/skip (`Space`, `1`, `a`, `n`) in index order, not natural order (§5.7 lower-severity
  note). The dashboard has no details yet (P3-09 renders an empty `PaneFrame` in the details slot).
- qBittorrent's property tabs (General, Trackers, Peers, Content, Speed; `qBittorrent
  src/gui/properties/proptabbar.cpp:50-100`) are the model, minus HTTP sources (§2.6) plus Pieces and Log; the
  "Speed" tab's graph becomes the status-line sparkline (P6-03).
- The shell has no Checkbox component (use ☑/☐ text); `wl-copy` copies text; the engine refuses file toggles
  while a torrent is `checking`.

## Goal and user value
W1 inspection: what is this torrent, what is in it, why is it not moving. Overview answers the first (poster,
rating, state and reason, seed switch spelled out), Files the second (natural order, per-file progress, `o`
opens one file), Log the third (P1-14's ring filtered by hash: "why is this torrent not moving" next to the
torrent, where today the message disappears after 8 or 15 s). The detail-topic discipline (subscribe only
while visible) is what keeps per-torrent sampling cheap (§3.4.7).

## Do (exact steps)
`views/DetailsPane.qml`, `components/PosterCard.qml`, and the service and store work they need, per §4.7:
1. **Layout**: the pane is `Style.space(360)` wide, docked right of the list while the window is 1,400 px or
   wider and a sheet over the list below that (§4.3.3; Enter opens the sheet, Esc closes it; the sheet is
   `min(window − 2 × panelGap, Style.space(720))` wide on the §4.6 scrim). The docked pane follows the list
   cursor after a 150 ms debounce; its edge drags between `Style.space(300)` and `Style.space(480)` and stops
   where NAME would drop below 210 px; the width persists in `~/.local/state/fbittorrent/dashboard.json`
   (`{"details_width": px, "sort": {…}}`, written by `Service.qml` through `Quickshell.Io.FileView` with a 500
   ms debounce). Tabs `[`/`]` from the list or the pane; `h`/`l` move focus (Enter on the list focuses the
   pane in docked mode); keys route by the focused pane (Space, `a`, `n`, `o`, `/` act on the Files tab only
   while the pane has focus); Peers, Trackers and Pieces tabs exist only when `caps` has `peers`, `trackers`,
   `pieces`.
2. **Overview**: from `Torrent` (A.9; `uploaded_bytes` is added to `Torrent` for this tab) and one
   `torrents.get` on open for the `TorrentDetail` extras (`file_count`, `piece_count`, `piece_size`,
   `comment`, `created_by`, `private`, `undo_until`; refetched on `engine.changed`), plus `imdb.lookup {name}`
   once per torrent (debounced 300 ms, cached per `imdb_id` for the session in `Service.qml`; a `null` card
   shows nothing): poster from `poster_path` as `file://` (`Image { asynchronous: true; sourceSize }`), title,
   year, rating, blurb, `i` IMDb and `w` Wikipedia (`openUrl` → `xdg-open`); state word and the reason text of
   §4.3.4; the "Ready to watch · 4 min buffered" / "may stall" line only when `playable` is present (P5-05);
   size, progress, `completed_bytes`, `uploaded_bytes`, ratio, ETA (`Model.js` formats); save path (copy) and
   content path (open with `Settings.open_command`, default `xdg-open`); info hash (copy); added and completed
   as `Model.when(ts)`; the seed `ToggleSwitch` (`u`, `checked` bound to the confirmed `seed`, `busy` while
   pending) with the §4.7 meaning text ("upload capped at 32 KiB/s while downloading; stops when complete",
   "seeding allowed", or "upload capped at N KiB/s" for `upload_policy: custom`); queue position; an action
   row of `Button`s ("Recheck…" from P5-03, "Move…" from P7-02), each hidden when its cap is absent.
3. **Files**: the `torrent:<h>.files` topic (own `subscribe` call; `Store.js` gains the keyed reducer), rows
   sorted by `File.sort_key` (A.9: a plain string compare yields natural order), ☑/☐ text checkboxes, Space →
   `torrents.set_files {hash, include: [i]}` or `{skip: [i]}`, `a`/`n` → include or skip the filtered subset
   (an empty set is allowed; the toggles are disabled while the torrent is `checking`), per-file progress, `o`
   → `torrents.open_target {hash, file}`, a case-insensitive substring filter field (`/` while the pane has
   focus), "resolving metadata…" before metadata; a per-file "ready" dot (P5-05).
4. **Log**: P3-15's `LogView` component embedded with `hash` pre-filtered over the one `log` subscription the
   service holds while any log consumer is visible.
5. **Topics**: the detail topics are subscribed when the pane shows a torrent and unsubscribed when it hides,
   the torrent changes (after the debounce) or the view switches (§3.4.7).
6. **Service and store**: actions `setFiles`, `lookupImdb`, `copyText` (`wl-copy` through `Util.execArgv`),
   `openUrl`, `subscribeDetail(hash, topics)`, `unsubscribeDetail()` in `Service.qml`; `Store.js` reducers for
   `torrent:<h>.files` and the append-only `log` topic.
7. `state().view` gains `details: {tab, hash, width, mode: docked|sheet, files: [index…] (display order),
   poster: loaded|none}`; the `setPaneWidth(px)` test hook (§4.17) sets the width as a drag would.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.7 tab table: Overview (`torrents` + `torrents.get` once + `imdb.lookup`; P3-10); Files
  (`torrent:<h>.files`; P3-10); Peers (`torrent:<h>.peers`; P5-02); Trackers (`torrent:<h>.trackers`; P6-01);
  Pieces (`torrent:<h>.pieces`; P6-02); Log (`log` filtered; P3-10). Why Pieces and Log: Pieces is the one
  view that shows sequential plus first/last working; Log answers "why is this torrent not moving" next to the
  torrent.
- §3.4.7 detail topics exist only while a details view is visible and are closed with `unsubscribe`; per-peer
  and per-piece data are the expensive part; only the visible torrent pays; the server releases a detail
  topic's sampling when its last subscriber leaves.
- §4.3.4 reason phrases: `user` "paused by you"; `queue_full` "waiting for a download slot";
  `complete_no_seed` "complete; seeding is off"; `vpn_down` "waiting for <interface>"; `restore_failed` "could
  not restore: <error>"; `metadata_timeout` "no peers answered"; `missing_files` "files are missing";
  `disk_full` "disk full". `Model.when(ts)`: "12:41 today", "Oct 12", "2025-10-12".
- A.9 `File {index, path, size, progress, included, sort_key, ready?}`; `TorrentDetail` extras; A.5
  `torrents.set_files {hash, include?, skip?}`, `torrents.open_target {hash, file?}` → `{path, kind}`.
- Appendix B: `[`/`]` details tabs (new); Files: toggle / all / none = Space / `a` / `n` (dashboard has no
  `1`); `i`/`w` IMDb/Wikipedia; `y` copy magnet.
- §6.3 row "Better Files view (P3-10, P4-07)": `torrents.files` adds per-file `progress` (exists) and
  natural-sort keys; fixture with E01..E10 out of order.

## Acceptance criteria
- The natural-sort fixture (`E1`..`E10`, unpadded, out of index order) renders in natural order.
- Include/skip persists across a pane reopen and a daemon restart (the ledger's `only_files`).
- The poster renders from its file against the IMDb fixture server.
- The detail topics are unsubscribed when the pane hides (`app.info.subscriptions.by_topic` has no
  `torrent:<h>.*` entry).
- The pane width set through `setPaneWidth` survives `omarchy-restart-shell` and a window reopen.
- `[`/`]` cycle the tabs and the sheet opens at 1,399 px.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-dashboard.sh::{files_natural_order, files_toggle_persists, detail_topic_released, pane_width_persists,
  details_tabs_cycle, details_sheet_below_1400, overview_poster_renders, log_tab_filters_hash}`.
- Fixtures: `regression_tests/fixtures/states/files-natural.json` (a ten-file torrent named
  `E1.mkv`..`E10.mkv` built by `fixtures.multi_file_fixture(names)`, added to `fixtures.py` here) and the IMDb
  fixture server with `FBT_IMDB_BASE_URL`.
- Logging (bead review, 2026-10-18): each `qs-dashboard.sh` case logs `state().view.details` (tab, hash,
  width, mode, the files' display order, poster state) after every key as `FBTQS-STEP` lines;
  `detail_topic_released` logs `app.info.subscriptions.by_topic` before and after the pane hides;
  `files_toggle_persists` logs the ledger's `only_files` before and after the daemon restart.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-09 (the view that hosts the pane), P3-04 (`imdb.lookup` and `poster_path`), P1-14 (the `log`
  topic).
- Consumed by P3-16, P5-02 (Peers tab), P5-03 (Recheck button), P5-05 (ready line and per-file dots), P6-01
  (Trackers tab), P6-02 (Pieces tab), P7-02 (Move…), P7-03 (inline rename), P7-06 (download cap field).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q15 (open, default `xdg-open`; `open_command`).

## Risks and decisions
- R3: detail topics only while visible; posters loaded asynchronously from local files with `sourceSize`.
- DL-30 (details 360; NAME floor 210), DL-62, §4.18 (details tabs borrowed from qBittorrent's
  `proptabbar.cpp`).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The natural-sort fixture (`E1`..`E10`, unpadded, out of index order) renders in natural order.
- [ ] Include/skip persists across a pane reopen and a daemon restart (the ledger's `only_files`).
- [ ] The poster renders from its file against the IMDb fixture server.
- [ ] The detail topics are unsubscribed when the pane hides (`app.info.subscriptions.by_topic` has no `torrent:<h>.*` entry).
- [ ] The pane width set through `setPaneWidth` survives `omarchy-restart-shell` and a window reopen.
- [ ] `[`/`]` cycle the tabs and the sheet opens at 1,399 px.

title: P3-11: Add sheet, drag and drop, handler mode
description:
# P3-11: Add sheet, drag and drop, handler mode

Plan item **P3-11** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4715). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 15 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-05 (Settings operations), P3-06 (Staged add), P3-09 (Torrents view).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-13 (Shows view), P3-16 (Dashboard smoke, captures, README), P6-11 (Destination
picker with free space in the add sheet).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The TUI's add prompt has the F4 seed toggle (`README.md:67-69`); there is no file selection before the
  download starts and no destination choice except `add --save`. `Quickshell.clipboardText` is empty unless a
  Quickshell window has focus, so the service reads the clipboard with `wl-paste --no-newline` (§4.4). Drag
  and drop onto a `FloatingWindow` is unverified on Hyprland (§10.4, R12).
- After P3-06 the daemon has `stage`, `commit` and `discard`; after P3-05 `Settings.handler` exists (`add |
  confirm`, A5).

## Goal and user value
Deliberate downloads (principle 2; §4.8): one Enter more than today, in exchange for seeing what is about to
be downloaded. The sheet is the dashboard's one add path (from `a`, Ctrl+V, drag and drop, Search/Shows/RSS
Enter, and the handler in `confirm` mode). Appendix C has the mockup: "Add torrent /
The.Diplomat.S04.1080p.WEB-DL 8.9 GiB · 8 files / ☑ S04E01.mkv 1.1 GiB … ☐ sample.mkv 40 MiB / Seeding (off)
upload capped at 32 KiB/s, stops when complete / Save to ~/Downloads 412 GiB free / [Discard (Esc)] [Download
(Enter)]".

## Do (exact steps)
`views/AddSheet.qml` per §4.8 "The add sheet":
1. Opened by `a` or Ctrl+V (prefilled from the clipboard through the service's `wl-paste --no-newline` read;
   accepts a magnet, an http(s) URL or a `.torrent` path) and by a `DropArea` on the window (file URLs become
   `{path}`, dropped text is checked for a magnet).
2. Step 1: `torrents.add {source, stage: true}`.
3. Step 2: the name, the size or "resolving metadata… 0:12", the file list with ☑/☐ checkboxes in natural
   order (`File.sort_key`), the seed `ToggleSwitch` defaulting to `Settings.seed_by_default` with the meaning
   text ("upload capped at 32 KiB/s, stops when complete"), the destination (default `save_path`; P6-11 adds
   the picker with free space), "Already in your list" for a duplicate (`duplicate: true`).
4. Step 3: Enter → `torrents.commit {hash, files, seed, save_path}`; Esc → `torrents.discard {hash}` (never
   deletes files).
5. Step 4: after 90 s without metadata "No peers answered yet." [Keep paused] [Discard].
6. **Handler mode**: the `handler = "add" | "confirm"` setting (A5, `Settings.handler`): in `confirm` mode
   `fbittorrent add` from the desktop handler sends `torrents.add {stage: true, origin: "handler"}` and runs
   `fbittorrent dashboard --view torrents --hash <h>` so the sheet opens on it.
7. The sheet is a card on the §4.6 scrim, at most `Style.space(560)` wide, padding `Style.space(18)` (§4.2.2
   dialogs).
8. The P5-07 refusal arrives later: "Needs 8.9 GiB · 1.2 GiB free" in urgent when `size > free_space`.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.8 sources: the popup's `a` and right click → the offer strip (P2-03); the dashboard's `a` or Ctrl+V → the
  add sheet prefilled from the clipboard; drag and drop onto the window (`DropArea`); the `magnet:` handler
  and the CLI: immediate, with a notification (A5); `handler = "confirm"` opens the sheet instead.
- §4.4 clipboard: `Quickshell.clipboardText` is empty unless a Quickshell window has focus, so the service
  reads it with a short-lived `wl-paste --no-newline` process and checks the btih against the store first
  ("Already in your list: <name>", Fragments' dedupe).
- §4.2.2: dialogs are centred cards at most `Style.space(370)` wide for confirms and `Style.space(560)` for
  the add sheet, padding `Style.space(18)`.
- §4.6 surfaces: the add sheet, the details sheet and the help overlay are cards on a
  `Util.alpha(Commons.Color.background, 0.7)` scrim with `Border.surfaceSpec("popups", "border", …)`.
- Appendix B: Add: dashboard `a` or Ctrl+V: add sheet; TUI `a` prompt (F4 seed toggle), `c` from clipboard;
  popup `a` or right click: the offer strip.
- A.5 `torrents.commit {hash, files?, seed?, save_path?}`, `torrents.discard {hash}`; A.9 `Settings.handler:
  enum(add|confirm)`.
- §3.9: QML uses `Util.execArgv` for anything built from data, never `execDetached` with a string.

## Acceptance criteria
- The staged flow works end to end with a local magnet fixture.
- Discard leaves files.
- A `.torrent` dropped from a file manager opens the sheet (manual check; unverified on Hyprland until then).
- In `confirm` mode the handler opens the sheet instead of adding.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-dashboard.sh::{add_sheet_commit, add_sheet_discard, handler_confirm_mode}`.
- `daemon.py::handler_confirm_stages`.
- Manual DnD check logged in the receipt.
- Logging (bead review, 2026-10-18): `add_sheet_commit` and `add_sheet_discard` log the sheet's `state()` and
  the `torrents.add {stage: true}`, `torrents.commit` / `torrents.discard` requests and replies;
  `handler_confirm_stages` logs the handler's argv, the `torrents.add {stage: true, origin: handler}` reply
  and the summon payload; the manual DnD check is one receipt line naming the file dropped and what the sheet
  showed.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-09 (the view), P3-06 (stage/commit/discard), P3-05 (the `handler` setting).
- Consumed by P3-13 (Shows stages into this sheet), P3-16, P6-11 (destination picker in this sheet).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q9 (open, default add immediately): `handler = "add"`; `confirm` is the owner's alternative.

## Risks and decisions

  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

description:
# P3-12: Search view

Plan item **P3-12** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4736). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-01 (Search in the daemon), P3-04 (IMDb service in the daemon), P3-06 (Staged
add), P3-08 (Dashboard window shell).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-16 (Dashboard smoke, captures, README), P3-17 (Poster-rich browse grid), P7-05
(Quick-add and search overlay palette (separate overlay plugin id)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Search exists only in the TUI (screen 2): results from Python providers, a poster card at 100+ columns,
  duplicates and mojibake (D15), hidden columns at 160 (`src/tui/mod.rs:3000,3023`), a stale query shown over
  browse lists (RC §9 defect 14). The TUI keys: `/`, `e` focus query; Enter downloads; `b` browse lists; `P`
  providers; `O` source page; `f`/`F` follow; `i`/`w`; `v` card.
- After P3-01 the daemon streams results on `search:<id>` with `added` (the ledger entry with the same btih,
  DL-51) and `providers: [str]`; after P3-04 `imdb.lookup` returns `poster_path`; after P3-06 Enter can stage.

## Goal and user value
W1 steps 1 to 3 in the dashboard: type a query, results stream in deduplicated with size, seeds, uploaded
date, provider and IMDb rating; resting on a result shows its poster card; Enter stages the result in the add
sheet. "In your list" (`+`) and Enter selecting the existing torrent is the "better than qBittorrent" touch of
DL-51. The M2 demo starts here ("search 'Sintel'; see deduplicated results with posters and IMDb ratings;
Enter stages the add").

## Do (exact steps)
`views/SearchView.qml`:
1. The `FilterInput` query field focused on open and with a `query` payload (`search.start`).
2. Results streamed from the `search:<id>` topic into a `TorrentTable` variant with the columns of §5.6 wide
   (Name, Size, Seeds, ★, Uploaded, Provider) and the `+ In your list` marker for `SearchResult.added` (§4.3.4
   row "in your list": `+`).
3. `s` sorts by Seeds, Size, Uploaded, Name, ★ on typed values; `S` reverses (Appendix B "Sort").
4. The providers sheet (`P`: `search.providers`, `search.set_provider`, `search.install`).
5. Browse lists (`b`: `search.browse_sources`, `search.browse`, shown as rows; P3-17 adds the grid and shows
   the list name in the query box).
6. The poster card on rest (`imdb.lookup` by `imdb_id`, debounced 300 ms; `PosterCard` from P3-10).
7. Enter stages the add (`search.grab {…, stage: true}`) and opens the add sheet, or selects the existing
   torrent when `added` is set.
8. `f` follows the show (`shows.follow {imdb}`); `O` opens `page_url`; `y` copies the magnet (`wl-copy`).
9. The sort, cursor and empty states of §4.11 ("No results for …").

## Canonical rules copied in
- Appendix C Search view (rows) mockup: header `NAME SIZE SEEDS UPLOADED FROM ★`; rows `▸ Sintel 2010 1080p
  BluRay x264 1.4G 812 2011-02 tpb, yts 7.4`, `Sintel 2010 4k FLAC mkv 6.1G 96 2019-06 bitsearch 7.4`,
  `Sintel.2010.720p.WEB 690M 41 2015-01 eztv 7.4`, `… 84 more · 3 providers still searching`; the poster card
  on the right (`Sintel (2010) ★ 7.4 Short film by the Blender Institute`); key row `Enter add  f follow  i
  IMDb  O source  b browse  P providers  Esc back`.
- Appendix B rows: Search: focus query `/` (dashboard); run, or download the result: Enter (stages the add);
  browse lists / providers / source page `b` / `P` / `O` (`P` has no force-start meaning on Search; `s` is
  sort there as everywhere); copy magnet `y`; follow show `f`; IMDb/Wikipedia `i`/`w`.
- §4.15: at most 500 rendered search rows (the daemon caps results at 5,000).
- §3.4.9: `uploaded_at` (search) absent when the source did not provide it; `seeds?` absent when unknown (no
  YTS "0").
- A.9 `SearchResult.added: hash?` (the row shows `+ In your list` and Enter selects that torrent instead of
  adding).
- §4.11: "No results for …" empty state; the dashboard's search field hint in the no-torrents state ("press /
  to search").

## Acceptance criteria
- The fake-provider fixture shows deduplicated rows with provider lists; browse lists load.
- Enter stages one torrent.
- A result whose btih is in the ledger shows `+ In your list` and Enter selects the existing torrent.
- `s` sorts by Seeds, Size, Uploaded, Name, ★ on typed values.
- The query field has focus when the view opens with a `query` payload.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-dashboard.sh::{search_stream, search_browse, search_enter_stages, search_added_marker,
  search_sort_typed, search_focus}`.
- Logging (polish round 1): each `qs-dashboard.sh` case logs `state().view` (rows, cursor, sort, the `added`
  marker) after every key as `FBTQS-STEP` lines; `search_stream` logs the number of `search:<id>` frames
  received and the provider list of the deduplicated row.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-01 (search in the daemon), P3-04 (poster card), P3-08 (the window), P3-06 (Enter stages).
- Consumed by P3-16, P3-17 (the grid replaces the browse rows), P7-05 (the palette reuses the first ten rows).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q20 (open, default wanted): "In your list" on search results. Q14 (open): `P` providers, `y` copy magnet.

## Risks and decisions
- DL-51 (`added` and `+ In your list`), DL-34 (`P` providers on Search; `s` sort on every list; `y` copy
  magnet).

  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  value.

# P3-13: Shows view

Plan item **P3-13** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4756). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 16 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-03 (Shows in the daemon), P3-06 (Staged add), P3-08 (Dashboard window shell),
P3-11 (Add sheet, drag and drop, handler mode).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-16 (Dashboard smoke, captures, README), P3-18 (Show quality per show and inbox
filters).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Shows exist only in the TUI (screen 3): followed shows, an "All unread" inbox, the read model `m`/`M`/`u`,
  the columns RELEASE key, SHOW, QUAL, SIZE, SEEDS, the transfer symbols `↓ … ‖ ✓ +` on help page 3 ("↓
  downloading · … queued/waiting · ‖ paused · ✓ complete · + added earlier"). The Shows IMDb card is squeezed
  to a fixed 9 rows (RC §9 lower-severity note).

  Enter can stage; after P3-11 the add sheet exists.

W2 in the dashboard ("Done when: the inbox survives restarts, a check never downloads anything, and read state

(DL-64; the TUI downloads directly). The M2 demo: "open Shows, set a show's quality to 2160p, mark a release

`views/ShowsView.qml`:
1. A two-pane layout (shows list `Style.space(260)`, releases fill; one pane with a breadcrumb below 1,100 px,

   fields of A.9) and the inbox ("All unread", newest first) as the first row of the shows list.

   unread_by_show, last_read_undoable}`.

   read) on a local port and starts the daemon with `FBT_EZTV_BASE_URL` pointing at it (P3-03's override).

  or gain `●`.

  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in

  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,

  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,

  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

# P3-15: Settings sheet, Log view, Help overlay

Plan item **P3-15** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4801). Phase P3; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `quickshell`; first milestone this item feeds: **M2**;
topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-14 (Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters), P3-05 (Settings
operations), P3-08 (Dashboard window shell).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P3-16 (Dashboard smoke, captures, README), P6-04 (Statistics, session and
all-time), P6-09 (Peer port setting and sleep inhibitor).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Settings were F6-only with three fields (RC §9). Feedback disappears after 8 or 15 s (RC §9 defect 13). Help
  is the TUI's `?` pages. After P3-05 every `Settings` key has an API path and the `settings` topic confirms
  changes; after P1-14 the `log` topic exists; the dashboard keymap is hand-written here in the Appendix B
  schema and generated by P4-02 later.
- Shell controls: `Dropdown`, `TextField`, `ToggleSwitch`, `FilterInput` (`Ui/*.qml`).

## Goal and user value
Three views that complete the dashboard's "full app" job (§2.4): Settings (every key, live), Log (why is it
not moving), Help (`?`, every key of Appendix B). The M2 demo: "open Settings, change max downloads, see it
apply live". The Log view is also what the details pane's Log tab embeds (P3-10).

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`views/SettingsSheet.qml`** (`,` or the menu): every live `Settings` key of A.9 as a shell control:
   `Dropdown` for `peer_encryption` (off | prefer | require), `handler` (add | confirm); `TextField` for
   `max_active_downloads`, `idle_exit_secs`, `save_path`, `open_command`; `ToggleSwitch` for
   `seed_by_default`, `notify`, `autostart`, `clipboard_watch`; the VPN interface from `app.network`'s
   `interfaces`; each change sent as `app.settings.set {key}` and confirmed by the `settings` topic;
   restart-class keys show "applies after restart; restarting now" and the connection survives (the limits
   fields arrive with P5-04, the port with P6-09, a Stats section with P6-04).
2. **`views/LogView.qml`**: the `log` topic with `level` and `source` filter chips and a `hash` filter from
   the details pane, newest last, auto-follow.
3. **`views/HelpOverlay.qml`** (`?`): every row of Appendix B's Dashboard column read from
   `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` (hand-written here in the Appendix B schema; P4-02 generates it)
   grouped by scope, on the §4.6 scrim, Esc closes.

## Canonical rules copied in
- Appendix B keymap schema (one shape for `keymap.json` and `robot-docs keys --json`): `{"version": 1,
  "actions": [ … ]}`, the array in the table's row order; each element `{"id": "torrents.remove", "label":
  "Remove, keep files", "scope": "screen:torrents" | "global" | "pane:<screen>.<pane>" | "modal:<kind>" |
  "prompt", "keys": {"tui": ["d", "x", "Delete"], "dashboard": ["d", "x", "Delete"], "popup": ["d", "x",
  "Delete"]}, "note": str?}`; a surface that does not offer the action has `null` in `keys`; keys spelled as
  in the table (`Ctrl+k`, `Shift+Tab`, `F6`, `Space`, `Enter`, `Esc`). P4-02 generates exactly this shape, so
  this hand-written first version needs no migration.
- Appendix B Dashboard column (the rows the help lists): Move `j`/`k`, ↑/↓; Page PgUp/PgDn; First/last
  `g`/`G`, Home/End; Switch screen `1`-`4`, Tab/Shift+Tab; Pane focus `h`/`l`, ←/→; Help `?`; Filter `/`; Back
  one layer Esc; Log `L`; Settings `,`; Turtle `z`; Close `q` (Esc at the top level never closes); Stop
  fbittorrent `Q`, Ctrl+Q; Enter opens details, double-click too; Open `o`; Pause/resume `p`, Space; Seed `u`;
  Remove keep files `d`, `x`, Delete; Remove and delete files `D`; Undo `U` / the toast's button; Bulk remove
  `X`; Add `a` or Ctrl+V; Recheck `R`; Reannounce `e` (Trackers tab); Force start `P`; Queue `K`/`J`,
  Ctrl+k/Ctrl+j, Ctrl+↑/↓; Sort `s`, `S`, header click; Follow show `f`; Show quality: the dropdown;
  IMDb/Wikipedia `i`/`w`; Details tabs `[`/`]`; Poster grid toggle `v`; Files Space / `a` / `n`; Search `/`,
  Enter stages, `b`/`P`/`O`, `y`; Shows Enter, `m`/`M`/`u`, `r`,`R`/`n`,`+`/`x`/`O`, `d`; RSS Enter, `m`/`M`,
  `r`,`R`/`n`/`x`, `d`; Clipboard offer `y`/Esc; Confirm `y` or the focused button; Cancel Esc, Enter on
  Cancel.
- §4.6: the last message row opens the Log view; status line shows "starting", upgrade pending, the idle
  countdown.
- §4.11 dashboard: "Engine failed to start" → banner with the message and "Show log".
- A.9 `Settings` and A.4 `app.settings.set` → `{applied, restart}`; A.7 `log` topic (keyed append-only by
  `seq`); A.9 `LogEntry {seq, ts, level, source, hash?, message}`.
- Appendix B: Settings: TUI F6 (`,` new alias); dashboard `,`. Log (new): `L` in both.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each setting round-trips through the daemon.
- Restart-class changes show "applies after restart; restarting now" and the connection survives.
- The Log view shows an injected error with its source.
- `?` lists every dashboard key of Appendix B.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `qs-dashboard.sh::{settings_roundtrip_each, settings_restart_class_banner, log_view_filter,
  help_lists_every_key}`.
- `contracts/ipc/v1/settings.ndjson`.
- Logging (bead review, 2026-10-18): `settings_roundtrip_each` logs, per key, the `app.settings.set` request,
  its reply and the `settings` topic frame; `settings_restart_class_banner` logs the banner text and the
  connection's unchanged `instance`; `log_view_filter` logs the injected entry and the rows shown under each
  filter; `help_lists_every_key` logs every Appendix B dashboard key it matched and any it did not.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-05 (settings ops), P1-14 (the `log` topic), P3-08 (the window).
- Consumed by P3-16, P6-04 (Stats section in Settings), P6-09 (the port field).

- Q14 (open): `,` settings, `L` log. Q15: `open_command` in Settings.

  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the

  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`

  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,

  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;

  with new names.

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed

  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent

  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.

  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] Enter on a cell stages the add.

fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays

and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want

add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)

  follows shows at 1080p by default and wants 2160p for some (§6.2 row 29, new, T1 dashboard / T2 TUI). The
  inbox has no filters.

§2.7 "Show inbox with quality": followed shows, unread inbox, per-show quality. The owner's real workflow
(1080p default, 2160p for some shows) gets a UI instead of a CLI flag. T1 in the dashboard here; the TUI's `=`

1. `shows.set_quality {imdb, quality: enum(2160p|1080p|720p|480p)?}` → `{show}` (A.6; `null` = default;
   idempotent) saving `Show.quality` and used by the next check as the preferred quality.
2. A `Dropdown` on the show row (2160p, 1080p, 720p, 480p, default) in `ShowsView.qml`.
3. Inbox filter chips (unread only; quality) driving `shows.releases {inbox: true, unread_only, quality}`.
4. CLI `shows quality <show> <q>` (Appendix F: `shows.set_quality` or in-process; starts: no; JSON new; exit
   0, 2, 6, 7); contract patch bump with a `changes[]` entry.
5. The TUI's `=` prompt lands in P4-07 (`shows.set_quality` from the TUI).

  chip row on the inbox; CLI `shows follow --quality`, `shows quality <show> <q>`.

- Setting 2160p on a show persists and the next fixture check prefers 2160p releases.

## Canonical rules copied in

- Logging (polish round 1): the golden test prints the unified diff of any changed render; `lint-sizes.sh`

  (the goldens that prove isomorphism).
