## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- DL-47 (the same split-then-change discipline as P1-02/P1-19).
- RC §10: the seams are visible in the function list; `mod.rs` under 400 lines is the structural outcome.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

Plan item **P4-02** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4881). Phase P4; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item feeds: **M3**;

**Depends on (blocked by):** P4-01 (Isomorphic split of `src/tui/mod.rs`).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P4-04 (Responsive layouts at 80, 120 and 160 columns), P5-03 (Recheck), P5-04
(Global and alternative speed limits (turtle)), P6-01 (Tracker status and reannounce (fork change)), P6-05
(Force start and queue order).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)

running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Footer hints, help text and key handlers are three hand-kept copies of the key map (§1.7); the footer drops
  actions silently at narrow widths (RC §9 defect 11); key meanings change by screen (defect 12). Zellij's
  release notes name exactly this drift as a source of confusion (UX "action legend").
- After P4-01 `src/tui/actions.rs` exists empty; `footer.rs` and `help.rs` are separate files. `RobotDocs` has
  a positional `section` (`src/main.rs:56-60,322-328`). P3-15 hand-wrote `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json`
  in the Appendix B schema.
- Legacy `s`/`f` toggles on Torrents exist until P4-09 (`src/tui/mod.rs:1331-1336` before the split).

## Goal and user value
Principle 7 (same letters everywhere) made machine-checked: one action table generates the footer, the help,
the README keys table and `keymap.json`, so the TUI, the dashboard's `KeyHint` rows and the README cannot
drift (R4). The footer's priority packing with an overflow cue `…` fixes defect 11;
`no_duplicate_key_per_scope` and `global_keys_never_rebound` fix defect 12.

## Do (exact steps)
§5.4 in `src/tui/actions.rs`:
1. Types: `KeyChord { code: ftui_core::event::KeyCode, mods: ftui_core::event::Modifiers }`; `Scope::{Global,
   Screen(Screen), Pane(Screen, Pane), Modal(ModalKind), Prompt}`; `Action { id: &'static str, keys: &'static
   [KeyChord] (primary first, then aliases), scope, label: fn(&TuiApp) -> Option<String> (None hides the
   action), enabled: fn(&TuiApp) -> bool, priority: u8, run: fn(&mut TuiApp) -> Cmd<Msg> }`; every `Action`
   also carries `surfaces: &'static [Surface]` (`Tui`, `Dashboard`, `Popup`) and an optional `surface_note`
   (the popup's "Enter opens the file"), so dashboard- and popup-only rows (popup `w`/`t`) live in the same
   table with `run: None`.
2. Conditional keys are `enabled` closures: the undo toast is `Scope::Screen(..)` with `enabled: |a|
   a.toast.is_some()`; the legacy `s`/`f` toggles are `enabled: |a| !a.cfg.native()` until P4-09 deletes them;
   `y` in a prompt is `Scope::Prompt`.
3. Key dispatch looks up the key in scope order: modal, pane, screen, global; dispatch goes through
   `actions::dispatch` only.
4. `fbittorrent robot-docs keys [--json] [--surface tui|dashboard|popup|all]` (default `tui`) prints the
   Appendix B table in Markdown, or with `--json` the keymap schema. Listed in `capabilities.commands[]`
   (additive, 1.2.x).
5. `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` runs `robot-docs keys --json --surface all` into
   `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` (P3-15's hand-written first version follows the same schema) and
   rewrites the README block between `<!-- keys:begin -->` and `<!-- keys:end -->` (added by this item under
   "Keys").
6. **Footer row 1**: enabled actions of the focused scope in `priority` order (10 Enter/primary, 20 open and
   pause, 30 seed and remove, 40 add and recheck, 90 the rest), each as `(key) Label` separated by two spaces,
   `…` appended when any did not fit, `(?) Help` always reserved at the right; **row 2** is the selected
   item's full name and context (§5.5.4).
7. **Help** lists every action grouped by scope in Appendix B's order, paged with PgUp/PgDn as today's help
   pages.

## Canonical rules copied in
- Appendix B keymap schema: `{"version": 1, "actions": [{"id", "label", "scope": "screen:torrents" | "global"
  | "pane:<screen>.<pane>" | "modal:<kind>" | "prompt", "keys": {"tui": [...], "dashboard": [...], "popup":
  [...]}, "note"?}]}`, action-keyed so that `no_duplicate_key_per_scope`, the README table and Appendix B are
  the same rows; `robot-docs keys --surface <s>` prints the same elements with the other surfaces' `keys`
  omitted.
- Appendix B rules: `u` means "seed" on Torrents and "undo the last inbox read" in the Shows inbox; `U` undoes
  a removal while its toast shows, on every surface (never `u`: a `u` meant for the next row must not silently
  re-add a torrent); `Q` means "quit" everywhere; show quality is `=`; `s` sorts on every list; Search's
  providers sheet is `P`; `no_duplicate_key_per_scope` treats "while the toast shows" as the same scope as the
  screen, so the `u`/`U` split is machine-checked. Until P4-09 removes legacy mode, `s` and `f` on Torrents
  keep their legacy-only meanings when `engine = "qbittorrent"`; in native mode they are free, which is why
  `s` (sort) and `f` (follow) can take them.
- Appendix B exceptions: two, both in the popup (Enter opens the file; `w` opens the dashboard); `q` is not an
  exception; Space is not an exception.
- §5.4 tests: every key a handler accepts appears in the table; no key appears twice in one scope; the
  generated README keys table matches the committed one; `keymap.json` is generated from the same table.
- §5.5.4 typography: bold only for the pane title, the selected row, keys and errors; footer row 2 carries the
  selected row's full name (no marquee, P4-06).
- §9.3 preamble: an item that adds a key regenerates `keymap.json` and the README keys block with
  `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` and adds the Appendix B row.

## Acceptance criteria
- The invariant tests pass.
- The footer shows `…` when actions overflow.
- The README keys table and `keymap.json` match the generated output (test).

## Tests (and what they log)
- `actions::tests::{table_covers_appendix_b (every key in keymap.json for the TUI surface is in the table and
  vice versa), no_handler_outside_table (`rg -c 'KeyCode::Char\(' src/tui/screens src/tui/modals` is 0),
  no_duplicate_key_per_scope, readme_table_matches, keymap_json_matches, global_keys_never_rebound (`q`, `Q`,
  `?`, `1`-`4` mean the same on every screen; modals are not screens, so Files' `1` is allowed)}`.
- Golden `footer-overflow-80x24.txt` with a fixture state that enables nine actions.
- Logging (polish round 1): each invariant test prints the offending key, scope and action id on failure;
  `readme_table_matches` and `keymap_json_matches` print a unified diff of generated vs committed; the
  overflow golden prints the footer line. A `tui_smoke.py` step at 80×24 (P4-10) captures the footer and
  asserts the `…` cue with the pane text as `observed`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P4-01 (the empty `actions.rs` and the separated `footer.rs`/`help.rs`).
- Consumed by P4-04 (layouts dispatch through the table), P5-03 (`R`), P5-04 (`z`), P6-01 (`e`), P6-05 (`P`,
  `K`/`J`).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q14 (open, default as listed): `U`, `=`, `P`, `y`, `q`/Esc.

  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.

  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait

  s; bye{reason:idle}

  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`

  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

# P4-03: The TUI on API v1

Plan item **P4-03** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4916). Phase P4; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item feeds: **M3**;
topological level 17 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-07 (CLI search, RSS and Shows through the daemon, with fallback), P4-01
(Isomorphic split of `src/tui/mod.rs`).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P4-04 (Responsive layouts at 80, 120 and 160 columns), P4-08 (Log modal, toasts
and message history), P4-09 (Remove legacy qBittorrent mode and the compat paths), P5-02 (Peers views), P5-03
(Recheck), P5-04 (Global and alternative speed limits (turtle)), P5-05 (Ready to watch), P5-07 (Low disk space
warning and `disk_full`), P6-01 (Tracker status and reannounce (fork change)), P6-02 (Pieces bar), P6-04
(Statistics, session and all-time), P6-05 (Force start and queue order), P6-09 (Peer port setting and sleep
inhibitor), P7-03 (Rename display name).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- After P1-15 the TUI is a client over the compat socket (`engine.sock`, 4-byte framing, `qbt::Client`, the 2
  s poll at `src/tui/mod.rs:1670-1674`) with a presence connection on `api.sock`; search, RSS, Shows, IMDb and
  browse still run in-process or read the store files (`qbt.rs:576-578`, `tui/mod.rs:219`). The existing
  `SearchSub` turns a background job into messages through an ftui `Subscription` (`src/tui/mod.rs:309-350`).
- After P3-07 the daemon serves every feature namespace and the CLI shaper exists; after P1-11 `api::Client`
  has a reader thread, a `subscribe` iterator and the reconnect ladder; after P2-02 `Store.js`'s reducer
  semantics are fixed by the `contracts/ipc/v1` `expect` models.

## Goal and user value
§5.2 step 2: the TUI as a pure API client (A2): one client contract, no polling, features from the daemon. The
mirror store in `src/tui/store.rs` is tested against the same fixtures as `Store.js`, which is how the two UIs
cannot drift (R4). Every T1 feature after this reaches the TUI through `store.rs` (P5-02, P5-03, P5-04, P5-05,
P5-07) and every T2 feature when cheap (A2). The compat adapter loses its last consumer here, so P4-09 can
remove it.

## Do (exact steps)
1. Replace `qbt::Client` in `src/tui/` by `api::Client` (`src/api/client.rs`, P1-11) with `client.name =
   "tui-<pid>"`, `kind: "tui"`, `interactive: true`; the presence connection becomes the only connection.
2. `src/tui/store.rs` mirrors the `summary`, `torrents`, `network`, `settings`, `rss.feeds`, `shows` topics
   and the detail topics of the visible torrent with the same reducer semantics as `Store.js` (P2-02), tested
   against the same `contracts/ipc/v1/*.ndjson` `expect` models; sorting on typed values lives here (§5.8: the
   ftui table widget's own sort compares cell text and would order "900 MiB" after "1.1 GiB").
3. An `ApiSub` ftui `Subscription` turns frames into `Msg::Api(Event)` (the `SearchSub` pattern); the 2 s poll
   is gone.
4. Search (`search.start` and the `search:<id>` topic), RSS, Shows, IMDb and browse go through the daemon; the
   TUI no longer reads `rss.json`/`shows.json` itself.
5. `Q` sends `app.shutdown {reason: "user"}` (after the confirm when transfers are active, P1-15).
6. A lost connection shows the §4.11 banners: "Connecting…" (first 2 s), "Reconnecting… (retry in N s)" with
   last-known rows dimmed, "fbittorrent stopped" with Enter → `ensure_daemon()`; the version-skew and
   protocol-mismatch banners from `hello` (§3.2.12).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.4.10: the TUI mirrors the same six topics as the plugin (`summary`, `torrents`, `network`, `settings`,
  `rss.feeds`, `shows`) plus details; the 16-subscription bound is why.
- §3.2.11 client rules: on a socket close show "reconnecting" and retry after 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 s (then every
  10 s); a successful reconnect brings a new `instance` id and a fresh snapshot; a mutation in flight at crash
  time is ambiguous: say "result unknown; check the list" and never retry a remove automatically.
- §3.4.7: revision checks (gap → resubscribe the topic; new `instance` → resubscribe all); heartbeats every 15
  s; 45 s of silence is a dead connection; after `engine.changed` a fresh snapshot arrives.
- §3.4.8: a pending mutation renders as a verb in progress on a dimmed row; never the expected end state
  before a delta confirms it.
- §3.7: "on app open" refreshes are the daemon's (when the TUI says hello as interactive); search sessions
  belong to the connection and are retained 30 s after it drops.
- §4.11 banner wording (shared with the popup): "Connecting…"; "Reconnecting… (retry in 4 s)"; "This plugin
  speaks API 1; the running fbittorrent speaks API 2…" (TUI: "this fbittorrent speaks API 1…"); "fbittorrent
  0.2.0 runs; 0.2.1 is installed. Restart to update."; "Waiting for ProtonVPN (proton0). Downloads resume when
  it connects."; "Result unknown; the list will tell."
- Appendix F `tui [--search|--rss|--shows]`: `ensure_daemon`, presence `hello`, then data (compat until P4-03,
  API after); exit 0, 2 (no TTY), 4.
- Appendix D "Presence connection" ends here: it becomes the only connection.

## Acceptance criteria
- `src/tui` no longer uses `qbt::Client` (`rg -n "qbt::Client" src/tui` is empty).
- No 2 s poll.
- The presence connection is the only connection (`app.info.clients.tui == 1` with one TUI).
- The interaction tests pass after adaptation; search, RSS and Shows behave as before.
- `store::tests` pass every `expect` model the QML runner passes.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Interaction tests; `store::tests::fixtures`; the native tmux smoke (P4-10 extends it);
  `daemon.py::tui_single_connection`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `store::tests::fixtures` prints the fixture file, frame index and the first
  differing JSON pointer; `daemon.py::tui_single_connection` logs `app.info.clients` before and after the TUI
  starts; the interaction tests print the `Msg::Api` events they fed.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P4-01 (the split tree with the empty `store.rs`) and P3-07 (search/RSS/Shows/IMDb served by the
  daemon with the CLI shaper; the TUI's on-open refreshes already removed).
- Consumed by P4-04, P4-08, P4-09, P5-02, P5-03, P5-04, P5-05, P5-07, P6-01, P6-02, P6-04, P6-05, P6-09, P7-03
  (every TUI feature that reads a topic or sends an op).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- A2 (assumed): the TUI stays long-term as a pure API client at its current scope plus the T1 features.

## Risks and decisions
- R4 (drift): one store semantics, one fixture set. R2 (when the shell breaks, the TUI still works): this item
  keeps the TUI a full fallback.
- DL-03 (keep the TUI), DL-06 (the compat socket period ends with this item's consumer), DL-29 (ftui 0.6
  suffices).

  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `src/tui` no longer uses `qbt::Client` (`rg -n "qbt::Client" src/tui` is empty).
- [ ] No 2 s poll.
- [ ] The presence connection is the only connection (`app.info.clients.tui == 1` with one TUI).
- [ ] The interaction tests pass after adaptation; search, RSS and Shows behave as before.
- [ ] `store::tests` pass every `expect` model the QML runner passes.

description:
# P4-04: Responsive layouts at 80, 120 and 160 columns

Plan item **P4-04** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4936). Phase P4; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item feeds: **M3**;
topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P4-02 (One action table for keys, footer and help), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P4-07 (Remaining UX defects), P4-10 (Native tmux smoke at three sizes), P4-11
(Poster card rules), P6-01 (Tracker status and reannounce (fork change)), P6-03 (Speed history and
sparklines), P6-08 (Origin field, filters, bulk remove, undo for keep-files removal).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- RC §9 defect 1: below 140 columns state, peers, path and the IMDb card vanish; state is colour-only. The
  Torrents details pane needs 140 columns and the Search pane 100 (`src/tui/mod.rs:2770-2785`); the owner's
  real tiled window is about 90 columns (`screens/tui-real.png`); the UX score is 5.3/10. Mouse hit-testing
  re-derives the layout (`src/tui/mod.rs:796-843`).
- FrankenTUI 0.6 ships `ftui_widgets::table` (rendering, header hit-testing via `TableState::handle_mouse`,
  selection/offset state; its own sort compares cell text, `ftui-widgets-0.6.0/src/table.rs:228-259`),
  `virtualized`, `scrollbar`, and `unicode-width` (the crate ftui uses) for `display_width()`.
- After P4-02 keys dispatch through the action table; after P4-03 the store holds typed values; after P2-08
  `contracts/ui/states.json` carries `text_glyph` and `short`.

## Goal and user value
The owner's window is about 90 columns wide, and today it hides state (§5.7 rows 1 and 4). After this item
every list row has a state cell of glyph + word, width 9, never hidden at any width (§5.5.3), and the details
become a modal at narrow widths. The §5.6 mockups are the goldens. §9.5's P4 human check: "the owner uses the
TUI at 90 columns over SSH and sees state words on every row".

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`src/tui/layout.rs`** with the breakpoints of §5.6 (narrow < 100, medium 100–139, wide ≥ 140) and the
   per-screen column sets:

| Screen | Narrow (80) | Medium (120) | Wide (160) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Torrents | State (9), Name, %, ↓ when live, ETA. No side pane; Enter opens details full-screen (Overview first; `]` reaches Files), `h`/Esc returns. | Adds Size and Peers, and a one-line strip above the footer with the selected torrent's state, reason and path. | Side pane with the IMDb card and details, as today, plus the State column; Size and Peers visible. |
| Search | Name, Size, Seeds, IMDb ★; poster card toggled with `v` | Adds Uploaded and Provider | Side pane with poster; Uploaded, Source and Peers stay visible (today they hide when the pane shows, `src/tui/mod.rs:3000,3023`) |
| Shows | One pane with a breadcrumb ("Shows › It's Always Sunny"); Right/`l` enters, Left/`h` leaves; the episode key column never truncates | Two panes, card under the list | Two panes and the IMDb card at full height |
| RSS | One pane with breadcrumb; episode key at the left of the title, middle elided; size column only when sizes are known | Two panes | Two panes |
| Details (modal) | Tabs Overview · Files · Peers · Log (`[`/`]`), full screen | a modal of 100×30 (full screen under 30 rows) | the side pane plus the same modal on Enter |

   Column widths at narrow: `▌` in column 0, STATE 9, `%` 5, `↓` 6, ETA 6, NAME fills; medium adds SIZE 9 and
PEERS 5, and the one-line strip above the footer (state word · reason phrase of §4.3.4 · queue position · cap
text · path, middle-elided), distinct from footer row 2, which at every width carries the selected item's full
name and context (P4-02). A cell is blank when the value does not apply (`↓` and ETA when `dl_bps` is absent,
§5.7 row 8) and `—` when it applies but is unknown (SIZE before metadata).
2. **The state column** of §5.5.3: `text_glyph` + `short` from `contracts/ui/states.json` (embedded with
   `include_str!`: a contract, not configuration), exactly 9 cells: `◌ Meta`, `⟳ Check`, `↓ Down`, `~ Stall`,
   `… Queue`, `‖ Pause`, `✓ Done`, `↑ Seed`, `⏚ VPN`, `! Error` (bold, the message in the details strip), `!
   Disk` (P5-07), `▶ Ready` replacing `↓ Down` while downloading and playable (P5-05); a spinner runs in the
   footer while metadata resolves.
3. **Rectangles** recorded during render: `layout::Rects { rows: Vec<(hash, Rect)>, headers: Vec<(Column,
   Rect)>, tabs, footer }` per frame, read by `src/tui/mouse.rs` hit testing (a header click sorts, as in
   §4.6).
4. `ftui_widgets::table` for rendering with `sort_column: None` (sorting on typed values in `store.rs`),
   `virtualized` for every list (no threshold; only the visible slice of a long result list is turned into
   `Row`s), `scrollbar` on the right border of every list (visible when content overflows).
5. **The details modal** `src/tui/modals/details.rs`: tabs Overview · Files at this item, Log from P4-08,
   Peers from P5-02, Trackers from P6-01, Pieces from P6-02; `[`/`]` stop at the ends; full screen at narrow,
   a centred 100×30 at medium that falls back to full screen under 30 rows, on Enter at wide too; the 80×24
   mockup of §5.6 is its golden.
6. **The banner slot**: one line above the footer, the §4.11 popup wording, bold with a leading `!` on
   low-chroma themes, priority disk > VPN > stopped/reconnecting > upgrade pending.
7. The width check uses `text.rs::dw` (`unicode-width`) and is the one `state_glyph_width_one` test.
8. Goldens for Search, Shows and RSS at the three sizes and for Torrents at 160 have no mockup in §5.6:
   generate them from the P0-16 fixture here and review them in the receipt; Appendix C's Search and Shows
   mockups at 80 are their targets.

## Canonical rules copied in

removed in polish round 1 so only one version exists)

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

# P4-05: Contrast and low-chroma themes

Plan item **P4-05** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 4971). Phase P4; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M3**; topological level 17 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P2-08 (Design tokens, visual capture harness and contrast test), P4-01
(Isomorphic split of `src/tui/mod.rs`).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M3 (TUI client (v0.4.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D16 / RC §9 defects 2, 3, 16: the TUI's "dim" colour is `dark_foreground` (`#505050`, about 2.6:1 on black)
  even though the theme also ships `muted = #7a7a7a` (about 4.9:1); `theme.rs:66-67` loads `muted` and then
  overwrites it. The owner's active theme has `red = #a4a4a4`, `green = #b6b6b6` (difference 18), so red and
  green collapse; dimmed text is unreadable. `Theme::load` reads `colors.toml` (`src/tui/theme.rs:57-79`,
  `:58`); borders are at `theme.rs:85-86`.
- After P2-08 `contracts/ui/themes/*.toml` and `expected.json` exist (computed by `contrast.py`); after P4-01
  `src/tui/palette.rs` exists empty. Installed themes live under `/usr/share/omarchy/themes/*/colors.toml`;
  `rose-pine`'s foreground is 6.7:1, every other installed theme above 7:1.

## Goal and user value
A8 (the monochrome theme is the design constraint) and principle 4: the TUI uses the same palette and the same
rules as the shell (§5.5), so the TUI's secondary text on the owner's theme becomes `#b6b6b6` (10.4:1),
identical to the popup (Q24), and keys use the grey accent `#8d8d8d` (6.3:1) as the rule says (Q25). One
ladder for both surfaces (DL-31/DL-53), one fixture, ±1 per channel.

## Do (exact steps)
`src/tui/palette.rs`:
1. `palette::dim(fg, bg)` as the §4.2.1 ladder: rung 1 Qt's HSV darken by 1.4 (value × 100 ÷ 140, hue and
   saturation unchanged); rung 2 `mix(fg, bg, 0.75)` per 8-bit sRGB channel, `round(0.75·fg + 0.25·bg)`; rung
   3 the same at 0.85; rung 4 `fg`; the first rung with WCAG ≥ 4.5:1 against `bg`.
2. `palette::accent_text(accent, fg, bg)`: bold `fg` when `accent` is below 4.5:1 against `bg`, or when
   `accent` and `fg` differ by less than 32 in every channel **and** are within 1.3:1 of each other (§5.5.1).
3. `palette::low_chroma(theme)`: red and green differ by less than 32 in every channel (§5.5.2).
4. The roles of §5.5.1 from `Theme::load` (`src/tui/theme.rs:58`); fix D16 (`theme.rs:66-67`): neither `muted`
   nor `dark_foreground` is a text colour now.
5. `theme.rs::colors_path()` looks under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml` before
   `~/.local/state/…` (today it uses `dirs::home_dir()` only, `src/tui/theme.rs:42-46`), so a test can plant a
   theme without reading the owner's (§9.1: fixtures local only).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §5.5.1 colour roles: text = `foreground`; dim (headers, hints, secondary) = `foreground` and `background`
  through the ladder, must reach 4.5:1 (on the owner's theme rung 1 gives `#b6b6b6`, the same hex the shell's
  own panels use); accent (focused border, keys, sorted header) = `accent`, with the two fallbacks above
  (`kanagawa`, whose accent equals its foreground, qualifies; the owner's `#8d8d8d` against `#ffffff` does
  not: channels differ by 114 and the luminance ratio is 3.3, so the grey accent stays; tokyo-night's blue
  accent on grey-white, luminance ratio 1.19 but channel difference 47, does not either; `catppuccin-latte`
  4.3, `miasma` 3.9, `rose-pine` 3.1 fall to bold foreground); a luminance-only rule ("within 2.0:1") would
  strip accent from most dark themes; selection = `selection` (the selected row is also marked by `▌` in
  column 0, so the background is reinforcement); ok/warn/err = `green`/`yellow`/`red`, **used only as
  reinforcement**, collapsing to `text` on low-chroma themes; border = dim, focused pane `accent`
  (`theme.rs:85-86`); poster placeholder = `selection`.
- §5.5.2 low-chroma: on such themes error rows are bold with a leading `!`, success feedback is plain text
  with a `✓`, errors in the status row are bold with `!`, and the seed/rating colouring is dropped. Nothing
  else changes, because every state already has a glyph and a word.
- §4.2.1 token table "Dim text": one ladder, defined there and nowhere else; `contrast.py` computes the
  reference hex per fixture theme into `contracts/ui/themes/expected.json` (`{"owner": {"foreground":
  "#ffffff", "background": "#000000", "accent": "#8d8d8d", "dim": "#b6b6b6", "dim_rung": 1, "dim_ratio": 10.4,
  "fg_ratio": 21.0, "accent_ratio": 6.3, "accent_text": false, "low_chroma": true}}`); QML and TUI must match
  it within ±1 per channel.
- §5.5.1 contrast test: loads every `colors.toml` under `/usr/share/omarchy/themes/` plus the owner's current
  one and asserts the computed dim reaches 4.5:1 and `foreground` reaches 4.5:1 on each (`rose-pine` is 6.7:1,
  so 7:1 is not a gate the TUI can meet; the ratio is printed so a theme below 7:1 is visible in the log).
- §5.5.4: reverse video only for the active tab and for errors on low-chroma themes.

## Acceptance criteria
- The computed dim reaches 4.5:1 and `foreground` reaches 4.5:1 on every installed theme and on the owner's
  (the ratio is logged per theme; `rose-pine` 6.7:1 passes).
- The low-chroma fallback triggers on the owner's theme and not on `tokyo-night`.
- The accent fallback triggers on `catppuccin-latte`, `miasma`, `rose-pine` (below 4.5:1) and `kanagawa`
  (accent equals foreground), and not on the owner's theme (6.3:1, channel difference 114) or `tokyo-night`.
- The dim hex per fixture theme equals `contracts/ui/themes/expected.json` within ±1 per channel.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `palette::tests::{contrast_every_installed_theme, low_chroma_detection, accent_fallback_table,
  dim_matches_fixture}` reading `contracts/ui/themes/*.toml` and, when present,
  `/usr/share/omarchy/themes/*/colors.toml` (the live sweep is skipped with a logged reason off Omarchy; the
  fixture sweep always runs); each logs the theme name and ratio.
- Logging (polish round 1): each `palette::tests` case prints the theme file, the rung chosen, the hex and the
  ratio (`theme=everforest rung=2 dim=#… ratio=4.7`), so a failing theme is identifiable from the test output
  alone.
- Added in bead review (2026-10-18), e2e: `tui_smoke.py::low_chroma_theme_markers` (P4-10's harness) plants
  the owner's monochrome `colors.toml` (`red = #a4a4a4`, `green = #b6b6b6`) under the temp
  `XDG_STATE_HOME/omarchy/current/theme/`, injects an engine error (`FBT_TEST_INJECT_ERROR`, P1-14) and
  asserts the captured pane shows the `! Error` cell and a status row starting with `!`; a second pass with
  `tokyo-night`'s `colors.toml` asserts the status row has no `!` prefix (hue carries the state there); each
  step logs the theme file used and the pane capture as `observed`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P4-01 (the empty `palette.rs`) and P2-08 (the theme fixture and `expected.json`;
  `dim_matches_fixture` lives here because `palette.rs` did not exist then).
- Consumed by M3.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q24 (open, default identical `#b6b6b6`), Q25 (open, default grey accent as the rule says).

## Risks and decisions
- DL-23 (superseded), DL-31/DL-53 (one dim ladder; `muted` and `dark_foreground` never text colours; the TUI's
  text gate is 4.5:1, not 7:1), §5.7 rows 2, 3, 16.

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:

  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.

  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;

  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle

- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`

   footer row 2, P4-02).
2. A hovered name scrolls once at 8 cells/s to its end, then resets to the start and stops.
3. `reduce_motion = true` in `config.toml` (a new key, also in `Settings`) disables scrolling entirely.

- §5.7 row 10: no marquee on the selected row; its full name shows in the second footer row; hover scrolls
  once and stops at the start; `reduce_motion = true` disables scrolling.

- Interaction tests with a fake clock: `marquee_once_then_stops`, `reduce_motion_no_scroll`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `marquee_once_then_stops` prints the rendered name cell at each fake-clock tick

- Depends on P4-01 (the split screen file). It does not depend on P4-02 in the graph; the footer-row-2 name

- Consumed by M3.

- None.

  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.

  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.

  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`

  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,

  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).

  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on

  value.

description:
# P4-07: Remaining UX defects

Plan item **P4-07** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5006). Phase P4; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item feeds: **M3**;
topological level 19 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-01 (Search in the daemon), P3-18 (Show quality per show and inbox filters),
P4-04 (Responsive layouts at 80, 120 and 160 columns).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M3 (TUI client (v0.4.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- RC §9's remaining defects after P4-04/P4-05/P4-06: row 4 (RSS at 80 columns loses the episode id; a "0 B"
  size column); row 8 (SPEED shows the size for inactive torrents); row 9 (misleading counts "0 seeds", "0s",
  RSS "0 B"); row 12 (key meanings change by screen); row 14 (hidden columns at 160; a stale query over browse
  lists); row 17 / D17 (the tab bar spends eight cells on the theme name, which reads "omarchy" because
  `current/theme` is a directory, not a symlink: `src/tui/theme.rs:74-77`; `screens/01-torrents-160x45.txt`
  line 1). Lower-severity notes: the in-app browse lists sit after the Cloudflare-blocked 1337x entry
  (`src/browse.rs:34-36`); the files modal is not natural-sorted; F6 has three fields; the Shows IMDb card is
  squeezed to 9 rows; "(F)ollow show" is offered for non-TV titles. README claims corrected in P0-12 (YTS
  browser-only, UPLOADED column, dedupe) wait to be restored when the code matches.
- After P4-04 layouts exist; after P3-01 search is deduplicated in the daemon; after P3-18 `shows.set_quality`
  exists. `src/tui/format.rs` is empty since P4-01. At 80 columns the tab row has 14 spare cells, not the 21
  the daemon-state text needs.

## Goal and user value
The rest of the 5.3/10 score (§1.5): every remaining UX defect gets a test or a golden. `src/tui/format.rs`
becomes the Rust twin of `Model.js` (§4.2.3), shared with the CLI's human output so `fbittorrent list` and the
TUI print the same strings, with one fixture (`contracts/ui/format.json`) read by both QML and Rust (R4).
D14's README claims are restored where the code now matches (§8.5).

## Do (exact steps)
1. §5.7 row 4: RSS at 80: episode key kept at the left of the title, middle elision, no size column when sizes
   are unknown.
2. Row 8: the rate column blank unless downloading; Size its own column.
3. Row 9: unknown is absent everywhere: no "0 seeds", "0s", "0 B".
4. Row 12: the Appendix B keymap through the action table: `s` sort on every list (Torrents by Added, Name,
   Progress, ↓, Size, State, ETA; Search by Seeds, Size, Uploaded, Name, ★; Shows releases by Date, Seeds,
   Size; `S` reverses), `U` undo (while the toast shows), `=` show quality, `P` providers, `y` copy magnet
   (`wl-copy`), `L` log, `,` settings alias, PgUp/PgDn and Home/End on every list, `g`/`G`, `x` as a remove
   alias, `f` follow on Torrents.
5. Row 14: columns kept at 160 (Uploaded, Source, Peers stay visible with the pane); the browse list name in
   the query box.
6. Row 17: the tab bar shows the daemon state from `Summary.daemon` ("idle · stops in 4 min", "waiting for
   VPN"); the theme name is dropped; the state text takes the place of the rate text, which it replaces only
   while both rates are 0 or the engine is parked (a transferring daemon needs no state word; DL-69).
7. Lower-severity notes: browse lists before 1337x (`src/browse.rs:34-36`); natural sort in the files modal
   (`File.sort_key`); F6 gains save path, seed default, idle exit (limits in P5-04, port in P6-09); the Shows
   IMDb card takes the height it needs; "(F)ollow show" only for TV titles; unread badges on tabs with ftui
   `badge` (§5.8).
8. **`src/tui/format.rs`**: sizes, rates, ETA and percent as §4.2.3 defines them (the Rust twin of
   `Model.js`), shared with the CLI's human output (`fbittorrent list`). Create `contracts/ui/format.json`:
   one object per case `{input, kind, expect}`, read by both `format::tests` and `qs-format.sh`.
9. The Shows quality prompt (`=`, P3-18's TUI side → `shows.set_quality`).

    hash).

  h 05", "2 d" (never seconds above a minute; never "∞": absent renders "—"); percentages as integers below
  99.5 and "99.9" above; counts with thin spaces above 9,999; `text.rs::when` ("12:41 today", "Oct 12",
  "2025-10-12") and `text.rs::ago` ("12 s ago").
- §5.5.4: numbers follow identical rules to `Model.js` via `src/tui/format.rs`, shared with the CLI's human

  `format.rs` widths so numbers align in every pane.
- §4.3.4 secondary texts the strip and rows use: stalled "no peers" or "no data for 2 min"; queued "3 of 3
  slots busy"; seeding "↑ rate · ratio"; waiting_vpn the interface name; the `reason` phrases.
- Appendix B rows added here: Page PgUp/PgDn (new on lists); First/last `g`/`G`, Home/End; Log `L` (new);
  Settings `,` alias; Remove `x` alias; Sort `s`/`S`; Follow show `f` (new on Torrents); Show quality `=`;
  Copy magnet `y`.
- §8.5: the stale claims of D14 are corrected in P0-12 and restored in P4-07 when the code matches them.
- A.9 `Summary.daemon: {state, idle_exit_in_s?, busy_reasons, upgrade_pending}` (the tab-bar text's source).

# P4-08: Log modal, toasts and message history

Plan item **P4-08** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5032). Phase P4; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item
feeds: **M3**; topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-14 (Daemon log ring, `fbittorrent log`, usage counters), P4-03 (The TUI on API
v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M3 (TUI client (v0.4.0)), P6-08 (Origin field, filters, bulk remove, undo for
keep-files removal).

fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,

toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays

running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

§5.7 row 13 and §6.3 "Execution log (P1-14, P3-15, P4-08)": the TUI's Log modal `L` fed by the daemon log,

   level filter (`warn` → `info` → `debug` → `error` → `warn`; the default shows `warn` and `error`) and `h`

description:
# P4-09: Remove legacy qBittorrent mode and the compat paths

Plan item **P4-09** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5045). Phase P4; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `tui`; first milestone this item feeds: **M3**;
topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P2-01 (Plugin restructure and the shared API client), M1 (First demo (v0.2.0)),
P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M3 (TUI client (v0.4.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never

exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The owner left qBittorrent on purpose (§2.6 "Remote qBittorrent backend: Out"); legacy mode (`engine =
  "qbittorrent"`) is a WebUI client in `src/qbt.rs` (with `src/qbt_tests.rs`, 11 legacy client tests);
  `qbt::Client` branches native/legacy in every method (`src/qbt.rs:278-366`, `547-629`; §1.7). The legacy TUI
  keys are the `s`/`f` toggles and priorities 2 and 3 (`src/tui/mod.rs:1331-1336` before the split); the
  legacy unit text is `src/setup.rs:7-20`; the legacy backend functions are `src/backend.rs`;
  `src/engine/legacy_import.rs` holds `migrate_legacy`, whose completion is recorded in
  `~/.local/share/fbittorrent/legacy-migration.json` on the owner's machine.
- `seq`, `first-last` and `reconcile` already refuse in native mode (`src/main.rs:314-318`); they stay as
  stubs so the CLI contract remains 1.x (DL-14). After P4-03 the compat adapter (`src/api/legacy.rs`, P1-10)
  has no consumer; after M1 the v0.1 plugin is gone.

## Goal and user value
§3.6 v0.4.0: `engine.sock` removed; one transport, one client, one code path per method. Removing legacy mode
deletes the branching that made every change twice as hard (§1.7) and the remote-backend non-goal becomes
structural. The agent contract stays 1.x because the three stubs keep answering.

## Do (exact steps)
1. Delete the legacy WebUI transport and its tests (`src/qbt.rs`, `src/qbt_tests.rs`), the legacy TUI keys
   (`s`, `f` toggles, priorities 2 and 3), the legacy unit text (`src/setup.rs:7-20`) and the legacy backend
   functions (`src/backend.rs`).
2. Remove the `engine.sock` adapter (`src/api/legacy.rs`, P1-10) and the probe in `ensure_daemon()`.
3. Remove `src/engine/legacy_import.rs` after checking on the owner's machine that
   `~/.local/share/fbittorrent/legacy-migration.json` records a completed migration (the check and its output
   go in the receipt).
4. Keep `seq`, `first-last` and `reconcile` as documented stubs (they already refuse in native mode), so the
   CLI contract stays 1.x.
5. `engine = "qbittorrent"` in `config.toml` becomes an error at startup naming this release.
6. Update the action table (P4-02): the `enabled: |a| !a.cfg.native()` rows for the legacy `s`/`f` toggles are
   deleted; `s` is sort and `f` is follow unconditionally (Appendix B).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.6 migration table: v0.4.0 (M3): `api.sock` daemon; `engine.sock` removed (P4-09); CLI, plugin and TUI all
  API v1.
- DL-14: legacy qBittorrent mode is removed in v0.4.0; `seq`, `first-last` and `reconcile` remain as stubs, so
  the CLI contract stays 1.x.
- P1-11: in legacy mode every command printed "engine = \"qbittorrent\" is deprecated and is removed in
  v0.4.0; see the README" plus a `warnings[]` entry; this item is that release.
- Appendix F: `seq`, `first-last` → none (stubs); exit 2 (`unsupported`); `reconcile` → the P0-07 stub, exit
  0.
- §2.6 non-goals: remote qBittorrent backend (the owner left qBittorrent on purpose); network access to
  fbittorrent (WebUI, TCP API) stays out.
- §9.1 git safety still applies: none of the deletions touches files an agent did not create except through
  this item's reviewed commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- `rg -n "qbittorrent-nox|engine\.sock" src plugin` finds nothing.
- The agent contract checks pass.
- The owner's data opens unchanged.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Full suite; `agent_contract.py::stubs_still_refuse_with_hint`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `stubs_still_refuse_with_hint` logs argv, exit code and the refusal envelope for
  `seq`, `first-last`, `reconcile`; the receipt carries the `legacy-migration.json` check output and the `rg`
  results.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P4-03 (the TUI no longer uses `qbt::Client` or the compat socket), P2-01 (the plugin no longer
  spawns the CLI; legacy paths in the plugin are gone), M1 (v0.2.0 shipped; the compat period of §3.6 has
  run).

## Owner decisions this item rests on

1. Replace `regression_tests/tui_smoke.sh` with `regression_tests/tui_smoke.py` on `fbtlog.py`: a disposable

   80×24, 120×30 and 160×45 in turn.
2. Per size, the steps: list, state column, details modal (`[`/`]`), files modal, prompts (`d` then Esc),

  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on

  value.
