# P5-01: Seed count and peer list in the engine and API

Plan item **P5-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5095). Phase P5; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `api`; first milestone this item feeds: **M4**;
topological level 12 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** P5-02 (Peers views).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake

`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D6: seeds are always 0 (`num_seeds: 0`, `src/engine.rs:1480`); every peer is a leecher in every UI. P0-11
  removed the lie ("N peers connected"); nothing counts seeds yet. The fork has `per_peer_stats_snapshot`
  (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/torrent_state/live/mod.rs:782`); `PeerStats` carries counters, state, connection
  kind and client name (`live/peer/stats/snapshot.rs:27-32`) but no seed flag; the live peer's `bitfield: BF`
  is at `live/peer/mod.rs:259` and the all-pieces test `has_full_torrent` at `:297-299`; the `From<&Peer>`
  impl is at `snapshot.rs:57`.
- `seeds` means connected seeds (DL-19); no tracker scrape (§2.6).

## Goal and user value
§6.2 row 8 (Peers view, T1): diagnoses slow downloads and makes the seed count true (D6). §2.7 "Truthful bar":
no "0 seeds"; `peers.ndjson`. API-first: this item is the engine and API half; P5-02 is the two UIs. Both land
before M4.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **Fork**: `seed: bool` on `PeerStats` (`snapshot.rs:27-32`) set in the `From<&Peer>` impl (`:57`) from the
   live peer's `bitfield: BF` (`has_full_torrent`).
2. **Daemon** (`src/api/ops/torrents.rs`): `torrents.peers {hash}` → `{peers: [Peer]}` with the `Peer` fields
   of A.9 (`addr`, `client?`, `conn: enum(tcp|tcp_mse)`, `incoming`, `state:
   open(connecting|live|dead|queued)`, `downloaded`, `uploaded`, `dl_bps?`, `ul_bps?`, `seed?`); per-peer
   rates derived from successive `counters` samples one second apart (`per_peer_stats_snapshot`).
3. The `torrent:<h>.peers` topic (A.7: keyed by `addr`, 1,000 ms; a detail topic, sampled only while
   subscribed).
4. `Torrent.seeds` = connected peers with `seed: true` (absent until the engine is live for that torrent,
   §3.4.9; always present afterwards for live torrents).
5. `caps` gains `peers`; `show <sel> --json` gains `seeds` and `peers[]` (Appendix F; the contract-1.x
   `num_seeds` is now filled from `seeds`, DL-69); contract bookkeeping (`contracts/ipc/v1/peers.ndjson`,
   `docs/IPC.md`, `api::ops::TABLE`, patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in

  peer's bitfield; the daemon derives per-peer rates from successive `counters` samples; API `torrents.peers

- Appendix E.2: the fork test runs through `cargo test --locked -p librqbit-core -p librqbit --features

title: P5-03: Recheck
description:
# P5-03: Recheck

Plan item **P5-03** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5126). Phase P5; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M4**;
topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-09 (Mutations: refs, pending, confirmed), P1-16 (Lazy restore of completed
torrents), P3-10 (Details pane: Overview, Files, Log), P4-02 (One action table for keys, footer and help),
P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M4 (T1 complete (v0.5.0)), P6-06 (App-owned fast resume (fork change)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Recheck is implicit on every open and on start after an error (§6.2 row 1); there is no explicit operation.
  The engine already rebuilds and re-checks through `AppEngine::rebuild` (`src/engine.rs:262-277`), called
  today only from the start-error branch at `:756-760` (its "changing upload cap" error wording must be
  generalised); `ManagedTorrent::wait_until_initialized`
  (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/torrent_state/mod.rs:602`) says when a check ends. The TUI's prompt helper is
  `open_prompt` (`src/tui/mod.rs:1255-1280`); only `y` confirms since P0-13.
- After P1-16 completed torrents are dormant; after P1-09 long mutations answer `pending` and
  `mutation.result`; after P3-10 the Overview has an action row; after P4-02/P4-03 the TUI dispatches through
  the action table over API v1.

## Goal and user value
§6.2 row 1 (T1): after a crash, a disk swap or a doubt about data, the user needs an explicit check.
Correctness rules matter more than the button: a recheck that finds missing data must reset completion so
P1-16 can never restore a corrupt torrent as dormant `done`, and completion fires again when the repair
completes. M4 demo: "`R` rechecks after a deliberate corruption and the torrent heals".

## Do (exact steps)
**Daemon** (`src/api/ops/torrents.rs`, `src/engine/ops.rs`):
1. `torrents.recheck {hashes (1..256)}` → `{state: "pending"}` at once, then one `mutation.result {ref, op,
   outcome, result: {rechecked: [hash], failed: [{hash, message}], have_bytes: {hash: bytes}}}` for the call
   (A.8); the work runs in a spawned task outside the ledger lock and off the dispatch pool, one hash at a
   time, through `AppEngine::rebuild` and `wait_until_initialized`.
2. While a hash is being rechecked the daemon holds it in an in-memory `rechecking` set and the §3.5 mapping
   shows `checking` whatever `Initializing { paused }` says; the re-add keeps the record's intent (`paused:
   true` stays paused and never "recovers"; `run` resumes after the check); a recheck never takes a download
   slot (the queue reconciles after the check).
3. If the check finds missing data, `completion_on` is reset to 0 and `completed_at` cleared, so P1-16 can
   never restore a corrupt torrent as dormant `done` and P1-13's completion fires again when the repair
   completes.
4. A dormant torrent (P1-16) is restored with its check, which is the recheck (no second check).
5. Refusals: a staged torrent or one without metadata is `invalid_state`; a hash already in `rechecking`
   answers `pending` with the same outcome; while parked, `engine_unavailable`. A pending recheck is a
   `mutation` busy reason (§3.2.10). `recheck` has no timeout and always ends `done` or `failed` (P1-09).
   Resume files are P6-06's business (it deletes the record's resume file first and depends on this item).
6. `caps` gains `recheck`; contract bookkeeping (`api::ops::TABLE` row: mutating, not idempotent per A.1;
   `docs/IPC.md` changelog; `contracts/ipc/v1/recheck.ndjson`; contract patch bump).
**CLI**: `fbittorrent recheck <sel>… [--wait] [--timeout N]` (Appendix F): exits 0 at `pending` with `{ok,
action: "recheck", count, hashes, pending: true}` (the `act()` shape), or with `--wait` waits for
`mutation.result` and reports `{…, rechecked, failed}`; `all` beyond 256 hashes is sent in chunks of 256; exit
codes 0, 1 (`invalid_state`), 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 (`--wait --timeout`).
**TUI**: `R` on a torrent row (`Scope::Screen(Torrents)`, priority 40) opens the prompt "Recheck '<short(name,
50)>'? It re-reads all data. y/N" through `open_prompt` (only `y` confirms) and sends `torrents.recheck` over
API v1; the row shows `⟳ Check` until the delta.
**Dashboard**: `R` in the list and in the details pane, and the "Recheck…" `Button` in the Overview action row
(§4.7), open `ConfirmDialog` with `selectedIndex: 0`, message "Recheck '<name>'? It re-reads all data.",
`confirmText: "Recheck"`; the row shows "checking…" (§4.10) until the `state: checking` delta; the action is
hidden when `caps` lacks `recheck`.
**Fixture**: `fixtures.corrupt_byte(path, offset)` on a completed local payload of the 256 KiB magnet fixture
(16 KiB pieces, so 16 pieces).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.5 `checking` row: `Initializing { paused: false }`, or any `Initializing` while the daemon holds the hash
  in its `rechecking` set (P5-03).

  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent

  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers

  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`

  value.

# P5-04: Global and alternative speed limits (turtle)

Plan item **P5-04** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5177). Phase P5; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M4**;
topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P3-05 (Settings operations), P3-09 (Torrents view), P4-02
(One action table for keys, footer and help), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M4 (T1 complete (v0.5.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- No global speed limits (`src/engine.rs:417-439`) and no alternative limits (§6.2 rows 5 and 6). `Session`
  exposes `pub ratelimits: Limits` (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/session.rs:140`) with live setters
  `set_download_bps`/`set_upload_bps` (`limits.rs:85-91`), so no fork change is needed. The per-torrent 32
  KiB/s default upload cap (`src/qbt.rs:44`) is separate and must never be lifted by a global setting.
- omaqbt's `z` turtle is the most-used control in that plugin's design (FO §5); the owner named turtle mode as
  one of the OmaTorrent capabilities they like (§2.5). A scheduler is Out (no background schedule fits an
  on-demand daemon; §2.6).
- After P3-05 settings keys have an API path; after P2-03/P3-09 the popup hero and dashboard top bar have the
  turtle slots; after P4-02/P4-03 the TUI dispatches `z` and F6 over API v1.

## Goal and user value
§6.2 rows 5 and 6 (T1): streaming next to a video call; one key (`z`) in every surface toggles the turtle; the
state survives a restart (DL-61). M4 demo: "throttle the connection below the bitrate (`z` with a 200 KB/s
turtle limit)" is also what makes P5-05's "may stall" visible.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `transfer.set_limits {download_bps?, upload_bps?, alt_download_bps?, alt_upload_bps?}` → `{limits: Limits}`
   (each a number, or `null` for unlimited; omitted keys unchanged) and `transfer.set_alt {on}` → `{alt}`
   (A.4; both idempotent), applied live through `Session.ratelimits.set_download_bps/set_upload_bps`.
2. The config and `Settings` keys `download_limit_bps`, `upload_limit_bps`, `alt_download_limit_bps`,
   `alt_upload_limit_bps`, `alt_limits_on` (A.9; the turtle state survives a restart; `transfer.set_alt`
   writes `alt_limits_on`).
3. `Summary.alt: bool` and `Summary.limits: Limits`; the global upload cap never lifts the per-torrent 32
   KiB/s default.
4. `z` toggles `alt` in every surface (Appendix B): the popup hero's turtle button `󰢃` and the tortoise glyph
   after the bar icon's state glyph (P2-04 row "Turtle on"; tooltip "… · turtle limits on"); the dashboard
   top-bar indicator and the Settings sheet's four limit fields (`TextField`, bytes per second with `K`/`M`
   suffixes, empty = unlimited); the TUI's F6 fields and tab-bar turtle glyph.
5. CLI `fbittorrent limits [--down N] [--up N] [--alt on|off] [--alt-down N] [--alt-up N]` (Appendix F:
   `transfer.set_limits`, `transfer.set_alt`; `app.settings.set` when the daemon is down; starts: only to
   apply live; JSON new; exit 0, 2).
6. `caps` gains `limits`; contract bookkeeping (fixture, `docs/IPC.md`, `api::ops::TABLE`,
   `capabilities.commands[]`, patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Global and alternative limits (P5-04)": `session.ratelimits.set_download_bps/set_upload_bps` live;
  config keys with the `Settings` names of A.9 so the turtle state survives a restart; `summary.alt` mirrors
  it; the global upload cap never lifts the per-torrent 32 KiB/s default; tests: unit limits applied to
  `Limits`; `daemon.py::alt_limit_holds` (with a 64 KiB/s alt limit a local transfer stays within ±25 % over
  20 s); `daemon.py::alt_survives_restart`.
- A.9 `Limits {download_bps?, upload_bps?, alt_download_bps?, alt_upload_bps?}`; `Summary.alt`,
  `Summary.limits`.
- §4.2.4 turtle glyph MDI `tortoise` `U+F0883`, shown in the hero and the dashboard top bar when on; §4.5
  "Turtle on" icon row.
- Appendix B: Turtle limits (new, P5-04): `z` in TUI, dashboard and popup.
- §2.6 non-goal: alternative-speed scheduler (no background schedule fits an on-demand daemon; manual turtle
  covers the need).
- §3.4.7 coalescing: `Summary` rates ride the tick; `alt` is structural (goes out at once).

## Acceptance criteria
- A local transfer under a 64 KiB/s alternative limit stays within ±25 % over 20 s after a 5 s warm-up.
- The bar, popup, dashboard and TUI show the turtle state within one push interval.
- The per-torrent 32 KiB/s default is unaffected by a global upload limit of 0 (unlimited).
- The turtle state survives a daemon restart.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit tests on `Limits`; `daemon.py::{alt_limit_holds, global_unlimited_keeps_cap, alt_survives_restart}`
  (logging the measured rate per second); `qs-smoke.sh::turtle_toggle`; TUI interaction test;
  `agent_contract.py::limits_verb`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-05 (settings path and keys), P2-03 (the popup hero's turtle button), P3-09 (the dashboard
  indicator), P4-02 (the `z` action), P4-03 (F6 and `z` in the TUI set limits over API v1).
- Consumed by M4.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None (turtle mode is one of the capabilities the owner named on 2026-10-18).

title: P5-05: Ready to watch
description:
# P5-05: Ready to watch

Plan item **P5-05** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5200). Phase P5; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M4**;
topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-13 (Daemon notifications and the icon), P1-18 (Agent event stream and raw API
verb), P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P2-04 (Bar icon states), P3-10 (Details pane: Overview, Files, Log), P4-03 (The
TUI on API v1), P5-06 (Fork: have-bitfield snapshot accessor).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M4 (T1 complete (v0.5.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Sequential download plus first/last piece priority exists for streaming
  (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/file_info.rs:14-25` computes per-file first pieces from file offsets), but no
  surface tells the user when streaming can start (RC §3 #2). Fragments and qBittorrent have nothing like it.
- After P5-06 the fork exposes `have_pieces_snapshot()`; after P1-13 the notifier exists; after P1-18 `wait
  --until` and `events` exist; after P2-03/P2-04/P3-10/P4-03 every UI has the slot for the badge, the icon
  state, the details line and the state cell.
- A container duration can be read cheaply from `mkv`/`mp4` headers: **unverified** (§10.4); if not,
  `buffered_s` is omitted.

## Goal and user value
A6: "Ready to watch" is a first-class state, the product's reason to exist (§2.7 row "Ready to watch": the row
says "Ready to watch · 4 min buffered" as soon as the contiguous prefix of the largest video file crosses the
threshold, and "Playable · may stall (finishes in 18 min)" while the current rate cannot keep ahead of
playback; a notification offers "Open"; `o` opens it; `wait --until playable` and `--until stall-free` return
for agents). `stall_free` is where "better than qBittorrent" is earned: the notification is deliberately early
(32 MiB is about 30 s of 1080p), so on a link slower than the bitrate the player would stall a minute later
and the owner would learn to ignore the notification; the row text tells the truth per second (DL-39). M4's
demo centrepiece.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **`src/daemon/watch.rs`**: once per second per live incomplete torrent, from P5-06's bitfield snapshot,
   compute the contiguous byte prefix of the largest video file (by extension `mkv mp4 webm avi mov m4v ts`)
   from the file's own first piece (not torrent piece 0; R15).
2. **`playable` in `Torrent`** (A.9 `Playable`): `file: u64`; `ready: bool` when prefix ≥ max(32 MiB, 3 % of
   the file) and the file's last piece is present (DL-26); `prefix_bytes`; `buffered_s = prefix_bytes /
   bitrate` with `bitrate = file_size / duration`, only when a container duration is cheaply available (an
   `mkv`/`mp4` header read of at most 1 MiB; otherwise omitted); `finishes_in_s = (file_size − prefix_bytes) /
   dl_bps` (absent when `dl_bps` is absent or 0); `stall_free = prefix_bytes / bitrate ≥ (file_size −
   prefix_bytes) / dl_bps` (absent when no duration is known or the torrent is not downloading), recomputed
   every second; `acked: bool` set by the acknowledgement rule of §4.5 (the popup or the dashboard was opened
   after the event, `o` was pressed on it in any UI, or it completed). Without a duration the fallback for the
   row text is `dl_bps ≥ file_size / 2 h`, labelled as an estimate in the details line (§3.5). `playable` is
   present only when the `watch` cap exists and metadata is known, and absent for non-video torrents.
3. **The event** `torrent.playable {hash, name, file, open_target, buffered_s?}` (A.8), once per torrent per
   daemon life; after a daemon restart it does not fire again for an already-playable torrent that is still
   incomplete unless the prefix was lost.
4. **The notification** "Ready to watch" with `default` and `open` (play) through P1-13's notifier; the body
   click (`default`) opens the player like its "Open" button.
5. **UIs**: the TUI state cell `▶ Ready` (replacing `↓ Down` while downloading and playable) and the details
   line (`ready ▶ 4 min buffered · (O)pen`); the popup row badge "Ready to watch · 18% · 4 min buffered
   [Open]" (accent, the one glyph allowed to use accent colour on a row) with Enter/`o` opening, and the §4.11
   "Playable, may stall" row "Playable · may stall (finishes in 18 min)"; the dashboard sidebar "Ready" filter
   (counts from `Summary.counts.ready`), the row badge, the Overview line, a per-file "ready" dot in Files
   (`File.ready?`); the bar icon state play-circle-outline while `acked == false` (P2-04); `o` works in both
   wordings.
6. **CLI**: `wait --until playable` keeps the threshold semantics and `wait --until stall-free` is added (exit
   8 on timeout as for every `--until`); `show` carries `playable`; `list` gains `playable` (a new field with
   a new name, contract 1.x); `events` shows the event; `caps` gains `watch`; contract bookkeeping and the
   patch bump (`--until playable` at P5-05, §8.5).
7. The coalesced set (§3.4.7) includes `playable.buffered_s` and `playable.finishes_in_s`; a `ready` or
   `stall_free` flip is structural and goes out at once.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.5 watch-readiness: `playable: {file, buffered_s?, ready, stall_free?, finishes_in_s?, acked}` for the
  largest video file, present only when the `watch` cap exists and metadata is known; the rows show "Ready to
  watch · 4 min buffered" when `stall_free` is true, or unknown with `buffered_s ≥ 120`; "Playable · may stall
  (finishes in 18 min)" otherwise.
- §4.3.4 ready row (overlays `downloading`): QML glyph play-circle-outline, text glyph `▶`, word "Ready to
  watch", `short` "Ready", secondary "4 min buffered" or "may stall".
- §4.3.1: the badge's "4 min buffered" updates with every delta (coalesced like a rate) so the owner can watch
  the buffer grow before pressing `o`.
- §4.5 bar icon "Ready to watch": play-circle-outline in `barForeground`, tooltip "Ready to watch: <name>",
  until acknowledged; the daemon keeps the flag as `Torrent.playable.acked` so the TUI and the bar agree.
- §3.8 notification row "ready to watch": title "Ready to watch", actions `default` and `open` (play).
- A.12 example: `fbittorrent wait 3f2a --until playable --timeout 600 --json` →
  `{"ok":true,"complete":false,"playable":true,"torrents":[{"hash":"3f2a…","playable":{"file":0,"ready":true,"prefix_bytes":41943040,"buffered_s":212},"open_target":"/home/oliver/Downloads/Sintel.2010.1080p.mkv"}]}`.
- Appendix F `wait <sel>… [--timeout] [--interval] [--until complete|playable|stall-free]`: `subscribe
  torrents` (falls back to `torrents.get` polling at `--interval`); extended (`playable`, `complete`,
  `stall_free`); exit 0, 4, 6, 7, 8.
- Appendix E.3 fixtures: the 64 MiB `.mkv`-named fixture (random bytes with a minimal Matroska header for the
  duration read), the `.iso` fixture, the two-file torrent whose second file starts mid-piece (R15), the local
  seed/leech pair with `--throttle`.
- Appendix D "Ready to watch / playable", "Stall-free".

## Acceptance criteria
- With the local seed throttled to 1 MiB/s and a 64 MiB `.mkv` fixture, `torrent.playable` fires with
  `prefix_bytes ≥ 32 MiB` before `torrent.completed`.
- The notification's "open" runs the fake `xdg-open` with the file.
- `wait --until playable` exits 0 before completion.
- An `.iso` fixture never becomes `playable`.
- A paused torrent keeps its `playable` state.
- After a daemon restart the event does not fire again for an already-playable torrent that is still
  incomplete unless the prefix was lost.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit `watch::tests::{prefix_from_bitfield, threshold_rules, largest_video_file, stall_free_rule (table over
  prefix, size, bitrate, dl_bps, logging each row), no_duration_fallback}`.
- `daemon.py::{playable_before_complete, playable_never_for_iso, playable_event_once,
  playable_two_file_mid_piece (the prefix is computed from the video file's own first piece, not torrent piece
  0; R15), wait_until_playable, playable_stall_free_flips (throttle the seed below the bitrate: ready true,
  stall_free false and the row says "may stall"; raise the throttle: stall_free true within 2 s),
  playable_acked_by_open}`.
- TUI goldens with a Ready row and a "may stall" row; `qs-visual.sh popup ready` and `popup may-stall`;
  `agent_contract.py::{wait_until_playable_exit_codes, wait_until_stall_free}`.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P5-06 (the bitfield snapshot), P1-13 (the notifier), P3-10 (details line and per-file dots),
  P4-03 (the TUI state cell over API v1), P2-03 (the popup badge), P1-18 (`events` and the `wait` client),
  P2-04 (the bar icon's ready state driven by `acked`).
- Consumed by M4.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q10 (open, default notify at the threshold; the row says "may stall"): is 32 MiB / 3 % the right moment for
  the notification, or should it wait until playback cannot stall?

## Risks and decisions
- R15 (medium, low): fires too early for high-bitrate files, or never for files whose first piece is shared
  with another file; mitigations: the threshold requires the last piece; `buffered_s` shown when known; the
  per-file first piece from file offsets; the two-file fixture test.
- DL-26 (threshold max(32 MiB, 3 %) plus the file's last piece; one event per torrent per daemon life), DL-39
  (`stall_free` next to `ready`; `wait --until stall-free`).
- §10.4 unverified: cheap container duration from `mkv`/`mp4` headers (omit the field if not).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths

  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by

  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one

# P5-07: Low disk space warning and `disk_full`

Plan item **P5-07** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5252). Phase P5; size

item feeds: **M4**; topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas), P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P2-04
(Bar icon states), P3-09 (Torrents view), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M4 (T1 complete (v0.5.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)

`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- No low-disk warning; `ENOSPC` becomes a raw engine error (§6.2 row 37, new, T1). qBittorrent, Fragments and
  Transmission all warn before it happens; Sprout's "-1 B" free-space bug (OR §6 gotcha 6) is why `free_space`
  is absent when `statvfs` fails or returns a negative value (§3.4.9).
- After P1-08 `Summary` is pushed; after P2-03/P2-04/P3-09/P4-03 every surface has a banner slot (popup
  banner, bar urgent icon, dashboard banner and sidebar "Errors", TUI banner slot of P4-04 with priority disk
  > VPN > …). `Summary.disk` is the one place free space lives (DL-59 cut `Summary.free_space`).

## Goal and user value
The likeliest failure after the VPN for a streaming user with a 3.4 GiB library on a laptop (§6.2 row 37):
principle 4 (truthful state) and error prevention at the one moment they pay off. M4 demo: "fill the
destination with a filler file and the 'Not enough space' banner appears in the popup, the dashboard and the
TUI before any torrent errors; delete the filler and the banner clears."

## Do (exact steps)
1. The supervisor computes `needed = Σ (size − completed_bytes)` over running, incomplete torrents and
   `statvfs` of each distinct `save_path` every 5 s (one syscall per path, no I/O).
2. When `free_space < needed + 512 MiB`: `Summary.disk = {free_bytes, needed_bytes, low: true}` and every UI
   shows the banner "Not enough space for the running downloads: 3.1 GiB needed, 1.2 GiB free" (urgent tint,
   §4.2.3 Banner; §4.11 state "disk low"); the bar icon is urgent.
3. When the engine reports `ENOSPC` the torrent's `state` is `error` with `reason: "disk_full"` and the word
   "Disk full" (§4.3.4 row: `󰀦`/`!`, word "Disk full", `short` "Disk", secondary "1.2 GiB free, 3.1 GiB
   needed"); the dashboard sidebar "Errors" counts it.
4. The add sheet refuses with "Needs 8.9 GiB · 1.2 GiB free" in urgent when `size > free_space` of the chosen
   destination; `fbittorrent add` prints the same in `warnings[]` and exits 0 (the engine may still finish if
   the owner frees space), and `add --json` carries `disk: {free_bytes, needed_bytes}`.
5. A notification "Disk almost full" (`normal`, action `window`) fires once per daemon life (§3.8 row).
6. `start` on a `disk_full` torrent retries; the supervisor also retries automatically when free space rises
   above `needed + 512 MiB` and logs `disk_full_recovered`.
7. Contract bookkeeping: `Summary.disk` and `add --json`'s `disk` are additive fields (patch bump,
   `changes[]`, fixture, `docs/IPC.md`); the `disk_full` reason is a new value of the open `reason` enum.

  space. "Disk full (P5-07, a torrent hit `ENOSPC`)": bar urgent; row `Disk full`; the banner above; dashboard
  sidebar "Errors" counts it.
- §4.3.4 reason phrase `disk_full` "disk full"; §5.5.3 TUI state cell `! Disk`.
- P4-04 banner slot: one line above the footer, bold with a leading `!` on low-chroma themes, priority disk >
  VPN > stopped/reconnecting > upgrade pending.
- §3.8 notification row "disk almost full": title "Disk almost full", action `window`.
- §4.2.3 Banner typography: `Style.font.body`, urgent text on `Util.alpha(urgent, 0.10)` fill with a 0.35

- §4.2.3 sizes in sentences: binary units, "GiB" (never "GB").

- With a 64 MiB tmpfs as `save_path` and a 100 MiB fixture, the banner appears before the first `ENOSPC`, the

  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers

description:
# P6-01: Tracker status and reannounce (fork change)

Plan item **P6-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5288). Phase P6; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds:
**M5**; topological level 19 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-08 (Event bus: subscriptions, snapshots, deltas), P3-10 (Details pane:
Overview, Files, Log), P4-02 (One action table for keys, footer and help), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1), P4-04
(Responsive layouts at 80, 120 and 160 columns).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)), P7-04 (Tracker add and remove (fork change)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- No trackers view and no reannounce (§6.2 rows 2 and 9; RC §8 missing). The fork knows the tracker list
  (`ManagedTorrentShared.trackers: HashSet<Url>`, `vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/torrent_state/mod.rs:186`) but
  records no per-tracker status; tracker comms live in
  `vendor/rqbit/librqbit-tracker-comms/src/tracker_comms.rs`: the HTTP loop's `Ok(interval)`/`Err` at
  `:255-266` (backoff 10 s doubling to 600 s), the UDP path at `:385,400`, the bencoded failure reason at
  `:314`, unsupported schemes dropped at `:160-165`; `TrackerComms::start` is called from
  `Session::make_peer_rx` (`session.rs:1378-1440`); private torrents are truncated to the first tracker
  (`session.rs:1408-1413`); tiers are flattened (`session.rs:1021-1031`). Comms live in the run region and are
  dropped on pause. `rqbit-runtime/src/http.rs:139` echoes the full announce URL in errors, which carries
  private-tracker passkeys (§3.9).
- After P4-04 the TUI details modal exists; after P3-10 the dashboard pane gates tabs on `caps`; after P4-02
  the action table takes modal-scope keys.

## Goal and user value
Diagnose stalls (§6.2 rows 2 and 9): why is this torrent not getting peers? The status view is T2; add/remove
is T3 (P7-04). Passkey hygiene is part of the feature: no query string ever appears in a UI, a log line or a
`message`.

## Do (exact steps)
**Fork** (`tracker_comms.rs`, `torrent_state/mod.rs`):
1. A per-torrent `TrackerStats` (`Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<Url, TrackerStat>>>`) owned by `ManagedTorrentShared`
   next to its `trackers`, so it survives a pause; `TrackerStat { status, last_announce_at:
   Option<SystemTime>, next_announce_at: Option<SystemTime>, peers: Option<u32>, message: Option<String> }`;
   passed into `TrackerComms::start` from `Session::make_peer_rx` and updated at every announce result (the
   HTTP `Ok`/`Err`, the UDP path, the bencoded failure reason).
2. `ManagedTorrent::tracker_stats() -> Vec<TrackerStat>` (sorted by URL) and `ManagedTorrent::announce_now()`
   (no URL argument: the API never passes one), a `Notify` that wakes both the interval sleep and the backoff
   sleep and sends `event=none`; at most one forced announce per tracker per 60 s (later calls are no-ops);
   DHT is untouched.
3. URLs the fork drops appear with `status: not_contacted` and `message: "unsupported scheme"` or `"private
   torrent: only the first tracker is announced"`.
4. The fork unit test lives in `librqbit` (inside CI's `engine-libs` command).
**Daemon** (`src/api/ops/torrents.rs`):
5. `torrents.trackers {hash}` → `{trackers: [Tracker]}` (A.9: `url`, `tier?`, `status: ok | error | updating |
   not_contacted`, `last_announce_at?`, `next_announce_at?`, `peers?`, `message?`), sorted by `url`; for a
   torrent that is not live (paused, done, dormant, metadata, parked) it returns the recorded stats if any,
   else every URL as `not_contacted`; `tier` is absent (the fork flattens tiers; tiers return only if the
   daemon re-reads the `.torrent`, not in this item); `message` capped at 200 characters; every URL in a
   message or a log line has its query string replaced by `?…` before it leaves the fork's error text; `url`
   itself is served complete to the owner's own clients but the UIs display it without the query string.
6. `torrents.reannounce {hashes (1..256)}` → `{state: "done"}` means "triggered"; idempotent (A.1); on a
   torrent that is not live `invalid_state`; while parked `engine_unavailable`.
7. The `torrent:<h>.trackers` topic (A.7: keyed by `url`, 5,000 ms): a status change is structural and goes
   out at once; rates and times ride the tick. `TorrentDetail.tracker_count` counts every URL in the torrent's
   list. `caps` gains `trackers`; contract bookkeeping (`api::ops::TABLE` rows; `docs/IPC.md`;
   `contracts/ipc/v1/trackers.ndjson`; patch bump).
**UIs**:
8. Four rows added to `contracts/ui/states.json`: `tracker.ok` `✓` "OK", `tracker.error` `!` "Error",
   `tracker.updating` `⟳` "Updating", `tracker.not_contacted` `…` "Not contacted".
9. Columns: URL (fill, middle-elided, no query string), STATUS 14 cells / `Style.space(120)`, LAST 10 cells /
   `Style.space(80)` as "12 s ago" (`text.rs::ago`; `Model.ago()` added to `Model.js` here), PEERS 6 cells /
   `Style.space(56)`; `message` on a second dim line under an `error` row; next announce and tier are not
   shown.
10. Dashboard: the Trackers tab in `DetailsPane.qml` (§4.7), subscribed per tab (P5-02's rule), hidden when
    `caps` lacks `trackers`; `e` reannounces the torrent. TUI: `src/tui/modals/trackers.rs` as the Trackers
    tab of the details modal (P4-04), `e` in that tab (`Scope::Modal(Details)`, the Appendix B row
    "Reannounce").
**CLI**: `fbittorrent reannounce <sel>…` (Appendix F): `{ok, action: "reannounce", count, hashes}`, exit codes
0, 1 (`invalid_state`), 4, 6, 7; `show --json` gains `tracker_count` and `trackers[]`.
**Fixture**: `fixtures.tracker_server(fail_first=2, interval_s=5, peers=[seed])`: an HTTP tracker that answers
the first `fail_first` announces of an info hash with a bencoded `failure reason: "fixture: not yet"`, then
valid responses with `interval: 5` listing the local seed, appending `(ts, info_hash, event, port)` to
`<tmp>/tracker.log` for every announce.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §4.7 Trackers tab: URL, status, last announce, peers returned, error; reannounce (`e`); topic
  `torrent:<h>.trackers`; P6-01.
- A.9 `Tracker {url, tier?, status: enum(ok|error|updating|not_contacted), last_announce_at?,
  next_announce_at?, peers?, message?}`; `TorrentDetail.tracker_count?`.
- §3.9: no secret ever appears in argv or logs; the passkey redaction here is that rule applied to tracker
  URLs.
- Appendix B: Reannounce (new, P6-01): TUI `e` in the Trackers tab of the details modal; dashboard `e` in the
  Trackers tab; popup n/a. Appendix F `reannounce <sel>…` (new): `torrents.reannounce`; starts: yes; JSON new;
  exit 0, 1 (not live), 4, 6, 7. Determinism: trackers by `url`.
- §4.18: details tabs borrowed from qBittorrent's `proptabbar.cpp`; the tracker status words are rows of the
  shared state table (DL-32).

- Against the fixture, the first announce shows `status: error` with the failure-reason text and a
  `reannounce` (not the 10 s backoff) turns it `ok` with `peers: 1`, in both UIs.
- A reannounce produces an announce in `tracker.log` within 2 s; a second reannounce within 60 s produces
  none.
- A paused torrent keeps its last recorded status.
- No query string appears in any UI, log line or `message`.

- Fork unit test `tracker_stats_records_error_then_ok` (in `librqbit`).
- `daemon.py::{tracker_status (subscribes to the topic and logs each frame), reannounce,
  reannounce_rate_limited, reannounce_not_live_invalid_state, tracker_url_redacted}`.
- TUI golden `details-trackers-120x30.txt` from fixture state `trackers` (the modal renders at 100×30 at that
  width).
- `qs-dashboard.sh::trackers_tab` (`state().view.details.trackers` lists two rows with the expected status
  words); `agent_contract.py::reannounce_verb`.

- Depends on P1-08 (the detail topic), P3-10 (the dashboard pane), P4-02 (the `e` action), P4-03 (the TUI
  store over API v1), P4-04 (the details modal).
- Consumed by M5 and P7-04 (tracker add/remove).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R8 (fork drift): a fork change in tracker comms. R10 (privacy): passkey redaction.
- DL-32 (one state table gains the tracker rows), A2 (T2 reaches the TUI because the work is small: one modal

## Background (what exists today)

  `properties/downloadedpiecesbar.cpp` is the borrowed model (§4.18: "Proves sequential download visibly").
  After P5-06 the fork exposes `have_pieces_snapshot()`; after P5-05 the playable prefix exists; after P3-10
  and P4-03 both details views exist with tabs gated on `caps`. FrankenTUI 0.6 ships `canvas` in
  `ftui-extras`.

  before encoding (100,000 pieces → 16.7 KB), bounded by construction (DL-42).

## Goal and user value
§6.2 row 25 (T2): visible proof that sequential and first/last pieces are working, which is what streaming

   file, `playable_end?` from P5-05's prefix).
2. The `torrent:<h>.pieces` topic (A.7: `state` frames, 2,000 ms; a detail topic sampled only while
   subscribed).
3. `components/PiecesBar.qml`: one row of `Style.space(4)` cells, `Color.foreground` for have,
   `Util.alpha(foreground, 0.22)` for missing, `Color.accent` for priority pieces (subject to the §4.2.1
   accent rule), the playable prefix underlined; in the dashboard's Pieces tab (§4.7), hidden when `caps`
   lacks `pieces`.
4. The TUI's Pieces tab as a one-line ftui-extras `canvas` row with `█` (have), `▒` (missing) and `▲`
   (priority) (§5.8), in the details modal.
5. `caps` gains `pieces`; contract bookkeeping (`contracts/ipc/v1/pieces.ndjson` with a 1,000-piece fixture;
   `docs/IPC.md`; `api::ops::TABLE`; patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in
- A.9 `Pieces {count, piece_size, have: str (MSB-first as in BEP 3, base64; ceil(count/8) bytes before
  encoding, so 100,000 pieces are 16.7 KB and the frame is bounded by construction, which a run-length form is
  not), priority: [u64] (first and last pieces per file), playable_end?}`.
- §4.7 Pieces tab: pieces bar from the have-bitfield; first and last pieces marked; the playable prefix
  shaded; topic `torrent:<h>.pieces`.
- §3.4.1: every pushed frame is under the 1 MiB line cap; a 200,000-piece frame is 33 KB of base64 plus the
  priority list.
- §3.4.7 unkeyed small topics (`torrent:<hash>.pieces`) send `state {data}` with the whole object when it
  changes, at most once per interval; detail topics are released when the last subscriber leaves.
- §5.8: pieces bar = a one-line `canvas` (ftui-extras) row.

## Acceptance criteria
- A 1,000-piece fixture renders with first and last pieces and the playable prefix marked in both UIs.
- A 200,000-piece `Pieces` frame is under 64 KiB.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Unit `pieces::tests::{bitfield_roundtrip, frame_under_64k_200000}`.
- TUI golden; `qs-dashboard.sh::pieces_bar`; fixture `regression_tests/fixtures/states/pieces-1000.json`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `frame_under_64k_200000` prints the encoded frame size; `pieces_bar` logs

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P5-06 (the bitfield accessor), P1-08 (the state topic), P3-10 (the dashboard pane), P4-03 (the
  TUI store).
- Consumed by M5.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)

  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait

  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.

  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table

  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.

  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.

  checklists are not items; scripts are.

  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`

  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,

  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.

  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.

  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

item feeds: **M5**; topological level 19 of 22 (0 = ready now).

writes JSONL with expect/observed).

   --json` gains `history` (Appendix F).
3. `components/Sparkline.qml` in the dashboard's status row (redraw on data, no interpolation, §4.13).
4. ftui `sparkline` in the TUI tab bar (§5.8), redrawn on data.
5. `caps` gains `history`; contract bookkeeping (fixture, `docs/IPC.md`, patch bump with the `status.history`
   field in `changes[]`).

- §4.6 bottom rows: contextual keys, the last message with its time, plus the speed sparkline.

# P6-04: Statistics, session and all-time

Plan item **P6-04** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5383). Phase P6; size

item feeds: **M5**; topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

view, Help overlay), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every

add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake

lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI

description:
# P6-05: Force start and queue order

Plan item **P6-05** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5397). Phase P6; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M5**;
topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-09 (Mutations: refs, pending, confirmed), P3-09 (Torrents view), P4-02 (One
action table for keys, footer and help), P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Pause/resume exists; no force start, no reorder (§6.2 row 20, partial). `Record` is `src/engine.rs:37-53`
  (with a `resume_after_migration` serde default), `reconcile_queue` at `:280-343` (after P1-02:
  `src/engine/ledger.rs`, `src/engine/queue.rs`); the only ledger insert is `ledger.records.push`
  (`src/engine.rs:949`); `max_active_downloads` default 3 (`src/config.rs:15`); start/stop while parked write
  the ledger and apply on unpark (`src/engine.rs:1341-1348`). `PanelKeyCatcher` has `reorderable` and one
  `reorderRequested(dy)` signal (`Ui/PanelKeyCatcher.qml:39,42`) that fires for Ctrl+k/Ctrl+j and
  Ctrl+↑/Ctrl+↓ (`:64-70`).
- After P1-09 idempotency classes exist; after P3-09 the table and sort exist; after P4-02/P4-03 the TUI
  dispatches `P`/`K`/`J` over API v1.

## Goal and user value
§6.2 row 20 (T2): "watch this one now" when the three slots are busy. The ledger order becomes the queue order
so reordering is a durable, visible thing (`queue_pos`), admission is a pure function with unit tests, and
reordering never pauses a running torrent.

## Do (exact steps)
**Ledger and queue** (`src/engine/ledger.rs`, `src/engine/queue.rs`):
1. `Record.force: bool` (serde default `false`); the ledger order is the queue order (restored, undone (P6-08)
   and deferred (P7-09) records go to the end; no code path may sort and save `ledger.records`, guarded by
   `ledger::tests::save_preserves_order`).
2. Admission is a pure function `queue::admit(records, stats, limit) -> Decisions` that `reconcile_queue`
   applies: forced records always run and do not count toward `max_active_downloads`; unforced records with
   intent `run` are admitted in ledger order while unforced running records are fewer than the limit;
   reordering never pauses a running torrent (a moved torrent takes the next slot that frees; slots are
   released only by pause, stop, completion or error).
3. `Torrent.queue_pos` (A.9) is the 1-based position among records with intent `run`, `completion_on == 0` and
   `force == false`, including those in `error`, `metadata`, `waiting_vpn` or without a handle (they are
   waiting too); held records stay `queued` with `reason: queue_full` and the secondary text "N of M slots
   busy · #pos" (§4.3.4).
4. `force` turns off on `torrents.stop`, on completion and on `force_start {on: false}`, which puts the record
   back at its ledger position (it keeps running if a slot is free, else `queued`).
**API** (`src/api/ops/torrents.rs`):
5. `torrents.force_start {hashes (1..256), on}` → `{state: "done"}` (idempotent, A.1): `on: true` also clears
   a user pause (an explicit "run now"); on a `done` torrent with seeding off `invalid_state` with the hint
   `fbittorrent seed <hash>`; on an `error` torrent it retries like `start`; on a staged torrent
   `invalid_state`; while parked it writes the ledger and applies on unpark.
6. `torrents.queue_move {hash, to: top | up | down | bottom}` → `{state: "done", queue_pos}` (not idempotent,
   A.1; refused with `invalid_state` after a restart like every non-idempotent op, P1-09): `up`/`down` swap
   with the nearest record that has a `queue_pos` (paused, done and forced records are skipped),
   `top`/`bottom` move to the first or last position among positioned records; on a torrent without
   `queue_pos` `invalid_state`; while parked it reorders the ledger offline.
7. `torrents.start {force: true}` sets `force` and lists an already-running torrent in `started`, not
   `skipped`. `Torrent.force`, `Torrent.queue_pos` (A.9, A.10); `caps` gains `queue`; contract bookkeeping
   (`contracts/ipc/v1/queue.ndjson`; `docs/IPC.md`; `api::ops::TABLE`; patch bump).
**UIs**:
8. The state word stays `Downloading` / `Queued`; a forced torrent shows "· forced" in the secondary text and
   the `⚡` text glyph after the state cell in the TUI (a `forced` row in `contracts/ui/states.json`);
   `queue_pos` shows as "#3" in the secondary text of queued rows and as the sort key "Queue" (`s`, Appendix
   B); `P` toggles `force` on the selection (`hashes`) and `K`/`J` move the cursor row (`queue_move {to:

# P6-06: App-owned fast resume (fork change)

Plan item **P6-06** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5457). Phase P6; size
**L (more than three days or more than 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds:
**M5**; topological level 19 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-16 (Lazy restore of completed torrents), P5-03 (Recheck).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)), P7-02 (Move / set location).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- D3: every open re-hashes all data (7 s for the owner's 3.4 GiB); `fastresume: false` (`src/engine.rs:437`);
  the fork refuses a trusted have-bitfield (`vendor/rqbit/librqbit/src/session.rs:567-568`,
  `torrent_state/initializing.rs:113-114`). P1-16 covers completed torrents (dormant, no trust needed); live
  and seeding torrents still check at every start.
- After P5-03 `torrents.recheck` exists and must invalidate resume data; `docs/engine-evaluation.md` has an
  "Ownership and durable state" section (EE) and will gain a fast-resume section (§8.5).

## Goal and user value
The rest of D3 (§6.2 additional item "App-owned fast resume for all torrents", T2): remove the remaining
start-up checks safely. Trust is earned, not assumed (R7): only after a clean-shutdown marker and matching
size and mtime for every file; `recheck` stays the escape hatch.

## Do (exact steps)
1. **Fork**: `initializing.rs` accepts a trusted have-bitfield (today it refuses at `:113-114`).
2. **Daemon**: writes `engine/resume/<hash>.bin` (the bitfield plus size and mtime of every included file) on
   clean drain and every 5 minutes for live torrents, and `engine/resume/CLEAN` as the clean-shutdown marker
   (removed at start, written at drain).
3. On start a record is restored with the trusted bitfield only when the marker existed and every file's size
   and mtime match, else with a full check; `checked: true` after a trusted restore (A.9).
4. `torrents.recheck` deletes the record's resume file first (P5-03).
5. `docs/engine-evaluation.md` gains the fast-resume section (§8.5).
6. No new API surface (behaviour only; `checked` already exists).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Fast resume (P6-06)": fork: `initializing.rs` accepts a trusted have-bitfield; the daemon writes
  `engine/resume/<hash>.bin` on clean drain and every 5 min for live torrents, and `engine/resume/CLEAN`; a
  record is restored with the trusted bitfield only when the marker existed and every file's size and mtime
  match, else with a full check; `torrents.recheck` deletes the record's resume file first; tests
  `daemon.py::{resume_trusted, resume_touched_file, resume_after_kill9}`, fork unit test
  `trusted_bitfield_accepted`.
- §3.2.7 crash recovery: data is re-checked on the next start (until P6-06); after this item only when the
  marker is missing or a file changed.
- §3.2.8 shutdown order: the resume files and the marker are written in the drain, before the sockets are
  unlinked and the lock released.
- Appendix D "Fast resume": trusting a saved have-bitfield on start instead of re-checking data (P6-06).
  "Dormant / lazy restore" (P1-16) remains the no-trust path for completed torrents.
- P7-02 (move) restores with fast resume so a completed torrent stays `done` without a re-check.

## Acceptance criteria
- Restarting with untouched data shows no `checking`.
- Touching one file re-checks only that torrent.
- `kill -9` (no marker) forces a full check of every torrent.

## Tests (and what they log)
- Fork unit test `trusted_bitfield_accepted`.
- `daemon.py::{resume_trusted, resume_touched_file, resume_after_kill9, recheck_drops_resume_file}` (each logs
  which torrents entered `checking`).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P1-16 (the restore task and `checked`) and P5-03 (recheck deletes the resume file first).
- Consumed by M5 and P7-02 (move relies on fast resume).

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

- R7 (low, high): fast resume trusts data that changed or is corrupt; mitigations: the clean-shutdown marker,

# P6-07: Live per-torrent upload cap without rebuild (fork change)

**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `daemon`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M5**; topological level 9 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-19 (Typed operations and the normalized model).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)), P7-06 (Per-torrent download cap).

fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,

toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays

the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,

## Goal and user value
§6.2 row 23 (T2): removes a surprising re-check; the per-torrent download cap (P7-06) reuses the same live

## Do (exact steps)
1. **Fork**: expose the live torrent's `Limits` through `ManagedTorrent::set_upload_bps(Option<u64>)` so a cap
   change applies without a rebuild.
2. `torrents.set_upload_limit` answers `{state: "done"}` synchronously (A.5; `pending` until this item) and
   `torrents.set_seed` uses the same path; `seed`/`noseed` stop re-checking.
