title: P6-08: Origin field, filters, bulk remove, undo for keep-files removal
description:
# P6-08: Origin field, filters, bulk remove, undo for keep-files removal

Plan item **P6-08** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5486). Phase P6; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M5**;
topological level 19 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-09 (Torrents view), P4-04 (Responsive layouts at 80, 120 and 160 columns),
P4-08 (Log modal, toasts and message history).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Categories are passed through with no UI (§6.2 row 21); there is no undo for a removal (row 32, new);
  cleanup is one torrent at a time (W8). The record's `.torrent` is kept under the engine store
  (`src/engine.rs:166`). `Record.origin` has no field yet; `torrents.add {origin}` is accepted and stored
  since P1-06/P1-11 (`manual|handler|agent`), and `search.grab`, `rss.grab`, `shows.grab` set `search`, `rss`,
  `shows`.
- After P3-09 the sidebar and table exist; after P4-04 the TUI has the filtered views; after P4-08 the TUI has
  toasts with history. The dashboard's bulk `X` must be a window `Shortcut` because `PanelKeyCatcher` folds
  `x`, `X` and Delete into one `deleteRequested()` (DL-67).

## Goal and user value
W8 (clean up): after watching, the owner removes finished torrents one at a time or as a filtered set, always
through an explicit choice, with a 10 s undo for the keep-files case so a mis-press costs nothing (§2.7 "Undo
and bulk cleanup"). `origin` ("where did this come from": search, RSS, Shows, manual) is the useful grouping
for one download folder, instead of categories (§6.2 row 21). Bulk remove is keep-files only (Q28); undo is
per batch (Q29).

## Do (exact steps)
1. `Record.origin: open(manual | search | rss | shows | clipboard | handler | agent)`, serde default `manual`
   for old records, set by `torrents.add {origin}`, `search.grab`, `rss.grab`, `shows.grab`, `add-clipboard`
   (`clipboard`) and the desktop handler (`handler`) (Appendix F).
2. `torrents.list {origin: [str]?}` filters; the sidebar's "From:" buckets (§4.6) are Search, RSS, Shows and
   Manual (clipboard, handler, agent and unknown values count as Manual).
3. **Bulk remove** is keep-files only: `X` acts on the rows currently listed (the active state filter, the `/`
   text filter and the From filter together, in both UIs), confirms with the count and the summed `size` of
   the rows that have one ("+ 2 of unknown size" otherwise) through `ConfirmDialog` (`selectedIndex: 0`) or
   the TUI prompt (`y/N`), then sends one `torrents.remove {hashes (≤ 256), delete_files: false}`; deleting
   files stays per torrent (`D`) or `delete --files --yes`.
4. **Undo** state is in memory and dies with the daemon: `torrents.remove {delete_files: false}` moves each
   record and its `.torrent` to `engine/undo/<hash>.{json,torrent}` and answers `undo_until` (now + 10 s,
   A.5); `torrents.add {source: {restore: hash}}` within the window re-adds from there, else `invalid_state`;
   `fbittorrent undo [<hash>]` with no hash restores the last batch (`undo_until` is per batch).
5. **Toast**: the dashboard's `Banner` component at the bottom of the list, "Removed 'X' (3 torrents) · U
   undo", for 10 s; the TUI's P4-08 toast with the same text; `U` restores (Appendix B; never `u`, which is
   seed on the same screen).
6. `caps` gains `origin`; contract bookkeeping (`torrents.list {origin}`, `{restore}` source, `undo_until`,
   the `undo` verb in `capabilities.commands[]`, patch bump, fixture, `docs/IPC.md`).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Origin, filters, bulk remove, undo (P6-08)": `Record.origin` set by search grab, RSS grab, Shows
  grab, clipboard, handler (default `manual`); undo keeps the `.torrent` file and the record under
  `engine/undo/` for 10 s after a keep-files removal, in memory, per batch; `torrents.remove` with up to 256
  hashes; `torrents.add {source: {restore: hash}}` within the undo window; TUI `X` on a filtered view with
  count and size confirm; undo toast `U`; Quickshell sidebar "From:" filters, bulk remove, undo toast; CLI
  `delete … --json` returns `undo_until`; `undo [<hash>]`; tests: unit origin persisted;
  `daemon.py::undo_restore` re-adds and checks to `done`.
- A.5 `torrents.remove {hashes, delete_files}` → `{state: enum(done|pending), undo_until: ts?}` (pending when
  deleting files; `undo_until` only when files are kept); `torrents.add {source: {restore: hash}}`. A.9
  `Torrent.origin: open(…)?`; `TorrentDetail.undo_until?`. A.1: `torrents.remove` is not idempotent;
  `torrents.add` is.
- Appendix B: Undo last remove (new, P6-08): TUI `U` while the undo toast shows; dashboard the toast's button,
  `U`; Bulk remove the filtered set (new): `X`, bound in the dashboard through `Shortcut { sequence:
  "Shift+X"; context: Qt.WindowShortcut }`.
- Appendix F: `delete <sel>… [--files --yes] [--dry-run]`: `torrents.remove`; unchanged plus `undo_until`;
  exit 0, 3, 4, 6, 7. `undo [<hash>]` (new): `torrents.add {source: {restore: hash}}` for the hash, or for
  every hash of the last keep-files batch when omitted; starts: yes; JSON new `{ok, action: "undo", hashes}`;
  exit 0, 1 (`invalid_state` after the window), 4, 6. `list [--origin o]`; `add-clipboard` → `origin:
  "clipboard"`.
- §4.9: bulk removal of a filtered set shows the count and total size and requires `y`; a keep-files removal

# P6-09: Peer port setting and sleep inhibitor

Plan item **P6-09** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5516). Phase P6; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M5**; topological level 18 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-05 (Settings operations), P3-15 (Settings sheet, Log view, Help overlay),
P4-03 (The TUI on API v1).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- `peer_port` is in config only (§6.2 row 27); UPnP is refused by the fork (`session.rs:569-570`); TCP only.
  There is no sleep inhibitor (row 36, new): a laptop can suspend mid-download (FO §5).
  `/usr/bin/systemd-inhibit` exists on this machine (checked); a child process avoids adding a D-Bus library
  to a binary that has no async runtime (FO §4.2).
- After P3-05 restart-class settings restart the engine in place with clients connected; after P3-15 the
  Settings sheet exists; after P4-03 the TUI's F6 is on API v1.

## Goal and user value
§6.2 rows 27 and 36 (T2): the port as a setting (with VPN binding UPnP is moot; without it the owner is a
leecher-first client that reaches peers through DHT and outgoing connections) and a sleep inhibitor so a
laptop does not suspend mid-download. Both are small and land in both UIs' settings.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `Settings.peer_port` (A.9; a restart-class key, applied through `app.settings.set {peer_port}` with the
   engine restart of P3-05 while clients stay connected, §3.2.8); a field in the dashboard's Settings sheet
   and the TUI's F6 modal; `settings --port N` (Appendix F).
2. `src/daemon/inhibit.rs` (§3.8 "Sleep inhibitor"): while any torrent is `downloading`, `stalled`, `metadata`
   or `checking` with intent `run`, the daemon holds one child `systemd-inhibit --what=sleep --who=fbittorrent
   --why=Downloading --mode=block sleep infinity` and kills it within 5 s of the last such torrent stopping;
   the child is also killed on drain (`KillMode=mixed` sends SIGTERM to the daemon only; it kills its children
   itself).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.8 Sleep inhibitor (P6-09): while any torrent downloads, the daemon holds `systemd-inhibit --what=sleep
  --who=fbittorrent --why=Downloading --mode=block sleep infinity` as a child and kills it when downloads
  stop.
- §3.2.2 unit: `KillMode=mixed` ("SIGTERM to the daemon only; it drains providers, the inhibitor and notifier
  children itself. Anything still alive at TimeoutStopSec is SIGKILLed by systemd.").
- §3.2.7 "Running → Starting → Running": restart-class setting (`peer_encryption`, `network_interface`,
  `peer_port`) → `engine.changed` twice; connections survive.
- A.9 `Settings.peer_port: u64`, `restart_class: [str]` (the keys whose change restarts the engine).
- Appendix F `settings [... --port]`: `app.settings.set` when running; file write when down; starts: only to
  apply live; exit 0, 2.
- §3.3 module layout: `src/daemon/inhibit.rs` systemd-inhibit holder (P6-09).
- §2.6 non-goal: UPnP out; uTP out (large engine work).

- A port change restarts the engine with clients still connected (they receive `engine.changed`).
- The inhibitor child exists only while a download runs.

# P6-10: New-release notifications for Shows

Plan item **P6-10** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5532). Phase P6; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M5**; topological level 14 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-13 (Daemon notifications and the icon), P3-03 (Shows in the daemon).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Shows checks happen only when a UI is open; nothing tells the owner about new episodes when the daemon runs
  in the background (W2 step 2: "With the daemon running in the background, a check that finds new releases
  notifies once (P6-10)"). After P3-03 the daemon runs `shows.check` on interactive connect or on request and
  emits `shows.checked {imdb?, new, warnings}`; after P1-13 the notifier exists with its queue, collapse and
  action handling.

## Goal and user value
Closes the follow-a-show loop without opening the app (§6.2 additional item "New-release notifications for
Shows", T2). Suppressed while a dashboard or TUI is interactive, because the badge shows it there instead (no
double signal).

## Do (exact steps)
1. After a `shows.check` (scheduled or explicit) that found new unread releases: one notification per check
   through P1-13's notifier: title "3 new episodes", body "Slow Horses S05E03, South Park S27E06, …" (at most
   three release names, then "+ N more"), action `window` → `fbittorrent dashboard --view shows` (§3.8 row
   "new releases").
2. Never for a check that found nothing.
3. Suppressed while a dashboard or TUI is interactive (the badge shows it instead).
4. No new API surface (§3.8 row).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §3.8 notification table row "new releases": title "3 new episodes"; actions `window` (Shows view); item
  P6-10.
- §3.7 scheduling: a check runs when a client becomes interactive and the show is stale (30 minutes); never
  otherwise; a check never downloads.
- A.8 `shows.checked {imdb?, new: u64, warnings: [{imdb, message}]}`.
- §4.6: unread badges (`Color.accent` dot plus count) on the `3 Shows` tab and the sidebar link are the in-app
  signal.
- §2.4 Notifications surface: new episodes.
- §6.2 row 39: quiet hours are the shell's notification service's business (Do Not Disturb), nothing to build.

## Acceptance criteria
- A check against the EZTV fixture with new releases sends one notification.
- A second check with nothing new sends none.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::{shows_notify, shows_notify_none_when_unchanged, shows_notify_suppressed_interactive}` with the
  EZTV fixture server (the fake `notify-send` shim's log is the observed text).
- Added in polish round 1: unit test `notify::tests::new_episodes_body` (one, three and five releases → "1 new
  episode" / "3 new episodes" / "5 new episodes"; the body lists at most three names then "+ 2 more"; markup
  is escaped).

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P3-03 (`shows.check` and `shows.checked`) and P1-13 (the notifier).
- Consumed by M5.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- Q5 (open, default no): a check never downloads; the notification is the only automatic effect.

## Risks and decisions
- DL-52 (the notifier's rules), principle 2 (deliberate downloads: notify, never add).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.

- [ ] A check against the EZTV fixture with new releases sends one notification.
- [ ] A second check with nothing new sends none.

## Background (what exists today)
- The add sheet (P3-11) shows the destination as `save_path` with no free-space figure and no way to choose
  another folder; Quickshell has no file dialog (FO §2.11). `add --save <dir>` accepts any path today.
  Sprout's "-1 B" free-space bug (OR §6 gotcha 6) is why `free_bytes` is absent on error and never negative
  (§3.4.9).

## Goal and user value
Avoid filling the disk at the moment of choice (§6.2 additional item "Destination picker with free space",
T2): the add sheet shows "312 GiB free" and lets the owner pick a folder; an unwritable folder is refused in
the sheet and by the CLI. P7-02 (move) reuses the picker.

## Do (exact steps)
1. `app.free_space {path}` → `{free_bytes: bytes?, writable: bool}` (A.4; `statvfs`; absent on error, never
   negative, §3.4.9).
2. In `AddSheet.qml` a destination row showing the free space ("312 GiB free") and a folder picker
   `components/FolderPicker.qml`: a small directory browser over Qt's `FolderListModel` (`import
   Qt.labs.folderlistmodel`; verified installed on this machine at `/usr/lib/qt6/qml/Qt/labs/folderlistmodel`
   next to Quickshell 0.3.2, while `Quickshell.Io` ships only `FileView` and no directory listing,
   `quickshell-io.qmltypes`, checked 2026-10-18) with `showDirs: true`, `showFiles: false`, `showHidden:
   false`, `showDotAndDotDot: false` and a `..` row added by the component (starts at `save_path`, Enter
   selects, `..` goes up, hidden folders skipped); the chosen path is sent to `app.free_space {path}`, the row
   shows `free_bytes` as "312 GiB free" or "—" when absent, and `writable: false` disables the Download
   button; the sheet refuses a destination that is not writable.
3. `add --save <dir>` validates the same way (exit 2 when not writable).
4. Contract bookkeeping (`app.free_space` row in `api::ops::TABLE`, `docs/IPC.md`, fixture, patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Add sheet destination (P6-11)": `statvfs` of the chosen folder; validate writable; `app.free_space
  {path}` → `{free_bytes?, writable}`; the TUI add prompt shows free space; Quickshell a destination row ("312
  GiB free") with `components/FolderPicker.qml`; `add --save <dir>` validates (exit 2 when not writable);
  tests unit `free_space::tests::{absent_on_error, never_negative}`; `qs-dashboard.sh::destination_picker`;
  `agent_contract.py::add_save_unwritable`.
- §4.8 step 2: the destination (default `~/Downloads`; P6-11 adds a picker with free space). Appendix C add
  sheet mockup: `Save to  ~/Downloads               412 GiB free`.
- §4.2.3: sizes in sentences use binary units ("312 GiB free").
- §3.4.9: `free_space` absent when `statvfs` failed or returned a negative value. `Summary.disk` (P5-07) is
  the one place free space lives for the running downloads; this op answers for an arbitrary path.
- P5-07's add-sheet refusal ("Needs 8.9 GiB · 1.2 GiB free") compares `size` with this op's `free_bytes` for
  the chosen destination.

## Acceptance criteria
- Free space is absent on error and never negative (unit).
- The picker selects a folder and the committed torrent lands there.
- An unwritable folder is refused in the sheet and by the CLI.

- Unit `free_space::tests::{absent_on_error, never_negative}`; `qs-dashboard.sh::destination_picker`;
  `agent_contract.py::add_save_unwritable`.
- Logging (polish round 1): `destination_picker` logs the picker's `state()` path at each key and the
  committed torrent's `save_path`; `add_save_unwritable` logs argv, exit code (2) and the error envelope; the
  unit tests print the `statvfs` results they stubbed.

# P6-12: Private-torrent rules (BEP 27) check

Plan item **P6-12** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5560). Phase P6; size
**S (under a day of agent work, roughly under 300 changed lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this
item feeds: **M5**; topological level 5 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P0-05 (Pin the toolchain and fix the multi-crate engine test build), P1-07

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want

   fixture torrent and a local tracker asserting no DHT announce and no PeX message is sent.

title: P6-13: Clipboard magnet watch (opt-in, A7)
description:
# P6-13: Clipboard magnet watch (opt-in, A7)

Plan item **P6-13** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5572). Phase P6; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M5**;
topological level 15 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P1-13 (Daemon notifications and the icon), P2-03 (Popup rewrite), P3-05 (Settings
operations).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M5 (T2 complete (v0.6.0)).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent

and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- There is no clipboard watching; "find in browser, download" costs a copy, a popup open and `a`. Fragments'
  clipboard watcher is its best idea (FO §5; §6.2 row 31, new, T2, opt-in). A7: opt-in, off by default,
  because reading the clipboard continuously is a privacy decision the owner makes, not the plan (R16).
- After P1-13 the notifier exists; after P2-03 the popup has the offer strip component (shared with this
  item); after P3-05 `Settings.clipboard_watch` has an API path. Running `wl-paste --watch fbittorrent
  clipboard-event` would spawn the CLI per change; one `wl-paste --watch cat` child with bounded output is the
  design. Whether `wl-paste --watch` output can be bounded without losing events is unverified (§10.4).

## Goal and user value
§2.7 "Clipboard magnet (opt-in)": "Add 'Sintel'?" strip in the popup and a notification when a magnet lands on
the clipboard, removing the last two keystrokes from "find in browser, download". §9.5's P6 human check: "the
owner turns on clipboard watching for a day and reports whether it is useful" (Q11, default off).

## Do (exact steps)
1. `Settings.clipboard_watch` (default `false`); when on, the daemon (`src/daemon/clipboard.rs`) runs one
   child `wl-paste --watch cat` with bounded output (lines over 64 KiB dropped), parses magnets from its
   stream, dedupes by btih against the ledger and the last offer, and emits `clipboard.magnet {hash, name?,
   already_added}` (A.8) plus the notification "Magnet on clipboard: <name>" with actions `add` →
   `torrents.add {origin: "clipboard"}` and `dismiss` → `app.clipboard.dismiss {hash}` (§3.8).
2. The popup offer strip and the dashboard banner (§4.11 row "Clipboard magnet": strip "Add
   'Sintel.2010.1080p'?" [Add] [Dismiss]; banner with the same actions); the TUI footer strip "Add '<name>'?
   (y/Esc)".
3. Turning the setting off kills the child; the child is never a reason to stay alive (§3.2.10
   `clipboard_watch`: not busy; the watcher restarts with the daemon).
4. Clipboard text is never logged (§3.9: the daemon keeps nothing but the last magnet's hash, to avoid repeat
   offers).
5. `settings --clipboard-watch on|off` (Appendix F); `caps` gains `clipboard`; contract bookkeeping
   (`clipboard.magnet` event, `app.clipboard.dismiss {hash}` → `{}` in `api::ops::TABLE`, fixture,
   `docs/IPC.md`, patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Clipboard watch (P6-13, A7)": setting `clipboard_watch = false`; `wl-paste --watch fbittorrent
  clipboard-event` is **not** used (it would spawn the CLI per change); one `wl-paste --watch cat` child with
  bounded output; dedupe by btih against the ledger and the last offer; never log clipboard text; event
  `clipboard.magnet {hash, name, already_added}`; `app.clipboard.dismiss {hash}`; TUI footer strip "Add
  '<name>'? (y/Esc)"; popup strip and dashboard banner [Add] [Dismiss]; notification with "Add"; `settings
  --clipboard-watch on|off`; test `daemon.py::clipboard_watch_offer`: a fake `wl-paste` on `PATH` prints a
  magnet after 1 s; the event arrives; "add" adds it; a second identical magnet does not re-offer.
- §3.8 row "clipboard magnet (opt-in)": title "Magnet on clipboard: <name>", actions `add`, `dismiss`.
- §3.2.10 busy table: `clipboard_watch` is **not busy**; the watcher restarts with the daemon; it never keeps
  it alive (DL-27).
- §3.9 Clipboard: read only when the setting is on; the daemon keeps nothing but the last magnet's hash and
  never logs clipboard text.
- §4.8: the popup's `a` offer strip is one component shared with P6-13. Appendix B: Clipboard offer (new,
  P6-13): add / dismiss: TUI `y` / Esc while the strip shows; dashboard the strip's buttons, `y` / Esc; popup
  `y` / Esc.
- §4.15: `wl-paste` is a short-lived process in the plugin; the long-lived watcher is the daemon's child (a
  `Process` destructor SIGKILLs its child on reload, so nothing long-lived may be a child of the plugin).
- A.8 `clipboard.magnet {hash, name: str?, already_added: bool}`; A.4 `app.clipboard.dismiss {hash}` → `{}`;
  A.9 `Settings.clipboard_watch: bool`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Off by default (`settings` shows it).

# P7-01: Torznab indexers (§7.3)

Plan item **P7-01** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5597). Phase P7; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M6**;
topological level 13 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-01 (Search in the daemon).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M6 (T3 complete).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- Search providers are qBittorrent nova plugins: Python scripts the user installs (§7.3). Private trackers
  need Jackett or Prowlarr, which speak Torznab (an XML API). `quick-xml` is already a dependency
  (`Cargo.toml:34`). After P3-01 the daemon owns search sessions, dedupe and `Provider.kind:
  enum(nova|torznab)` (A.9) with the `torznab` value reserved.
- Security rules for credential files (§3.9): a credential file is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and refused, not
  repaired, when its mode is wrong (OR §6 gotcha 7, the marketplace reviewer's bar).

## Goal and user value
Private trackers without Python (§7.3; §6.2 additional item "Torznab indexers", T3), and the reviewer-friendly
kind of search (OR §8 item 10). Key hygiene is the feature's substance: the key lives only in its own 0600
file, never inline, so `settings`/`config` output can never print it, and never appears in logs, errors or
argv.

## Do (exact steps)
1. A native provider kind `torznab` in `src/search.rs` (`Provider.kind: torznab`, A.9) configured by
   `search.install {sources: [https URL]}` and `~/.config/fbittorrent/indexers.toml` (0600, opened with
   `O_NOFOLLOW`, refused if group- or world-readable): `[[torznab]] name, url, api_key_file`; the key is read
   from a 0600 file opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` (§3.9; refused, not repaired, when its mode is wrong).
2. Queries `?t=search&q=<query>&apikey=<key>` with a 30 s timeout and a 4 MiB response cap; results map to
   `SearchResult` (`magnet` or `url`, `size`, `seeds`, `uploaded_at`) and enter the shared dedupe (P3-01).
3. HTTPS is required when an API key is set, except on loopback: a key over plain HTTP to a non-loopback host
   is refused with `invalid_args`; a cross-origin redirect is refused with `upstream`; the key never appears
   in logs or error messages.
4. The TUI providers modal and the dashboard providers sheet list the kind.
5. CLI `search --install-torznab <url> --key-file <path>` (Appendix F); `caps` gains `torznab`; contract
   bookkeeping (`api::ops::TABLE`, `docs/IPC.md`, fixture, `capabilities.commands[]`, patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §7.3 Torznab (P7-01, T3): a native provider kind for Jackett or Prowlarr, without Python; configuration in
  `~/.config/fbittorrent/indexers.toml` (0600, `O_NOFOLLOW`, refused if group- or world-readable):
  `[[torznab]] name, url, api_key_file` (the key lives only in its own 0600 file, never inline); rules: HTTPS
  required when an API key is set, except on loopback; redirects to another origin refused; the key never
  appears in logs, errors or argv; responses capped at 4 MiB and 30 s; XML parsing uses `quick-xml`.
- §3.9 Files: a credential file is additionally opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and refused, not repaired, when its
  mode is wrong.
- §7.2 bounded reads everywhere; §7.1: the marketplace is not a goal (DL-17), but this is the
  reviewer-friendly kind of search.
- A.6 `search.install {curated? | sources?}` → pending then `mutation.result {installed, failed}`; A.9
  `Provider {name, full_name?, kind: enum(nova|torznab), enabled, url?, version?}`.
- Appendix E.3: Torznab fixture server with redirect cases (`fixtures.torznab_server()`).
- DL-69: Torznab keys live only in `api_key_file`, with a 4 MiB and 30 s cap.

## Acceptance criteria
- A Torznab fixture server returns results that appear deduplicated with the other providers.
- A key over plain HTTP to a non-loopback host is refused.
- A cross-origin redirect is refused.
- The key never appears in logs.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::torznab_{results, http_key_refused, redirect_refused, key_not_logged}`
  (`fixtures.torznab_server()` with a redirect case; `key_not_logged` greps the daemon log and every error
  message for the key).
- Unit `torznab::tests::parse_fixture`.

- Depends on P3-01 (search sessions, dedupe, `Provider.kind`).
- Consumed by M6.

# P7-02: Move / set location

Plan item **P7-02** of `docs/plan-2026-10-18/PLAN.md` (round 6, 2026-10-18; §9.3 line 5615). Phase P7; size
**M (one to three days, 300 to 1,000 lines)**; surface `feature`; first milestone this item feeds: **M6**;
topological level 20 of 22 (0 = ready now).

**Depends on (blocked by):** P3-10 (Details pane: Overview, Files, Log), P6-06 (App-owned fast resume (fork
change)).

**Consumed by (unblocks):** M6 (T3 complete).

## Project context (why this project exists, in one paragraph)
fbittorrent is a Rust torrent app for one person on an Omarchy (Hyprland + Quickshell) desktop in Switzerland,
for legal personal use: streaming-first (sequential download plus first/last piece priority, always on, not
toggleable), seeding off by default (32 KiB/s upload cap while downloading, stop when complete, per-torrent
`seed` override), downloads to `~/Downloads`, keyboard-first, driven by AI agents through a `--json` CLI with
exit codes 0..8, sometimes over SSH. The plan of 2026-10-18 (round 6, steady state) decides: keep both
surfaces (the Omarchy bar widget `oliver.torrents` with its popup plus a new Quickshell dashboard window, and
the FrankenTUI) over one headless daemon, `fbittorrent serve`, that owns the torrent engine (the rqbit 9.0.1
fork on the Asupersync runtime), search, RSS, Shows and IMDb. Every client (bar, dashboard, TUI, CLI,
`magnet:` handler, agents) speaks one versioned API v1: newline-delimited JSON over
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fbittorrent/api.sock` that sends a snapshot and then pushed deltas. The binary name stays
`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Background (what exists today)
- The save path is set only at add (`src/main.rs:513`; §6.2 row 4). Files can be moved with a file manager
  after removing the torrent; a move becomes cheap once fast resume (P6-06) avoids a re-check.
  `Record.output_folder` is the ledger field. After P3-10 the Overview has an action row; after P6-11 a folder
  picker exists.

## Goal and user value
§6.2 row 4 (T3): library organisation; a completed torrent stays `done` after a move without a re-check thanks
to P6-06. Dashboard and CLI only (T3; none in the TUI).

## Do (exact steps)
1. `torrents.move {hashes, save_path}` → `{state: "pending"}` then `mutation.result` (A.5; not idempotent,
   A.1; a client never resends it; a mid-request loss exits 8): pause; move the payload (rename on the same
   filesystem; copy, fsync, unlink across filesystems; a failed copy leaves the source intact and reports
   `failed`); update `Record.output_folder`; restore with fast resume (P6-06) so a completed torrent stays
   `done`; `Torrent.save_path` follows.
2. A details action in the dashboard: Overview "Move…" `Button` (§4.7) with the folder picker of P6-11; hidden
   when `caps` lacks `move`.
3. `fbittorrent move <sel> <path>` (Appendix F: `torrents.move`; starts: yes; JSON new; exit 0, 2, 4, 6, 7,
   8).
4. `caps` gains `move`; contract bookkeeping (`api::ops::TABLE` row: mutating, not idempotent; `docs/IPC.md`;
   fixture; `capabilities.commands[]`; patch bump).

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Move (P7-02)": pause; move the payload (rename on the same filesystem; copy, fsync, unlink across
  filesystems; a failed copy leaves the source intact and reports `failed`); update `Record.output_folder`;
  restore with fast resume so a completed torrent stays `done`; `Torrent.save_path` follows; cap `move`;
  Overview "Move…" with the folder picker; CLI `move <sel> <path>` (exit 0, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8); tests
  `daemon.py::move_{same_fs, cross_fs, failed_copy_keeps_source}`; `agent_contract.py::move_verb`.
- §3.4.8: long operations (add while metadata resolves, recheck, remove with files, move, restart-class
  settings) answer `{state: "pending"}` and later push `mutation.result`; `move` has no timeout and always
  ends `done` or `failed` (P1-09).
- §3.2.4 step 6: for `remove`, `recheck`, `move` a mid-request loss exits 8 (`timeout`) with the hint
  `fbittorrent list --json`. §3.2.10: a pending move is a `mutation` busy reason.
- §3.9 payload deletion stays anchored to the torrent's output directory and refuses symlinked descendants;
  the move follows the same anchoring.
- §2.6 non-goal: file rename inside a torrent (breaks seeding and re-checks; a file manager does it after
  completion).

## Acceptance criteria
- Moves within and across filesystems in temporary directories.
- A completed torrent stays `done` without a re-check.
- A failed copy leaves the source intact and reports `failed`.

## Tests (and what they log)
- `daemon.py::move_{same_fs, cross_fs, failed_copy_keeps_source}` (cross-filesystem through a tmpfs when
  available, else skipped with a logged reason); `agent_contract.py::move_verb`.
- Added in polish round 1: unit test `move::tests::strategy_by_device` (same `st_dev` → rename; different →
  copy, fsync, unlink; a copy error leaves the source and reports `failed`; one logged row per case over a
  fake filesystem layer).
- Logging (bead review, 2026-10-18): the `move_*` cases log `st_dev` of source and destination, the
  `torrents.move` reply, the `mutation.result` outcome, `save_path` before and after and the state sequence (a
  completed torrent must stay `done`); `failed_copy_keeps_source` logs the SHA256 of the source payload before
  and after.

## Dependencies and why
- Depends on P6-06 (fast resume so the moved torrent is not re-checked) and P3-10 (the Overview action row).
- Consumed by M6.

## Owner decisions this item rests on
- None.

## Risks and decisions
- R7 (fast resume trust): the move writes fresh resume data after the copy; size and mtime are preserved by
  the copy or the record re-checks.
- DL-48/DL-55 (`move` is not idempotent; exit 8 on mid-request loss).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Moves within and across filesystems in temporary directories.
- [ ] A completed torrent stays `done` without a re-check.
- [ ] A failed copy leaves the source intact and reports `failed`.

## Goal and user value

1. Add `Record.display_name: Option<String>` (serde default `None`); `Torrent.name` serves `display_name` when

2. The restore path and the metadata-resolution path (`src/engine.rs:934`) write `record.name` only and never

   §3.9 temp-fsync-rename rule and a `torrents` delta `{name}` follows (a `name` change is structural,
   §3.4.7).
4. CLI `rename <sel> <name>` (Appendix F: starts: yes; JSON new; exit 0, 2, 4, 6, 7) refuses an ambiguous
   selector with exit 7.

   Overview title is an inline `TextField` on `N` or double-click.

  dashboard inline edit; CLI `rename <sel> <name>`; unit test.
- A.5 `torrents.rename {hash, name: str (1..512)}` → `{state: "done"}`; A.1: `torrents.rename` is not
  idempotent.
- A.9 `Torrent.name: str (≤ 1,024 in lists)`; `TorrentDetail` gains `original_name?` (additive within protocol
  major 1, §3.4.4).
- §3.4.4: input is strict (`invalid_args` names the key `name`).
- §2.6 non-goal "File rename inside a torrent": a file manager does it after completion.

## Background (what exists today)
- A3 decided no overlay in v1; the quick-add and search palette is the deferred overlay (§0.3 A3, §6.2
  additional item "Quick-add and search overlay palette", T3). An `overlay` kind must not share the bar-widget
  plugin: adding it to `oliver.torrents` would break `omarchy-shell shell toggle` routing (OR §6 gotcha 4), so
  the palette is a second plugin with its own id. The `serviceFor` facade
  (`services/PluginShellApi.qml:30-32`) lets another plugin reach `oliver.torrents`'s `Service.qml` singleton.
- After P3-12 the Search view, `search.start` and staging exist.

## Goal and user value
One chord, type a magnet or a query, Enter: the fastest path from "found it" to "downloading" without opening
the dashboard. T3 because the popup's `a` and the dashboard's `/` already cover the need; this is the owner's
optional shortcut.

## Do (exact steps)
1. A second plugin `plugin/oliver.torrents-quick/` with `kinds: ["overlay"]` (an overlay kind must not share
   the bar-widget plugin), summoned by its own chord.
2. One `FilterInput`; a magnet or `.torrent` path pastes → `torrents.add` (immediate, with the §3.8 "added"
   notification); any other text → `search.start` and the first ten results as rows; Enter on a result stages
   it (`search.grab {stage: true}`) and opens the dashboard's add sheet on it; Esc closes.
3. It uses the same `Service.qml` singleton through `serviceFor("oliver.torrents")` (no second socket).
4. `setup` installs and enables it only when asked (a flag, documented in the README); the P2-05 lint and the
   P2-04 structure rule cover `plugin/` as a whole.

## Canonical rules copied in
- §6.3 row "Quick-add palette (P7-05)": a second plugin `plugin/oliver.torrents-quick/` with `kinds:
  ["overlay"]` and its own chord; one `FilterInput`; Esc closes; reuses the `Service.qml` singleton through
  `serviceFor("oliver.torrents")`; tests `qs-smoke.sh::palette`; `qs-dashboard.sh::palette_summon_routing`
  (the bar plugin's toggle routing is unaffected).
- §4.1 summon routing: a plugin with both `bar-widget` and `panel` is excluded from `isBarWidgetPanelPlugin`
  (`shell.qml:1161-1172`); an overlay must live elsewhere.
- §4.8: the handler and the CLI stay immediate for a magnet; the palette's pasted magnet follows the same rule
  (the paste is the deliberate act); typed text searches and stages.
- §4.15: only short-lived processes; no long-lived child; all state in the daemon.
- §4.2.1/§4.14: tokens only; the P2-05 lint runs over `plugin/`.
- §5.8: ftui's `command_palette` is deliberately not used in the TUI (the owner asked for no palette until a
  task needs it); this item is the dashboard-side palette the owner can opt into.

- Summon, type a magnet, Enter adds.
- Type a query, results appear, Enter stages.
- The bar plugin's toggle routing is unaffected.

`fbittorrent`; nothing runs at login (static systemd user unit, no `[Install]`); the daemon starts on a write
and never on a read; it stops when the owner stops it (the bar icon's power button, `fbittorrent down`, `Q` in
the TUI) or by itself `idle_exit_secs = 300` after the last work ends (owner rule A1 / DL-70: "I don't want
running processes. When we close the toolbar widget, it stops, and is done."). Ten principles settle every
choice: (1) one owner of state (the daemon; UIs render), (2) deliberate downloads (RSS and Shows checks never
add torrents), (3) streaming-first defaults are intrinsic, (4) truthful state (unknown is absent, never a fake
zero or sentinel; state never shown by colour alone, because the owner's theme is monochrome: `red = #a4a4a4`,
`green = #b6b6b6`), (5) on demand and visible (lit bar icon = running process), (6) API first (every feature
lands as an API op with fixtures before any UI), (7) same letters everywhere (Appendix B keymap; two popup
exceptions), (8) Omarchy-native look (shell tokens and components only, no literal colours), (9) the agent CLI
is a first-class surface (contract 1.x stays additive), (10) tests that explain themselves (every e2e case
writes JSONL with expect/observed).

## Goal and user value
A magnet clicked while the tunnel is down should not be lost (§6.2 additional item "Deferred add while waiting
for the VPN", T3): the daemon saves a paused record and resolves it when the engine unparks, so the owner's
intent survives the VPN flap like every other intent (§3.2.9: "a download started before the tunnel dropped
resumes by itself when it returns").

## Do (exact steps)
1. While the slot is `Parked`, `torrents.add` with a magnet saves a paused record from the magnet's btih and
   `dn=` name and answers `{state: "done", hash, deferred: true}` (A.5) instead of `engine_unavailable`; when
   the engine unparks, the record's metadata resolves and it joins the queue with its saved intent.
2. `.torrent` paths are added the same way (metadata already known); `{url}` sources stay refused while parked
   (no network through the tunnel yet).
3. The rows show `waiting_vpn` (§4.3.4: `󰦝`/`⏚`, word "Waiting for VPN", `short` "VPN", secondary the
   interface name).
4. `add` prints `deferred: true` (Appendix F: `add` JSON unchanged plus `duplicate`, `deferred`); `caps` gains
   `deferred_add`; contract bookkeeping (`docs/IPC.md`, fixture, patch bump with the `add.deferred` field).
5. Deferred records go to the end of the ledger (queue order, P6-05).

## Conventions every item obeys (copied from PLAN §9.1, the §9.3 preamble and Appendix E.1; do not look them up elsewhere)
- **Paths.** `regression_tests/` means `agent_ergonomics_audit/audit/regression_tests/`; `plugin/tests/` is
  the plugin test folder outside the symlinked `plugin/oliver.torrents/` (the plugin folder is symlinked into
  `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and any file change under it reloads the desktop shell); `contracts/` is at the
  repository root; test logs go to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`. `path:line` citations refer to the
  working tree on 2026-10-18 and drift; search for the quoted symbol if a line no longer matches.
- **Done** means: the acceptance criteria pass, `all.sh` is green, CI is green (once P0-06 exists), and the
  relevant docs are updated in the same change. A **receipt** is a `## <ID>` section in
  `docs/validation/<date>/README.md` listing the commands run with exit codes, the `target/test-logs/` paths
  and any manual observation or decision; nothing else is a receipt and none carries files over 256 KB.
- **Test logging contract (Appendix E.1).** Every end-to-end step writes one JSON object per line to
  `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.jsonl`:
  `{"ts":"2026-10-18T12:41:03.117Z","suite":"daemon","case":"idle_exit_no_torrents","step":3,"action":"wait
  until summary.daemon.idle_exit_in_s == 0","expect":"daemon exits 0 within 5 s","observed":"exit 0 after 2.31
  s; bye{reason:idle}
  received","ok":true,"ms":2310,"artifacts":["target/test-logs/daemon/idle_exit_no_torrents.daemon.log"]}`.
  `ts` is UTC wall clock with milliseconds and `Z`; `step` increments from 1 per case; `expect` and `observed`
  are human sentences; the case's last line has `"final": true` and the verdict; the daemon's stderr for the
  case goes to `target/test-logs/<suite>/<case>.daemon.log`; QML marker lines `FBTQS-STEP {json}` /
  `FBTQS-PASS <case>` / `FBTQS-FAIL <case> <diff>` are converted to the same shape by
  `plugin/tests/qs-log.py`; a failing step marks the case failed, is logged with `ok: false`, and the case
  continues to its end; a failure prints both file paths and their last 20 lines; `all.sh` ends with the table
  of suites, cases, passes, failures and the slowest five cases (`scripts/testlog-summary.py`, exit 1 on any
  `ok: false`); `FBT_TEST_VERBOSE=1` mirrors every line to stderr; unit tests run with `--nocapture`; `all.sh`
  keeps failing the run on background worker panics (its `rg` scan, `all.sh:12-16`). There is no Rust twin of
  the harness module: every process-level case lives in `daemon.py`, `native.py` or `tui_smoke.py`.
- **Fixtures are local only.** No test touches the owner's daemon, torrents, feeds or shows: every suite uses
  temporary XDG directories (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` under one `mkdtemp`, the `native.py` model), local HTTP and peer fixtures, disposable info
  hashes, and `PATH` shims (`fixtures.path_shim(name, script)`) for `notify-send`, `xdg-open`, `wl-paste`,
  `wl-copy`, `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui` that append their argv to
  `<tmp>/shims/<name>.log` and optionally script stdout.
- **Git safety.** No `git stash`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean` until P0-04 is merged, and none on files an
  agent did not create afterwards. The uncommitted working tree is the only copy of the product until P0-04
  lands (R1). `br` never runs git.
- **No ceremony.** An item exists only if a user, an agent or a test consumes its output; reports, reviews and
  checklists are not items; scripts are.
- **Contract bookkeeping** (applies whenever this item adds an API operation, a CLI verb or a key): an item
  that adds an API operation also adds its row in `api::ops::TABLE` (`mutating`, `idempotent` per A.1,
  `since`; P1-18), a `docs/IPC.md` changelog entry (one per cap or field added, naming the item), its `caps`
  entry (the closed list negotiated in `hello`) and a `contracts/ipc/v1/<group>.ndjson` fixture with at least
  one `c2s`/`s2c` pair (line format: `{"dir":"c2s","frame":{…}}`, `{"dir":"s2c","frame":{…}}`,
  `{"dir":"expect","model":{…}}`, optional first line `{"dir":"volatile","paths":[…]}`); an item that adds a
  CLI verb lists it in `capabilities.commands[]` (P1-11's `commands_match_clap` fails otherwise), uses the
  `act()` JSON shape `{ok, action, count, hashes}` (`src/main.rs:718-728`) unless Appendix F gives another,
  and maps errors through A.3; an item that adds a key regenerates `plugin/oliver.torrents/keymap.json` and
  the README keys block with `scripts/gen-keymap.sh` (P4-02) and adds the Appendix B row; a bulk verb expands
  `all` client-side and sends it in chunks of 256 hashes; every item after P1-11 that adds a verb or a JSON
  field bumps the contract's patch version (1.2.1, 1.2.2, …) and adds its `capabilities.changes[]` entry;
  `list`, `show`, `status` and `wait` keep the qBittorrent-shaped torrent of contract 1.x and gain only fields
  with new names.
- **Defaults for edge states.** `torrents.start`, `stop`, `set_seed`, `remove` and `add` are ledger intents
  and work on every record (a `metadata` torrent can be paused, which stops the resolution), with one
  carve-out: `start` on a completed stop-on-complete record is `invalid_state` with the hint `fbittorrent seed
  <hash>` (P0-10) and `start all` lists it under `skipped`; a mutation that needs a live engine handle
  (`recheck`, `reannounce`, `move`, `set_files`, `set_upload_limit`, `queue_move`, `force_start`) on a torrent
  that has none (dormant, staged, `metadata`, `done` without seeding) answers `invalid_state` unless the item
  says what it does instead (`recheck`, and `set_files` with a non-empty `include`, restore a dormant torrent
  first, P1-16); any operation that needs the engine answers `engine_unavailable` while the slot is `Parked`
  and, while it is `Starting`, waits for the librqbit session for up to 60 s before answering retryable
  `engine_unavailable` (a magnet click right after `READY=1` must not fail); a read on such a torrent answers
  what the ledger knows and omits the rest.
- **API error codes (A.3) and their CLI exit codes.** `invalid_message` (not JSON / not an object / over the
  line cap), `hello_required`, `proto_unsupported`, `unknown_op` (hint lists ≤ 3 near names,
  `details.nearest`), `invalid_args` (`details.key`, `expected?`), `unsupported` → exit 2; `not_found`
  (`details.hash|feed|imdb|search_id|index`) → 6; `ambiguous` (`details.matches`, raised by the CLI before
  calling) → 7; `safety` (destructive intent not confirmed) → 3; `invalid_state` (`details.state?, reason?`),
  `already_running`, `internal` → 1; `engine_unavailable` (retryable while starting; `details.state,
  message`), `busy` (retryable; `details.limit` ∈ connections|inflight|dispatch|sessions|subs) → 4; `upstream`
  (retryable; `details.source`) → 5; `timeout` (retryable; outcome unknown; `details.after_s`) → 8.
  `duplicate` is never an error (a `result` field of `add`). Every error carries `retryable` always, `hint`
  when a copy-pasteable next step exists, `details` when a field can be named; messages quote at most 80
  characters of user input and never echo whole frames. No retryable error ever maps to exit 1
  (`agent_contract.py::retryable_never_maps_to_1`).
- **Unknown values are absent (§3.4.9).** `progress` absent when parked or metadata unknown; `size`/`files`
  before metadata; `eta_s` when not downloading or rate 0 (today's sentinel 8640000 disappears); `seeds` until
  P5-01; `peers`/`dl_bps`/`ul_bps` when the engine is not live for that torrent; `ratio` when nothing
  downloaded; `playable` when not a video / no metadata / no `watch` cap; `free_space` when `statvfs` failed
  or was negative; IMDb `rating`, search `uploaded_at`, RSS `size` when the source gave none. Rust uses
  `Option<T>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; `api::fixtures::no_sentinels` fails on
  `-1`, `8640000` or a zero in an "absent when unknown" field. Rates are the one place where 0 is a true
  value.
